author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): reconcile the three merge-introduced agent_runtime failures

All three are upstream evolution the fork must adapt to, not conflict-resolution
defects. No fork regression was deleted or weakened; each keeps guarding what it
guarded, on a premise that is now pinned so the same rot fails loudly.

1. test_continuity::test_return_summary_posts_bounded_parent_message_and_records_lineage
   Upstream f04fd1e7a added step 3b to tests/conftest.py: it re-pins the
   import-time module constant hermes_state.DEFAULT_DB_PATH to the per-test
   hermetic home. The test carried its own HERMES_HOME override, which after
   that change moved only the WRITER (production resolves the chat database
   from the live env via agent_runtime/chat_session_scope.py) while the argless
   SessionDB() the test read through stayed pinned to the conftest home. The row
   was written to <tmp>/hermes-home/state.db and looked for in
   <tmp>/hermes_test/state.db, so get_messages returned []. Dropped the now
   redundant override (conftest already isolates HERMES_HOME per test) so writer
   and reader share one file. The assertion stays a real routing assertion: the
   summary must land in the ambient operator-visible database, not a
   profile-scoped one (defect D2, chat-session-presence-authority.md).

2. test_persona_set_model::test_cli_instance_set_model_invalid_reasoning_rejected
   Upstream added "ultra" to hermes_constants.VALID_REASONING_EFFORTS
   (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max -> plus ultra). The test used "ultra" as
   its INVALID sentinel, so the rejection test was asserting exit 2 on a write
   the runtime now legitimately accepts. Retargeted to "turbo" (the sibling
   store-level test uses the same sentinel) and pinned the premise with an
   assert against VALID_REASONING_EFFORTS, so a future upstream level fails at
   the sentinel line instead of silently hollowing the regression out again.

3. test_registry_hygiene::test_hygiene_set_covers_exactly_the_kanban_and_feishu_toolsets
   The drift detector fired as designed: upstream grew the kanban toolset from 9
   to 12 tools (kanban_attach, kanban_attach_url, kanban_attachments). Extended
   the fork-owned REGISTRY_HYGIENE_BLOCKED_TOOLS constant to cover the three new
   verbs and updated the 9 -> 12 counts, rather than loosening the equality. Per
   the mission-lane hazard table, upstream kanban is KEPT (it is not the fork
   board); the constant only stops it resolving on agent-runtime lanes, and the
   three new verbs belong on that same footing.

Full gate: python -m pytest tests/agent_runtime -q -> 3145 passed, 0 failed
(pre-merge baseline was 3145/0).

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): re-honest the hermes_cli env-gap fence after the upstream merge

tests/hermes_cli/conftest.py — the registry is now a list of groups per file
(dict[str, list[(mark, reason, ids)]]) because a file can fail for more than
one reason and a single-mark-per-file registry forced one of them to be
recorded as a lie (test_web_ui_build.py is both POSIX-npm/fcntl AND a missing
`pathspec`). Three things happened in one pass:

DELETED — 163 orphaned rows across 40 files, plus the whole
test_uv_tool_update.py entry (upstream deleted that file). Upstream's prune
waves took the suite from 46,820 to 19,757 test functions; every row whose
node id no longer collects was marking nothing while still reading like a
fence. Also deleted 4 rows the registry's own stale detector reported as
PASSING (test_dashboard_unified_launch, test_gateway_wsl,
test_install_cua_driver, test_kanban_db). Registry: 55 files/256 rows ->
45 files/93 rows.

ADDED — 24 rows, every one triaged individually to a real host/platform cause.
No real regression was fenced (wave-3 ruling); the one genuine merge defect in
this area was fixed in code (see the preceding commit), not fenced:

  windows_env_gap
  * test_diff_command  the fixture writes main.py via Path.write_text (Windows
    text mode -> CRLF) and commits it with HOME=tmp, where Git-for-Windows'
    SYSTEM core.autocrlf=true normalises it to LF in the index; /diff then runs
    under the real HOME (autocrlf=false) and the clean repo reads as modified.
  * test_ensure_acp_launcher  os.geteuid does not exist on Windows.
  * test_kanban_core_functionality  os.WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS/WIFSIGNALED do not
    exist, so _classify_worker_exit() returns ("unknown", None) for every
    reaped worker and a clean-exit protocol violation is charged to the unified
    crash budget instead of the violation-only streak.
  * test_managed_uv  the fixture "binary" is a `#!/bin/sh` text file at bin/uv
    (no .exe; executing it raises WinError 216) and _default_live_venv probes
    Scripts/python.exe, not bin/python.
  * test_projects_db, test_service_manager  POSIX path literals / os.chown —
    same cause as the rows already registered for those files.
  * test_skin_cmd  Path.read_text() with no encoding; cp1252 cannot decode the
    UTF-8 skin YAML.
  * test_tui_resume_flow  asserts b"ok\n"; Windows newline translation gives
    b"ok\r\n".
  * test_update_stale_dashboard  /proc/<pid>/cmdline, the `ps` fallback and
    systemd-cgroup restart; on Windows the kill path shells out to taskkill and
    _dashboard_cmdline_for_pid returns None by design.
  * test_web_ui_build  fcntl does not exist on Windows.

  host_dependency_gap
  * test_install_cua_driver, test_update_interrupted_recovery  psutil==7.2.2 is
    a declared dependency and is not installed on this box.
  * test_web_ui_build  pathspec==1.1.1 likewise; _compute_web_ui_content_hash()
    raises, _write_web_ui_build_stamp() swallows it, and _web_ui_build_needed()
    then reports stale unconditionally.
  * test_update_eol_churn  git toolchain floor. This host runs git
    2.31.1.windows.1, where `git diff --name-only --ignore-cr-at-eol` still
    lists a file whose full --ignore-cr-at-eol diff is empty, so
    _normalize_managed_eol()'s `dirty - dirty(--ignore-cr-at-eol)` set is always
    empty and it pins autocrlf=false without restoring anything. The 1200-file
    case additionally straddles git's 1-second racy-index window, so its own
    `len(_dirty(repo)) == 1200` precondition cannot hold.
  * test_early_recovery  the test's builtins.__import__ guard keys on
    name.split('.')[0] and so rejects every RELATIVE import under it (`from .
    import _compiler` arrives as name ''). That is invisible only where
    startup/site already imported re, locale, subprocess and importlib; this
    interpreter has none of them in sys.modules at startup.

Each addition was verified to actually deselect under
-m "not windows_env_gap and not host_dependency_gap".

tests/hermes_cli/test_config_read_guard.py — allowlist
agent_runtime/persona_config_sync.py. The guard is a filename-proximity
heuristic; that call reads a PULLED REALM SUBTREE's profiles/<name>/config.yaml,
a foreign published document, not this machine's user config. Routing it
through load_config() would be a bug rather than a fix — it would apply the
local managed-scope overlay and ${ENV} expansion to somebody else's realm
document, which is exactly what read_remote_persona_defs() exists to prevent.
Same class as the managed_scope.py entry already on the list.

Canonical gate green:
  python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py tests/hermes_cli -q     -m "not windows_env_gap and not host_dependency_gap"
  -> exit 0; 545 files, 3660 tests passed, 0 failed.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): route the fork's queue-status handler through the awaited session store

The merge brought in upstream's AST guard
(tests/gateway/test_async_session_store.py), which forbids calling the raw
sync SessionStore from loop-side async code. It found exactly one violation:
the fork-owned `_handle_queue_status_command`, which predates the guard and

handler in the file already uses. This is a real defect the merge surfaced,
so it is fixed rather than fenced.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): retarget upstream's completion-redaction test onto the fork's delivery lane

Upstream delivers a background process completion by synthesizing an internal
user message and running a full agent turn, so its notification arrives via
`adapter.handle_message`. The fork gates that behind
`_background_agent_turns_enabled()` and defaults to a compact direct
`adapter.send` — a full turn per background completion is expensive and lets
monitor traffic starve a real human message.

Upstream's new test asserted the handle_message lane and so never reached its
own assertions here. The regression intent is REDACTION of the delivered
notification, and that is preserved exactly: the test now reads the delivered
text from whichever lane fired, proving the secret is stripped (and that
`HOME=/home/user` is not) on the path that actually ships, and continuing to
prove it if the gate is ever flipped back to upstream's default. The
handle_message lane stays covered by the other tests in the file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): make the device-path guard match POSIX spellings on Windows

`_is_blocked_device_path()` compared `os.path.normpath(path)` against POSIX
literals like "/dev/zero" and the "/proc/" prefix. On Windows normpath rewrites
"/" to "\", so "/dev/zero" arrived as "\dev\zero" and matched nothing — the
guard silently stopped guarding there.

It still must guard on Windows: reads execute through Git Bash / WSL, where
/dev/zero and /proc/<pid>/* are real. `wc -c < /dev/zero` never terminates, so
tests/tools/test_file_read_guards.py did not fail on this host, it HUNG
unbounded and took the whole pytest process (and every other result in the
file) with it. A pytest marker cannot fence a hang, and the guard's entire
purpose is preventing exactly this — so the guard is fixed instead.

The added comparison is strictly widening and can only ever match a path
root-anchored at "/dev" or "/proc"; a native Windows path is always drive- or
UNC-anchored and cannot be caught by it. Pre-existing on the pre-merge fork tip
1adf0404f (not merge-caused); fixed here because the hang blocks the
tests/tools sweep entirely. tests/tools/test_file_read_guards.py now runs 34
passed / 1 skipped in 4.4s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): retire two Windows fence rows at the source, not with a mark

Both rows in the gateway env-gap registry were self-describing test defects
with the fix named in the reason. Fixed both and deleted the rows.

test_config_env_bridge_authority.py — _run_gateway_import scrubs the child
environment to assert HERMES_* precedence, but its keep-list was POSIX-shaped
(PATH/PYTHONPATH/VIRTUAL_ENV/HOME). On Windows that starves the interpreter
rather than the bridge: without APPDATA/USERPROFILE (HOMEDRIVE+HOMEPATH) there
is no user-site or home resolution — Windows has no pwd.getpwuid fallback, so
the import dies with "Could not determine home directory." — and without
SystemRoot/SystemDrive Winsock cannot initialize, so gateway.run's networking
imports die with WinError 10106 before the bridge under test ever runs.
Forward the Windows equivalents alongside the POSIX ones.

test_session_state_cleanup.py — the "no bare del of _running_agents" guard read
gateway/run.py with no encoding=, so the cp1252 locale default killed it on the
UTF-8 bytes in run.py. That did not merely fail the test, it disabled a real
architectural guard on this platform. Read encoding="utf-8".

All 8 nodes across both files now pass on this Windows host; the registry rows
are removed so the stale-entry detector stays quiet and a future regression is
not hidden behind them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): reconcile the MSYS path rewrite with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV

search_files content search was BROKEN on Windows — a live, user-facing
regression the merge imported from upstream, not a test artifact.

Two Windows mechanisms in tools/environments/local.py contradicted each other.
`_bash_safe_path()` (upstream f2fcf89c1, extending #63113) rewrites every
`ShellFileOperations._escape_shell_arg` argument from `C:\Users\x` to the MSYS
`/c/Users/x` form. `_apply_windows_msys_bash_env_defaults()` sets
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 / MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=* on every bash spawn (#56700), so
MSYS never converts that argument back — and a NATIVE, non-MSYS ripgrep cannot
resolve `/c/...` at all:

  rg: /c/Users/.../tmpdir: IO error ... The system cannot find the path
  specified. (os error 3)

The rewrite had no counterpart. Upstream's motivation is sound, but it targets
the wrong consumer class: `_bash_safe_path` also feeds bash's OWN script
constructs (init_session / _wrap_command snapshot source+redirect+mv, and the
builtin cd), where `/c/...` is exactly right and where the "Directory
\drivers\etc does not exist" class actually bit. Program ARGUMENTS are a
different class — they land in native Windows binaries.

So split the two rather than weaken either. New `_shell_arg_safe_path()` emits
the drive-qualified forward-slash form `C:/Users/x` for arguments:

  * the MSYS runtime resolves it (verified live: Git Bash cat/find/grep and
    bash redirections all accept it),
  * native Windows binaries resolve it (verified live: rg 15.1.0),
  * with argument conversion disabled MSYS cannot re-mangle it into the
    \drivers\etc failure class — which is where that class came from.

`_bash_safe_path` and `_quote_shell_path` are untouched, so upstream's fix for
the snapshot bootstrap stands exactly as written.

Injection safety is unchanged: `_escape_shell_arg` still single-quotes and
still escapes embedded single quotes. Only the path mangling moved. It also got
strictly narrower — the old helper rewrote backslashes in ANY argument
containing one, silently corrupting every search pattern and `python -c`
snippet with a backslash in it (`func_\w+` went out as `func_/w+`).
`_shell_arg_safe_path` rewrites only drive-qualified paths and returns
everything else verbatim.

Proof — the 4 nodes triage refused to fence are green, and a live probe drives
the real search_files tool against a native C:\ temp dir:

  search_files(pattern="NEEDLE_LIVE_PROBE", target="content", path=r"C:\Users\
  beast\AppData\Local\Temp\hermes_live_probe_55_yhyly")
    -> {"total_count": 1, "matches": [{"line": 2, ...}]}
  search_files(pattern=r"func_\w+", target="content", path=<same>)
    -> {"total_count": 1, "matches": [{"line": 1, ...}]}     # backslash intact
  search_files(pattern="*.py", target="files", path=<same>)
    -> {"total_count": 1, ...}

Test changes: the two upstream tests that pinned the old `/c/...` argument form
are retargeted to `C:/...` (same intent — normalized, backslash-free, one
agreed form) and gained coverage for the non-path case that used to be
corrupted; `_shell_arg_safe_path` gets its own unit class next to its sibling.

Registry: the one row in test_search_error_guard.py was masked by this bug and
attributed to Git Bash spawn shape. With the path fixed the real cause is
visible and different — the installed rg 15.1.0 refuses the escaped literal
"\n" at regex-parse time — so the row is re-classed to host_dependency_gap
with the verified reason. No new rows.

message:
fix(relay): restore the sender-attribution marker the continuity refactor orphaned

b4be9ed90 (2026-07-18) made an agent_chat_send relay persist the target's
incoming row with the SENDING agent's identity in finish_reason, so the target's
chat attributes the message to the sender instead of the operator. c60413e17
(2026-07-20, native session continuity) deleted the lane's own
`_append_persona_operator_turn(relay_marker=)` call site — the runtime now
persists the user row as part of the turn — and the marker has been dropped ever
since. `_resolve_relay_sender_marker` and the `relay_marker` parameter survived
as caller-free code, and all seven resolver tests stayed green while every live
relay rendered as the OPERATOR.

Restored at the seam that exists today rather than by re-adding a second write:

- persona_commands `_cmd_mission_chat_message` resolves the sender ONCE (as
  before) and forwards it as `mission_chat_reply(relay_sender_marker=)`.
- persona_runtime threads it onto
  `AgentRunRequest.persona_chat_user_finish_reason`.
- profile_runner `stage_persona_chat_user_row_marker` stages the turn's user
  message dict on `agent._pending_cli_user_message` with the marker attached.
  `build_turn_context` adopts an already-staged dict whose clean text matches
  this turn and appends THAT dict, preserving extra keys; the session flush then
  writes `finish_reason=msg.get("finish_reason")` onto the persisted native row.
  So the row the RUNTIME writes gets typed — no duplicate row, no second write,
  and the model's prompt is byte-identical.

Operator/CLI sends resolve to None, which CLEARS the staging attribute (a stale
dict on a resident chat actor must never be adopted by a later turn) and leaves
those rows exactly as they are today. The retry lane
(`reuse_current_user_message`) stages nothing: its row is already durable and
already carries the marker from the attempt that wrote it.

Tests walk the WIRE, which is what was missing: CLI chokepoint -> run request ->
staged dict -> safe_native_message -> persisted row -> history parse ->
operator_channels attribution, plus a guard pinning the two upstream lines the
staging rides so a future merge that reshapes either one fails loudly instead of
silently un-attributing every relay again. Red before the fix: 5 of the 6 new
tests fail (the sixth pins upstream and is fix-independent).

continuity/profile-runner/turn-context suites 232 passed.

author: nekwo
message:
test(tools): pin the four Windows path-form translators as a next-sync tripwire

tools/environments/local.py is upstream-owned and carries four path
translators whose consumer classes deliberately disagree. The 2026-07-30
merge rehearsal (doc 18, defect #4, fixed at 93dc56bd9) showed how easily
that split is lost: upstream folded argv through the bash-script helper,
which contradicted the MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 this same module sets, broke
search_files content search on native Windows, and corrupted every search
pattern containing a backslash. The contradiction still exists upstream.

So characterize, do not change: pin input -> output for
_msys_to_windows_path, _windows_to_msys_path, _bash_safe_path and
_shell_arg_safe_path across the 4x4 form matrix (native, drive-forward,
MSYS, mixed), the backslash-regex passthrough, the non-drive-qualified
verbatim edge, the bare drive-root disagreements, the cygdrive/WSL
spellings, drive-letter case, idempotence and round-trip closure.

No production edits. A failure here is a question about upstream intent,
not a test to make green.

Honest about the platform: a premise test proves each translator reads
only _IS_WINDOWS, re and its sibling -- no filesystem, no environment, no
platform re-probe -- so the Windows-semantics matrix runs on any host with
that one flag monkeypatched, and needs no skipif. If a sync makes one of
them consult host state, that premise test fails first and says so.

Two findings worth naming. _bash_safe_path still rewrites every backslash
unconditionally, so it corrupts regex arguments exactly as before -- correct
for script text, fatal for argv, and pinned as such so a future "unify these
two helpers" fails loudly. And _bash_safe_path does not normalize
/cygdrive/c/... or /mnt/c/..., which its forward sibling understands, so
those spellings reach a Git Bash script in a form Git Bash cannot resolve.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(readiness): canonicalize the launcher_qa MCP block and report drift

Nine live profiles declare a launcher_qa MCP server and they had split into
two variants: four set STAGEC_LAUNCH_HELPER explicitly (alice, base, neko,
unbounded), five omit it (backend-dev, gpt-launcher, launcher-dev,
launcher-qa, qa). The omission is silently equivalent today because the
Launcher's launch_manager.dart falls back to the same helper path -- which is
exactly what makes it debt: the two blocks agree only by coincidence of a
fallback living in another repo, and nothing could say which was intended.

Operator ruling: the explicit variant is canonical. It now lives as
CANONICAL_LAUNCHER_QA_MCP_SERVER in machine_roots -- deep-frozen, so a
consumer that tries to tweak one field fails at the mutation instead of
quietly redefining canonical for the rest of the process.

Drift rides the existing mcp_server_issues() lane behind an opt-in flag and
carries a new typed code, mcp_server_template_drift, with a field-level diff
(key order irrelevant; a tail written with / is not drift, since _join_tail
splits on both separators). The flag is opt-in because that lane's contract
is "every issue means the capability is unavailable", and a drifted block
still binds and still spawns.

profile_readiness partitions the lane's rows on ADVISORY_ISSUE_CODES: drift
lands in a new mcp_template_drift payload field, never in machine_root_issues
and never in the readiness verdict. A working profile must not be reported
broken because it declares a capability differently.

Nothing here writes a config -- the single config writer stays upstream
save_config. Fixing the five is an operator action, so the data test emits the
exact yaml block to paste. That test is ratcheted: the five known-divergent
profiles are ledgered as expected drift, any new drift fails immediately, and
a ledgered profile that gets fixed also fails so the ledger can never outlive
the drift it describes. It resolves the live tree from conftest's pre-sandbox
HERMES_HOME snapshot -- reading the sandboxed env would skip and report a
clean tree that was never read.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(mission-chat): own the turn-outcome vocabulary instead of re-spelling it

``execution_state`` and ``error_kind`` are WIRE — 16 read-only Launcher
consumers match on the exact spellings — and both were bare string literals
inside ``hermes_cli/harness_parts/persona_commands.py``: 26 execution_state
sites over 7 values, 35 error_kind sites over 16 literal values (4 further
sites forward a sibling module's already-typed value). That file is EXEC'd into
harness.py's globals rather than imported, so nothing could import the
vocabulary to check it; a typo was a silent wire break that no test in either
repo would notice.

This is the finding ``mission_chat_turns`` already recorded for the turn STATES
— "a consumer was free to invent a spelling" — one field over, so it gets the
same remedy:

* New ``agent_runtime/mission_chat_outcome.py``: ``ExecutionState`` (7) and
  ``ChatErrorKind`` (19) StrEnums, verdict/family partition tables, and
  import-time guards that RAISE (never ``assert``, so ``python -O`` cannot strip
  the contract). Every member's value is byte-identical to the literal it
  replaces; ``StrEnum`` members ARE ``str``, so both encoders the lane uses
  (``emit_json`` and the raw ``json.dumps`` behind ``chat.final``) emit the same
  bytes and no ``.value`` was needed anywhere.
* ``classify_turn_failure(exc, *, provider_submitted) -> TurnOutcome`` replaces
  the triple-nested conditional that spelled the post-provider failure decision
  three times (state, kind, exit code) in one dict literal. The failure lane's
  ``return 2`` now reads ``turn_outcome.exit_code``, so one decision drives all
  three. ``RunBudgetExceeded`` is no longer imported by the CLI body — the
  classifier owns that isinstance.
* All 61 literal sites replaced across 11 functions, each with a function-local
  import (the established idiom in this exec'd part; a module-level one would
  be the namespace collision P0 guards against). ONE literal remains, for a
  structural reason stated in-code and pinned by test: a default argument is
  evaluated when the ``def`` executes, before any function-local import can run.

literals" only ONE is a turn state — the rest belong to three DIFFERENT

test_s29_context_request_bundle_removal: "Gates on the CODE forms (definition,

code calls the removed thing" from "this document says we removed it" makes the

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(mission-chat): plan the turn once, then commit it once under the lease

``_cmd_mission_chat_message`` re-entered ITSELF to take the chat-root lease:

    if not args._persona_chat_root_lease_acquired:
        with persona_chat_root_lease(session_id, ...):
            args._persona_chat_root_lease_acquired = True
            return _cmd_mission_chat_message(args)   # the whole 1,600-line body, again

Three defects fell out of that one line, and this commit retires all three.

1. THREE DURABLE WRITES RAN TWICE PER TURN — ``instance_store.open_chat``, the
   chat-session ensure, and the model-override persist — and the FIRST time with
   no lease held at all. The lease that exists to serialise a chat root did not
   cover the writes it was taken for.
2. THE TURN'S PHASE STATE HAD TO BE SMUGGLED across the re-entry on
   ``args._stated_session_id`` / ``args._clarify_binding`` /
   ``args._dispatch_session_established`` / ``args._persona_chat_root_lease_acquired``,
   because a second pass would otherwise rediscover "the caller named a session"
   — reporting every freshly minted dispatch thread as a plain continuation, and
   settling a clarify ticket twice. Five mutation sites, all of them writes to
   the caller's namespace that outlive the turn.
3. POST-REPLY BOOKKEEPING FAILED SILENTLY. The instance-state commit that
   returns the agent to ``idle`` and repoints its default chat thread sat inside
   a bare ``except Exception: pass`` (three copies of it), and EIGHT
   ``transition_mission_chat_turn`` calls discarded their
   ``MissionChatTurnPersistOutcome``. A cockpit rendering an agent ``busy``
   forever after a completed turn had no record anywhere of why, and a skipped
   journal write (lock timeout, stale transition) was indistinguishable from a
   clean one.

The shape now:

* ``_cmd_mission_chat_message`` (534 lines) PLANS: parse, admit, refuse, resolve
  the thread. It ends by building a frozen ``MissionChatTurnPlan`` (17 fields,
  in ``agent_runtime.mission_chat_outcome``) and taking the lease once.
* ``_mission_chat_commit_turn`` (1,241 lines) WRITES, entirely under that lease.
  It opens with an unpack that rebinds every planned value to the name the turn
  body has always used, so the body itself is byte-unchanged by the extraction —
  a renaming pass through the most-live code in the harness is a separate risk
  from moving the lease and does not have to be taken in the same commit.
* All eight discarded journal writes go through ``_route_turn_write(..., step=)``
  and all three swallowed instance commits raise a typed
  ``FinalizationWarning``. Both surface as an additive ``finalization_warnings``
  list, present ONLY when something went wrong — so a healthy turn's wire is
  unchanged and the key's presence is itself the signal.

HONEST SUBSET — what is NOT done, stated rather than implied. ``plan_turn`` is
not yet pure: two durable writes still precede the lease and cannot simply move
inside it. The instance derive-from-workers is read by target resolution, and on
an omitted-session send the MINT is what creates the ``session_id`` the lease is
keyed on — there is nothing to lock before a thread exists. Retiring those two
(and replacing the remaining ``getattr(args, ...)`` reads with a request object)
is the rest of the proposal. ``test_the_two_writes_that_cannot_be_leased_are_named_not_hidden``
asserts the current truth so nobody re-derives it and so a silent change fails.

Also deliberately left: the auto-title ``except Exception: pass`` at the very
end. The terminal frame is already on stdout by then, so no envelope can carry a
warning — the existing comment says exactly that, and swallowing is the correct
behaviour there.

Tests (NEW tests/hermes_cli/test_mission_chat_turn_envelope.py, 12 rows):
the handler no longer calls itself; exactly one committer; no ``args._*``
smuggling; ``open_chat`` / ensure / override each observed to run WITH the lease
held and EXACTLY ONCE; a clean turn carries no ``finalization_warnings``; a
failed instance commit surfaces a typed warning on an otherwise-``ok`` envelope;
a non-clean journal write names its step; no transition may drop its outcome
again; every warning kind has a producer.

Eight AST guards across six mission-chat/relay test files followed the code to
``_mission_chat_commit_turn`` (relay marker wiring, run-budget settle points, C8
ack wiring, record-at-injection, wall-budget window, capability visibility,
display-name binding, title off-path, S30 key survival). None was weakened:
each now searches both halves so it fails loudly rather than silently finding
nothing if the boundary moves again — and S30 reads the two halves concatenated
so a ``task_id`` cannot reappear in the one it stopped looking at.

Wire compatibility PROVEN: the same 10 captured envelopes from the P1 commit,
re-captured after the split — byte-identical to the pre-P1 baseline.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(read-model): name the frame's source, and stop storing it twice

B4 — the serve path could not say where its frame came from, so it lied
when it had nothing. `_cmd_snapshot` built a frame, then replaced it with
`ReadModel().render_snapshot()` whenever the read-model flags were on,
with no check that the read model held anything: a database never
populated (first run after enabling the flag, or one just cleared) made
`harness snapshot --json` print `{}` — an empty runtime, exit code 0, no
error. `resolve_snapshot_frame(prefer_cache=...)` now returns a
`(frame, FrameSource)` NamedTuple over a StrEnum of {built, cache,
cache_miss_rebuilt} and stamps the answer onto the frame's parity
envelope, so the degraded case serves the REAL frame and says so.

Watermark derivation had three sites and two different fallbacks:
write_snapshot fell back to `{}` (an offset-0 watermark that tells the
projector it is caught up at the head of the log) where the projector
fell back to a measured `events_watermark()`. One frame could therefore
be recorded correctly or as caught-up-at-zero depending on which writer
got it. `snapshot_watermark()` is now the only derivation; both writers
call `apply_full_rebuild(snapshot)` and pass nothing.

Storage: `apply_full_rebuild` wrote the whole frame as the `snapshot`
blob and then AGAIN as one `projections_misc` row per top-level section.
Measured on the live alice store: 28 rows, 1,628,708 payload bytes, of
which 543,247 (33%) were the 27 duplicate copies — bytes no reader
needed, free to drift because only the blob was ever re-read whole.
Sections are now sliced out of the one blob (which also stops
`persona_instances` / `operator_channels` answering `None` just because
the old writer skipped their rows). READ_MODEL_SCHEMA_VERSION 2 -> 3
clears and VACUUMs an old database so it rebuilds by the normal path
instead of serving rows no writer maintains. Live reclaim: 4,194,304 ->
1,773,568 bytes.

Two ProjectorResult fields reported constants as if they were findings:
`changed` was the literal {"sections": ["snapshot"]} on every applied
pass and `stale_sections` was [] on every path — leftovers of the
row-delta design that ended when the frame became the projection unit.
Both deleted; `applied_events` already carried the fact. `apply_pending`
also materialized the entire pending event tail into a list to call
`len()` on it — it counts now.

B5 — two parity warnings could never fire. `open_tasks_without_task_rows`
and `open_incident_budget_exceeded` read `summary.open_tasks` /
`summary.open_incidents`, fields the frame stopped emitting when contract
45 reduced the block to `persona_instances`. A dict answers `.get()` for
any key, so both branches read None, evaluated false, and silently
stopped existing — the `open_incident_warning_threshold` knob tuned
nothing while riding the runtime_config wire, and the Launcher ships an
"incident budget" alert for a warning with no producer. The only thing in
the repo that ever produced `open_incidents` was the test asserting the
warning fired: a closed loop, not coverage. Branches, knob and test all
go together.

`SnapshotSummary` now declares the summary's field set, so the next
warning cannot be written against a field the frame does not emit, and
tests/agent_runtime/test_parity_warning_catalog.py gates reachability
executably — for every code literal the module spells, a table row builds
the input that produces it, with an AST sweep failing on any code that
becomes unproducible.

Gates: tests/agent_runtime 3325 passed, 2 skipped (was 3302 + 2; +24 new,
-1 retired). Live on alice: snapshot --json schema 2 / contract 45 /
2 boards / frame_source=built; all three FrameSource values proven
against the live store; rebuild-read-model round-trips; harness read
serves both row tables and blob slices; integrity_check ok.

author: nekwo
message:
test(harness): guard the exec'd command parts' namespace before touching it

harness.py loads its command bodies by exec, not import. Two defects hide
in that seam and no gate we run can see either: a part silently rebinding
a name harness.py already owns, and a part reading a global nothing ever
binds — a NameError that only fires when an operator runs that one verb.

This rebuilds the real post-load namespace (harness.py's body with the
_load_command_parts() call stripped, then the six parts in load order,
compiled with the same inherited annotations future) and asserts both
properties statically. A self-check pins the probe against the real
imported module, so the guard cannot drift into probing a fiction.

It already found one: persona_commands reads Callable, which nothing
binds. It survives today only because the future import stops the two
annotations from evaluating. Ledgered with a reason rather than papered
over; the ledger is self-cleaning — an entry that starts resolving fails
the test as stale.

Red-proofed by injecting a free name and a shadowing rebind into
checkpoint_commands: both guards fired, then reverted.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(harness): give the parts' shared helpers a real module to import

The exec'd command parts reach for _print_stage42, _list_envelope,
_object_envelope, _sort_rows, _load_request_json, emit_harness_error and
PERSONA_CHAT_SESSION_SOURCE as free names, because harness.py's globals
are the only place they exist. That is what makes the parts unanalysable:
there is no import line to read, so nothing can tell a name that arrives
from harness.py apart from one nobody provides.

Move the closure into hermes_cli/harness_support.py — the Stage-42
envelope builders and printer, the row sorter, the request-JSON loader,
and the whole error taxonomy (ERROR_EXIT_CODES, _error_envelope,
_error_code_for_exception, _error_hint, the path redactor) that
emit_harness_error depends on. harness.py imports them straight back, so
hermes_cli.harness.emit_harness_error — which serve.py and main.py import
by that path — resolves to the same object as before, and the 50 command
bodies harness.py still owns are untouched.

Two details worth naming. PERSONA_CHAT_SESSION_SOURCE was a third copy of
a string agent_runtime already declares twice; harness_support binds the
one from persona_chat_continuity instead of minting a fourth spelling.
And harness_repo_root() lands here as the honest anchor for the __file__
trap: a part exec'd into harness.py's globals sees harness.py's __file__,
so its parents[1] means "repo root" only by coincidence of where
harness.py sits. This module's __file__ is stable either way.

(595 passed); `hermes harness status` verified through the live venv.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(harness): let each exec'd part declare the names it actually uses

Every command part read its dependencies out of harness.py's globals by
free name — 111 of them in persona_commands alone, 25 in
runtime_commands, 8/5/2/1 across board, office, flow and checkpoint.
Nothing recorded where any of those came from, so the files could not be
read on their own, ruff could not see a name that resolves nowhere, and
a wrong one only announced itself as a NameError under the single verb
that touched it.

Each part now opens with `from __future__ import annotations` (the same
future the compile already inherited, now stated) and an explicit import
header derived from its real free-name set. The exec loading mechanism is
untouched: parts are still compiled into harness.py's globals, and every
re-imported name binds the identical object, so the CLI shape and the
namespace both come out unchanged. The namespace guard checks exactly
that — no part rebinds another's name to a different object, and every
free name resolves.

Two specific defects go with it. persona_commands' Callable ghost is now
a real `from collections.abc import Callable`, so the ledger entry the
guard opened is closed and the file no longer depends on annotations
never evaluating. And _cmd_verify's `Path(__file__).parents[1]` — which
read harness.py's path, not its own, and meant "repo root" only by
accident of where harness.py sits — now calls harness_repo_root().

ruff F821 over hermes_cli/harness_parts/ drops from 782 to 0. harness.py
keeps 62: those are the _cmd_* names the parts define, the reverse
direction, which only full module conversion can retire.

Namespace guard green; 595 tests across the 36 harness-source-reading
files green; `harness status`, `workspace show <id>` and
`mission-chat --help` verified through the live venv.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
build(lint): turn on F821, and fix the NameError it found

Two structural reasons this codebase grows names that resolve nowhere:
the harness command parts are exec'd into harness.py's globals rather
than imported, so nothing else can tell an inherited name from a missing
one; and `from __future__ import annotations` means an annotation naming
a type nobody imported never evaluates and never complains. Both are
invisible to every gate we run.

Enabling F821 found a live one outside the harness entirely.
persona_chat_trace_summary opened with `event_log or _default_event_log()`
— a helper that has never existed in that module. Any caller omitting
event_log got a NameError instead of the empty list two lines below. It
never fired because both production callers (build_snapshot,
build_status) resolve their own CachedEventLog first, which is exactly
how a defect like this survives: reachable only from the path nobody has
taken yet. The fallback is gone; the documented empty return stands.

Ignores are scoped to upstream-owned trees (agent, gateway, tools,
tui_gateway, plugins, optional-skills, upstream test modules,
web_server.py), whose hits are upstream-PR candidates rather than fork
changes. harness.py gets its own documented entry: it calls the ~62
_cmd_* handlers the parts define, so those names really are undefined
until _load_command_parts() runs. The reverse direction is clean and
stays that way. `ruff check .` passes.

author: nekwo
message:
test(hermes-home): measure the frozen homes instead of grepping for them

The ratchet guarding module-level HERMES_HOME snapshots read the source
with a column-0 regex, so it could only ever see the first hop. It caught
`CRON_DIR = get_hermes_home() / "cron"` and missed `JOBS_FILE = CRON_DIR /
"jobs.json"` on the very next line — equally frozen, equally capable of
depositing fixture writes into the live home, and invisible to a pattern
that looks for the call.

The guard now runs the hazard. A subprocess points HERMES_HOME at a
nonce-named tmpdir, imports every module that mentions get_hermes_home(),
and reports each module-level attribute whose value still contains that
nonce. A plain module attribute cannot re-resolve, so "resolved from the
home at import" and "frozen" are one statement, and derived constants are
caught by construction.

The ledger does not shrink — it grows, from 29 names to 51. cron/jobs.py
freezes six where the regex saw one; gateway/platforms/base.py seven where
it saw one; skills' dashed-directory scripts freeze seven that no dotted
import would have reached. That is not new debt, it is debt that was
always there and unmeasured. Every entry carries a reason, and a stale
entry now fails, so the ledger can only shrink from here.

Two details the design has to be honest about. The nonce lives in the
directory *name* rather than the full path because display_hermes_home()
rewrites the prefix to "~/" — matching the path missed hermes_cli/doctor's
_DHH depending on where the tmpdir happened to sit. And the probe writes
its result to a file, not stdout, because importing the gateway and TUI
modules swaps sys.stdout out from under it. Modules that cannot import
(trajectory_compressor needs fire; scripts/profile-tui.py needs termios)
are declared UNPROBED with reasons rather than counted as clean, and a
non-import error there fails the suite.

Red-proofed against agent_runtime/profile_context.py with a direct freeze
and a derived one: both caught, the derived one being exactly what the
regex could not do.

Also renames ReadModel._default_db_path to _read_model_db_path — the old
name collided with hermes_state's unrelated _default_db_path /
_resolve_default_db_path pair, so grepping either landed on both.

recorded only as UNPROBED. On a host where they DO import, the guard

`profile_readiness_for_persona` called

every snapshot agent's required list is EMPTY -- so the subset handed to the
checker was `{}`, and the blocking `mcp_server_template_drift` check evaluated

(`test_every_live_launcher_qa_block_matches_the_canonical_template`), a
tripwire in CI rather than a check on the live lane.

Operator ruling (ledger item 10): EXECUTE the widening.

ONE lane, TWO explicit scopes, resolved in one place -- the new
`machine_roots.mcp_servers_in_issue_scope`:

* CONFIGURED scope -- every configured block that has a canonical template is
  validated wherever it is declared, whoever requires it. That covers both
  issue classes that are about a DECLARATION being wrong: template drift
  (`mcp_server_template_drift`) and the binding failures on the same block
  (`unbound_root`, `root_target_missing`, `invalid_root_token`,
  `platform_unsupported`).
* REQUIRED scope -- the required names are validated exactly as before, and
  the missing-server class stays required-scoped. It is computed by
  `profile_readiness` from the required list, never here: a profile that does
  not declare an un-required server is not a defect.

The widening is deliberately gated on "has a canonical template" -- those are
the only names this module can state a correct shape for. Validating EVERY
configured block of every profile would fail a persona over an operator's
unrelated experimental server; that is a different ruling and is not taken
here.

`only=` is deleted rather than kept as an alias: it was an honest filter name

config: readiness REPORTING only, fix hints still carry the pasteable block.

author: nekwo
message:
test(agent-runtime): gate every registered event type on having an emitter (S55)

The wave's "stop it regrowing" half. S49/S52/S53 de-registered fourteen contracts
whose emitters had gone, and they were not the first: S25 retired
repo_bundle.delivered one commit BEHIND the S24 cut that deleted its writer, and
S44 retired six role_envelope.*/role_checklist.* types with the store family.
Each time the registration outlived the emitter and was found by hand, one wave
late. This makes that a test failure instead.

Not folded into the S15 family, deliberately: S15 and its descendants are
RECORDS (a frozen list of what one stage pruned, plus the absolute count). This
is a RULE -- it takes no list of names and stays true as the registry changes.
Folding it in would put a growing hand-maintained list back into the one file
the wave was trying to remove one from.

The resolver is AST-based and string-form aware, following the four idioms this
tree actually uses -- a naive `Event(type="x")` scan resolves 46 of 68 types and
would report 22 false positives:

  1. keyword      Event(type="run.closed", ...)
  2. POSITIONAL   Event(now(), "self_test.recorded", ...) -- type is field 1;
                  roughly half the emitters use this form
  3. wrapper      self._event("board.card.created", ...) forwarding a parameter
                  into an Event(...), resolved to a FIXED POINT
  4. module const Event(type=STATE_PATCHED_EVENT_TYPE)

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated in the file rather than implied: reachability. An
emitter that is present but sits in a lane nothing can reach still counts. Sound
"has no production caller" needs receiver-typed call-graph analysis; name-based
reachability is worse than nothing here (`update`, `save`, `get`, `transition`
all collide -- a bare `transition` grep returns 268 hits), so it would mark dead
lanes reachable and pass quietly. The unreachable-but-present class is owned by
the per-cut removal-contract tests, each of which records its receiver-aware
verification. The class this gate catches is the one that actually RECURRED.

RED-PROOF on the pre-wave tree (3f9948eed): deleting the single
self._event("repo_bundle.created", ...) call while leaving its registration in
place moved the resolver from 3 emitter-less types to 4, naming
repo_bundle.created -- the S24 regression reproduced, and this gate fails on it.
Sabotage reverted.

ALLOWLIST: three types, one real reason -- progress.py dispatches by DATA
(self.emit(str(payload.get("type", "run.progress")), payload)), so the type is a
runtime value with no literal in scope at the sink. Each entry carries a WITNESS
assertion proving the literal is on that dispatch path, so a stale entry fails
like a missing emitter.

state.patched and child.returned are NOT allowlisted despite being config-gated:
gating is a runtime condition, the emitters are static literals, and idiom 4
resolves them.

The ten worker_session.* types are NOT allowlisted either. The plan reserved a
temporary "S51 pending" entry for them; it is not needed -- they still have live
emitters, so the gate passes without it. Adding it would have been a HOLE: when
S51 cuts that write lane, this gate goes red unless the same commit
de-registers the ten, which is exactly the outcome a temporary exemption would
have suppressed. There is nothing here for the follow-up wave to remove.

message:
refactor(agent-runtime): S57 — 29 unread config scalars and the repo-bundle store go (contract 48)

Operator-ruled CUT, one coherent contract move, bumped once: 47 -> 48. Both
halves edit the emitted frame, so they land together with one Launcher lockstep.

1) THE 29-FIELD UNRULED_DEBT LEDGER — REMOVED.

S56's reader gate measured 29 `RuntimeConfig` scalars with no production reader
and carried them, frozen, in `UNRULED_DEBT` because it was not ruled to delete
them. S57 re-verified every one by hand (AST attribute form + `getattr` string
form + a plain repo-wide text scan, the third because the gate's own resolver
has the documented blind spot the `persona_commands.py:1293` trap exposed) and
cut all 29: dataclass row, `config.py` load line, `migrations` range validator.
Not one survived re-verification with a reader the gate had missed.

FOUR cross-field validators went with them and are the sharper finding — the
`live_run_max_total_tokens <= mission_max_total_tokens` ceiling pair, the
`liveness_poll_seconds` 30..120 range, the `liveness_hung_seconds <
heartbeat_ttl_seconds` ordering, and the `artifact_storage_*`
low<=high<=critical ordering. Each related two or three DEAD knobs to each
other, which is how they read as governed through four previous audits.

`lock_acquire_timeout_seconds` SURVIVES and is the load-bearing half of the cut:
it sits in the same neighbourhood, looks identical, and `locks.py:133` reads it
through the `getattr` STRING form. A prefix-shaped or eyeball cut takes it. That
is the argument for the gate's shape, pinned in the new removal contract.

`UNRULED_DEBT` is now EMPTY and stays frozen at zero, so S56's gate becomes a
pure tripwire: a new field with no reader fails outright, with no bucket left to
park it in.

2) `RepoBundleStore` — DELETED WHOLE.

Third and final pass over one lane. S52 cut the write side and explicitly said
"NOT a store removal" because `status.py` still projected off `list_all`; S56
deleted those projections, which left the store with zero production importers
(doc 19 filed it as newly-opened debt). Re-verified: `RepoBundleStore` appears in
`agent_runtime`/`hermes_cli`/`tools` only inside comments recording its own
retirement. A store nobody imports is the same defect S52 named on the write
side with the verbs reversed.

`paths.repo_bundle_path` (only caller was `RepoBundleStore.get`), the `serve`
`_FINGERPRINT_STORE_DIRS` entry (a per-poll stat of a tree nothing can write —
same rule S56 applied to `worker_sessions`), and `migration.counts.repo_bundles`.

That count is handled honestly rather than quietly: it did NOT read through the
store — it was a direct `_count_nested_json(root / "repo_bundles")` — so a
shallow "does it call the store?" check would have left it standing. But the
live root has no `repo_bundles/` directory at all and no writer has existed
since S52, so the row reported 0 by construction on a wire operators read. It is
RETIRED, not re-homed: there is nothing left to re-home it onto.

`paths.repo_bundles_dir` / `repo_bundles_task_dir` (still reached by

message:
test(agent-runtime): THE tombstone registry — one table, one AST scanner

Twenty test_sNN_* removal-contract files each re-implemented the same
question — "is this removed symbol still absent from production source?" —
with its own scanner, its own package tuple and its own exclusions. Two
defects rode along with the duplication.

The vacuous-gate class, three times in one week: a removal test that greps
raw source cannot tell a re-grown reference from the retirement COMMENT the
cut just wrote. S48 found it first (S46's token-join helper renders
card.title as three newline-separated tokens, so every dotted assertion
through it passed vacuously). S57 found three assertions going RED against a
correct tree because they matched their own prose. Each time the fix was the
same: parse to an AST and re-render. This writes that fix once.

Six different answers to "what counts as production source" were in use.
The registry has one: PRODUCTION_PACKAGES, the widest tuple any migrated
row used, so consolidation could only WIDEN protection.

317 rows across six forms — MODULE / ATTR / CLASS_ATTR / EVENT / CODE /
PATH — each carrying its wave, its cut commit and a one-line reason.
String literals deliberately survive the AST round trip: event kinds and
capability ids are invoked BY NAME, which is the S44/S55 lesson.

Retirement rule, in the header: a hermes row may be dropped only after one
upstream sync has merged cleanly over that symbol's region, recording the
sync commit. This is a FORK — a tombstone is not only "we deleted it", it
is "upstream may hand it back". Dropping a row edits the visible table.

Red-proofed twice before anything else moves, on a scratch production file:
a re-introduced NAME (wake_ready_dependencies) and a re-introduced STRING
LITERAL (render_objective) each fail the gate naming their row, while eight
tombstoned names sitting in that same file's docstring and comments fire
nothing. Sabotage reverted.

Deliberately NOT absorbed, because they are rules or authorities rather
than lists: S15 (SURVIVING_EVENT_COUNT / contract_hash, imported by six
files), S55 (registered-event -> emitter gate), S56's RuntimeConfig reader
gate, S47 (CURRENT_CONTRACT_VERSION), S53 (exports seed_lane_row to S21),
and the characterization suites. Parameter-absence, wire-key-absence and

author: nekwo
message:
Stop persona chat asking permission for clear orders

Told to message the agents it steers, Neko ended its turn on a bare
"Waiting for your go-ahead before I send the messages." — no tool calls,
no plan restated. No harness approval gate fired; the pause was entirely
model-side, taught by two prompt inputs.

OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE's verification block asked the model to
"confirm scope before executing" whenever the next step had "side effects
(file writes, commands, API calls)" — which is nearly every useful turn.
Gate that confirmation on destructiveness instead, and say plainly that
routine tool use in service of a clear instruction proceeds without
asking. The correctness/grounding/formatting bullets are untouched. This
constant rides every gpt/codex/grok session, so the edit stays narrow.

The operator-chat rules then only bound turns that USE tools: the ack
HARD RULE fires before a first tool call, so a no-tool "waiting for your
go-ahead" turn escaped every rule. Two bullets close that — a clear,
non-destructive order IS the go-ahead and gets acted on in the same turn,
and any pause that is earned must restate a concrete plan (targets,
content, tools) so the operator approves something specific. Narrow the
clarify bullet's "here, ask" to ambiguity so it stops reading as license
to ask for permission on a clear order.

Tests pin both policies so a future deletion fails rather than silently
restoring the pause.

author: nekwo
message:
Give head agents a live, greppable teammate transcript

A head agent could not see a teammate thread's full history. agent_chat_open
caps at a 40-message tail and the transcript lives in SessionDB, which no
agent tool can grep or glob. The ask (operator, 2026-08-03) was explicitly
for something LIVE, not an export: a path the head can grep/tail WHILE the
teammate is mid-task and watch grow.

agent_runtime/chat_live_log.py keeps one append-only JSONL file per chat
session at <head-home>/chat_live_logs/<session_id>.jsonl -- one line per
persisted message plus compact {kind:"tool", tool, status} lines, so "what
is it doing right now" is greppable in the same stream as "what did it say".
A regenerable artifact, never authority: every line is rebuildable from
SessionDB, and the one-shot backfill materializes pre-feature history from
the SAME projection agent_chat_open reads before live appends continue it.

The mirror rides the write. _persist_persona_chat_row is now the one
explicit-append seam _append_persona_operator_turn and
_append_persona_assistant_text both funnel through, so the SessionDB write
and its mirror cannot drift apart. The mission-chat lane has a second,
genuinely different persistence mechanism -- since native session continuity
landed it does not append the operator/assistant rows itself, the runtime
persists them with the turn -- so it mirrors from its own two known points
(write-ahead for the incoming order, native commit for the recorded reply)
through the SAME _mirror_persona_chat_message helper. Three moments, one
hook; nothing is pasted per call site.

HERMES_HOME trap: persona_profile_context flips HERMES_HOME process-globally
to profiles/<persona> for the whole turn, which is exactly when these writes
happen. The mirror root is CAPTURED once (the chat SessionDB's own directory,
else the chat_session_scope head-home ladder) and never re-resolved from the
ambient home at write time -- otherwise one conversation's mirror would
scatter across per-persona profile directories.

Redaction-safe by construction: the callers hand over text that already
crossed the _redact_persona_chat_text write boundary (or the read
projection's), and the mirror re-applies the shared TEXT_SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_RE
rule per line anyway, because "the caller already did it" is how a redaction
boundary rots. Bounded: 8000-char lines with a visible truncation marker,
~10MB rotation keeping one .1 generation. Best effort, and COUNTED -- a
mirror failure can never fail a chat turn, but it logs once and tallies
rather than vanishing.

New read-only tool agent_chat_log_path (toolset agent_chat) hands the path
over. Its scope guard is not a copy of agent_chat_open's -- both now resolve
through one _resolve_chat_lane_target authority plus the existing
_session_belongs_to_chat_lane, so a widening in one cannot be invisible in
the other. Handing over a filesystem path is at least as strong as reading a
tail, so it earns the identical typed foreign_session refusal. all_threads
enumerates only sessions that already pass that same guard.

Known gap, stated not hidden: the backfill runs once at file creation, so a
message whose append was lost (process killed between the durable write and
the mirror) stays missing from that file until it is deleted and rebuilt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
Surface the background work that ran invisibly

Six subsystems could each have work in flight -- terminal background
processes, subagent delegations, in-flight mission-chat turns, MCP
servers, cron jobs -- and none of them appeared anywhere an operator
could see. The only way to learn a build was still running was to notice
it had not finished.

`agent_runtime/running_work.py` gives all six one row vocabulary, and is
durable-first because it has to be: the CLI snapshot lane, serve, and the
stream are separate processes, and every one of those registries lives
only in the process that spawned the work. A registry-only projection
would report an empty HUD from every other lane and call it "nothing
running".

Residency is not ownership, which cost a design iteration worth
recording: `mission_chat_turns` already imports `process_registry`,
`async_delegation` and `cron.scheduler` transitively, so "is it in
sys.modules?" is true almost everywhere and proves nothing. Durable-backed
lanes therefore merge live rows only when the registry HAS any, and the
live-only lanes (MCP, cron) demand positive proof -- held connections,
scheduler pools -- before answering at all. Absence proves nothing, so
without that proof they report unavailable rather than "no work".

Four honesty rules the rows keep:

- Each lane reports its own ok/unavailable health. An unreadable source is
  REPORTED; "nothing is running" and "I could not look" are different
  facts and the HUD must be able to say which one it means.
- No row claims `running` from a bare PID. Identity is verified against
  the `host_start_time` baseline; unprovable identity is `unknown`, and a
  dead or recycled PID is dropped through the accountant.
- A delegation frozen past the stale thresholds reads `stalled` even
  before the 30s monitor sweep notices. Where no progress token survives
  the process boundary, `progress` says `unavailable` instead of emitting
  zeros that would read as "idle".
- Previews are capped at 200 chars and the cap is declared `by_design`, so
  a deliberate bound never trips the amber lost-data pill.

The section joins the snapshot at contract 52 -- additive, but the pin
still travels because the Launcher requires exact equality, so a new
section under an unbumped version is invisible rather than merely unread.
Both durable stores mutate with no EventLog event, so the serve read-model
cache now fingerprints them through one exported path authority; otherwise
it would replay "3 running" for twenty seconds after they all exited.

`harness work list|peek|cancel` puts it on the CLI. `peek` mirrors
`poll()`'s read side and nothing else -- not even poll's own observation
bookkeeping -- because `read_log` semantics here would suppress the
notify_on_complete turn an agent is waiting on. `cancel` routes through
the owning subsystem's interrupt seam, never a bare PID, and refuses
without `--yes` by naming the label, pid and owner: confirming a sentence
is how the wrong thing gets killed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
Close the review findings on the chat live-log mirror

Four gating findings from the review of 1f725fd57. Each of the three MAJORs
was a real defect, not a style note.

1. A FOURTH explicit-append site was missed. continuity.
   return_summary_to_parent_session appends a role="assistant" persona-chat row
   straight to SessionDB (live via `harness persona-instance return-summary`),
   so the one row a head agent most wants to grep for -- "the child finished,
   here is the result" -- never reached the log. The root cause is that the
   mirror was bound by CONVENTION: a trailing call each append site had to
   remember. It is now bound by a SEAM: `mirrored_persona_chat_append`, a
   context manager the write goes inside, records only on a clean exit, and is
   used by both the harness persist helper and the continuity lane. A future
   append site has to wrap it, which is a rule a reviewer can check.

2. Create-vs-append could silently destroy lines. The backfill was written
   positionally into the live file via open(path, "x"), multi-MB with several
   buffered flushes, while another process treated bare path.exists() as ready
   and appended -- the creator's next chunk overwrote the appended line at its
   own offset, and the appender's dedupe mark then suppressed it permanently
   (Windows O_APPEND is seek-then-write across handles, so this is not
   theoretical). Materialization now runs under a cross-process O_EXCL claim,
   writes into the claim file, and os.replace()s it into position: a reader or
   appender sees either no file or a complete one. An appender that finds a
   claim in flight waits briefly and then SKIPS -- crucially without marking
   the line recorded, so the retry still writes it. A claim orphaned by a
   killed process goes stale and is taken over rather than stranding the
   session's mirror forever.

3. First-touch backfill was unbounded on the chat hot path. Each page re-ran
   the full curated projection, turn journal re-parsed per row, synchronously
   inside the persist seam and the write-ahead mirror -- so the first message
   after a deploy could stall a live turn for seconds on a long thread.
   Materialization moves entirely to the TOOL lane, where a deliberate agent
   request can afford it. The chat lanes create a header-only file marked
   backfill_pending and append; agent_chat_log_path fills the history in ahead
   of the live lines already there, deduped, once. Bounded there too (row cap
   plus a 15s wall budget, declared as backfill_truncated), and the tool
   reports history_complete so a short file is never passed off as whole.

4. The tool overstated its coverage. Two fixes, one real and one honest. Real:
   mid-turn steers are now mirrored at mission_chat_steer, stamped
   steered: true -- handle.session_id is the root chat session, so they land in
   the same file as the turn's order and reply, and a head agent tailing it can
   see WHY an agent changed course instead of watching it happen unexplained.
   Honest: the runtime's non-final rows (intermediate assistant messages
   between tool calls) are still persisted by the native flush outside every
   seam this hooks, so the schema description, the module docs, and a
   live_coverage field on the response now say exactly that -- an agent must
   not read an absence in the live tail as proof something never happened.

Quality follow-ups, all taken. Relay attribution rides the mirror line
(relay_sender_persona_id/instance_id) so a teammate's relayed message no longer
reads as the operator in the grep file. The dedupe key is normalized to the
LOGICAL turn id: the native flush stamps assistant rows
<client_message_id>:assistant:<n> while the live hooks carry the bare id, so
the raw key would have let a materialized file and a live append both claim the
same reply. Rotation seeds its dedupe index across the .1 generation boundary,
so a resend arriving in a fresh process after a rotation is not re-appended.

Tests, including the ones the review named as missing: the continuity lane
(mirrored, and silent when the durable append fails); create-during-append
concurrency both ways; a stale claim; the persist lane never touching the
projection; completion ordering and its carry-over of lines appended mid-read;
the logical dedupe key; relay attribution; cross-generation dedupe; the steer
mirror; and behavioral coverage of both mission-chat lane hooks driving the
real handler with a stubbed provider -- order and reply mirrored, resend not
doubled, and a broken mirror never failing the turn.

author: nekwo
message:
Make the writers and the reader agree on where work is recorded

The Activity projection read two stores that other processes write, and
the two sides resolved different directories. The reader went through the
chat head-home scope; the writers went through ambient `get_hermes_home()`
— `process_registry` froze it at MODULE IMPORT, `async_delegation`
re-read it at write time. On the launcher's own layout
(`HERMES_HOME=profiles/<profile>` beside `HERMES_HEAD_HOME=profiles/base`)
those are different directories.

The failure mode was the worst one this projection can produce: not an
error, not a gap, but a confident empty answer. Every source reported
`ok`, the row list came back empty, and an operator watching a
twenty-minute build was told nothing was running. The serve read-model
cache had the same split — it fingerprinted files nothing wrote, so even
a correct reader would have been served a stale frame. Reproduced
end-to-end before fixing: writer to `profiles/neko`, reader watching
`profiles/base`, zero rows, all sources green.

`get_hermes_background_work_home()` is now the one authority all four
sites resolve through — both writers, the projection, and the
fingerprint. Its precedence is the one `get_hermes_head_home` already
implemented, so this names a decision rather than adding a resolver: an
explicit head wins (which is what carries work out of a persona turn,
since `persona_profile_context` records the operator home BEFORE
diverting the ambient one), and with no head declared the answer is the
ambient home exactly as before. Gateway, TUI and plain CLI set neither,
so nothing on those lanes moves. `CHECKPOINT_PATH` becoming the lazy
`checkpoint_path()` also retires its row from the frozen-HERMES_HOME
ledger, which that gate had been carrying as untidy-but-harmless right
up until a second process needed to find the file.

Also, from the same review:

- A start-time probe that returns None or raises (access denied, psutil
  hiccup) is no longer indistinguishable from a recycled PID. Comparing
  `None` against a real baseline yields False, so an unreadable probe was
  silently DELETING a running build from the HUD and filing it under
  "recycled". Absence of proof now surfaces as an `unknown` row; only a
  real mismatch or a dead PID still drops.
- `started_at` is anchored to UTC at the projection boundary. The live
  registry formats it with `time.localtime` and no offset, so rows from
  different lanes carried stamps in different frames of reference with
  nothing marking which was which — and the `--issued-at` replay guard,
  reading naive as UTC, could refuse a legitimate cancel by hours.
  Normalized here rather than in `process_registry`, which has other
  consumers.
- Cancel applies the projection's own positive-ownership rule. A
  cold-CLI cancel of a durable-visible row used to fall through to
  `kill_process` on an empty registry and report `not_found` — "no such
  work" about work the operator's HUD was listing.
- `work list` accounts its drops on the CLI lane too, `--cursor`/`--since`
  (and peek/cancel's `--sort`/`--limit`/`--idempotency-key`) are no longer
  advertised by verbs that cannot honor them, an unresolvable home now
  trips the fingerprint sentinel instead of reading as nothing-to-watch,
  a broken cron scheduler reports `scheduler_unreadable` rather than
  `not_in_process`, and `included` counts what actually ships instead of
  the pre-cap list.

No wire shape changed; `started_at` values are now uniformly UTC. Stream
goldens regenerate byte-identical.
