author: nekwo
message:
fix(runtime): take ambient filesystem state off the running_work contract

`running_work` folded machine-local state into the same per-source `detail`
prose that carried its contract, and one half of that state was perturbed by
the projection's OWN lazy import: `_collect_chat_turns` does
`from . import mission_chat_turns`, which drags `model_tools` ->
`tools.registry.discover_builtin_tools()` -> `tools.process_registry`'s
module-scope singleton -> `async_delegation.restore_undelivered_completions()`,
and THAT creates `state.db`. The delegation lane runs first and reported whether
that file existed, so build 1 of a cold process emitted
`"head_home=X; no state.db"` and build 2 emitted `"head_home=X"` for identical
work. Under pytest, which one you got was decided by whichever module had
already dragged the chain in. A wire field no consumer can rely on and no test
can pin honestly is worse than no field.

The split:

* CONTRACT, per source entry — `status` / `lane` / `reason`, the bounded
  machine token an `unavailable` lane attaches (unchanged, still an exception
  class name), and a new typed `live_enrichment_error` replacing the
  `"; live enrichment failed: TypeError"` suffix.
* AMBIENT — one clearly-named `ambient` block beside rows/sources/counts,
  naming the resolved background-work home (provenance + basename). Published,
  never consulted; nothing branches on it. It keeps the diagnostic that told
  "nothing is running" apart from "nothing is running in the home I resolved".
* OFF THE WIRE — store presence ("no checkpoint file" / "no state.db" /
  "no async_delegations table"). Those describe storage layout, not work: a
  durable lane answering `ok` with zero rows out of a named home is already
  complete. Two of the three were self-perturbed and could never have been
  honest.

NO CONTRACT BUMP, ruled and recorded in the snapshot ledger. Nothing LEAVES the
wire: `detail` keeps its key, type and documented meaning, is byte-identical on
the `unavailable` entries a consumer renders from, and was already conditional
and modelled optional on both sides (three of five lanes ship `ok` entries
without it today; the Launcher reads it with `fallback: ''`). The additions are
"merely unread", not "invisible" — `sources` is parsed as a map with named-key
reads, exactly the constraint the WP-H2 ruling put on the consumer.

The response-envelope fixture gate no longer needs its `_normalise_detail`
workaround: the producer is byte-stable as emitted, so the comparison is raw.
Both fixture families are regenerated. The stream goldens also pick up
`runtime_config.mission_chat.compaction_threshold_tokens`, pre-existing drift
from 3d6f9ae81 which never regenerated them — the shape gate compares only
top-level `runtime_config` keys, so a nested addition stayed green.

Pins written after the implementation and watched fail first, headline included:
two builds in ONE cold subprocess must emit the same frame, and forcing the
chat-turn import chain before the first build must not change what the producer
says. Both are subprocess pins on purpose — in-process, `mission_chat_turns` is
already imported before the first assertion, which is why the defect survived to
be found on a fixture instead of by a unit test.

Filed, not fixed: a read-only projection still triggers delegation recovery
through that import chain. The root cause is `model_tools`' module-scope
`discover_builtin_tools()` call, and it needs its own slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
test(harness): green main by retiring a stale witness and pinning what survived

`test_omitting_a_flag_is_scoped_to_the_verb_that_asked` has failed on `main`
since 3a09a4b69 (2026-08-03 23:40) with `SystemExit: 2` on
`--cursor abc --since x`. Diagnosis: the flags were REMOVED from the surface
and the test was left behind. Not a CLI regression.

The test (fddf800af, 16:46 the same day) was written when the work verbs
narrowed the shared contract by opting OUT — `omit={"--cursor","--since"}` —
while every other stage42 verb was handed those two flags globally. A sibling
verb accepting them was then a real witness that the narrowing was per-verb.

3a09a4b69 inverted the mechanism to opt-IN `controls=` and handed
`--cursor`/`--since` to NO verb at all. It rewrote test_harness_cli.py to
match and never touched test_harness_work_cli.py, so the witness stopped
existing while the assertion kept asking for it.

What survives, and where it is pinned:

- The `controls=` half is already pinned, both directions, by
  test_harness_cli.py::test_stage42_controls_remain_available_on_their_real_owners
  and ::test_stage42_controls_are_refused_when_the_handler_cannot_honor_them,
  plus the work-lane pair in test_harness_work_cli.py. Restating it would be a
  second mechanism satisfying one pin.
- The `omit=` half was genuinely UNPINNED. `omit` survives 3a09a4b69 with one
  live call site (`persona instance repair-steering`, which writes a fixed
  human report and so drops `--output/--quiet/--fields`), and nothing drove
  it: test_harness_cli.py models `omit` only inside its own AST ownership
  extractor, which is bookkeeping, not behaviour. New
  ::test_omit_is_scoped_to_the_verb_that_asked drives both halves — the verb
  refuses the three, keeps `--dry-run`, and a sibling on the same helper keeps
  all three. Refusal alone would still pass if the flags had been deleted from
  `_add_stage42_global_args` outright; the sibling half is what makes it about
  scoping.

Recorded, not fixed here: `--cursor`/`--since` now have registration branches
in `_add_stage42_global_args` that no call site can reach. Nothing on the
stage42 lane offers pagination or history filtering, and nothing pins that
absence as intentional.

author: nekwo
message:
test(stream): pin the golden against the producer's whole shape, not its top-level keys

The stream fixture gate compared `set(core)` and `set(core["runtime_config"])`
— top-level key sets only. So when 3d6f9ae81 added
`runtime_config.mission_chat.compaction_threshold_tokens` without regenerating,
nothing the gate looked at changed: `mission_chat` was already in the
`runtime_config` key set, and the new key lives one level below it. The golden
sat stale and green, and the launcher then mirrored those stale bytes
cross-repo. A later agent regenerated the goldens, so the data is correct; the
gate that let it through was not.

The gate pinned the neighbourhood. It now pins the guarantee: rebuild each of
the four generated frames from the same production builders
`scripts/generate_agent_runtime_stream_fixtures.py` calls, and compare the full
set of nested key paths against the committed golden.

Balance, deliberately chosen. Paths, not values: values (timings, counts, the
generator's normalized stamps, machine-probed flags) are exactly what churns,
and a gate that reddens on churn gets regenerated reflexively without being
read — which is how goldens rot in the first place. List elements collapse onto
one `[]` segment for the same reason: a golden holding two entries where the
producer holds three is data, not contract. A key appearing or leaving anywhere
in the tree is never churn, and it now fails naming the exact dotted path with
the one command that fixes it. Verified zero-churn against `main`: all four
frames agree on every one of their 272/259/6/277 key paths today, under both an
ambient and an isolated HERMES_HOME.

Also added:

- `test_the_gate_covers_every_frame_the_generator_writes` — the rebuilt set is
  checked against the generator's own `GENERATED_FRAME_FILES`, so a fifth
  generated frame cannot be unpinned by construction (the S59 failure one level
  up).
- Anti-vacuity in both directions. Four drift classes planted into a copy of
  the real golden, each asserting first that the RETIRED comparison was blind
  to it — including the real 2026-08 `compaction_threshold_tokens` miss — and
  one test proving value churn and list length do NOT redden.
- `delta_batch.json` is now compared against a live `delta_batch_frame`; before
  this it had no producer comparison at all, only golden-vs-golden.

The shallow-compare was not shared: there is no common helper. The response
envelope gate (`test_response_contract_fixture.py`) already ends in full
`live == committed` equality with the key-set compares demoted to diagnostics,
and the other stream-fixture consumers only hash bytes against the manifest.
One gate carried the flaw; one gate is fixed.

Shape assertions duplicated in the per-frame tests were removed rather than
left alongside the new gate — two mechanisms satisfying one pin is how a
sabotaged gate stays green. Those tests keep only what shape cannot express
(`type`, a delta never shipping without a core, a heartbeat never carrying one,
parity capability VALUES).

Fixture bytes unchanged; `tool/test_quality/check_producer_contracts.py`
re-runs the generator and still reports byte-identical producer/consumer.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(gateway,windows): stop a pre-#45610 Scheduled Task from silently running the gateway in a killable console

hermes update's launcher refresh rewrites gateway.cmd + gateway.vbs and
reasons that "the task /TR points at a stable script path, so rewriting the
files retargets it with no schtasks call and no UAC". That holds only when
the registered action already names the .vbs. A task registered before
#45610 names the .cmd — a cmd.exe launch that owns a VISIBLE console
window — and no amount of file rewriting changes that. So the exact class of
install the refresh was written to rescue keeps a console-window gateway
forever, and nothing ever says so.

That is not cosmetic. The gateway dies with STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT
(0xC000013A) the moment the window is closed or the console process group
takes a stray control broadcast, and the ONLOGON-only trigger leaves it down
until the next login. Observed live: a fully healthy boot (Telegram
connected, cron job run) followed by a silent death, with `hermes gateway
status` reporting nothing but a bare `Last Run Result: -1073741510`.

Re-registering the action needs schtasks /Create (elevation), which the
update path deliberately avoids — so the fix is to make the condition
legible rather than to mutate it behind the operator's back:

* gateway_windows._task_action_is_console_less() classifies a schtasks dump
  by which launcher path the action names. Locale-independent on purpose:
  Windows translates the field labels, never the paths.
* gateway_windows.task_action_is_console_less() probes the live
  registration; None for absent/unreadable/unrecognised so unknown is never
  reported as broken.
* `hermes gateway status` names the cause next to the exit code an operator
  is already staring at.
* the post-update refresh says it too, with the elevated command to run.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(gateway,windows): resolve the console-probe platform guard, and pin the probe BODY

11a8db6f5 guarded task_action_is_console_less() with is_windows(), a name
this module never imports. Every test mocked the function out and every
caller mocks it too, so nothing executed those lines — the join between two
correct halves was the untested part. Live, `hermes gateway status` printed
a NameError traceback on the one command an operator runs when the gateway
is missing.

Guard on sys.platform, which is what the rest of the module uses, and pin
the probe by calling it for real over a stubbed schtasks dump instead of
stubbing its return value. Reverting the guard reproduces the NameError and
turns both new tests red.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(gateway,windows): render the autostart launcher from the managed interpreter, and let doctor see the drift

The Windows gateway launcher took its interpreter from get_python_path(),
which ends in a sys.executable fallback. That fallback is right for ephemeral
work in a dev checkout and wrong the moment it is persisted: the launcher
outlives the process that wrote it, so `hermes update` run from a bare system
Python stamps that Python into an artifact nothing re-examines, and every
gateway boot afterwards runs against a package set no update syncs.

Same class twice on one install: a fatal `ModuleNotFoundError:
concurrent_log_handler` that killed the gateway at import (2026-06-27), and a
`nemo_relay` traceback that made a fully healthy boot look like a fatal crash
and got reported as "the gateway crashed on compile errors". Recurrence is
the finding.

There was no accessor for "the interpreter Hermes is installed into" — which
is why the renderer had nothing better to ask. That absence was the defect:

* gateway.resolve_managed_python() reuses the layout knowledge _detect_venv_dir()
  already has (sys.prefix, $VIRTUAL_ENV, the .venv/venv checkout layouts that
  _venv_core_imports_healthy and managed_uv._default_live_venv treat as the
  install). No second hardcoded path.
* It raises ManagedPythonUnavailable with a single-line reason naming what was
  looked for, and NEVER degrades to a guess. get_python_path() keeps its
  fallback for the ephemeral callers that legitimately want it.
* _write_task_script() renders from it and lets the error propagate — refusing
  to write beats pinning a guess. The update path prints the reason instead of
  swallowing it into a debug log.
* gateway_windows.launcher_interpreter() reads the interpreter back out of the
  artifact, and `hermes doctor` fails when it isn't the managed one. That check
  is what would have surfaced this in June instead of on a dead gateway.

This reaches installs with no elevation: the update path rewrites the launcher
FILE contents, which needs no schtasks call and no UAC.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(tests,tools): retire ten standing reds — nine stale fixtures and one real frozen-home defect

Three files had been red long enough that every agent read them as
scenery. None of the ten failures was a guarantee Windows cannot hold.

tests/tools/test_approval.py (2) — destructive-command safety logic,
fenced in tests/tools/conftest.py as "POSIX temp-dir and symlink
canonicalization semantics that Windows does not reproduce". Wrong
diagnosis: Windows reproduces both. The fixtures hardcoded POSIX path
SPELLING — a literal "/tmp" that os.path.realpath resolves against the
current drive (-> "X:\tmp"), and unquoted separators that
shlex.split(posix=True) eats. Both now build their operand from the
platform's own temp dir. Fence rows deleted.

tests/tools/test_process_registry.py (3) — patch("os.getpgid") raised
AttributeError before the test body ran, though the behaviour it pins is
guarded by `if not _IS_WINDOWS` and reaches proc.kill() directly here;
the patch is now applied only where the attribute exists, so BOTH
branches are pinned. test_kill_detached_session_uses_host_pid mocked
psutil.Process().terminate(), which _terminate_host_pid never constructs
on Windows (it shells out to taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F) — it was
unfalsifiable, not inapplicable, and now mocks whichever primitive the
platform reaches. The PTY stdin test is gated on its actual dependency
(pywinpty / ptyprocess) rather than on the platform: Windows CAN run it.

tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py (5) — four assert _run_prompt_submit
was called, but the completion -> agent-turn hand-off has been opt-in
(_tui_background_agent_turns_enabled) since the fork foundation; they
now set the opt-in, so the ownership routing they exist to pin stays
pinned. The fifth broke on d0f5ef704 (2026-07-24), which swept the
run_conversation test doubles for the new persist_user_message kwarg and
missed this one; red for 16 days.

The real defect underneath: tools/environments/singularity.py and
modal.py both resolved get_hermes_home() at module import. Both are
imported by tools/terminal_tool.py, which ProcessRegistry.spawn_local
imports on its first call — so a caller that legitimately scrubs the
environment took `RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory` out
of a snapshot-store path it never touches. This was invisible only
because the PTY test above FAILED late enough to warm the import first;
gating it surfaced the red in isolation too. Both stores are now lazy
(_snapshot_store_path(), matching vercel_sandbox.py) and their rows are
dropped from the frozen-home ledger, which now enforces it.

Also pins the exemption's second guard: deleting the realpath check that
rejects an in-temp symlink resolving outside temp left the whole
TestDetectDangerousRm class green. Every change here was sabotage-
verified red-first with the sabotage confirmed applied — which is how
the two vacuous greens above were caught rather than shipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(feishu,agent,tests): retire 58 env-gap rows — a constructor-I/O defect and a Windows-path regex drift, not environment

Audit of the three unaudited environment-gap registries (tests/agent,
tests/gateway, tests/hermes_cli). This commit covers the agent and
gateway halves; the registry rows themselves are deleted in a follow-up.

Two real defects, both fenced as "Windows env gap":

* plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py — __init__ did
  `self._dedup_state_path = get_hermes_home() / ...` and then called
  `_load_seen_message_ids()`. That froze the path against whatever
  HERMES_HOME was set at construction AND made construction itself do
  disk I/O against the home, so an adapter built before a profile switch
  kept writing dedup state into the previous profile's home. Same hazard
  tests/test_no_frozen_hermes_home.py exists for, one scope down, and the
  same class 5c234e12a just fixed in tools/environments. The path is now
  a live-resolving property and the cache hydrates on the first dedup
  decision. 38 of the 39 fenced feishu rows were this defect; the 39th
  was an over-broad `patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=True)` that only
  looked hermetic because POSIX falls back to pwd.getpwuid().

* agent/image_routing.py — _LOCAL_IMAGE_PATH_RE anchored only on `~/`
  and `/`, though its own comment claims parity with gateway's
  extract_local_files(). Gateway's copy grew a drive-letter anchor in
  #34632; this one did not. While they were out of sync a Windows
  operator who pasted C:\Users\me\shot.png had it silently dropped here
  while the identical path delivered fine through the gateway.

The rest were stale tests, not gaps. The recurring mechanism is
`monkeypatch.setenv("HOME", ...)`: ntpath.expanduser prefers USERPROFILE,
so the reflex silently expanded ~ to the developer's REAL profile and the
test quietly stopped testing anything. tests/_home_env.point_home_at
patches what the platform's expanduser actually reads. The remainder are
POSIX SPELLING assertions (a "/" separator, a "cache/images" substring, a
lowercase env-var name Windows upper-cases, a file:// envelope whose
quoting is invisible only when the path quotes to itself), plus one
leaked SessionDB handle that Windows refused to unlink — a thread and
atexit leak on every platform that POSIX simply hid.

Every touched file was re-run whole after the fix; no newly-surfaced
failures. The feishu fix is sabotage-verified in both halves (freeze
restored -> red; constructor I/O restored -> red), with each sabotage
confirmed applied before the run.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(tests): give the env-gap fence a probe, and make a stale row fail instead of print

The fence deliberately did not skip, so a gap would stay visible. It made
main permanently red instead, which taught everyone to read reds as
scenery — and a standing red is excellent camouflage. Two consecutive
audits found the same thing under it: mostly stale tests, plus real
defects.

This audit's proof that the honesty mechanism did not work: the two
`test_api_server` / `test_readiness` rows described a HERMES_HOME volume
at 93.8% capacity. It is no longer full. Both rows had been dead for an
unknown length of time and NOTHING failed to say so — the stale detector
only prints, into a terminal summary nobody reads on a suite that is red
by design.

So a row now carries a live probe and becomes a real skip:

  * probe TRUE  -> really skipped, mechanism as the reason, plain run GREEN;
  * probe FALSE -> the test RUNS, and tests/test_env_gap_registry.py FAILS
    on the row.

That inverts the failure mode: staleness is a failing test rather than a
silent non-fence. The ledger also parses each fenced file's AST and fails
on a row naming a test that no longer exists — the rot that quietly
orphaned 163 rows through the 2026-07-31 upstream prune.

A probe must interrogate the MECHANISM, never the platform name.
`not hasattr(os, "chown")` and `find_spec("croniter") is None` are probes.
`sys.platform == "win32"` qualifies only where the code under test itself
branches on sys.platform, i.e. where the assertion pins a branch the host
never selects.

tests/agent: 24 rows -> 4. tests/gateway: ~62 -> 8. Everything else was a
stale test or a defect, both fixed. Of what remains, three groups are
DEPENDENCY-bound rather than platform-bound (defusedxml here; croniter,
pathspec, pywinpty in hermes_cli) and retire by installing the package.

Both halves of the ledger are sabotage-verified: probe forced False -> red,
bogus node id added -> red, each sabotage confirmed applied first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(hermes_cli,tests): retire 50 more env-gap rows — three real defects, and 3 tests that proved nothing

Second half of the environment-gap registry audit. tests/hermes_cli
registered 82 node ids across 44 files as pre-existing Windows/host gaps.
Every one was reproduced individually. Fifty were not gaps.

Three were REAL DEFECTS, which rule 3 of the fence contract forbids
registering at all:

* utils.atomic_replace retried only EXDEV/EBUSY, so concurrent os.replace
  onto one target lost roughly 3 writes in 10 on Windows (measured with a
  standalone probe). It now retries Win32 rename contention.
* hermes_cli/uninstall.py compared os.readlink()'s extended-length target
  against an unprefixed root, so Path.resolve() kept the prefix and the
  containment check was False for every Hermes-managed link: uninstall
  silently left its own node/npm/npx symlinks behind, via a bare
  `continue` with no logging. The candidate dirs include ~/.local/bin on
  EVERY platform.
* hermes_cli/main.py swallowed the web-UI stamp failure at DEBUG, so a
  missing pathspec meant a full npm install + Vite build on every boot
  with nothing above DEBUG to say why — and the reader called the same
  hash unguarded, where every other trouble path in that function returns
  True. `hermes web` would have died on an unhandled ModuleNotFoundError
  the moment a stamp existed; it never crashed only because the
  swallowing writer guaranteed no stamp ever existed. Both halves fixed
  and pinned by tests that mock the import failure, so they run with or
  without the package.

The rest were stale tests: a dozen read a UTF-8 file with no encoding=,
several asserted a POSIX path spelling that os.path.abspath
drive-qualifies, several pinned a sys.platform-selected POSIX branch
without pinning the branch — in files whose own siblings already showed
the convention — and two leaked an open sqlite handle through
`with kb.connect(...)`, which commits but never closes, though
kb.connect_closing exists for exactly that.

THREE VACUOUS GREENS surfaced once those tests actually ran. The worst:
test_setup_matrix_e2ee's guard used ast.walk(), which descends into
function bodies, so it matched a DEFERRED `import shutil` — deleting the
module-level import left it GREEN, which is precisely the NameError it
exists to prevent. It now walks tree.body. Two more passed only because
Windows never found their fixtures.

Two registry reasons were simply false. `bash -n <X:\...>` was blamed on
Git-bash not resolving drive paths; it resolves them fine, and the real
cause is that a bare "bash" argv hits CreateProcess's System32-before-PATH
order and silently ran the WSL shim in a different filesystem namespace.
And a kanban row claimed it asserts POSIX signal delivery, though
_pid_alive is stubbed and no signal is ever sent.

What remains is 32 probe-backed skips. Seventeen of them are
DEPENDENCY-bound rather than platform-bound — croniter, pathspec,
pywinpty and windows-curses are installable, and three of the four are
already declared dependencies — so installing them retires those rows
outright. That needs a ruling, per the fire/psutil precedent.

Four tests are deliberately left RED and unregistered, because they are
defects and rule 3 says a defect gets fixed, not fenced:

* test_hooks_cli.py (3) — agent/shell_hooks.py runs shlex.split() in POSIX
  mode over the hook command, which eats every backslash in a Windows
  path. Hooks report "command not found", doctor calls every hook
  non-executable, and script_mtime_iso returns None, so the "script
  modified since approval" TAMPER CHECK at hermes_cli/hooks.py:369-376 can
  never fire. An approved hook can be rewritten with anything and doctor
  still prints OK.
* test_commands.py::TestSlackNativeSlashes::test_telegram_parity —
  slack_native_slashes() drops entries at the 50-command cap in
  registration order with no accounting, so parity is a function of how
  many plugins are installed.

Both fixes are policy decisions (argv parsing on a security path; command
curation), so they are escalated rather than taken unilaterally.

41 of the 43 audited files now run fully green. Every fix was
sabotage-verified red-first with the sabotage confirmed on disk first —
29 cycles across the two halves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
test(hermes_cli): make the four deliberate reds announce themselves as defects

The registry audit left test_hooks_cli.py (3) and
test_commands.py::TestSlackNativeSlashes::test_telegram_parity red on
purpose: rule 3 of the fence contract says a failure caused by a defect
in our own code gets fixed, not registered, and both fixes are owner

A bare red on Windows is exactly what gets re-filed as an environment
gap, which is how the tamper-check hole below stayed invisible in the
first place. The run now prints a KNOWN DEFECTS section naming the
mechanism and telling the reader NOT to re-register it.

The hooks one is a security finding, not a Windows quirk:
agent/shell_hooks.py parses the hook command with shlex.split() in POSIX

executes, doctor calls every hook non-executable, and script_mtime_iso()

author: nekwo
message:
fix(tools): make Windows PTY stdin actually deliver, and retire 12 install-gap rows

The env-gap registry filed 17 hermes_cli rows against croniter, pathspec and
pywinpty. None of them was an environment gap. All three are DECLARED in
pyproject.toml and all three were already installed in the managed runtime venv
— they were missing only from the ambient C:\Python312 the tests run under. A
broken local install had been recorded as a property of this host, which is the
one thing rule 1 of the fence contract exists to prevent.

Installing them retired 12 rows outright (croniter 2, pathspec 3, pywinpty 7),
matching the fire/psutil precedent. windows-curses stays fenced: it is
deliberately not declared and curses_ui.py:623-624 falls back to a numbered
text menu, so it is a genuine optional extra rather than a broken install.

The 13th pywinpty row is why the distinction is worth the words.

  * test_win_pty_bridge's test_cwd_is_respected matched the PTY's RAW bytes for
    a tmp_path longer than the terminal's 80-column width. A ConPTY is a
    terminal: it breaks the line with a real CRLF mid-token, so the assertion
    pinned terminal geometry rather than the cwd, and the child had been
    correct all along. Now compared through a wrap-aware unwrap.

  * Underneath it sat a REAL DEFECT. tools/process_registry.py's Windows PTY
    stdin path was completely non-functional while reporting success:

      - submit_stdin appended "\n". On a Windows ConPTY the Enter key is a
        CARRIAGE RETURN, and a bare LF does not commit the line, so the child's
        read() never saw the data — while write_stdin returned {"status":
        "ok"} because the bytes had reached the pty.
      - close_stdin called pywinpty's sendeof(), which writes Ctrl-D: the POSIX
        EOF character, inherited from the ptyprocess API it mirrors. Windows
        consoles use Ctrl-Z; Ctrl-D arrives as an ordinary byte. The child
        blocked forever and we returned {"status": "ok", "message": "EOF
        sent"}.

    So any caller closing stdin to let an EOF-driven child finish — the agent,
    and the dashboard /chat tab through /api/pty — waited on a process that
    could never exit, and was told it had succeeded. Both halves verified
    against a live ConPTY before and after, and each is pinned red-first.

The single test that would have caught this was gated on importorskip("winpty"),
so the never-installed declared dependency kept it skipped and the defect
invisible. It also spawned a bare `python3`, which does not exist on Windows —
it exited 127 and the assertions measured a command-not-found. Every other
spawn in that file already used sys.executable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
test(tools): migrate the last fence onto probes — 109 rows to 14, and nine defects out from under them

`tests/tools` was the only registry still on the mark-only mechanism, so it
alone kept `main` red — which is what the previous two sweeps were for. All 109
rows were re-run individually and audited. NINETY-FOUR were not gaps.

NINE were REAL DEFECTS in our own code, which rule 3 forbids fencing. Every one
is a Windows-only SILENT failure — none raised, so none was noticed:

  * tools/file_tools.py `_check_sensitive_path` compared only the normpath
    form, which rewrites "/etc/hosts" to "\etc\hosts", so every prefix stopped
    matching and the guard returned None — ALLOW — for exactly the paths it
    exists to refuse. The container backends hand it real Linux paths from this
    host. The same bug had already been fixed 300 lines above for
    `_BLOCKED_DEVICE_PATHS` and left open-coded, so the second instance
    survived the first fix; both now share `_posix_match_forms`.
  * tools/environments/file_sync.py held a NamedTemporaryFile handle open and
    passed its path to a downloader that reopens it (refused on Windows), and
    built `remote_path` with native separators so nothing matched
    `_pushed_hashes`. sync_back applied NOTHING, three times per attempt,
    swallowed by the retry loop's warning.
  * tools/process_registry.py sent "\n" to a ConPTY (which commits lines on CR)
    and called pywinpty's sendeof(), which writes POSIX Ctrl-D rather than
    Windows Ctrl-Z — returning {"status": "ok", "message": "EOF sent"} both
    times. Interactive PTY stdin was wholly non-functional while reporting
    success.
  * tools/credential_files.py and tools/environments/daytona.py built
    SANDBOX-side (always-Linux) paths with the HOST separator.
  * tools/skills_guard.py sorted Path objects where tools/skills_hub.py sorted
    relative POSIX strings, and skills_hub wrote bundles without newline="" so
    every "\n" landed as "\r\n" — making content_hash and bundle_content_hash
    disagree, reporting every fresh install as drifted and binding the scan
    attestation to a digest the installed bytes never had.
  * tools/checkpoint_manager.py rmtree'd a git object store; git writes loose
    objects read-only and Windows refuses to unlink those, so every checkpoint
    deletion failed and each call site only logged a warning.
  * scripts/check_subprocess_stdin.py keyed KNOWN_SAFE with the native
    separator, so its allowlist matched nothing on Windows.

The rest were stale tests. Note how many stated REASONS were wrong, not just
the verdicts: rows blaming "_SEP" were an _IS_WINDOWS branch, a cp1252 decode,
a read-only unlink. A blanket "Windows is different here" reads identically
whether the CODE or the TEST is at fault — and for a path crossing into a Linux
sandbox, os.sep IS the bug. That ambiguity is what hid nine defects.

The 14 survivors are probe-backed and become real skips. Each probe MEASURES
its mechanism — a chmod round trip, a real shebang spawn — never the platform
name.

Also closes a hole in the gate itself: `_load_registry` returns None when a
conftest has no `_ENV_GAP_SKIPS`, so both existing checks SKIPPED `tests/tools`
entirely and reported green while auditing nothing — two rows in it had already
gone orphaned with nothing failing to say so. A third check now fails when any
fenced directory still uses the mark-only lane.

Left deliberately RED and announced: test_search_error_guard.py. Content search
for a literal backslash is silently corrupted because the search PATTERN is
routed through an MSYS shell to a native ripgrep, and Git Bash collapses a
doubled backslash even inside single quotes. Third incident in that seam, so
the shell hop is the bug, not the escaping — a real change to the search
execution path, filed rather than smuggled into an audit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(security): make tirith_fail_open honest on platforms tirith cannot run on

check_command_security() returned {"action": "allow"} unconditionally when
is_platform_supported() was False, and only THEN read tirith_fail_open. An
operator who set security.tirith_fail_open: false therefore got a silent
fail-open on Windows with nothing anywhere saying their setting was inert —
while tools/approval.py goes to real trouble (two code paths, #20733) to
honour that same flag on ImportError. The codebase contradicted itself about
whether the flag binds.

Owner ruling: make it honest, not strict. The platform arm still ALLOWS —
tirith publishes no build for this OS+arch, so there is no scanner to fail
closed against and blocking every command would take the machine offline
rather than make it safer. What changes is that the arm now READS the flag,
and when it proceeds to allow despite an explicit fail-closed request it says
so: warned once per process through the existing _warn_once dedupe (this sits
on the per-command hot path), naming the flag, the platform and why it cannot
bind, and named in the returned summary so callers that surface it get it too.
The default fail-open path is unchanged and stays completely silent.

Tests are red-first: reverting the short-circuit to the flag-blind form takes
both fail-closed tests red (no warning recorded, summary unset), and removing
the fail_open early return takes the two silence tests red.

FILED, not fixed here — the shared seam. approval.py reads this same flag at
two more sites and does not agree with this one:

  * both of its readers sit in `except ImportError:` branches for
    `from tools.tirith_security import ...`, so the seam CANNOT live in
    tirith_security.py — that is the module that just failed to import;
  * they read hermes_cli.config directly and so ignore the TIRITH_FAIL_OPEN /
    TIRITH_ENABLED env overrides that _load_security_config honours. Setting
    TIRITH_FAIL_OPEN=false binds inside tirith_security and is invisible to
    approval.py's ImportError paths — a third disagreement about one flag.

The fix is a tiny import-light config accessor (default, tirith_enabled
interaction and env override stated once) that all three sites read. That
reaches into approval.py, which another session owns right now, so it is
reported rather than half-done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(hooks): stop POSIX shlex eating the hook path, so the tamper check can fire

agent/shell_hooks.py tokenized the configured hook command with
shlex.split() in POSIX mode at three sites (_spawn, _command_script_path,
script_is_executable). POSIX mode reads `\` as an escape, but on Windows it
is the path separator, so shlex.split(r"C:\tools\hook.py") returned
["C:toolshook.py"]. Downstream: the hook never spawned, doctor called every
hook non-executable, and script_mtime_iso() returned None — and the "script
modified since approval" check reads

    if mtime_now and mtime_at and mtime_now > mtime_at

so a None fell straight through. The TAMPER CHECK could never fire: an
approved hook could be rewritten with arbitrary content and `hermes doctor`
still reported OK.

Mechanism established before choosing the fix. This is NOT the Git Bash /
MSYS command-line rebuild (MSVCRT escaping, backslashes collapsed even
inside single quotes) that bit us elsewhere tonight: the command string is
read out of cli-config.yaml by Python and never crosses a shell boundary.
The mangling is purely in-process, so the fix is the tokenizer mode.

All three sites now route through one _split_command(): POSIX mode off
Windows, `posix=False` plus outer-quote stripping on it — matching the
existing `posix=(os.name != "nt")` convention in hermes_cli/mcp_security.py
and hermes_cli/main.py. _command_script_path also accepts os.sep as a path
separator so an extension-less Windows path resolves to the script rather
than to the interpreter.

Red-first, each with a sufficient mechanism:
  * forcing the POSIX tokenizer back takes 4 of the 5 new tokenization tests
    red plus TestHooksDoctor::test_flags_mtime_drift (the node that pins the
    tamper check);
  * the 5th pins quote stripping, which that sabotage does not reach — it is
    red under a _strip_outer_quotes identity mutation instead. Worth
    recording: quoting the path in cli-config.yaml was an accidental
    workaround, because POSIX shlex keeps backslashes inside double quotes.

The deliberate-red banner entry for test_hooks_cli.py is REMOVED — a banner
announcing a live defect that no longer exists is the same stale claim in the
other direction. The file's other two reds turned out to have a second,
independent cause underneath the tokenizer one, which the fix does not touch:
both spawn a bare `#!/usr/bin/env bash` script and this loader cannot exec a
shebang (WinError 193). That is a genuine platform gap, so it is registered
in _ENV_GAP_SKIPS with a live probe that performs the spawn rather than
testing a platform name. tests/test_env_gap_registry.py stays 12/12.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(tools): teach the verification-cleanup exemption the MSYS spelling of temp

_find_shell() returns Git Bash on Windows, so the cleanup command an agent
actually writes spells its temp artifact `/c/Users/.../Temp/hermes-verify-x.py`
— which the exemption could never match (it only knew `C:\Users\...`) and which
a leading `/` also hands straight to the "delete in root path" rule. It failed
closed: routine cleanup was refused, every time.

Widened by translating the ONE spelling, not by loosening a pattern.
_windows_spelling_of_msys_path() does a pure `/c/x` -> `C:\x` rewrite (Windows
only; a path already carrying a backslash is left alone), and the result is
handed to _is_exempt_verification_artifact_path() — the same literal-spelling
and post-realpath guards the native path has always gone through, now factored
out so the two lanes cannot drift. Nothing is exempt through MSYS that would
not be exempt natively: traversal, a second operand, -rf, a glob, command
substitution, a trailing `;`, a path outside temp, and an in-temp symlink
resolving outside temp are all still refused, re-pinned in the MSYS spelling.

The new pins assert the exemption FIRED rather than that the verdict was
permissive, and pin non-vacuity by showing the same shape with a non-artifact
basename is still flagged — the trap that let a Windows-native pin stay green
with the exemption deleted outright.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(hermes_cli): stop deciding Slack slash parity with an unaccounted clamp

Slack allows an app 50 slash commands. The registry is over that, and the
overflow branch in slack_native_slashes() just returned — so which commands
kept a native slash was a function of how many plugins happened to be
installed, discoverable only by diffing generated manifests. The limit is
SLACK'S and stays at 50; what changes is that losing to it is now said out
loud.

The clamp is recorded at the one branch that performs it, so the list and its
accounting cannot disagree. slack_native_slashes() logs every dropped name at
WARNING, `hermes slack manifest` prints them to stderr next to the paste
instructions (stdout stays pure JSON), and slack_clamped_slashes() returns the
same accounting without logging. Deliberate omissions — Slack built-ins and
_SLACK_VIA_HERMES_ONLY — are excluded: reporting curated decisions as cap
casualties would bury the names that really did lose a slot.

test_telegram_parity stays RED, deliberately. The finding had two halves and
only one is fixed: /platform is still a gateway command everywhere except
Slack, and giving it a slot means taking one from something else — product
curation, an owner decision. The KNOWN DEFECTS banner is reworded to say
exactly that, rather than continuing to announce a silence that no longer
exists.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent_runtime): make persona_runtime the only operator-channel policy layer

Two repos served contradictory operator-channel rules into ONE system message
and the model picked one. 7fd38cdd (launcher) scoped the text so they agree;
this removes the cause, because nothing kept them agreed and the failure is
silent -- it surfaces only as an agent behaving oddly in a live session.

THE INJECTION MECHANISM (established before changing anything -- it decides
whether the fix is even possible as specified):

  Mission Control workspace picker resolves <operator-selected dir>/AGENTS.md
  (launcher lib/features/mission_control/data/mission_agent_context.dart)
    -> ships it as the "agents_file" action arg
    -> mission_control_bridge.dart emits "--agents-file <abs path>"
    -> hermes_cli/harness.py "mission-chat message --agents-file"
    -> agent_runtime/mission_chat_turn_context.py
    -> prompt_observability.load_workspace_agents_context() validates
       (absolute, basename "agents.md", <=128KB)
    -> persona_runtime._mission_chat_surface_message() pastes the body into the
       SAME system message that already carries _mission_chat_operative_rules().

  The two texts land contiguously, separated only by the workspace preamble.
  Verified in the runtime capture
  .hermes/agent-runtime/prompt_observability/ctx_63bdeb96c3bdf7cf.json --
  /prompt_layers[4]/source_context_file => AGENTS.md, and final_model_input
  carries "...never inside it." then the workspace preamble then the launcher
  AGENTS.md body, whose "WAIT for Tony's go-ahead" sits a few hundred chars
  after the runtime rule saying a clear instruction IS the go-ahead.

  Injection is GENERIC, not launcher-specific: the picker accepts any
  directory, and the loader accepts any absolute path whose basename is
  "agents.md". So a hermes-side allowlist naming one repo's file would be
  answering a question the mechanism does not ask. It is not built.

WHAT CHANGES

- _mission_chat_operative_rules() absorbs the operator intent that used to live
  in the launcher AGENTS.md, so the policy is stated once, here: the pause now
  has a third earned case (a technical or multi-step task where the agent
  filled in a substantive detail the operator never stated), framed explicitly
  as a COMPREHENSION check that restates its plan -- never a permission
  request. The act-directly carve-out keeps the two shapes the operator named
  (relaying a dictated message, repeating an approved action against a newly
  named target), read-only work stays free, and a briefed agent is told the
  brief is its authorization. The 2026-08-03 regression guard is untouched and
  still green.

- MISSION_CHAT_WORKSPACE_AGENTS_PREAMBLE states the boundary once, ahead of any
  workspace body: repo instructions describe the repo and do NOT govern this
  channel; where they touch confirmation/permission/go-ahead the operator-chat
  rules win. One scope sentence, not a policy-precedence engine -- and because
  it is a property of the layer rather than a reaction to its contents, it
  protects ARBITRARY workspaces, which is the only thing that answers a generic
  injection path. prompt_observability reuses the constant for char
  attribution, so no drift.

TESTS (written after the implementation, each watched fail first, against main
in a throwaway detached worktree so no fix-tree state was mutated):

- own_the_confirm_back_scope -- RED on main (no "exactly three cases").
- may_not_redefine_operator_channel_policy -- RED on main (no scope sentence);
  pins ordering rules < scope < body, and asserts the workspace body is really
  injected so the pin cannot pass vacuously.
- permission_policy_has_exactly_one_layer -- forward-looking pin, green on main
  by construction; proven red-capable by injecting a go-ahead clause into
  _mission_chat_identity_prompt in the throwaway worktree, which failed it as
  designed. Carries an internal non-vacuity assert that the rules layer DOES
  contain the vocabulary.

tests/agent_runtime/test_persona_runtime_fake.py 31 passed;
test_prompt_observability + test_mission_chat_turn_context + the two
persona_runtime residue suites 70 passed.

Companion launcher commit reduces its AGENTS.md to a pointer and gates every
tracked AGENTS.md there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(tools): give path identity one authority, so the next guard cannot re-derive it wrong

Four defects in one night, three mechanisms, one root cause: nothing owned the
question "does this operand denote the same real file as that one?", so every
guard re-derived it and each got it wrong differently. normpath('/etc/hosts') is
'\etc\hosts' where os.sep is a backslash, so _SENSITIVE_PATH_PREFIXES'
startswith('/etc') returned False and the write guard answered ALLOW for exactly
the paths it exists to refuse. The identical defect had already been found and
fixed for _BLOCKED_DEVICE_PATHS three hundred lines above it and left
open-coded there - which is how the second instance survived the first fix, and
is the proof the cause is structural rather than incidental.

tools/path_identity.py owns spelling (posix_match_forms,
windows_spelling_of_msys_path) and identity (denotes_same_file). Pure and total:
os and re only, no logging, no config, no exceptions out; the sole I/O is
realpath, and resolution failure degrades to the spelling comparison the callers
already used rather than raising or inventing identity.

Migrated, each with its rejection table re-pinned rather than trusted:

  * file_tools._posix_match_forms -> thin shim that tilde-expands (profile HOME
    is Hermes policy, not a spelling fact) and delegates. Both device and
    sensitive-root guards keep calling it, so no caller can forget the expansion.
  * file_tools._check_sensitive_path config arm -> denotes_same_file. Closes the
    fallback branch: when _resolve_path_for_task raised, the only remaining
    comparison was a normpath, which follows no symlinks, so a symlink to
    config.yaml was writable - and writing config.yaml is how an agent turns
    approvals off.
  * approval._windows_spelling_of_msys_path -> re-export from the authority
    (approval was the SECOND place to re-derive an MSYS translation;
    environments/local.py was the first). Behaviour byte-identical.
  * approval._is_exempt_verification_artifact_path -> its identity half asks the
    authority; its literal-spelling half deliberately does NOT, because that
    string equality is what refuses '/tmp/nested/../x' and every alternate
    spelling of temp.
  * browser_tool reaper environ binding and tts_tool in-place transcode
    detection -> denotes_same_file. Both compared normpath/abspath strings and
    so folded neither case nor symlinks.

Deliberately NOT built: is_within. tools/path_security.validate_within_dir
already owns containment with resolve()+relative_to; a second one here would
recreate the duplicate-authority defect this module exists to retire.

The gate is AST, not source-grep (that class is retired here - see
tests/test_no_source_grep_assertions.py). It resolves the producing call and
follows the value: a normpath/realpath/abspath result reaching ==/!=/in/
startswith/endswith anywhere under tools/ fails, unless registered with a reason.
Three exemptions, each a defensible claim that the raw comparison IS the right
question. Proven non-vacuous against the code as it actually shipped: the
detector fires on _check_sensitive_path at f7fe6ce3e^, on _is_blocked_device_path
before its fix, and on the reaper at ad0a8e080 - and stays quiet on
Path.resolve() comparisons, which are correct and would otherwise bury the real
findings under an allowlist nobody reads.
