author: nekwo
message:
fix(stream): EG-1.2 (RD-H3) — an empty patch frame can never promote

A `patch` frame that advances the client's watermark must carry the state that
justifies it. It did not. `batch_is_patch_coverable` is an `all(...)` with no
"at least one patch" requirement and a COVERED DOMAIN EVENT is coverable on its
own — it carries no fold state precisely because its paired `state.patched` is
supposed to ride the same batch — so a batch carrying the event WITHOUT its pair
shipped `{"type":"patch","patches":[],"watermark":<batch>}`. The client folded
nothing and advanced anyway; the row it should have folded is stale until some
unrelated full core happens by, and no downstream gate can see it, because the
watermark says the span was applied.

Five producer paths re-open the missing pair — the three best-effort patch-emit
swallows in OfficeStore, `update_surface`'s NO-EXCEPTION skip when the surface
did not previously exist (:383-384), and the cross-process split of
`delta_patches_enabled` (writer and stream producer evaluate it independently,
so a transient root-config fault suppresses the patch in one process while the
other happily promotes the event-only batch). So the guard lands at the ONE
chokepoint that sees the filtered list rather than in five producers:

- `_batch_frames_with_liveness` asks `batch_carries_patch_rows(batch)` before
  promoting; empty falls through to the full-core classification, where the
  existing `snapshot_build reason=demote` receipt already bills it. Coverable is
  not the same as EXPRESSIBLE, and the honest answer for a batch that moved
  state this lane cannot express is the core;
- `patch_batch_frame` additionally refuses an empty filtered list (`ValueError`),
  belt to the caller's braces — same one-authority pairing the coverage token's
  own comment argues for. The predicate is a bare `any(...)` and not a second
  list build: the gate runs on every drained batch and only needs emptiness.

Producer receipts, no control flow: the three OfficeStore swallows now put the
exception CLASS in the message rather than only in the traceback, so the demote
this stage forces is attributable instead of mysterious.

Tests (+5, tests/agent_runtime/test_stream_patch.py 14 → 19):
- a coverable `office.surface.updated`-only batch demotes — asserted coverable
  FIRST (anti-vacuity: the demotion must be this guard's work, not the coverage
  gate's), then `type != "patch"` and positively `delta` with a core;
- the discriminator: the SAME event WITH its paired `office_surface` row still
  promotes, which kills the over-demoting mutant that would take the lane dark;
- the builder unit refuses an empty filtered list, and the pre-existing
  empty-BATCH refusal stays distinguishable from it;
- the PAIRING pinned: `batch_carries_patch_rows` forced True at the promotion
  site (RD's caller-guard mutant, applied from the test) and the builder still
  refuses — without this a future edit could delete the caller guard, watch the
  builder unit stay green, and ship the frame anyway;
- regression fence: every committed `patch*.json` golden carries >=1 row, so the
  new refusal is unreachable for all of them. No fixture moved, no event type
  registered, no contract hash touched.

Killing mutations run and reverted:
- caller guard dropped -> the demote test reds; with the builder guard also
  dropped the type probe itself convicts: "a batch with no state.patched row
  must never ship as a patch frame; got patches=[]" / `assert 'patch' != 'patch'`;
- builder guard alone dropped -> "Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>" on
  the builder unit AND on the pairing case, while the demote test stays green;
- `batch_carries_patch_rows` forced False (over-demote) -> the discriminator plus
  both fielded steer/profile promotion tests red.

196 adjacent tests green (office state patches, fold negotiation, office
subscribe + live hub, state patches, shipped-default) and 100 more across the
stream, office-store, surface-update, orphan-archive and snapshot-contract
suites.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(office): EG-1.3 (RD-H1) — one scope authority for the office push sink (#57)

The office push lane could DROP a promoted batch with neither a patch nor a
resync. `patch_coverage` owns which entities may promote; the sink's scope test
was a private restatement of the id scheme that knew only `office_actor` and a
slash-prefixed id. WV-H3 (2026-08-16) widened the first vocabulary and not the
second, and `office_surface`'s id is the BARE workspace id — so a folder-only
frame failed BOTH conjuncts and took the bare `return`, violating this module's
own rule that a resync is recoverable and a dropped change is not. Reachable on
every folder rename with no actor write in the same ~450ms coalescing window;
masked because a mixed batch is forwarded whole, and because the argv `harness
stream` child still folds the same batch for the launcher.

So the scope parser moves to the module that owns the id scheme it reads
backwards:

- `state_patches.office_patch_scope(patch) -> workspace_id | None`, beside the id
  builders. `office_actor` splits on the FIRST `/` exactly as
  `office_actor_patch_id` joins on it (which is also what keeps `ws_pilot_2` out
  of `ws_pilot`'s scope); `office_surface` IS the bare workspace id; everything
  else, and any id that cannot be placed, is None. None is not "every
  workspace" — a persona row is forwarded INSIDE an in-scope frame and never puts
  one in scope;
- the sink's in-scope test and `_delta_touches_workspace`'s `state.patched` arm
  both call it. The resync twin carried the identical fork and was saved only by
  the `office.*` arm catching the paired domain event next door; saved by a
  neighbour is not an invariant, and the twin that had no neighbour lost the
  change outright. `prefix` is gone from both, so there is no second spelling
  left to drift. Forward-whole (V6) semantics unchanged.

After this a batch the coverage authority promotes is by construction FORWARDED
or RESYNCED, never dropped. No wire change, no event registered, no contract
hash or SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSION moved, no fixture regenerated — the launcher
fold already handles `office_surface` (WV-L3) and the cross-repo golden exists.
`OFFICE_FOLD_ENTITIES` is deliberately NOT widened: it is the server-side
fail-open default for a client that declared nothing, and widening it would
declare on behalf of every un-updated launcher in the field.

Tests (+5). Witness 1 — delivery (test_serve_rpc_office_subscribe.py 69 → 73):
- a folder-only frame is FORWARDED: its single row is mirrored off the committed
  `patch_office_surface.json`, and the expected `changed.folders` is read out of
  that golden rather than restated here;
- another workspace's folder change sends nothing — the second driven value, so
  neither drop-all nor forward-all passes the pair;
- the demoted-delta twin gains both halves as params: this workspace's bare-id
  folder row resyncs, another workspace's does not.

Witness 2 — authority → scope, in a DIFFERENT file, beside the existing
partition gate (test_stream_patch.py 19 → 20): every office entity enumerated
from `patch_coverage`'s OWN namespace must be placed into a workspace by
`office_patch_scope` under at least one id shape. That is the half that catches
the next WV-H3 — covering a new office entity without teaching the scope function
reds here even though no sink test for that entity exists yet — and the id shape
is left open on purpose, since the two live entities already use different ones.

Killing mutations run and reverted:
- `office_actor`-only sink predicate restored -> the folder-only test reds with
  "ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)": the mutant emits
  NOTHING, so every probe is on the content of a message it never constructs.
  Witness 2 stays GREEN, which is the point of having two;
- second-order: that mutant emitting a RESYNC instead of dropping -> reds too,
  "assert 'runtime.office.resync' == 'runtime.office.patch'" (a resync carries a
  different method and no `patches`), plus three addressed-not-broadcast tests;
- every `office_surface` row scoped in (forward-all) -> "another workspace's
  folder change" reds on the extra `runtime.office.patch`;
- the `office_surface` arm dropped from `office_patch_scope` (RD-H1's own
  predicate mutant) -> reds all three: sink delivery, the resync twin
  ("IndexError: list index out of range"), and witness 2 with "'office_surface'
  can be promoted by patch_coverage but office_patch_scope places no id shape of
  it into a workspace";
- the twin arm alone reverted to `office_actor`-only -> only the twin param reds,
  while every sink test stays green.

325 tests green across the subscribe, live-hub, stream-patch, office state-patch,
fold-negotiation, socket-lane and office RPC suites; 92 more across the
contract-version, event-registration and dead-symbol gates confirm nothing moved.

PENDING, and not this commit's to run: RD-H1's LIVE acceptance step — one real
folder gesture arriving on the push lane on the operator's runtime — is the
orchestrator's, and gates Plan C's TC-4 stream-child deletion together with R0-a.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(office): EG-1.1 — an unreadable event log refuses typed instead of minting baseline 0

`runtime.office.subscribe` asked the watermark a question it could not answer
honestly. `int(events_watermark().get("event_offset") or 0)` folded the module's
own typed unknown — `{"event_offset": None, "event_offset_error": ...}`, which
`events_watermark` documents as a ROUTINE outcome on this platform under AV
scanning — into offset 0, with no exception for the typed `except` to catch and
the error string discarded.

Offset 0 is the one value that module calls maximally damaging, and this lane is
where it costs the most: the sink's baseline gate is `<= baseline`, so a
subscription baselined at 0 has no gate. The hub's mandatory post-subscribe
hydrate then came back to the client as a resync; the client re-subscribed; the
producer restarted for the whole room; the next hydrate resynced it again — the
loop `office_patch_sink`'s baseline-before-type ordering exists to end, at a
full core per lap for every subscriber present.

Cannot-read is now its own answer, and it is asked in ONE place: the sink's
`_event_offset_of` becomes the public `event_offset_of` and the handler calls
it, so "what position does this watermark state?" has a single answer instead of
two opposite ones. None yields a transient `baseline_unavailable` refusal beside
`push_lane_unavailable` / `push_lane_draining` — same code, same `data.reason`
shape, same `prior_subscription_released` key — and NO registration happens on
that path, so a refused client leaks no subscriber and starts no producer. The
discarded half is kept for the operator: the platform error CLASS (never the
message) rides a `serve_office_subscribe_refused` line on the serve loop's own
log, reached through a new narrow `OFFICE_SUBSCRIPTIONS.service_log()`.

An empty log is still a real position. The paired discriminator test pins a
readable literal 0 registering at baseline 0 — refusing every zero would break
the first subscribe against a fresh runtime, and what separates the honest zero
from the fabricated one is presence, not the number.

Mutations run: restoring `or 0` reds the refusal test twice over (the reply has
no `error` key at all; the fake hub's record holds the leaked key), and
`if not baseline_offset:` reds the empty-log discriminator. Both reverted.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(office): EG-1.5 — the projection counts what it could not read, and an unreadable archive stops resetting the guard token

Two silent losses in one domain, both of them a store swallow that a reader
downstream then reported as a complete answer.

**The shortened projection that called itself complete.** `_read_actor_dir` has
always skipped an actor file it could not decode, and the skip has to stay — a
whole office must not vanish because one file is mid-write or held by an AV
scanner. What could not stay is the silence. Every reader got a SHORTER list, and
`_office_projection` then computed `actors_truncated` from that already-shortened
list and arrived at 0: a launcher could not tell a desk that was removed from a
desk whose file the platform would not open.

The count now leaves with the rows. `_read_actor_dir` returns an `ActorScan`
(rows + `unreadable`), logging once per scan aggregated by exception CLASS — not
per file, which would flood the log on every office read. `scan_actors` is the
chokepoint; `list_actors` is the thin list view over it, so the sixteen callers
that only want rows keep their signature. `actors_unreadable` rides
`_office_projection`, which means it reaches BOTH readers — `runtime.office.get`
and the `runtime.office.subscribe` baseline — and the test that proves it asserts
the two replies EQUAL rather than two literals that could drift.

**The guard token an unreadable archive silently reset to 1.** An archived key's
revision is where the office's concurrency token lives between a remove and the
re-add that follows it; `upsert_actor` bases the new revision on it so a re-added
key carries its history forward. The swallow made that `archived = None` → base 0
→ revision **1**, handing every peer and every launcher read model a token BELOW
the one they already held — a server that silently rewound, which the next
guarded write reads as its own stale prediction. EG-5.1 arms exactly that
comparison, so this is hard-before it.

Unreadable archive now raises typed `ArchiveUnreadable` (reason
`archive_unreadable`, `-32600`) on both write verbs — the upsert's base read and
the remove's idempotent arm, one string per condition rather than one per verb.
The remove arm's old behaviour was worse than an untyped crash: `JSONDecodeError`
is a `ValueError`, so it fell into `actor_invalid` and told the client to fix its
payload for a corrupt file on the server.

`archive_actors_for_instance` keeps its per-actor swallow — a prune must not die
on one bad file — but returns `{"archived": N, "failed": M}` so that 0-matched
and 3-failed stop being the same answer.

Mutations run, each reverted: bare `continue` reds the count test at both driven
values (0 == 1, 0 == 2) and reds the subscribe witness; forking the chokepoint
(count bolted onto `get` only) leaves the get-side test GREEN and reds the
subscribe witness with `KeyError: 'actors_unreadable'` — which is the whole point
of that witness; archive fall-through to base 0 acks `{'revision': 1}` verbatim;
dropping the remove-arm guard answers `-32602`; a bare-int prune return reds both
prune tests.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(parity): EG-6.4 — a retired placement's chat session stops counting as lost data

The "projection drops" chip counted the residue of the operator's own
first-class retires as anomalies. A retire archives the instance row and
deliberately leaves the chat session on disk (history is never destroyed),
so every retire added one permanent orphan to the count — forever, and the
drop that would actually mean something was buried under four that did not.

The classification is declared at the EMISSION site, per parity.py's own
contract: an unresolved binding whose instance id carries a retirement
tombstone emits `instance_retired` with `by_design=True`; an id that resolves
nowhere at all still emits today's anomalous `no_instance_match`. `by_design`
is additive on the completeness row, the envelope version does not move, and
the launcher's declaration path already subtracts declared codes with no
repo-B change.

The archive half of the retirement predicate gets a bulk reader
(`retired_persona_instance_ids`) sharing the `*_retire` selection rule with
the per-id probe through `_retire_archive_batches`, so a second, wider notion
of "retired" cannot be born by one of them widening its glob. The projection
reads that listing at most once per build, and only when an unresolved
binding actually appears.

Mutations run, each observed red before revert:
- classify EVERY unresolved binding as retired (the dangerous direction — it
  would hide real corruption behind a green chip): the case-(c) fixture goes
  red, `{'instance_retired': 2}` where `{'instance_retired': 1,
  'no_instance_match': 1}` was asserted.
- never consult the archive (pre-fix code): `{'no_instance_match': 2}`.
- any archive batch counts as a tombstone: the reconcile-only id appears.
- the two codes swapped: tallies stay 1/1, the drop sample convicts.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(snapshot): EG-2.1 — the build leader becomes visible; waits stop impersonating builds

Three `snapshot_build` lines inside the 2026-08-17 boot window read as three
concurrent builds and were not: one build, two riders logging their WAITS. Two
independent investigations spent their longest detours on that ambiguity (HY §1.2,
HC §0.3), and the most expensive build of that boot — the serve prewarm, ~21s —
had no line at all, because nothing on its path had one to emit. This is the
union of HY-0 and HC-0, which specified the same stage from the two ends of the
wire.

- `build_snapshot` gains `build_info`, one dict used in both directions: the
  caller pre-seeds `{"caller": …}` (the one fact the builder cannot derive), the
  builder fills `role` (led/rode/shared_next), `caller`, `generation`,
  `build_ms`. Pure out-param otherwise — return value and coalesce behaviour are
  byte-unchanged, and a caller that passes nothing gets today's function;
- the coalesce LEADER logs ONE `snapshot_build_core role=led caller=…
  generation=… build_ms=… offset=… sections_top=…` line per ACTUAL build, read
  off the parity envelope the build already computed (never measured twice — a
  second measurement of one span is a second authority on it). The build count of
  a boot is therefore the count of `role=led`, not the count of lines. Injected
  store builds are attributed but print nothing: a fixture is not a boot;
- the stream's wait line renames `elapsed_ms` → `waited_ms` and carries
  `build_ms`/`role`/`caller`/`generation` beside it, so a wait and the build under
  it are two numbers on one line instead of one number wearing both hats.
  `elapsed_ms` still ships with the SAME value for one release — a fielded
  launcher parses it. `sections_top` rides a wait line only when the build under
  it was ≥5s (HC-0); the leader's own receipt always carries it;
- `caller` is threaded: the serve hub's producer says `hub` (one producer, N
  subscribers — billing a subscriber would be a lie about who paid), the CLI
  stream command says `cli`, and the prewarm says `prewarm`, which is what puts
  it on the record for the first time;
- each of the three ATTACHMENT paths logs `stream_attach op=… purpose=…` at
  subscribe: the socket lane's `subscribe`, `runtime.office.subscribe`, and
  `harness stream`. That closes the third-rider census gap AND plan §8 item 5 —
  12 MB of serve-child log with zero office lines, which left "is the push lane
  even attached?" unanswerable from the log the operator actually has.

Tests (tests/agent_runtime/test_snapshot_build_logging.py, 14): both sources'
killing mutations, adopted. HY-0's pair — `role=led` records == 1 while callers
== 2 AND the test-owned builder counter == 1. HC-0's role matrix — one
`build_info` per caller, three roles produced by three code paths a test-owned
gate forces them down. One drift resolved against HEAD and named in the test:
HC-0 wrote the matrix with three callers (C == shared_next), but HEAD's
coalescer makes the first PLAIN waiter LEAD the next build (its own
`test_concurrent_storm_costs_at_most_two_builds` records this), so shared_next is
only reachable behind a SECOND plain waiter — four callers, and the C/D pair
asserted as a set, because which of them wins the lead is the condition's wakeup
order and no test owns that. Mutations run and reverted: hardcode role=led (3
red), a receipt per caller (3), everyone leads (3, on the invocation counter),
drop the prewarm's caller (1), drop the hub's caller (1), constant build_ms (4),
drop `elapsed_ms` (1), remove the office attach line (1).

No event type, producer contract hash, SNAPSHOT_CONTRACT_VERSION or committed
fixture moves: log text and an out-param are additive. The existing timing-log
test now reads the line as key=value pairs rather than a fixed field order —
a rigid full-match would make every later additive key a false failure here and
would teach the launcher-side parser to be equally brittle.

author: nekwo
message:
perf(serve): EG-3.2 — the provider prewarm follows the first build instead of fighting it

Two daemon threads raced from `ready`: the read-model build the launcher's canvas
is waiting on, and ~5-8s of provider warmup CPU (OpenAI SDK import ~1.7s, SSL
context / CA verification ~0.7s, and since BW-H3 the `model_tools` import plus
the discovery/check_fn storm ~1.2s+). Under the GIL the second is subtracted
from the first, and NOTHING the provider warmup produces is consumable before the
canvas is authoritative — its purpose is the first chat turn's latency, which is
after. Two independent investigations derived this same fix (HY-H2 = HC-H3);
adopted once.

- one daemon thread, sequential: `snapshot_prewarm()` then
  `_prewarm_provider_runtime()`, each step exception-isolated so a build that
  raised still leaves the providers warm (the property two threads had for free
  and a naive `then` would silently drop);
- the thread still starts BEFORE the `ready` emit, untouched: only the build that
  started first can be shared, so a warmup started after that frame loses the
  race to the launcher's first request and queues a redundant second build. The
  invariant the old comment block asserted — "the read-model build must not queue
  behind this one's ~3s SDK import" — is now provable rather than raced, because
  that import has not started yet;
- `_prewarm_provider_runtime` becomes an injectable `serve_loop` parameter with
  the same contract `snapshot_prewarm` has (HC-H3), wired at the real entry
  point. It was an unconditional `Thread.start()` inside the loop, which meant
  every unit test of the loop imported the OpenAI SDK to observe a ready frame.

The brief's one-line version of this fix — reorder the two `Thread.start()` calls
— stays REJECTED as a no-op, not as wrong-direction: starts issued microseconds
apart schedule nothing, and both measured boots reached `model_tools` ~5s in
regardless of order. Both sources refused it independently for the same mechanism.

Cost named rather than hidden: a chat turn sent inside the (now shorter) boot
window pays the cold SDK import inline, exactly as every turn did before the
prewarm existed — best effort by the prewarm's own contract, and the canvas is not
yet authoritative in that window. If receipts show first-turn warmup misses, the
refinement is "provider prewarm starts at first-request-enqueue OR
build-completion, whichever is first", not a revert.

Tests (tests/agent_runtime/test_harness_serve.py, 3 new + 2 tightened): the
gate-ordering witness — a snapshot-prewarm fake parked on a gate the TEST holds,
with the provider recorder asserted EMPTY at that instant (the BW-L5
never-completing-fake pattern; the mutant cannot un-append and cannot release the
gate); `ready` still on the wire before either prewarm completes, read off the
frames after the loop returns with the gate STILL held; a failed build still warms
the providers; and HC-H3's injectable-parameter contract at the entry point.
Ordering, counts and emptiness only — the seconds are read off EG-2.1's receipts
(plan #60), never asserted in a test. Mutations run and reverted: restore the two
parallel threads (2 red), join the prewarm thread before ready (1), drop the
per-step isolation (1), drop the entry-point wiring (1).

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(read-model): EG-6.3/RD-H6 item 1 — one resolver for read_model.enabled

`read_model.enabled` was answered in two places. `snapshot.write_snapshot`
gates the cache WRITE on it; `_cmd_snapshot` carried its own copy of the same
`getattr` ladder to compute the serve-side cache preference. Two copies of one
question, each free to resolve at its own scope — the exact misplacement class
that kept the neighbouring leaf dark for its whole life (`read_model.
delta_patches`: READ at the root, WRITTEN into a profile by the Launcher's own
seed template, `harness status` reporting `true` throughout because status
reads profile-aware, 822 KB shipped per field change where the lane's patch
frame is 486 bytes — measured live 2026-08-13).

What makes this seam worse than a duplicated constant: a disagreement between
the write gate and the serve preference does not surface as an error, it
surfaces as `frame_source: cache_miss_rebuilt` — the honest name for a COLD
cache. "Nobody warmed the cache" and "the flag is read at two scopes" render
identically to an operator, so the second is invisible until someone enables
the lane on a fresh root.

  * `read_model.read_model_enabled(config=None)` — THE resolver.
  * `read_model.prefer_cached_snapshot(config=None)` — the composite the serve
    entry points need (`enabled` AND `serve_snapshot_from_db`; the flags are
    only meaningful together). It resolves the scope ONCE and hands the config
    down, so it cannot become a second scope for the same key.
  * `_read_model_scope` — the scope decision, in one line in one place. Split
    out deliberately: the defect class is not "the ladder is spelled twice",
    it is "the same key resolved against two different files", and two copies
    of the load are two scopes waiting to drift. Measured: with the load
    duplicated in both public functions, the killing mutation below survived
    on the entry-point pair.
  * `_cmd_snapshot` calls the resolver instead of re-deriving.

RD-SPEC-vs-HEAD DRIFT, recorded rather than glossed. RD-H6 states
`snapshot.py:1758-1759` resolves profile-aware against `_cmd_snapshot`'s
root-only read. At HEAD both are ROOT: commit 2360f5b188 moved
`write_snapshot` from `load_agent_runtime_config()` to
`load_root_runtime_config()`, so the live divergence was already closed
incidentally and RD-H6's stated mutation ("revert to root-only") is a no-op
here. The consolidation still stands — the question was answered twice, which
is what makes a re-divergence a one-token edit — and the killing mutation is
run in the direction the spec claimed HEAD already had (see below).

Tests (5 new, `tests/agent_runtime/test_read_model_enabled_resolver.py`):

  * both entry points driven against a REAL config tree where the root and the
    active profile disagree, in BOTH directions (`HERMES_HOME` pointed at
    `<root>/profiles/seam` — the shape the CLI bootstrap installs). Probed
    field is the frame source, not a returned boolean, because the frame source
    is what an operator actually sees. `cache` is the load-bearing value: it
    requires the write gate to have populated the read model AND the serve
    preference to have consulted it, so it is the one source unreachable by
    half the seam acting alone. Second, independent witness on the write half:
    the read model is populated exactly when the root said so, read off the
    DATABASE rather than off the frame.
  * MEASURED MUTATION (`_read_model_scope` -> profile-aware): both fixtures go
    red in OPPOSITE directions — `root_true_profile_false` gets `built` where
    `cache` is demanded, `root_false_profile_true` gets `cache_miss_rebuilt`
    where `built` is demanded. No single scope other than the write gate's own
    satisfies the pair, and no constant satisfies either.
  * the composite's second conjunct has its own witness (`enabled` on,
    `serve_snapshot_from_db` off, must NOT prefer the cache) — a mutant that
    drops it passes every other test in the file.
  * an AST enumeration fence pins the set of places that read `enabled` off a
    `read_model` block. MEASURED MUTATION (re-grow the ladder in
    `_cmd_snapshot`): red, naming the new site.

The fence carries `agent_runtime/snapshot.py::write_snapshot` as a PENDING row,
not a sanctioned one: that inline ladder is the second copy this stage exists to
retire, and the swap was deferred because `snapshot.py` is held by the
concurrent EG-3.1 branch. Deleting the row and the two lines it names is the
follow-up; the fence is already live against any THIRD copy.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent-create): EG-6.3/RD-H6 item 2 — the CLI's roster fault takes the RPC lane's typed refusal

A roster fault answered the two create lanes differently.
`runtime.agent.create` passes no pre-resolved persona, so the service's own
strict read (`persona_roster`) wrapped the fault into a typed
`persona_roster_unavailable` refusal that names the RUNTIME as the subject and
the cure as `harness doctor`. `harness agent create` resolves its richer persona
object FIRST — `_persona_by_id` -> `ensure_persisted_personas`, the same call,
unwrapped, with an unwrapped config load above it — so an unreadable roster
printed a traceback out of the verb. One fault, two renderings, and the argv one
blamed nothing and named no cure.

  * `agent_create.roster_unavailable_outcome(cause)` — the fault as an
    `AgentCreateOutcome` refusal, for a lane that meets it BEFORE the service is
    entered (there is no outcome to carry it there). Returning the outcome, not
    a hand-rolled envelope, is what keeps the JSON-RPC code — and therefore the
    exit code via `_AGENT_CREATE_EXIT_CODES` — from being re-guessed at the call
    site.
  * `_cli_create_persona` — the CLI's resolution with the typed fault. Its
    `except Exception` mirrors `persona_roster`'s own net, for the same reason:
    the roster read reaches YAML, the filesystem and the persona store, and
    enumerating that surface would leave the remainder tracebacking. It is
    narrow in SCOPE instead — exactly the roster read. A bad id is NOT caught
    here; `persona_not_found` remains the service's answer for that.
  * the refusal falls through to the verb's ONE rendering arm, so it inherits
    the same exit code and the same root-observability envelope.

Tests (3 new, `tests/hermes_cli/test_agent_create_verb.py`). The corrupt-roster
fixture is a real unparseable persona FILE rather than a patched loader:
`AgentStore.list_all` catches only `NotFound`, so a non-JSON file is a genuine
roster-read fault, and it is the SAME fault on both lanes by construction,
reached through each lane's own resolver. A patched binding could be installed
on one lane and miss the other, which would make the parity test assert an
agreement it had arranged.

  * typed refusal, no traceback: MEASURED MUTATION (unwrap the roster read) —
    `json.JSONDecodeError` escapes the dispatch, so `code` is never bound and
    `data` never parses; the mutant satisfies no assertion at all.
  * SECOND MEASURED MUTATION (spend `persona_not_found`'s reason/message
    instead): still refuses, still exits 2, still writes nothing, still prints
    no traceback — every probe but the reason string and the two negative prose
    probes is satisfied. That is the collapse `PersonaRosterUnavailable` exists
    to prevent, and it is why "was it refused" is not the probe.
  * cross-lane parity: both lanes driven against the one fixture, `reason` AND
    the operator prose compared for EQUALITY, plus the code's exit-code mapping.
    A fix that shared only the reason would still hand two lanes two sentences
    for one fault.
  * MEASURED SURVIVOR, recorded rather than hidden: catching the fault and
    degrading to `persona=None` passes both tests above — on a DURABLE fault the
    service's strict read raises and the refusal is identical. The honest scope
    of that survival is one call, so it gets its own witness: a roster read that
    faults ONCE and then succeeds. Under the degrade the create PROCEEDS with no
    persona object and writes "Qa" into a durable roster row and placement where
    the configured name is "QA Agent" — a silent rename on a durable write,
    strictly worse than a refusal the operator can re-run. That test kills it
    (exit 0 vs 2, instance file present vs absent).

Second witness, byte-unchanged as required: the RPC lane's existing typed-refusal
test (`tests/agent_runtime/test_agent_create_service.py::
test_an_unreadable_roster_is_its_own_reason_not_persona_not_found`) and the whole
`test_serve_rpc_agent_create.py` suite are untouched — 50 passed across the three
create-lane files.

author: nekwo
message:
test(agent-create): EG-6.3/RD-H6 item 3 — the roster-check bypass gets its contract fence

`agent_create._persona_is_unknown` returns False for ANY non-None persona. That
is deliberate and documented (D-U1): the caller's resolver is a strict SUPERSET
of `resolve_persona` — it also handles `profile:` synthesis and persona-INSTANCE
id spellings — so "the caller found one" settles the question without a
narrower lookup contradicting it. It is also an unconditional bypass of the only
roster check that runs before a durable write, safe today only because every
caller resolves through the strict path, with nothing fencing the seam.

WHY THE FENCE IS A TEST AND NOT RUNTIME CODE, per RD-H6. Re-verifying the passed
object inside the resolver would re-introduce exactly the contradiction the
parameter exists to avoid — `profile:<token>` ids legitimately own no persona
row, and D-U1's carve-out has its own witness. The risk is "a NEW caller arrives
with a persona from somewhere else", i.e. a change to the CALLER SET, so a test
over the caller set is the instrument that matches it and it costs nothing at
runtime.

`tests/agent_runtime/test_persona_roster_bypass_contract.py` — 11 tests, two
independent halves:

  * the bypass BEHAVIOUR, asserted positively against an EMPTY roster (so
    `persona_not_found` is the answer for every id and the synthesised object
    still walks through — a test that seeded the persona would pass whether the
    bypass existed or not), through `_persona_is_unknown` AND through
    `require_known_persona`'s envelope, which is what makes the bypass reach a
    durable write rather than stopping at a private helper. Plus an AST pin that
    the short-circuit is the FIRST statement and the roster read is below it: a
    mutant that reordered them passes every value probe while turning the D-U1
    carve-out into a refusal for the launcher's template browser.
  * the CALLER SET, by AST enumeration over `agent_runtime/` and `hermes_cli/`,
    with each caller's RESOLVER resolved through its LOCAL BINDING rather than
    read as a variable name. Pinning `persona` (the name) would be satisfied by
    any mutant that kept the spelling and changed the right-hand side, which is
    the defect shape. Seven sites: three `param:` forwards inside agent_create,
    one `absent` (the RPC lane passes no persona, so the strict read happens
    inside the resolver), `_cli_create_persona(persona_id)`, and
    `_persona_by_id(cfg, persona_id)` twice.

MEASURED MUTATION (RD-H6's, as written): add a caller passing a synthesised
persona — `_runtime_agent_create` builds an `AgentPersona` from the request
params. The enumeration reds and names the synthesis verbatim.

SECOND MEASURED MUTATION, because the first is defeatable by editing the table:
keep the synthesised caller AND add its row to the declared set. The per-site
`test_each_declared_resolver_is_a_strict_one` leg reds (the resolver is not on
the strict allowlist), and `test_the_forwards_terminate_at_a_real_caller` reds
too (the `absent` row is gone). So the table is not self-certifying: widening it
requires a separate, visible edit to STRICT_RESOLVERS.

The third leg exists because the `param:`/`absent` exemptions could otherwise
swallow the whole table and pass vacuously — it asserts the table always holds at
least one `absent`, at least one strict resolver, and no stale allowlist entry.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(office-push): EG-4.5/WV-H4 — runtime.office.resolve_conflict, and the consent that stays off the wire

The last office write verb with no method on the wire. Seven methods were
registered; this is the eighth, and it is the unfinished MAIN PATH rather
than a fallback deletion (Plan EG §4.5 / RD Correction 4): `harness office
resolve-conflict` stays the operator's lane and keeps its flags, and this
method wraps the same `OfficeStore.resolve_conflict` the CLI verb calls.
Same conventions as the archive and folder legs beside it — `workspace_id`
validated first with the shared reason string, unknown workspace refused
BEFORE the store, store exceptions translated rather than re-implemented,
`RPC_CONTRACT_VERSION` unmoved (the set grows, the integer does not).

Four shape decisions worth naming:

* NO `allow_class_key`, and the asymmetry is the contract, not an omission.
  `take=remote` writes a peer's actor with `_write_actor`, past
  `upsert_actor` and every guard its callers hold, so its class-key fence
  lives inside the store where a second caller inherits it. This method is
  that second caller and arrives fenced by construction. The CLI flag is an
  operator who read the refusal and typed the override; the same value in a
  JSON frame is a constant in a client build, set once by whoever was
  debugging the day resolves started failing and thereafter sent by every
  install with no human in any loop. So the param does not exist, is not
  forwarded, and a test pins that sending it anyway changes nothing. The
  sanctioned arms are untouched: the CLI flag, and `office actor-restore`.

* the refusal message is BUILT here, not passed through. The store's
  sentence ends by offering `--allow-class-key`, which is advice this
  caller cannot follow — the upsert's arm already ruled that advice a
  caller cannot follow is worse than none — so the wire message names the
  one exit this lane really has, `take: "local"`. The machine-readable
  evidence rides `data` with the upsert's own collision keys, so one client
  branch covers `class_key_collision` whichever verb hit it.

* a repeat resolve is `4001 conflict_not_found`, which is the one place
  this verb deliberately disagrees with `runtime.office.remove`. A repeat
  archive describes the state the store is already in, so `ok` costs
  nothing. A repeat resolve has no sidecar left to read and the only way to
  answer `ok` would be to invent a remote copy. `SyncConflict` means the
  OPPOSITE thing here than on the upsert (there a sidecar EXISTING blocks
  the write, a 4090), and copying that arm would send the client for an
  operator to resolve a conflict already resolved. The test pins it by
  BYTES: a second adoption would bump the revision to 9.

* the tombstone is a SUCCESS with `revision` ABSENT. The edit-vs-remove arm
  returns no actor, and the missing key is what tells the client to stop
  guarding a row that no longer exists — filling it with 0 or null would
  pass a shape check and then have the launcher present `expect_revision:
  0` on its next write.

EG-1.5's `ArchiveUnreadable` gets an arm even though no path inside
`resolve_conflict` raises it today: it is an `AgentRuntimeError` and not a
`ValueError`, so without one the condition reaches the client as
`handle_request`'s catch-all `-32000 handler_failed` — a corrupt file on
the server reported as "the handler crashed". The test says out loud that
it injects at the store boundary, and the mutation shows the -32000.

19 tests. The chokepoint pin is the one that is not about shapes: it
poisons every sibling `OfficeStore` writer and guards `_write_actor` with
the assertion that an actor file may only be written inside
`resolve_conflict`'s own dynamic extent, so a handler that grew its own
writer is unfenced-by-construction and reds here. Refusal parity across the
two lanes runs BOTH on one seeded conflict — only possible because neither
refusal writes — and pins the code MAPPING rather than pretending the
stage-42 exit taxonomy and JSON-RPC's `data.reason` are one string.

What this does NOT do: touch coverage, the producer, or any fixture.
`office.actor.conflict_resolved` stays uncovered on purpose — the adoption
writes past the `_emit_actor_patch` chokepoint, so no patch carries the
adopted row and a client that folded the batch would render stale state.
Pinned with the tombstone arm as the positive control.

Dead code against every launcher until WV-L6 calls it.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(correlation): EG-2.3 / CI-0+1+2 — the gesture token, threaded and logged

The read side of this pipe was already shipped. `stream._delta_entity` has
lifted `payload["correlation_id"]` onto `entity.correlation_id` since it was
written, patch rows are a verbatim payload spread, and the contract names
the slot — so ~60% of Plan D was delivered and nothing populated it on any
gesture path. This lands the missing 40%: the write boundary accepts a
token, the chokepoints attach it to the payloads they already emit, and the
serve child says so out loud.

Why it is worth a commit at all. Causality across the pipeline was inferred
from timestamps, and on 2026-08-16 that inference produced a confidently
WRONG diagnosis: anchoring on the launcher's flush receipt — which lags the
real RPC by 250-650 ms — read 280-368 ms deletes as "3.8 s", and a wrong
prioritisation followed from it. The cost of no correlation id is not slow
diagnosis; it is fluent, confident, wrong diagnosis.

Additive, and that is asserted rather than intended:

* `correlation_id` is an optional payload key on exactly the `created`
  pattern — absent-when-unset, so every existing payload stays byte for
  byte what it was. Contract-hash neutrality holds by construction (the
  hash derives from the registry rows alone, and required-field validation
  checks PRESENCE only), so no fixture moves and there is nothing to mirror
  cross-stack. The 785 stream/fixture/contract tests confirm it.
* it rides INSIDE `build_state_patch`'s 4 KB shrink loop, so a payload
  already within the token's own width of the cap marks one more value and
  still lands legal, instead of overflowing at `EventLog.append`.
* `refresh` degrades KEEP the id. "Which gesture forced a full core" is the
  most valuable thing to know about a demote, so it is the one key a
  degrade must not drop.

Boundaries, and why the two disagree on purpose. `serve_rpc` REFUSES a
present-but-illegal token (`-32602`, `data.reason: correlation_id_invalid`)
— it has a reply channel, so a client sending prose where a generated token
belongs gets told, and the store is left untouched. `state_patches`
`normalize_correlation_id` DROPS one silently — it is the payload-side
fence every in-process producer passes, and `agent_create`'s own parser
admits 200 characters, looser than the cap. Nothing is sanitized either
way: a repaired id would print a value neither side used, which is worse
than no id.

`office_write` is the new serve-child line, shaped like
`stream.log_stream_attach`'s so an operator greps the two together instead
of parsing two formats. It prints `corr=-` for a gestureless write —
absence is a fact, and an omitted key is indistinguishable from an old
build. It is minted AFTER the store returns, so it means "this write
landed", never "a write was attempted"; a refused write leaves no line and
therefore cannot put a token into the join for a write that lost.

CI-4's free half is taken: `runtime.agent.create` already reserved the
param from birth and already echoed it, so the only hop it lacked was the
office one, and that is now a kwarg on a call the handler already makes. A
create's office half joins the same token as an ordinary drag. The 38 argv
capability lanes stay DEFERRED; the partial-coverage window narrows to the
roster half rather than closing.

Mutations run, observed, reverted:

* drop the mint (the boundary always answers None) -> 8 red, the
  `office_write` line reads `corr=-` and the CI-3 join loses its middle hop
* thread but never log (remove `log_office_write`) -> the two-log join
  fails with 2 of 3 hops, exactly as Plan D predicts
* stamp unconditionally -> the neutrality golden and both absent-when-unset
  arms red
* half-thread the pair (patch loses the kwarg, domain event keeps it) -> the
  paired-halves test reds while the domain arm stays green, which is the
  state a single-arm test would have shipped

20 new tests; 319 green across the office/state-patch/serve-rpc/agent-create
suites, 785 green across stream/fixture/contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(providers): EG-6.1 — absence stops meaning two things on the provider surface

S1 taught this file that a failed usage fetch must say WHAT failed. Its three
siblings on the same surface never learned it, and one of them was strictly
worse than the defect S1 fixed. All three close here (RD-H5, minus the
fall-through EG-0.3 already reaped).

1. `block_errors` on the provider-visibility payload. The four v2 blocks stay
   failure-isolated — that isolation protects the credential payload the
   launcher's model switcher depends on — but each isolator was a bare
   `except Exception: pass`, so an absent block meant EITHER "this hermes is too
   old to emit it" OR "this hermes tried and the builder threw". `catalog` made
   that worst: it exists precisely to separate "never configured" from
   "configured and dead", so a silent drop fell the client back into the exact
   indistinguishable rendering it was added to end. One chokepoint
   (`_record_visibility_block`) now records `block_errors[block] = <Class>` —
   class name only, never `str(exc)`, since a status probe's message can carry a
   resolved key or URL. Written ONLY when something threw, so all three wire
   states stay distinct.

2. Detector-raised lanes are EMITTED with their class. `_usage_lane_detected`
   ended in `except Exception: return False`, and its own docstring's rule is
   that undetected lanes are OMITTED — so a detector fault made the row VANISH
   from the Limits panel. Worse than S1: S1 at least left a row to carry a
   reason. Detection now has three outcomes (True / False / RAISE);
   `_detect_usage_candidates` isolates per provider and the lane is emitted
   unavailable, in its natural `_USAGE_LANE_PROVIDERS` slot, reading
   `usage detection failed (<Class>)`. That is `_usage_failure_reason` with one
   phase word — the SAME grammar, not a second reason-builder to forget the
   class-name-only rule in.

   The two OR-of-two-sources feeders had their own terminal
   `except Exception: return False`, which would have made the above vacuous for
   half the providers (`_usage_lane_detected` can only raise if its feeders do).
   They now hold the primary error and re-raise it only when no source affirms:
   a "yes" from the second source is still the truth; a fault that leaves the
   question unanswered is not "not signed in".

3. The degraded envelope never prints the false claim.
   "No account-usage lanes (no signed-in providers detected)" is a POSITIVE
   assertion about the operator's auth state, and it printed on any empty lane
   list — including when detection or fetch had collapsed. Each fail-open seam
   now stamps `degraded[stage] = <Class>` (the same `{unit: ExceptionClass}`
   idiom as `block_errors`), and the claim prints ONLY when detection actually
   ran and found none; a lane-suppressing degrade states
   `usage lanes unavailable (<Class>)` instead. `active_provider` is stamped too
   but is deliberately NOT lane-suppressing — a failed resolve eats no lanes, so
   the claim stays legitimate there, and the null instead names its cause rather
   than rendering "(none)", which was its own small claim about configuration.
   `_cmd_usage`'s and `_emit_usage_json`'s last-resort empty envelopes carry
   `build` / `serialize` stamps for the same reason: they report zero lanes at
   the exact moment they know something is broken.

Payload additions, all additive and feature-detected (old clients ignore them;
the S1 commit's presence-detection argument covers old launchers):
  provider_visibility/v2 : block_errors: {block: "<ExceptionClass>"}   — absent when healthy
  account_usage/v1       : degraded:     {stage: "<ExceptionClass>"}   — absent when healthy
                           stages: active_provider | detect | fetch | build | serialize
  account_usage/v1 lane  : unavailable_reason: "usage detection failed (<Class>)"
                           (existing lane shape, new phase word)

Tests: +21 (usage 33, visibility 16). Every pre-existing S1 / PL-1 / v2 pin is
byte-unchanged. 13 killing mutations run and all 13 red — including the one that
matters most: the first draft of the detector tests stubbed
`harness._usage_lane_detected`, and restoring its blanket swallow SURVIVED all of
them. The RD-L2 lesson, reproduced live. `test_a_raising_REAL_detector_...`
injects at the probe BELOW the seam instead — the same discipline that made the
S1 tests refuse to stub `_fetch_usage_lane` — and kills it.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(snapshot): EG-3.1 — the persisted core, validated by a stat fingerprint instead of reconstructed

A serve child's first read-model core costs ~20s on EVERY boot — the build is
per-process work, so a fully warm machine paid 24.2s of it on 2026-08-17. Doc 14's
own numbers say the cost is not bandwidth: serializing the core is ~5ms. The 20s
IS validation, done by reconstruction. So validation now costs what validation
costs: a stat set over every build input, compared against a sidecar written
beside the core the last build produced.

- new `agent_runtime/core_cache.py`. Fingerprint = sorted (path, mtime_ns, size)
  over SEVEN input classes, each resolved through the authority the BUILD reads
  through so there is no second list free to drift: the store-root subtree walked
  RECURSIVELY (`paths.store_root`) — added files flip the key, and the office
  tree, which no name list ever covered, is in it for the first time; the
  `running_work` stores (`running_work_store_paths`, the one path authority, both
  of which mutate with NO event); the chat SessionDB (`chat_session_db_path` — the
  db the CHAT LANE writes, not whichever one ambient resolution hands the process,
  which was defect D1) plus `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`, because a WAL commit that has
  not checkpointed leaves the main file's mtime alone; the profile inputs
  `agents_readiness` reads (`_get_profiles_root` + per-profile
  `profile.yaml`/`config.yaml` + the sticky `active_profile`); BOTH config
  authorities (`get_config_path` and `harness_root_config_path` — genuinely
  different files under the CLI profile redirect); the skill registries
  (`get_all_skills_dirs` + the harness-skill source root); and the event-rotation
  manifest + resolved live slice. Soundness ground: every durable write goes
  through `atomic_json_write`, and temp+rename ALWAYS moves mtime;
- `None` means "I could not fingerprint these" and every caller reads it as NEVER
  CACHE — not as "nothing changed" (#45). An unresolvable authority, an
  unmeasurable build stamp, or a walk past its bound all refuse;
- write-back after EVERY successful default-store build: the core's wire form plus
  `{fingerprint, build_stamp, contract_versions, event_offset, core_sha256,
  runtime_root}`, both atomic. `event_offset` is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY and is never an
  input to the match — BW-H1's offset key stays refused for cause (the events
  section is 3ms of a 5,485ms build; two shipped incidents came from non-evented
  writers; a tail replay would be a second validity authority beside the key). The
  sidecar binds to the core BYTES, so a half-replaced pair or a rollback that left
  an old `core.json` beside a new sidecar is refused rather than served;
- the key is stat'd PRE-build and threaded into the write-back. Only one direction
  is safe: a key taken after the build absorbs writes that landed while it ran, and
  the next process would serve a core missing a write as AUTHORITATIVE. Named
  consequence, not hidden: a cold store converges in two builds, because the build
  is not a pure reader (`ensure_for_personas` materializes rows; the SessionDB is
  created by the first process to open it);
- `build_snapshot` consults the cache before the coalescer while this process has
  not completed a build of its own, and closes the lane when it has. That is the
  honest generalization of "first build of a process": gating on the first
  CONSULTATION would have served the prewarm from the cache and then made the
  hydrate — the caller the launcher waits on — pay the full build anyway. A cache
  hit gets the fourth role, `BUILD_ROLE_CACHE`, and its OWN receipt
  (`snapshot_core_cache core_source=cache …`); it deliberately emits no
  `snapshot_build_core role=led`, because there was no build and EG-2.1 just made
  the boot's build count the count of `led` lines;
- MISMATCH: `stream_frames` paints the persisted core immediately, LABELED stale,
  and the authoritative hydrate replaces it when the build lands. The label reuses
  `parity.freshness.state = "stale"` — the field `MissionSnapshotEnvelope` already
  parses and `health()` already maps to `MissionSnapshotHealth.stale` — so the
  honesty half needs no launcher change and a stale frame can never read `live`. A
  MATCHING core is never painted stale: the pessimistic lie trains the operator to
  ignore the banner;
- the shadow-validation window (UP-4's pattern, applied to this cache): a cache-hit
  boot ALSO runs the full build on a daemon thread and compares field-for-field.
  Divergence is a warning NAMING the differing section, and the rebuilt core is
  ADOPTED — written back, the lane closed, the painter told. Once per process, and

feat(office): EG-6.6 — the class-key fence becomes ONE fence, at the store

Four callers of `office_class_key_guard` around one store became one fence
inside it. `OfficeStore.upsert_actor` now refuses the class-keyed write itself
(`_guard_class_keyed_write`, first inside the lock), and the four writers —
`runtime.office.upsert`, `agent_create`'s placement leg, `harness office
actor-upsert`, `workspace_template._copy_office` — keep only a transport-shaped
translation of the store's typed refusal. Nothing was wrong with any of the four
copies; what was wrong is that the store's contract said nothing about the
fence, so the rekey script had to WARN in prose that a new writer reaching
`upsert_actor` was unguarded by default. Prose does not fail a build.

The sanctioned overrides survive as EXPLICIT STORE PARAMETERS rather than as a
caller-side fence omission: `upsert_actor(allow_class_key=...)` beside
`resolve_conflict(allow_class_key=...)`. The difference is that an override is
now a value someone passed on the record, never a guard someone forgot to call —
the two being indistinguishable from the store's side is how a fence at four
call sites becomes a fence at three. The CLI's `--allow-class-key` refuses first
and re-issues with consent, so the recorded `office_actor_class_key_forced`
warning names the collision the store actually found. The wire lane still has no

disposition: un-archiving IS the deliberate resurrection the refusal points at.

Also closes the fence's own blind spot. `class_key_collision`'s
duplicate-placement half asked `list_actors`, which drops files that will not

subclass of `ArchiveUnreadable` so every "a file this write depends on will not

author: nekwo
message:
feat(stream-lane): EG-4.1/TC-1 — the hub lane made provably launcher-grade, and still inert

The push lane has existed since the socket slice and been dialled by NOBODY:
no `{"op":"subscribe"}` is sent from anywhere in the launcher's Dart tree, so
every claim about it has been a claim about code nothing exercises. Plan
SINGLE_TRANSPORT_COLLAPSE §V2 lists what has to be TRUE before a client may be
pointed at it; this is that list turned into tests, plus the one thing on it
that did not exist yet.

C-1 was FALSE and is now built. Nothing advertised the op lane, so a client
could only learn whether this runtime carries the push lane by sending a
subscribe and reading the answer's tea leaves — and that is not a detector:
`unsupported_lane`, `draining` and `already_subscribed` are all answers a LIVE
lane gives, so "too old to have the lane" and "refused this particular
subscribe" are the same observation. The ops now advertise themselves under
`"ops"`, on the three frames `"rpc"` already rides (`ready`, `hello_ok`, the
re-askable `version`), following the eighth RPC method's discipline verbatim
rather than minting a second scheme: a SET plus an integer, the set grows
because a client only ever sends what it FOUND, and no contract integer moves.
The gate EG-4.2 reads is `subscribe_lanes` containing `stream` — not the op
name; `"subscribe" in ops` says the verb is dispatched, the lane list says THIS
lane is carried.

Three shape decisions worth naming:

* PER TRANSPORT, because the answer genuinely differs. `shutdown` is the stdio
  owner's verb and is refused on the socket (`op_not_available_on_socket`), so
  the socket's set omits it and the test that asserts the omission exercises
  the refusal in the same breath — an omission nobody can justify is
  indistinguishable from an oversight. The block names the `transport` it
  describes so a cached copy cannot be mis-applied to the other lane.

* `hello` is deliberately in NEITHER set. It is the socket's first line,
  consumed by `serve_socket` before this dispatcher exists; a hello that
  reaches the dispatcher is a second one and is answered `unexpected_hello`.
  Its contract is already advertised as `hello_contract` on `server_hello`.

* the ops ride BESIDE `serve_rpc.manifest()`, never inside it. `subscribe` is
  not a JSON-RPC method and the `unknown_method` refusal enumerates `methods`;
  merging the two would hand every client that folds `rpc.methods` as the
  method set a list with a non-method in it. A test pins that `rpc` still has
  exactly `{contract, methods}`, so the six hardcoded manifest enumerations
  stay byte-unchanged and this stage touches no contract-versioned surface.

Byte parity is TRUE at the frame, and the caveat is in the commit rather than
discovered later. Both lanes run CONCURRENTLY over one seeded root and one
scripted append — the only arrangement in which they can be compared at all,
since a hydrate's watermark is the log's tail at build time and a sequential
comparison would compare two different tails and could only be normalized into
agreement. Hydrate and the demoted full-core batch come out byte-identical
(6379 B and 6456 B, both sides). What is NOT identical is the LINE: `harness
stream` writes `separators=(",",":")` and `_FrameWriter.emit` writes json's
defaults, so the same frame is different whitespace. Recorded as its own test
rather than hidden inside the comparison helper, and deliberately not fixed —
changing either encoder would move bytes on a lane in the field for no
consumer's benefit, and the contract already tells a consumer to parse per line
and branch on `type`.

NO fixture is minted. The comparison needs volatile stamps removed and it
imports the stream goldens' own normalizer rather than growing a second one,
because the failure mode of a second normalizer is that it normalizes away a
real divergence. `hydrate.json` is READ as the third leg — the shape witness —
and the superset is NAMED (`delta_patches`, `fold_entities`, the two v2 keys a
goldens-era `hydrate_frame()` had no reason to carry), so a third extra key
reds instead of riding in behind them. `MANIFEST.sha256` does not move, so §8's
cross-stack copy discipline is not engaged.

C-2 was TRUE and is now tested. Both lanes funnel into ONE writer per
connection, each holding one lock, so a fat core delays a small reply and can
never splice it: asserted at the wire, with six method calls fired while the
producer is pushing full cores, all replies arriving in the order they were
asked and every line on the pipe parsing as a whole frame (the parsed count is
compared against the raw line count, so a spliced frame shows up as two
unparseable halves). The question EG-4.2 actually needs answered is the blast
radius, and it is bounded: a stream subscriber dropped for backpressure does
NOT take the method lane on the same connection with it, and the drop's numbers
stay exact. No witness here is an elapsed-ms — head-of-line blocking is a
latency question and a latency bound in this suite would be a claim about the
machine running it.

Re-subscribe recovery is hydrate-FIRST with a watermark that did not go
backwards, and the office lane's restart-free join (O-H5) is shown not to
suppress it — one edit away from the stream lane's join, and if it ever leaked
there a subscriber would attach mid-generation and fold deltas onto nothing.

The advertisement is pinned in BOTH directions. Every advertised op is matched
against the typed frame it owns (an op the manifest names and the dispatcher
does not handle falls through to the argv lane as `invalid_request`, which from
the client's side is indistinguishable from a malformed request of its own),
and every `op == "…"` branch in serve.py must be advertised somewhere — that
half is a source-level gate because an unadvertised op is invisible to exactly
the test that would otherwise catch it.

Debt found and NOT fixed, recorded in the plan: `StreamHub.stop()` cannot
interrupt a generator parked inside `next()`, and the real producer parks up to
a heartbeat between frames — so a test attaching the REAL producer through
`serve_loop` can leave a thread alive past the isolation fixture's teardown,
whereupon its next read resolves against the operator's live store (observed:
`producer_error:JSONDecodeError` from reading a foreign event log mid-line).
These tests drain their producers and ASSERT the drain; nothing yet fences the
next author.

14 tests. Server-only and additive: no default moves, no launcher change, and
the argv stream is still the only lane anything dials. Dead advertisement until
EG-4.2 gates on it.

author: nekwo
message:
test(stream-lane): EG-4.1 — the two mutations the first cut survived, and the pins that kill them

Both survivals are real limits of what a frame comparison can see, so both are
recorded in the plan rather than quietly patched over.

`delta_debounce_seconds` 0.2 → 0 on the hub's `stream_frames` call left byte
parity GREEN. A scripted burst is coalescing-blind in the direction that
matters: whether two appends land in one batch depends on whether both were
already in the log when the producer polled, and a zero settle window usually
satisfies that anyway. Widening the burst does not fix it either — it makes the
outcome depend on where a 250 ms poll happens to fall, which is a coin flip
wearing an assertion. So the cadence is pinned where it IS decidable: at the one
function both lanes call, intercepted once, with the argv side's numbers read
off the REAL parser (`build_parser` → `_cmd_stream`) and the hub's read off
`stream_frames`' own signature — because the hub omits the cadence arguments, so
its effective cadence is the signature's defaults and a restated copy of them
would agree with itself forever after the real default moved. `resync` and
`max_frames` are deliberately excluded: both are argv-only operator flags and
the hub has no way to be asked for either. The scripted sequence gains its
second event anyway, 50 ms behind the first, so the compared batch is a
coalesced two rather than a lone one — the frame count and `coalesced_count` are
evidence even where the cadence is not.

`restart_producer=False` leaked from O-H5 onto the stream lane's own join left
the single-client rejoin GREEN, and the reason is structural: the last
subscriber leaving empties the room, which stops the producer, and the hub's
FLOOR rule then starts one regardless — so a rejoin gets its hydrate whether or
not it asked for a restart. The flag only becomes observable when somebody ELSE
holds the generation alive. That case is now its own test: two real socket
clients on the real producer, B never leaves, A leaves and comes back, and A's
first state-bearing frame must still be a complete baseline. Under the mutation
it reads `delta`. The peer's redundant full core is asserted too — a lane that
spared B would be a lane that skipped A's hydrate.

One scripted event after every join is what keeps both halves bounded: it
guarantees state-bearing traffic promptly, so "the first one is a hydrate" is a
decision between two available answers instead of a wait, and the reader skips
heartbeats because the contract says they are liveness only — a baseline
assertion a heartbeat could satisfy, or displace, would be measuring the 5 s
cadence rather than the join.

16 tests. Nothing in the production diff moves; every mutation above was applied,
observed, and reverted.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(cli): ArchiveUnreadable joins the error taxonomy — exit 7, not a crash

EG-1.5 typed the "a file this write depends on will not decode" condition and
EG-6.6 subclassed it, and the RPC write verbs have translated both since:
`-32600` with `data.reason` taken from `exc.code`. The CLI never learned it.
`_error_code_for_exception` had no row, so `harness office actor-remove` over an
undecodable archived copy fell through the `AgentRuntimeError` catch-all to
`internal_error` at exit 1 — the same store, the same file on the same disk,
reported as a harness crash on one lane and as a corrupt server file on the
other. That is precisely the names-the-wrong-party failure EG-1.5 fixed on the
wire and left standing here.

**Exit family: 7 (runtime/infra), not 1 (data integrity).** Read against the
taxonomy's own comments:

* the 1-family shares its number with `internal_error`. Spending it would name
  the fault correctly in `error.code` and then report the exact wrong story in
  the exit status — the honest half of the fix without the half a script reads;
* the condition is transient and retryable in the way this family already means:
  an AV hold releases, an operator repairs one file, and the identical call
  succeeds unchanged. That is the same reasoning the wire records for spending
  the "cannot serve this right now" band rather than a 4090 refusal, and the same
  reasoning `cancel_unavailable` sits at 7 on.

`retryable: true` rides along for the same reason the family is 7 — a 7 beside
`retryable: false` would have one envelope disagreeing with itself — and both
codes get a hint that names the FILE, because the taxonomy default ("retry after
correcting the request") is the one cure that cannot help: nothing about the
request is wrong.

The row returns `exc.code`, never a class constant: `ActorsUnreadable`
subclasses `ArchiveUnreadable` so it inherits the family and the cure SHAPE
while naming a DIFFERENT file, and a fixed string would tell an operator holding
an undecodable ACTOR file to go and repair the archive copy. Same rule the three
RPC arms already record. Two codes, one family: the family is the operator's next
move, the code is which file to repair.

EG-6.6's verb-local `except ActorsUnreadable` in `actor-upsert` is unchanged and
keeps passing `code=`/`message=` explicitly — it composes with the row rather
than being replaced by it, and its comment no longer claims to be what saves the
condition from `internal_error`. The row is what covers every office write verb
that has no arm of its own, `actor-remove` first among them.

Parity test on one staged archive, shaped after the class-key refusal's
(`test_serve_rpc_office_resolve.py`): both lanes read from the same undecodable
copy, the code pair pinned AS a pair so a rename on either side reds rather than
splitting the two stories. Killing mutation: drop the row and the CLI half
returns `internal_error` at exit 1 while the RPC half stays green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(serve): fence the leaking stream producer threads — source seam + tripwire

TC-1 recorded this as "Debt found, not fixed (owner: none yet)". `StreamHub.stop()`
cannot interrupt a generator parked inside `next()`, and the real producer —
`_stream_source` over `stream_frames` — polls its event tail every 250ms while
YIELDING only on a frame, so a quiet lane surfaces once per 5s heartbeat. A
`serve-stream-producer-N` daemon thread could therefore outlive the pytest test
that started it; `isolate_agent_runtime_root` then unwound the root pin and the
producer's next EventLog read resolved against the OPERATOR's live store.
Observed live as a `producer_error:JSONDecodeError` — the producer reading a
foreign event log mid-line. Same leak class as EG-0.1, by a route its tripwire
cannot see: that one watches the PINS, this one walks out on a THREAD.

**(a) the source seam.** `_stream_source` now takes the hub's per-generation stop
event (the hub probes for it by signature) and binds it to `request_control`'s
cancellation scope — the seam that module exists for: "the read-only `harness
stream` handler is infinite and must release its worker when its consumer
disconnects", which is this situation one caller over. Every
`request_cancelled()` probe in the tail loop (its bounded sleep slices at 100ms,
and the snapshot-build wait beside it) becomes a probe of this generation's
liveness, and the generator returns cooperatively at its own next safe point.

Not what the debt note suggested, and the difference is measured rather than
argued. Checking the stop event around the `yield` — the obvious reading, and the
shape `live_hub` mirrors — buys NOTHING: `StreamHub._produce` already re-tests
`_should_stop` the instant `next()` returns, so the wrapper would be a second
copy of a check already made. On the real producer at production cadences both
spellings left the thread alive 3.08s past `hub.stop(join_timeout=2.0)` —
identical to no fix. With the seam bound, `hub.stop()` returns with zero
producers alive. A fence that changes nothing while looking staffed is worse than
an absent one, so the no-op spelling is documented at the site as the thing NOT
to reach for.

**(b) the general fence.** An autouse tripwire in `tests/agent_runtime/conftest.py`
fails loudly when a `serve-stream-producer-*` thread survives a test body, worded
to name this incident and to hand the next author the three fixes in order. It
declares `isolate_agent_runtime_root`, so it is finalized BEFORE the root is
unpinned — which is what makes its bounded 2s grace safe rather than a weakening:
the wait is spent inside the still-pinned sandbox, so a producer that exits
within it never had an unpinned moment to read in. Only threads that appeared
during the test are reported, so one leak cannot redden every test after it.
With (a) landed it should never fire.

`test_serve_stream_hub.py::_staggered_source`'s docstring no longer claims the
real `_stream_source` is uninterruptible; it now says why deliberately deaf
generators are still the right fixture for the hub's own join contract.

Killing mutations, all four run: revert (a) → the behaviour test's 2s deadline
(deliberately under the 5s heartbeat) expires, and a body that does not drain
reddens (b) with the named thread; drop `_stream_source`'s parameter → the source
pin reds, because the hub falls back to a no-argument call in silence; stop (b)
probing → the staffing test reds.

author: nekwo
message:
test(hygiene): ML-4 — the no-undo gate covers the whole test tree

The structural no-`undo()` gate shipped scoped to `tests/agent_runtime` with a
written reason: other packages "have no runtime-root pin to unwind", and
widening without reading each site "would be a claim this file has not
checked". This stage does the reading. The second half held. The first half was
wrong, and reading is how that surfaced.

The root `tests/conftest.py` installs, autouse and through the SAME shared
per-test MonkeyPatch instance, for every test in the tree:
`_hermetic_environment` (HERMES_HOME redirected to a per-test tempdir, every
credential-shaped env var delenv'd), `_kanban_write_guard` (fail-closed against
writes resolving under the real ~/.hermes), `_live_system_guard` (blocks real
os.kill / systemctl / gateway-pid scans), plus the audio, webbrowser and
macOS-keychain neutralizers. So a mid-test `undo()` ANYWHERE under `tests/`
re-exposes the operator's real root and real credentials for the remainder of
that test — the EG-0.1 damage class, with a wider blast radius than the one the
gate was built for. The gate is scoped to the pin, and the pin is tree-wide.

The five sites outside the old scope, read and converted first:

* tests/cron/test_cron_profile_isolation.py — undid so the restoring
  `cron.jobs` reload ran with the env down. Context inside the `try`, reload
  left in the `finally` so it still runs on the assertion-failure path.
* tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py — undid to drop a sweep stub, then
  re-`setenv`'d HERMES_HOME on the very next line because the undo had taken
  that pin down too. Context around the stub; the repair line is deleted.
* tests/plugins/memory/test_holographic_store.py — undid so a sibling write
  reached the real `_rebuild_bank`. Context around the throwing stub.
* tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_sidecar_paths.py — undid in a `finally`
  ahead of restoring reloads. Context inside the `try`, reloads in the
  `finally`.
* tests/tools/test_lazy_deps_venv_barrier.py — a DELIBERATE drop, to probe the
  real `_venv_pip_install` past an autouse stub of it. Converted at the fixture,
  not in the body: the stub honours `@pytest.mark.real_venv_pip` (house idiom,
  cf. real_concurrent_gate / real_agent_prewarm), so the probe is never inside

author: nekwo
message:
feat(cache): ML-10 — the fingerprint core's refusals and non-convergence become receipts

Two ways this cache fails QUIETLY rather than wrongly. Neither changes a
decision; both stop being invisible to a census.

A4 — a walk that hits its entry bound refuses the whole fingerprint, which
turns the cache off for the install: every boot pays the full build, forever.
All that said so was a WARNING sentence carrying a number, and on the
store-root arm it did not even name the tree. It is now a receipt on the same
channel and in the same snapshot_core_cache family the shadow lane reports
divergence on — `fingerprint_refused reason=entries_exceeded scope=… bound=…
root=…`. The refusal itself is untouched: reaching a bound still means never
cache. A5's bound-over-loop-detection doctrine is kept deliberately and is
re-stated at _walk_tree, not changed.

A2 — a cache whose keys never settle was silent by construction. If some input
moves on every pass, no key a build writes can describe the store the next
build stats, so every process demotes, every process rebuilds, and the lane
costs a write per build while buying nothing; each individual demote is
legitimate, so nothing above notices. write_back now tracks whether this
process's consecutive write-backs ever agree, and past NEVER_CONVERGED_BUILDS
(3 — the measured virgin-root convergence, so the healthy cold-store shape,
which disagrees once, cannot trip it) emits `never_converged builds=N
diff_scope=… changed=… diff=…` NAMING the paths that differed on every pass.
That is the A1 rule made operational: widen the closure over a named input,
never trust the cache harder. Per C16, an arm that cannot compute the diff
says so in its own words (diff=diff_unavailable with a typed diff_reason)
rather than borrowing the oscillation sentence.

Only the digest of the last key is retained on a settled process; the entry
list is held only while a streak is live, so a healthy serve does not carry a
second stat set for a diagnostic that will not fire.

CACHE SEMANTICS UNTOUCHED, with evidence: every function that decides what is
read, how the key is computed, or how a persisted pair is judged is
byte-identical (_stat_entry, _entry_triple, _db_entries, _core_digest,
contract_versions, build_stamp_token, read_persisted_core, consult,
take_stale_first_core, label_core, compare_cores); _walk_tree is
docstring-only (AST code-identical); build_input_fingerprint differs in
exactly two statements, both the refusal arms' log call, with the if-tests and
the `return None` identical. A fixture root re-stat'd across the change gives
the same 1,039 entries, the same path-set hash, and the same digest.

Gates (tests/agent_runtime/test_core_fingerprint_cache.py), each driven with
two distinct values and each pinned by a killing mutation, observed red:
  - an entry-bound refusal is receipted, not just warned — two distinct store
    roots; plus the skill-root arm naming its own root. M1 (restore both bare
    warnings) reds both; M5 (skill arm names the store root) reds the skill
    gate alone.
  - an input that oscillates every build is named — two distinct oscillating
    paths, receipt must name the mover and must NOT name the stable inputs,
    with the per-write-back count pinning the exact build it appears on
    ([0,0,0,1]). M2 (drop the diff-naming) and M3 (drop the emission) each red
    both parametrizations.
  - the no-change case: a settling store emits nothing, driven both by keys
    and by four real consecutive builds (whose write-backs are counted so the
    silence cannot be vacuous). M4 (bound=1, the constant-emit shape) reds
    both, and reds the oscillation count too.
  - the diff-unavailable arm carries its own typed reason.

Witnesses are counts, typed reasons and named paths — never elapsed-ms.

message:
fix(sync): ML-8 — office publish/compare arms: an authority deciding on a lister that silently skips unreadable rows

`OfficeStore._read_actor_dir` skips a file it cannot decode and returns the
rest, so both office realm-sync arms read a SHORTER world that described itself
as complete. Both of them are writers, which is what makes this B2's class
rather than a wrong number:

* publish copies actor FILES verbatim, so the undecodable one travels — and
  since "removals propagate as absences", every peer's `apply_office_pull` then
  finds that actor key present locally, absent from the remote map it could
  decode, and ARCHIVES it. One quarantined file on one member's disk became a
  desk removal on every other member's.
* the pull's compare arm read the LOCAL actors to classify; an actor whose file
  will not decode arrived as "locally absent" — the exact input the three-way
  classifier reads as a local delete. The killing mutation demonstrates it:
  under the thin view the pull reports `adopted: 1`, having written the remote
  copy over the file it could not read.

Both arms now read `scan_actors` (the EG-1.5 chokepoint) and refuse the
workspace typed, `sync_unknowable`, carrying the count. `OfficeSyncRefusal`
mints that word in ONE place so no arm silently reuses another's sentence
(C16). The publish scan resolves artifacts, the persona ids those placements
pin, and the refusals in a single pass — three answers that used to be
independent walks of the same directories.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: on a store with a corrupt office actor file,
realm publish for that workspace goes from quiet-partial to a typed refusal.
That workspace publishes no office artifacts, pins no persona definitions, and
its baseline rows are left as they were rather than rewritten short; the pull
classifies nothing for it. Reported additively on the publish result under
`office_sync` (`refused` / `baseline`). Refusal scope is per-WORKSPACE, never
global — unreadability in one office says nothing about the next, and the
bystander rule the class-key fence already spends applies here too.

(+3). Counts driven 1 then 2; zero office artifacts for the workspace; the
baseline recorder shows the write happened and carried no key for it.

— 4 of 16 red; the mutant cannot mint a reason from a count it never took, and
