author: nekwo
message:
fix(sync): ML-8 — the board listers: an order-key allocator writing against a column it cannot see, and a projection that hid the shortfall

`_list_active_cards` / `list_all` skipped a file they could not decode. The
census splits what read those short lists into the two classes this stage is
about, and both are live here:

CLASS (i), a writer: every order-key decision — append, move-between, column
rebalance — is computed from the active-card list. The neighbour keys an insert
brackets between, and the keys a rebalance rewrites wholesale, were derived
from a column missing whatever the platform would not open, so the allocator
placed ON TOP of the invisible card and the rebalance reassigned every key
around a row it never saw. That is corruption WRITTEN, not merely read. The
three allocators now go through one `_ordering_cards` chokepoint that refuses
`CardsUnreadable` (code `cards_unreadable`, count in the message) — one
chokepoint rather than three guards, because two sufficient mechanisms
answering the same question is how a check survives its own sabotage.

CLASS (i), publish: a board whose cards do not fully read publishes nothing and
is refused typed (`sync_unknowable`) — the office arm's reasoning unchanged,
since publish copies card FILES verbatim and absences ARE removals, so a card
that merely would not decode here becomes a card archived on every peer.

CLASS (ii), the projections: `BoardScan` / `CardScan` carry the rows and the
count together (ActorScan's law), each board row gains `cards_unreadable`
(REQUIRED by keyword, like `actors_unreadable`, so a caller holding a bare list
must say 0 out loud), and the core gains `boards_unreadable` beside
`offices_unreadable`. All additive.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: adding or moving a card on a board with an
undecodable card file now fails typed instead of silently allocating a
colliding key. Reads are untouched — the board still lists.

Gates: `test_an_unreadable_card_file_refuses_order_key_allocation_typed`
(counts driven 1 then 2, directory census proves no card was written), its
bystander discriminator, `test_the_board_projection_states_how_many_rows_it_
could_not_read` (both counts driven with two values while readable rows still
project), and the publish refusal. Killing mutations: drop the `_ordering_cards`
guard (2 red); drop both `unreadable += 1` accumulators (4 red). Restores
verified byte-identical (board_store.py 237bdf29…).

author: nekwo
message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the persona scan seam: the rows and the count of what would not decode travel together

Infrastructure only; no arm changes behaviour yet. `PersonaInstanceStore.list_all`
and `PersonaAssignmentStore.list_all` have always skipped a row file they could
not decode and returned the rest, so every reader downstream received a SHORTER
world that described itself as complete — B2's class, third subsystem.

`scan_all` becomes THE chokepoint on both stores and `list_all` the thin list
view over it, so the many callers that only want rows keep their signature while
the arms that must not describe a short answer as complete can ask the fuller
question. That is `ActorScan`'s law, restated: the two facts have to travel
TOGETHER, because any seam carrying only the rows re-opens the hole at that seam.

Also mints the lane's vocabulary, each in exactly ONE place so no arm can quietly
reuse another arm's sentence for a condition it does not describe (C16):
`PERSONA_ROWS_UNREADABLE` for the word, `PersonaScanRefusal.for_scan` as the
report-shaped mint (returning None when the world was fully readable, so an arm
can neither report a refusal it did not earn nor default-construct one that
swallows the count), and `errors.PersonaInstancesUnreadable` as the raising form
— an `ArchiveUnreadable` subclass beside `ActorsUnreadable`/`CardsUnreadable`, so
every translation arm that already learned "a file the write depends on will not
decode" covers this one without a new branch, while carrying its own `code`.

`ActiveAssignmentScan` keeps the retire guard's two opposite empties apart:
"searched and found none" versus "could not search".

author: nekwo
message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the steering repair: a delete-shaped write minted out of a parse error

`repair_missing_steering_references` computed `live_ids` from the short lister and
then stripped, from every child, each steering parent absent from that set. The
strip is derived by SUBTRACTION, so a parent row that merely will not DECODE is
absent for a reason that has nothing to do with the parent being gone — and the
edge naming it is destroyed as dangling. A parse error became a delete.

There is no partial answer available here the way there was for a per-workspace
office publish: one unreadable row poisons the membership question for EVERY
child at once, because the set is what the predicate tests against. So the arm
refuses the whole sweep, writes nothing, and says how many rows it could not
read — `refused: {scope, reason: persona_rows_unreadable, unreadable: N}`, with
`refused: None` on the success arm so a consumer reads one shape and `None` is
the positive statement "the whole store was readable".

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: on a store with an undecodable persona
instance row, the steering repair goes from quiet-partial to a typed refusal. It
repairs nothing until the row is repaired or removed; a store that reads cleanly
still strips a genuinely dangling parent exactly as before.

Gates (+4): counts driven 1 then 2; the refusal shape, and SEPARATELY a recorder
gate asserting the store's bytes and the child's live edge are untouched — the
two witnesses are split on purpose (C5/C16), because a shape-only gate would
leave the serious claim (that the old code WROTE) unwitnessed. Killing mutation:
swap back to `PersonaInstanceScan(self.list_all(), 0)` — the shape gates red, and
the recorder gate reds separately because the mutant genuinely strips the edge.
G6 receipt: old token 1->0, new token 0->1; restore byte-identical
(persona_assignments.py dafc8a48…).

The recorder gate's first draft corrupted a BYSTANDER row and PASSED against the
mutant — nothing pointed at what it corrupted. It now corrupts the referenced
parent, which is the scenario that actually destroys data.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the retire guard: "could not search" stops reading as "searched and found none"

`_active_assignment_ids_for_instance`'s own docstring says a retire must never
orphan a live assignment, and it answered that by SEARCHING the assignment store
— so its negative was only ever worth what its enumeration was worth. It was
DOUBLY fail-open: the lister silently dropped assignment rows it could not
decode, AND the call was wrapped in `except Exception: return []`, which
converted any store-wide failure into the same confident "none active" the clean
path returns. Either way the retire proceeded and orphaned exactly the assignment
the guard exists to protect.

Both holes close. The guard now reads the scan-shaped chokepoint and returns
`ActiveAssignmentScan(assignment_ids, unreadable)`; `retire` refuses typed on a
nonzero count with a NEW code, `assignments_unknowable`, carrying the count and
the scope in `detail`. The blanket except is gone — a fault travels as a fault.

The new code is deliberately not `assignment_active`: "I looked and found one"
and "I could not look" are different conditions an operator acts on differently,
and collapsing them is C16's defect, one arm borrowing another arm's sentence.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: retiring a persona instance on a store with an
undecodable assignment row goes from silently proceeding to a typed refusal.
`runtime.agent.create`'s placement compensation reports it verbatim through

message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the backlink release: "every child" stops being a promise the short list cannot keep

`_release_parent_references` says "Transactionally release EVERY child backlink
before owner removal", and read the short lister to do it. A child whose row will
not decode keeps a backlink to an id that is about to stop resolving, and nothing
downstream will ever revisit it — the owner is gone, so no later sweep can
rediscover what the edge pointed at.

A DIFFERENT fact from the retire guard's (which is about assignment rows), so it
gets its OWN single chokepoint rather than a second mechanism for one fact: the
fence lives in `_release_parent_references` itself, which is where both owner-
removal paths pass through (`retire` via `_archive_instance_row`, and `_delete`),
and it runs BEFORE either moves or unlinks a file, so a refusal leaves the store
exactly as it found it. It raises `PersonaInstancesUnreadable`.

with an undecodable instance row refuses typed instead of silently leaving a
dangling backlink.

`test_office_class_key_guard.py::_instance_file` wrote `{"id": ...}` — enough for
the migration script, which only checks that the file EXISTS, but a row no
production writer can produce (`PersonaInstanceStore._write` always serializes a
whole `PersonaInstance`; the migration script never writes one at all, both READ
this SHA). It JSON-decoded and then failed model construction, so every reader
silently skipped it and the store carried an undecodable row as a matter of
course. That fixture now writes the row the way the store writes it. This is not
working around the fence: it removes an unreality, and the guard's subject
(class-keyed placement refusal) is untouched — 27 passed.

message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the session-uniqueness guard and the steering-cycle walk: two admissions taken on evidence neither could see

Both arms ADMIT a write by failing to find a reason not to, which is what makes a
short enumeration a fault rather than a wrong number.

`_session_owned_by_other_instance` asks "is this chat session already the default
of a different instance?" by scanning. An instance row that will not decode is an
owner the loop cannot see, so the guard answered False and a second binding landed
on a session that already had one — the class-key fence's blind spot, one
subsystem over. It now refuses `PersonaInstancesUnreadable` rather than answering
a False it cannot support.

`_validate_no_steering_cycle` admits the edge by exhausting its frontier without
reaching the child, so every node it could not open was a subgraph it silently
declared cycle-free: a cycle BEHIND an undecodable ancestor was admitted into the
graph. It now counts the ancestors it could not read and refuses.

The absent case is deliberately NOT the unreadable case: `get` re-raises
`FileNotFoundError` for an id with no row, which is a dangling reference the
steering repair exists to strip, and it genuinely does end the walk — nothing is
reachable through a node that is not there. Only a row that EXISTS and will not
decode is unknowable. Converting a dangling id into a refusal would have made the
repair unreachable, so the arms are kept apart.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: binding a chat session, and steering one
instance under another, refuse typed on a store with an undecodable instance row
instead of admitting a write on incomplete evidence.

Gates (+4): counts driven 1 then 2 on both arms, with the cycle fixture placing
the undecodable rows ON the ancestor path (the parent's `steered_by` names them)
so the walk genuinely reaches a node it cannot read; plus clean-store gates
pinning that the uniqueness guard still detects a real owner, that a dangling
ancestor is still admitted, and that a real cycle is still rejected. Killing
mutations: swap the guard back to the thin view (2 red); restore the walk's bare
`except Exception: continue` (2 red). The walk's mutation had to be anchored on
the `FileNotFoundError` arm above it — the bare three-line form occurs 3x in this
file, and a mutation hitting all three would have been testing something else.

(persona_assignments.py dafc8a48…).

author: nekwo
message:
fix(persona): ML-15 — the clarify-ticket index: a PERMANENT completeness claim minted from a momentary failure

`_rebuild_index` scanned the ticket files, wrote a per-session index from what it
could read, and then wrote the marker LAST. That marker is not a cache entry — it
is the sentence "the index may be trusted as complete" (`_ensure_index`), and it
is permanent: once written, every later lookup answers from the index and the
full-scan fallback is never taken again.

So a ticket file skipped during the rebuild was not skipped once, it was skipped
FOREVER. The tokenless settlement stops finding it, the turn that would have
closed it opens a second ticket for the same question, and no later pass can
recover it because nothing will ever rebuild again. And the skip is usually the
ordinary Windows failure this module already documents at `_read_index` — an AV
or indexer holding a file for the instant we touch it — so a momentary failure
punched a permanent hole.

`scan_records` becomes the chokepoint (`_iter_records` is the thin view over it),
and the rebuild refuses to claim completeness it does not have: nonzero unreadable
returns False. That is not a new failure mode, it is the one this method already
had, and its contract is exactly right — the caller falls back to the full scan,
which reads the store directly and is correct by construction. The store keeps
working, unindexed, until the file is repaired. This is `_read_index`'s own law,
UNREADABLE IS NOT EMPTY, applied to the ticket files instead of the index file.

Projection half: `scan_tickets` carries the count and the operator readout states
it beside `total` (additive). That readout computes an adoption RATIO over the
whole store, and the site building it says why it must not narrow silently — "an
adoption ratio that moved because the operator asked to see fewer rows would be a
lying metric". A file dropping out of the scan moved the denominator exactly that
way without anyone having asked.

One pre-existing test re-pointed, not weakened: the concurrent-mint union test
intercepted `_iter_records`, which the rebuild no longer calls, so it would have
passed while exercising nothing. It now intercepts `scan_records` — the seam the
code actually reads. Its `concurrent[0]` access self-proves the interception
fires. 66 passed.

Gates (+5): counts driven 1 then 2; the marker's ABSENCE is the asserted artifact
(the claim is the thing that must not exist), the lookup still answers while the
index is refused, a clean store still builds it, and the readout's count is
membership-checked against the surviving ticket. Killing mutations: drop the
fence — 2 red; constant-zero the readout count — 2 red (`assert 0 == 2`, which is
why two values are driven). The rebuild's mutation is a DELETION whose
replacement is a PREFIX of the original, so counting the new token alone is
vacuous — it was anchored on the following line and the removed `if unreadable:`
grepped 1->0. Restores byte-identical (persona_chat_continuity.py 1da196aa…,
a pure-CRLF file, so the driver matched on CRLF-spelled patterns).

author: nekwo
message:
fix(store): ML-15 — the workspace-delete cascade: its enumeration IS its delete list

`WorkspaceStore.delete` cascaded over `BoardStore.list_all()`, which drops a board
whose `board.json` will not decode, and deleted by MATCHING `board.workspace_id`.
So a board it could not decode was a board it could not ATTRIBUTE, and it silently
survived a workspace that no longer exists.

That orphan is worse than either outcome the operator chose between: no
workspace-scoped verb will ever list it again, and no later delete can re-reach
it, because the workspace row that named it is gone. `scan_all` already existed
(ML-8 landed it for the publish scope); this reads it.

Refused BEFORE the office subtree is removed — before the cascade takes its first
irreversible step — so the store is left exactly as found. A half-done cascade is
worse than a refused one: the refusal is repairable by fixing one file, the
half-done state is not repairable at all once the workspace row is unlinked. The
refusal rides the verb's existing typed vocabulary, `WorkspaceDeleteBlocked` with
a new code `workspace_boards_unreadable`, so it reaches the CLI error envelope
the same way `workspace_has_goals` and `realm_default_workspace` already do.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: deleting a workspace on a store with an
undecodable board definition refuses typed instead of cascading partially. A
readable store still cascades identically.

Gates (+3): counts driven 1 then 2; the typed code plus `safe_details.unreadable`
and `.workspace_id`, and then the whole cascade proved un-run — the workspace row
still on disk, the office subtree untouched, the workspace's boards still listed.
Plus a clean-store gate proving the fence is not a disabled verb. Killing
mutation: zero the count so the cascade decides on the thin view again
(`scan_all().boards` IS `list_all()`, so this restores the exact pre-fix
behaviour) — 2 red. G6 receipt: old token 1->0, new token 0->1; restore
byte-identical (store.py 664ea86d…).

author: nekwo
message:
test(cli): ML-7 / R-c — profile-bound pid discovery reads an injected lister, never the live process table

`_profile_bound_backend_pids` decides which processes get terminated, so the
OS process table is its INPUT — and it read that input inline. Two costs, one
cause: the function was answerable only against whatever happened to be
running on the machine (its user/ancestor/binding filters had no observable
drive), and every test reaching profile-delete walked the live table. Measured
here 2026-08-18: 448 processes, ~4.2s per scan, three scans in
tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py alone — ledger row F1, the reason that
directory could not be run as a directory.

The seam: `_ProcessFacts` / `_ProcessTable` name the per-process view the
function actually reads, `_PsutilProcessLister` is the production reader, and
the module-level `_PROCESS_LISTER` is the single injection point — replacing
that name replaces the whole input, with no path around it. Identity (self
pid, ancestors, current user) travels WITH the rows, so a test cannot end up
filtering driven rows through the live machine's facts. Behaviour is
unchanged: every filter still applies, to the same facts, in the same order,
and the "no inspector at all" arm still answers [] (kept as-is, not retyped —
the ML-7 report escalates whether it should become a typed refusal).

tests/hermes_cli/conftest.py gains the hermetic default: no test in this
directory reads the real table. Tests that are ABOUT the scan install their
own lister on top and drive the rows they mean to filter.

Witnesses: TestProcessListerSeam drives two distinct tables and asserts the
answer is that table's rows filtered by the real predicate (two driven sets,
counts and ordering, never elapsed-ms), that a refusing environ() reads as
"no signal" rather than a match, and that a `_RealEnumeratorRecorder` standing
in for psutil.process_iter is never called — including through profile delete.
The pre-existing test_backend_scan_only_matches_this_profile now says which
half it pins (the psutil adapter) so neither test can stand in for the other.

Mutation M1 (bypass the seam: `_PROCESS_LISTER.read()` becomes
`_PsutilProcessLister().read()`; removed-token count 0, added-token count 1):
3 of 4 gate tests red on the recorder. Mutation M2 (autouse=True to False on
the hermetic default): profile-delete reds and the file's runtime returns
2.20s to 12.46s. Both restored by byte-copy, hashes re-verified equal.

Counts: tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py 49 passed / 2 skipped (was 45/2),
real psutil.process_iter calls 3 to 0; test_profiles_s6_hooks.py 3 passed and
test_console_engine.py 3 passed, both 0 to 0.

author: nekwo
message:
test(cli): ML-7 / R-d — the surrogate-sanitization test never opens a socket

The file took 32.7s and died on the 30s per-test cap (ledger row F2). The
connect was not in the test's subject at all: constructing a real AIAgent
resolves the model's context length by probing the endpoint, and against a
base_url nothing answers, six probes each block until their own timeout —
`detect_local_server_type` (four dials), `_query_local_context_length`, and
`_query_ollama_api_show`, plus `fetch_endpoint_model_metadata`. Traced with a
socket recorder rather than guessed.

Faked at the transport boundary, which is two boundaries here: httpx gets a
MockTransport answering 404 (what a server that is not Ollama says), and
`requests` gets an HTTPAdapter that does the same — the adapter IS requests'
transport. Both were needed; faking one alone leaves the timeout in place at
reduced volume, which the mutations below pin. The production code still
builds its clients, sends its requests and reads the responses; only the
socket never happens. Mocking the probe functions would also have stopped the
hang and would have been wrong — it pins the test to today's call graph and
stops it telling us anything about construction reaching the network.

The witness is a separate layer from the fake, deliberately: the socket
boundary records anything dialled at the endpoint's port, so a path the
transports do not cover reaches the socket and the COUNT says so. Sockets to
anywhere else pass through untouched — a blanket ban breaks asyncio's own
self-pipe on Windows, which is how the first attempt errored 13 of 13 tests
in setup. The fixture is autouse so it cannot be forgotten, and requestable so
it can be asserted on.

Two defects the timeout was hiding, now fixed because the test finally runs
past construction: the response mock left `reasoning`/`reasoning_details`
unset, and an unset attribute on a MagicMock is not absent but a truthy
MagicMock the extractor tries to join — the turn errored and retried to
api_calls=89/90. And the assertion loop over stored messages asserted nothing
if it found none, so it now pins that exactly one user message was checked.

Mutations, each with G6 receipts (removed-token count 0, added 1) and byte-copy
restore verified equal by sha256: M3 (httpx transport fake removed) reds on the
connect count; M4 (requests transport fake removed) reds the same way; M5
(`_sanitize_surrogates` neutered to `return text`) reds the target test, so the
sanitization claims still bite and did not become decoration.

Counts: tests/cli/test_surrogate_sanitization.py 13 passed in 4.18s, was 12
passed / 1 timeout-failed in 32.7s.

author: nekwo
message:
test(conftest): ML-14 / C21 — the no-undo tripwire and the backend-spawn arm live where the six pins already live

Two holes in the root conftest, both of the same shape: the file installs the
guards, and the fences for those guards lived somewhere else or nowhere.

C21 — the BEHAVIOURAL no-undo witness was `tests/agent_runtime`'s alone while
the pins it protects are the root conftest's and are tree-wide. Outside that
package the fence was structural-only (an AST walker), so an `undo()` reached
through an alias, a callback or `getattr` unwound the hermetic HERMES_HOME, the
credential blanking, the kanban write guard, the live-system guard and the audio
guard with nothing going red. `_shared_monkeypatch_pin_tripwire` is that witness
hoisted: a per-test sentinel minted through the shared MonkeyPatch, never handed
to the body, asserted still-set at teardown. Declared FIRST among the file's

that the fixture is still autouse), and its "THE WIDENING" paragraph stops
describing a gap that is closed.

backend, never STARTING one. `hermes` resolves on this workstation to

author: nekwo
message:
docs(core_cache): ML-14 / C22 — every hermes receipt names its second channel, or says it has none

The core-cache lane emits eleven receipt shapes on one logger out of THREE
vocabularies that all word themselves `reason=` — the demote reasons
(`DEMOTE_*`), the write refusals, and ML-10's typed bound refusal — and nothing
said which family carried which. Two spellings turn out to COLLIDE across two
events: `reason=fingerprint_unavailable` and `reason=build_stamp_unknown` are
emitted BOTH by the write lane (`snapshot_core_cache_write ok=false`, hand-worded
literals) and by the read lane's demote (`snapshot_core_cache
core_source=rebuilt`, the `DEMOTE_*` constants). A census greppping a reason
without its family token counts two different facts as one — the launcher-side
class ML-6 retired, where a refusal worded `patch_gap:` on one channel and
`REFUSED gap:` on the other made a census MEASURE a false zero.

So the table is an INDEX keyed on the family token, mirroring ML-6's launcher
one (`| receipt (grep this) | second channel | what to grep there |`), landed in
the one place the vocabulary already lives — core_cache.py's module docstring.
What it records beyond the mapping:

* the COLLISION, named at the row rather than left for a census to discover;
* C22(i)'s census rule at the `never_converged` row: the token alone
  over-reports, `diff_scope=every_pass` is self-perturbation (the A2 defect
  worth acting on), `last_pair` is a store that is simply moving — the receipt
  is true there and names no defect;
* the ONE second channel that exists (the snapshot `parity` envelope) and, per
  row, whether it is a clean derivation (`core_source=cache` → `parity.core_source
  == "cache"`, same spelling) or a RESIDUAL SPLIT (`stale=true` → `parity.core_stale`
  / `parity.freshness.state`, whose spelling is a launcher consumer contract
  predating this lane);
* that `_log_demote`'s `reason=` reaches NO other surface — `CoreDecision.reason`
  is read by no caller — so this line is the only source for why a cache demoted;
* that `absent` is deliberately never logged, so its only trace is the ABSENCE
  of a line and a census must not read "no demote line" as "no demote";
* `snapshot_core_shadow adopt failed` as the one line in the lane with NO event
  token — uncountable, named honestly rather than quietly renamed;
* the SCOPE: three other `agent_runtime` things called receipts (persona-chat
  mint receipt FILES, `CHAT_COMPACTION_RECEIPT_KIND`, `build_receipt_facts`) are
  different artifacts on different channels and are ruled out by name, so this
  table cannot be read as the whole census.

`tests/agent_runtime/test_core_cache_channel_table.py` (11 tests) drives it from
both ends: the vocabulary is DERIVED (module constants under five prefixes, plus
every `reason=<token>` hand-worded into a log format string, plus every family
token, all read out of the source by AST — a text scan would read this
docstring's own quoted log lines as code) and compared to the table both
directions; then the writers are DRIVEN and the RENDERED lines matched against

docs(harness): ML-14 — F6 marked retired in §4, and the config-read guard stops walking the repo's fourteen copies

Two documents-vs-tree corrections and one guard fix, all of the same class: a
rule or a fence that stopped matching the tree it describes.

**B20(vii) — F6 RETIRED (§4 item 5, and §4.5's amendment).** The operator
dropped the stale pubspec pair on 2026-08-18; launcher agents run `flutter test`
and `flutter analyze` against the tree as-is and never touch pubspecs. The
procedure stays in the document as history, marked, so the record of why it
existed survives — but it is no longer instruction, and it must not be quoted
into a brief. §4.5 gets the same marker plus what OUTLIVES it: a cheap signal
can fail in the RESOLVER rather than in the tool, and an error naming neither is
how an implementer loses an hour. That is a diagnosis worth keeping; the
backup/restore window it prescribed is not.

**§4 item 1 — the F5 gap this bundle closed, and two of its three named reds.**
The paragraph still said a backend spawn "passes straight through" the root
conftest's chokepoint; it does not, since ML-14 / B20(i). Amended in place,
dated, with what the fix does NOT do stated beside what it does: the escape
marker is the guard's, not this arm's, so a test that needs a real child still
drops the os.kill and systemctl guards along with the spawn arm. The red-file
table's two fixable rows are marked fixed with what replaced them; the third
(`test_commands.py::test_telegram_parity`, a registered known defect that is not
`xfail`ed — B20(iv)'s always-red class) is untouched and still red.

**B20(iii) — `.claude` joins `EXCLUDED_DIR_PARTS`.** Agent worktrees live under
`.claude/worktrees/<branch>/` and each is a full copy of this repo, so the
repo-wide walk reported the COPIES' `gateway/config.py` as violations (the
allowlist is keyed on the path from the repo root, which a copy's path cannot
match) and every grep run beside it returned fourteen copies of every hit — C14
inverted. The guard sat red for a fortnight on that.

The operator has since pruned the worktrees, which is the interesting half: the
fix is now preventative, and removing `.claude` again would leave the guard
GREEN on this machine. A fence whose only witness is a hazard that comes and
goes is a fence you cannot check when you need it (the always-red-gate rule,
read the other way round). So the walk root became a parameter and the exclusion
gained a DRIVEN witness on a synthetic tree: a `.claude/worktrees/wave-2/…` copy
that must stay invisible, beside an identical first-party file that must be
reported. Without that control an exclusion set that had swallowed the whole
walk would look like a fix.

The launcher's C1-C4 made the consumer real: `AvatarSpriteSheet._deriveDirectionSectors`
(EterniaLauncher `packages/eternia_spatial/lib/src/cosmetics/avatar_sprite_resolver.dart`)
splits every row name on its LAST hyphen and matches the tail against eight direction
tokens. Hermes emitted `<state>@<direction>`, so every 8-way sheet we composed would have
covered ZERO sectors and degraded to two-way at runtime — silently, no error, no log. The
contract authority is now one document, the launcher SPEC
`docs/spatial/CHARACTER_8WAY_SPRITE_FORMAT_SPEC_2026-08-17.md`; hermes conforms to it and
no longer keeps a second copy of it.

Code:

- `agent/charsheet/spec.py`
  - `row_key` emits `<state>-<direction>`; module docstring names the SPEC as authority.
  - NEW `DIRECTION_TOKENS = ("e","se","s","sw","w","nw","n","ne")` — the launcher's
    `CharacterFacingSector` vocabulary in theta order. Row order is NOT required to be
    theta order; the launcher addresses rows by NAME.
  - `DirectionScheme.__post_init__` rejects any `order` token outside `DIRECTION_TOKENS`.
    Placed LAST so every pre-existing negative test keeps its own message.
  - `EIGHT_WAY.order = ("s","se","e","ne","n","nw","w","sw")`, authored
    `("s","se","e","ne","n")`; `FOUR_WAY.order = ("s","e","n","w")`, authored
    `("s","e","n")`. Front-first, authored-first: row 0 of CHAR8 is `idle-s`, so the
    launcher's degenerate row-0 clip fallback reads front-facing (SPEC section G risk 7);
    and the authored prefix is already what `pipeline.turnaround_order` produces out of
    the `prompts.VIEW_LANGUAGE` ring, so the prompt/turnaround lane did not move at all.
  - `_STATE_NAME_RE` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and `parse_states` refuses `-` by name (`@`
    now falls through to the generic "invalid state name"). Closed by construction: with
    the launcher splitting on the LAST hyphen, a `spin-kick` state would make row parsing
    depend on whichever tokens are in the direction table that day.
- `agent/charsheet/__init__.py` — `DIRECTION_TOKENS` exported (import + `__all__`).
- `agent/charsheet/draft.py` — `row_item` / `run_rows` / `sprite_payload` docstrings;
  `_strip_filename` drops its now-dead `@`->`-` substitution (filenames unchanged:
  `walk-e-3.png`).
- `agent/charsheet/pipeline.py` — `row_prefix` drops the dead `@`->`_` substitution.
- `agent/charsheet/prompts.py` — the `VIEW_LANGUAGE` comment claimed the dict was in the
  order `DirectionScheme` iterates. That is now false, and it was always the wrong reason
  to keep it stable: the real reason is that `turnaround_order` ranks ring distance
  against it. Reworded; dict contents and ORDER untouched.
- `agent/charsheet/revisions.py` — docstring example only.
- `hermes_cli/harness.py` — the two `--only` / `--row` help literals.

Revision-store keys are deliberately UNCHANGED (`row@walk-e`, `turnaround@n`): the leading
`<kind>@` is the store's item-kind separator, the store never parses keys, and `_KEY_RE`
already admitted the hyphen. Mirror baking also stays — assessed and kept: the launcher
runtime tries the exact row before its mirror and mirror-closes either way, so the only
cost is ~+60% decoded RAM per sheet, which belongs to the launcher's open RAM-cap
decision. `agent/pet/*` is upstream and untouched.

Five new witnesses, each carrying its own literals rather than deriving them from the code
under test:

1. `test_charsheet_spec.py::test_row_keys_are_the_launcher_deriver_vocabulary` — over both
   schemes and a fixture with two directional states plus a fixed one: every directional
   key has no `@`, `rpartition("-")` yields `(row.state, "-", row.direction)`, and the
   token is in a TEST-LOCAL transcription of the eight; that literal is also asserted

message:
docs(charsheet): C5 — Plan H defers the sheet contract to the launcher SPEC

Plan H was written before the launcher had an 8-way consumer, so it carried its own copy
of the sheet contract: literal direction tuples, a row-key example, a sheet-size figure.
That copy is exactly what drifted — hermes shipped `walk@ne` against a launcher that
splits on the last hyphen. Two documents cannot both be the authority, so this one stops
trying to be.

- Header blockquote gains a **Contract authority (2026-08-18, C5)** paragraph: row keys,
  direction tokens, row order, cell size and roster live ONLY in EterniaLauncher
  `docs/spatial/CHARACTER_8WAY_SPRITE_FORMAT_SPEC_2026-08-17.md`. What stays here is what
  is hermes-specific — packaging boundary, revision store, QA gate, CLI verbs, prompts.
- §2 loses the literal `("n","ne",…)` / 4-way tuples, the `Row key: "walk@ne"` example and
  the `1536×3328` figure. It now describes the SHAPES that carry the contract
  (`StateSpec` / `DirectionScheme` / `SheetSpec` / `RowSpec`), states the `len(order)`
  rule, the `--states name:frames[:fixed]` grammar and the `-` reservation, and points at
  SPEC §A/§C/§D for tokens, order and keys.
- §3 and §4: revision-store examples read `row@walk-e` / `row@<state>-<dir>`, with the
  `<kind>@` prefix explicitly labelled as the STORE's item-kind separator rather than the
  sheet's. The "mirrored rows are not QA items" rule is unchanged.
- §5: `--only walk-e` / `--row walk-e`; the payload field list stays (hermes -> launcher
  packaging is hermes-specific) and now says the row keys and `stateRows` order inside it
  follow the launcher SPEC.
- §6 CS-6: notes the launcher's committed generator at
  `tool/spatial/placeholder_character/` and why it is NOT a substitute for the fake
  provider here — it emits a finished atlas for the CONSUMER side, where the fake provider
  drives the extractor, geometry gate, mirror derivation and palette lock on the INPUT
  side. Keep both.
- NEW §12 "C5 conformance": the three closed divergences, `DIRECTION_TOKENS`, the
  mirror-baking divergence recorded as tolerated with the cost that would retire it, the
  unchanged store keys, and the fact that there is nothing in the field to migrate.

Cited by symbol and by repo-relative path throughout; no line-number citations added.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(cli): ML-16 / B20 — profile delete refuses when it cannot see who is writing, instead of deleting blind

`_profile_bound_backend_pids` answered `[]` when this machine had no process
inspector at all — the same answer as "the table was read and nothing is bound
to this profile". No caller could branch on the difference, so `delete_profile`
walked straight into the case the scan exists to prevent: `rmtree` on a
directory a live `serve`/`dashboard` backend was still writing into (the
ENOTEMPTY, and pre-fix the resurrected tree).

Two typed names now separate fact from policy:

* `ProcessTableUnreadable` (`code = "process_table_unreadable"`) — the lister
  cannot answer. Raised where `[]` used to be returned.
* `ProfileDeleteBlocked(code, message, safe_details=...)` — the delete refuses.
  Mirrors `agent_runtime.errors.WorkspaceDeleteBlocked`'s shape for the same
  reason ML-15 chose it: a delete that cannot establish its precondition
  refuses with a name the caller branches on.

`delete_profile` reads the process table in its pre-flight, BEFORE the service
teardown that is its first irreversible step, and refuses there — a refused
delete leaves the profile exactly as it found it (the gate pins
`_cleanup_gateway_service` call_count == 0, so refusing late reds). The reading
travels down to the stop step, so the machine is asked exactly once and the
refusal gate and the scan cannot disagree about it; `_ProcessTable.processes`
enumerates lazily, so that step still sees the processes alive when it runs and
the terminate/rmtree path is byte-for-byte the old one.

`--force-unverified-writers` is the override: default False everywhere (API
signature and argparse), billed on stdout when used. The dashboard endpoint
maps the refusal to 409 with the code, not to a `_log.exception` 500 — nothing
crashed — and deliberately exposes no override: forcing past an unknowable
writer set is a terminal decision, not a button.

Docstring corrected per C25: the "returns an empty list if the process table
can't be inspected" sentence described behaviour that is now gone.

Gates (tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles.py, hermetic via the ML-7 autouse fake
lister): refusal leaves the dir byte-identical and the teardown untouched;
the override proceeds and says so; a driven readable table deletes as before
with reads == 1; the parser defaults to refusing; the endpoint answers 409.
Six killing mutations, all observed RED, all byte-restored:
M1 raise -> `return []`; M2 drop the refusal; M3 override defaults True in the
signature; M4 override defaults True in argparse; M5 stop step re-reads the
seam (reads == 2); M6 drop the 409 arm.

with test_profiles_s6_hooks.py + test_subcommands_profile_gateway.py
60 passed / 2 skipped.

author: nekwo
message:
test(cli): ML-16 / B20 — the known defect is fenced strict, so the checkpoint can be all-green and the defect cannot be forgotten

`test_commands.py::TestSlackNativeSlashes::test_telegram_parity` has been red
since the command registry outgrew Slack's 50-slash app cap. It is a real,
registered, owner-owned defect — and it was left as a permanent red, which is
the always-red-gate class inverted: a file that can never be green has no red
left to spend on a REGRESSION, and the canonical per-file runner's red
definition (ML-7 / R-e) could never be all-green while it stood.

It is now `xfail(strict=True)`. The defect is NOT fixed and the mark says so.
`strict` is the whole point: the day parity actually holds, the test XPASSes,
the file reds, and someone must come delete the mark and the conftest row. A
non-strict xfail would let both a real fix and a mutant that fakes one pass
unnoticed — measured below, not asserted.

Two things had to move together, and they fail in opposite directions:

* The mark's `reason` is IMPORTED from the conftest
  (`TELEGRAM_PARITY_DEFECT_REASON`) rather than restated, so the fence and the
  terminal report cannot drift into two accounts of one defect (C25).
* `pytest_runtest_logreport` matched `outcome == "failed"` only. An xfail
  arrives as `skipped` + `wasxfail`, so the mark would have silenced the
  KNOWN DEFECTS banner the same day it landed — the defect fenced AND
  unexplained. It now matches failed OR wasxfail; the `failed` arm still earns
  its place because a strict XPASS arrives as `failed` with no `wasxfail`.
* The `_KNOWN_DEFECTS` prose no longer says "this red STAYS" / "deliberately
  not fenced" — it says the defect stays, fenced xfail(strict), and why.

Gates: the mark is strict and single-sourced; an xfailed known defect (and a
strict XPASS) still reach the banner, while an ordinary pass in the same file
does not. Killing mutations, all observed RED, all byte-restored:
  MA  test body made to pass, strict=True   -> XPASS(strict), file RED
  MB  same body, strict=False               -> `1 xpassed`, test_telegram_parity
                                               does NOT fail — the fence gate is
                                               the only thing that reds. That is
                                               exactly what strict buys.
  MC  strict flipped alone                   -> fence gate reds
  MD  reason restated inline                 -> single-sourcing gate reds
  ME  classifier back to failed-only         -> banner gate reds

author: nekwo
message:
test(cli): ML-16 / B20 — the desktop-build lock sweep reads the injected table, never the live one

`_stop_desktop_processes_locking_build` TERMINATES what it finds, so the OS
process table is its input — and it read that table inline. Ledger row B20(vi):
`test_gui_command.py` walked this machine's real processes once per run, via
`cmd_gui` -> the sweep -> `psutil.process_iter`. A test that reads the live
table is asking a question with no defined answer (what it holds depends on
what the developer happens to be running), and none of the sweep's filters were
observable at all.

It now reads `_DESKTOP_PROCESS_LISTER`, ML-7 / R-c's seam applied to the second
consumer — reusing `profiles._ProcessLister` / `_ProcessTable` / `_ProcessFacts`
rather than minting a parallel protocol. The COLUMNS differ (`exe` here,
cmdline/environ there), so `_ProcessFacts` gained `exe` and its per-consumer
fields became optional; that is one row type serving two callers, not two.

`_ProcessFacts.inspector_handle` carries the inspector's own object for rows a
caller must ACT on. Terminating through it, instead of re-resolving the pid
afterwards, is what keeps the pre-existing pid-recycle safety: between the walk
and the act, a number can belong to something else.

Behaviour preserved: win32-only, release dir must exist, never this process
(now `table.self_pid`, so identity travels with the rows it filters), exe must
resolve INSIDE the release tree, best-effort, returns the pids asked to stop.
The one mechanical change is `psutil.wait_procs(victims, timeout=5)` becoming a
deadline loop over the rows' `wait` — `wait_procs` IS a wrapper over
`Process.wait`, so the budget and the kill escalation are the same, and no
module-level psutil reference is left for a mutant to reach around the seam
through.

The directory's ML-7 autouse fixture was EXTENDED to default this second seam
rather than gaining a sibling: one place answers "does any test here touch the
live process table", because two places is how one of them silently stops
covering a call site.

Gates: `test_gui_command.py` gains an autouse refusing `process_iter` recorder
asserted at 0 calls in teardown, plus three driven tests — a locking process is
terminated and reported while an outsider and this very process are not (three
driven rows, two rejection reasons); a process that keeps the lock is waited on
once and then killed; no inspector stops nothing. NOTE the recorder needed the
teardown COUNT and not only the raise: the lister catches Exception around
`process_iter`, so a raising instrument alone is swallowed — measured under MI.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet): authored-only rows — one format, the CS-4 mirror gate deleted (ruling 3-B)

C5 (`8b8ea41dc3`) conformed hermes to the launcher SPEC everywhere except one line of it:
"ship authored directions only; never bake mirrors". Compose kept deriving the three
mirrored rows with `mirror_frames` and packing them into the sheet, and the divergence was
recorded as tolerated because retiring it deletes CS-4's shipped pixel-equality gate and
the launcher had no memory budget to weigh the cost against. It now does — owner ruling
2026-08-18, launcher ADR 0024 decision 3 = B ("hermes emits authored-only rows; one
format") on top of decision 2 = C (a byte budget for character sheets). Option C (a
`--authored-only` flag, two formats alive) was considered and ruled out; nothing here
keeps a flag, a parameter or a legacy path.

Nothing caught this because nothing could: both shapes are correct at runtime. Every
launcher candidate chain tries the exact row before its mirror and
`AvatarSpriteSheet._deriveDirectionSectors` mirror-closes its coverage set, so a baked
sheet and an authored-only sheet resolve the same eight sectors. The only difference is
decoded RAM, which no test can see — CHAR8 is now 10 rows / 1536x2080 / 12.19 MiB, against
16 rows / 1536x3328 / 19.50 MiB baked (ADR 0024 §0.6 arithmetic). Sheets composed before
this commit stay valid: the deriver still mirror-closes, and the backend sidecar validator
checks geometry, not authoredness. `$HERMES_HOME/characters/` is still empty on this box —
no installed sheets, no drafts, nothing to migrate.

Code:

- `agent/charsheet/spec.py`
  - `SheetSpec.rows()` iterates `scheme.authored` for a directional state instead of
    `scheme.order`. CHAR8 is 10 rows, `sheet_size()` 1536x2080, row 0 still `idle-s`.
    Deliberately NOT `[d for d in order if d in authored]`: `authored` is now the row
    order, so reordering it moves the rows — which is what makes the front-first
    guarantee mutation-killable at all (m3/m3b below).
  - `authored_rows()` KEPT and reduced to `return self.rows()`. It is the question the
    draft/QA lane and the CLI's `authoredRows` field actually ask, and delegating (rather
    than re-filtering) is what stops the two row lists ever drifting apart again.
  - `mirrored_rows()` KEPT but retyped `list[tuple[RowSpec, RowSpec]]` ->
    `list[tuple[str, RowSpec]]` — `(derived key, composed source row)`. Left as written it
    would have returned `[]` forever (it filtered `rows()` for mirrored directions, and
    there are none), which is worse than deleting it: a silently vacuous method, and every
    test that read it would have gone vacuous with it. The derived half is a KEY on
    purpose — a `RowSpec` would have to invent an `index` into a sheet that does not
    contain that row. Ordered by `scheme.order` per directional state.
    (The C6 plan §D says this method "still feeds the payload's `directions.mirrored`";
    it does not, and never did — `sprite_payload` reads `spec.scheme.mirrored` directly.)
  - Module docstring, `DirectionScheme` docstring, the `EIGHT_WAY` preamble and the
    `SheetSpec`/`rows` docstrings: `order` is no longer the row order, it is the direction
    vocabulary the CONSUMER resolves, and only its authored prefix becomes rows.
- `agent/charsheet/pipeline.py`
  - `compose_draft_frames` loses its step 2 entirely (`for derived, source in
    spec.mirrored_rows(): frames_by_key[derived.key] = mirror_frames(...)`), and
    `mirror_frames` leaves the upstream import block — there is now no `mirror_frames`
    call anywhere in `agent/charsheet/`. `normalize_cells` still runs over every row at
    once, so the one shared scale is unchanged in effect: a horizontal flip preserves
    every bounding box that scale is derived from.
  - Module + `compose_draft_frames` docstrings renumbered and corrected.
- `agent/charsheet/draft.py` — `sprite_payload`'s `framesByRow`/`stateRows`/`rows` shrink
  to the authored set by construction (they were already `spec.rows()`); its docstring no
  longer claims a "16-row sheet" and now states which rows the payload describes and why
  `directions.mirrored` survives. `_require_authored_direction`'s refusal no longer tells
  the operator that mirrored directions are "derived at compose" — nothing is.
  `spritesheetRevision` (`mtime_ns:size`) is untouched.
- `agent/charsheet/prompts.py` — two comments that asserted the old premise: the
  turnaround docstring's "they are derived at compose", and the `VIEW_LANGUAGE` note
  calling `DirectionScheme.order` the sheet ROW order.
- `hermes_cli/harness.py` is untouched: `authoredRows` now equals `rows` in the draft
  summary, and both are true. Removing a wire field is not this slice's call.

Tests. Deleted, because there is nothing left for them to check:
`pipeline::test_every_mirrored_row_is_the_pixel_exact_flip_of_its_source_row` (the CS-4
gate), `::test_a_mirrored_row_is_not_a_copy_of_its_source_row`,
`::test_mirroring_preserves_frame_order_rather_than_reversing_the_strip`.

Re-pointed: `pipeline::test_mirrored_rows_are_never_generated` now asserts never
*composed* as well as never *generated* — the mirrored keys are absent from the composed
cell dict and the sheet is exactly `len(SPEC.rows())` rows tall. Its derived keys are a
test-local literal (`idle-w`, `walk-w`), not `SPEC.mirrored_rows()`; read out of the
module under test the assertion would have gone vacuous the moment that method did.
`spec::test_authored_and_mirrored_rows_partition_the_sheet` became false (the sheet is the
authored half) and is replaced by `::test_no_mirrored_direction_ever_becomes_a_row`;
`::test_mirrored_row_pairs_cover_every_derived_row_and_point_at_a_drawn_one` became
`::test_a_mirrored_pair_names_a_row_the_sheet_lacks_and_a_row_it_has`. Row-count pins
moved from `len(scheme.order)` to `len(scheme.authored)` in seven more spec tests (two of
them renamed to say so), `keys[8] == "walk-s"` became `keys[5]`, and two draft tests that
read `SPEC.mirrored_rows()` for a row key now carry the literal. Total moved: 12 tests
across two files, against the plan's ~20 estimate.

Added, each carrying its own literals:

1. `pipeline::test_char8_composes_ten_authored_rows_at_1536x2080` — the ten row keys
   transcribed in order, `CHAR8.sheet_size() == (1536, 2080)`, no `-sw/-w/-nw` key, then a
   real `compose_sheet` of ten synthetic rows whose per-row colour is read back at each
   row's y offset, and `validate_sheet` clean with `filled_rows` equal to those ten keys.
   The literals are the ADR's, not the spec object's: 1536x2080x4 IS the 12.8 MB the
   memory budget was set from.
2. `draft::test_sprite_payload_state_rows_are_authored_only_and_front_first` — the payload
   the launcher actually receives, after compose + install + serialisation: the six
   FOUR_WAY row keys as a literal, no `-w` key, and the DECODED sheet height equal to
   `len(stateRows) * frameH`, so a payload that merely under-reported its rows would fail
   here too.
3. `draft::test_directions_mirrored_still_names_the_three_runtime_flips` — the map
   survives the baked rows: `directions` verbatim for the installed sheet, `EIGHT_WAY`'s
   three flips transcribed from the launcher SPEC §A.1 (`e<->w, se<->sw, ne<->nw`), and no
   CHAR8 row named after any of them. Dropping the map with the rows was the easy
   over-reach; the launcher reads the sectors off the row NAMES, and the map is what tells
   a sheet author which three directions never get drawn.

Red-first proof, written after the code was complete. Every mutation grep-proved applied,
every restore proved by SHA-256 against the pre-mutation hashes
`agent/charsheet/spec.py` 4bc9ddba07ba75d872c0771380062763d6633fe8dcbbdc96abc825581109f8ae
and `agent/charsheet/pipeline.py`
7ea2b13a58f77ded71766f87d1cef44f32548f76df7ccac0a35d83fe16d4bbdd — all restores matched.

  m1  `rows()` back to `scheme.order`
      grep `self.scheme.order if state.directional` -> spec.py:260 present
      RED: pipeline::test_char8_composes_ten_authored_rows_at_1536x2080
           (1 failed / 12 passed / 19 fixture errors);
           spec:: 15 failed / 61 passed, incl. test_char8_row_zero_is_the_front_facing_idle,
           test_no_mirrored_direction_ever_becomes_a_row[both schemes];
           draft:: 3 failed / 13 errors — the two new payload tests error at the module
           fixture, because with `authored_rows` delegating, compose demands strips for

      restore sha256 4bc9ddba... MATCH
  m2  the `mirror_frames` step restored in `compose_draft_frames` (+ its import)
      grep `mirror_frames(frames_by_key` -> pipeline.py:422 present
      RED: pipeline::test_mirrored_rows_are_never_generated (1 failed / 31 passed)
           — the re-point is not vacuous. draft:: 62 passed: with `compose_sheet` packing
           `spec.rows()`, baked cells are computed and silently thrown away, so the
           pipeline test is the ONLY gate that sees it. That is why it asserts on the cell

      restore sha256 7ea2b13a... MATCH
  m4  the whole pre-H1 shape: m1 + m2 + `authored_rows` re-filtering `rows()`

      RED: draft::test_sprite_payload_state_rows_are_authored_only_and_front_first,

  m3  `EIGHT_WAY.authored` -> `("se", "s", "e", "ne", "n")`
