message:
test(tombstones): MCF-53 sweep — 32 of 155 CODE rows scanned nothing, in the registry a deletion campaign is verified by

`_production_files` resolved a scope token as `HERMES_ROOT / token.replace(".","/")`
and required a DIRECTORY. Every scope naming a MODULE therefore resolved to a
path that does not exist, was silently skipped, and contributed zero files. All
eleven module-scoped tokens in the table are real `.py` files:
`agent_runtime.status`, `.observability`, `.stream`, `.persona_runtime`,
`.persona_assignments`, `.store`, `.continuity`, `.child_events`,
`.prompt_observability`, `.operator_channels`, `.runtime_hud`.

Consequence, measured: **32 of 155 CODE rows scanned an EMPTY file set** and have
been green since they were written for the same reason an empty `for` loop is —
there was nothing to look at. Among them every row protecting the retired
`RepoBundleStore` / `repo_bundle_summary` / `repo_lock_summary` status
projections, the retired `daemon_*` / `qa.verdict_recorded` observability
vocabulary, the retired `task.` / `daemon.` / `proof.*` stream kinds, and the
retired supervisor prompt strings.

This is the S66 meta-invariant's own rule — "an unresolvable scope must be
COVERED, never SKIPPED" — which S66 enforced for ATTR and CLASS_ATTR while the
identical silent skip stayed one layer down in the CODE arm's file resolver.
The file header even states the principle about `_rendered` ("a silent skip is
how a scan scope quietly shrinks").

Three changes:
- `_production_files` resolves a scope token to a package DIRECTORY or a single
  MODULE FILE. It still does not decide what an UNRESOLVABLE scope means — a
  silent skip is precisely what it did wrong.
- `_unresolvable_scope_tokens` reports that separately, and a new
  `test_every_code_row_scope_resolves_to_something` answers it under the same
  covered-or-fail rule the ATTR arm uses: a scope naming neither a directory nor
  a module must be covered by a MODULE row, and a resolvable scope must yield at
  least one file. The failure names what to add instead of decaying.
- `test_the_scanner_is_not_vacuous` gains a MODULE-scoped canary. Both existing
  canaries are package-scoped, which is why they could not see this.

No collateral: all 32 rows are genuinely absent from their real module, so the
widening lands green (registry 1076 passed, up from 921 by the 155 new
scope cases).

Kill proof, both halves:
- With `_SABOTAGE_PROBE = "repo_bundle_summary"` added to `agent_runtime/status.py`,
  the OLD resolver replayed against the same tree scanned **0 files** for scope
  `('agent_runtime.status',)` and the row PASSED. The fixed registry failed:
  `s56 repo_bundle_summary (code) reappeared in ['agent_runtime/status.py']`
  (and `s24` likewise). Sabotage reverted byte-exact, sha256 9950b037… restored,
  `git diff` on status.py empty.
- The new scope gate itself: a probe row scoped to a typo'd `agent_runtime.staus`
  scans 0 files and now FAILS naming the fix; the same row on the real
  `agent_runtime.status` resolves to 1 file and passes.

`test_the_status_frame_dropped_every_constant_wire_row` scanned
`inspect.getsource(status.build_status)`. That is ONE statement — a `with`
wrapping `return _build_status_in_runtime_scope(...)` — 12 lines and 713

`_build_snapshot_uncoalesced`, a third time, in a gate holding ten wire keys.

message:
test(agent_runtime): MCF-53 sweep — s46's two unique forms could not match, and they were the only thing this gate held

`test_no_surviving_module_re_grows_the_lane` gated five forms. Two of them —
`"def apply_pending"` and `".apply_pending()"` — CANNOT MATCH.
`_code_without_prose` joins surviving tokens with newlines, so `def
apply_pending` renders as two tokens on two lines and `.apply_pending()` as
four. Neither substring can ever appear in the stripped text the gate reads.

S48's own file docstring already diagnoses this exact failure of the token-join
helper ("so a dotted assertion can never match and passes vacuously"). S46 was
never re-aimed, and this file's header says those two forms are its UNIQUE
contribution: the bare name cannot be a registry CODE row because
`agent.agent_runtime_helpers.apply_pending_steer_to_tool_results` is live and a
repo-wide row would be red against a correct tree. So the two vacuous forms were
the only thing this gate held that nothing else does.

The vacuity was also load-bearing for the green: the raw prefilter matched 2 of
760 files, one of them only because `def apply_pending_steer_to_tool_results`
CONTAINS `def apply_pending` as a substring. A naive raw-substring fix goes RED
on a correct tree — which is why the fix is AST. `node.name == "apply_pending"`
is EXACT, so the live steering helper is structurally not the same name, and the
ambiguity that forced the text form in the first place disappears.

Also added: a `scanned > 500` floor, a loud failure if a scan package moves
(silently smaller scope), and `test_the_structural_detector_fires_and_stays_quiet`
— synthetic source where the detector must name a planted definition and a
planted call and must NOT name the live lookalike. The three IDENTIFIER forms
stay text; each is a single token and survives the strip intact.

Kill proof, once per arm:
- `def apply_pending` re-grown on `Projector`: measured `in RAW=True`, `in
  STRIPPED=False` — the OLD gate read the stripped text and PASSED; the fixed
  gate failed with `agent_runtime\projector.py:def apply_pending@28`.
- `.apply_pending()` as a CALL with no definition: OLD form still absent from
  the stripped text and PASSED; fixed gate failed with
  `agent_runtime\projector.py:.apply_pending()@29`.

message:
fix(tests): restore CRLF on test_s47_wire_constant_field_removal.py

Self-caught. `819046b70c` rewrote the whole file's line endings LF-for-CRLF as
a side effect of the MCF-47(ii) edit: the guard was `src.count("\r\n") == 0`
over text read in universal-newline mode, which has ALREADY translated CRLF to
LF, so the check could not fail and said "LF file" about a CRLF one. The commit
landed 360 insertions / 315 deletions for a ~50-line change.

Endings restored; the range diff for this file is now 49 insertions / 4
deletions, proportional to the edit. Content byte-identical apart from the
endings, suite still 13 passed. Every other file in the range was re-checked
BYTE-WISE against its pre-range blob and none was flipped.

same class of un-failable check this whole line of work is about — count bytes,
and read `git diff --stat` for a line count out of proportion to the edit.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(auth): the device-code login persisted a network URL the siblings validate

`_nous_device_code_login` took `inference_base_url` straight out of the
device-code poll response through `_optional_base_url` and wrote it into
`auth_state`. Three sibling sites in the same file wrap exactly that field in
`_validate_nous_inference_url_from_network` when it arrives over the network.
This one did not, and it printed "Using portal-provided inference URL" while
doing it.

The validator's own docstring names this threat verbatim: a poisoned response
"could otherwise redirect every subsequent proxy request - bearing the user's
inference JWT - to an attacker-controlled endpoint."

The fix fails soft. The validator returns None for anything non-https or off
the host allowlist, and the existing `or requested_inference_url` then falls
back to the URL we asked for - the same path an absent field already took.

Why nothing caught it: the guard listed two exact byte strings,
`refreshed.get(...)` and `mint_payload.get(...)`. Neither names `token_data`,
which is what this site reads. And `mint_payload` has ZERO occurrences in the
whole 8,900-line file, so one of the two needles could never fail at all,
while its sibling asserted `mint_count == 0` - an assertion that something
which has never existed still does not.

The gate is now derived instead of enumerated: an AST rule that a
`_optional_base_url(x.get("inference_base_url"))` call is safe only as the
DIRECT ARGUMENT of the validator. That admits the nested form the shared-merge
path already uses at line 6106, and refuses a bare one wherever it appears and
whatever the payload variable is named. It carries an anti-vacuity floor, so a
walk that resolves nothing says so instead of reporting a clean tree, and the
census became a floor rather than an exact count - an exact count goes red on
a correct tree the moment a legitimate site is added, which teaches people to
edit the number instead of auditing the site.

Kill proof: restored the vulnerability, watched BOTH new gates go red (the
offender check naming the line, and the floor at 3 >= 4), restored the fix,
10/10 green.

Found by the MCF-53 gate sweep; verified, fixed and gated here.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent_runtime): MCF-54(ii) — the reap may fail, but not without saying which directory it left

`_reap_superseded_generations` removed superseded generations with
`shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`, and its docstring argued that a failed
removal was "not an event worth a line in a log an operator reads". The first
half of that is right and is unchanged here: a reader in another process holding
a generation open makes the removal fail on Windows, and a write-back that has
LANDED must never report failure because its housekeeping did not. The second
half did not follow. With no survivor count and no bound, a store that kept
failing to reap accumulated whole cached cores with nothing counting them — a
silent drop with no accounting, which is the class this lane refuses everywhere
else.

Ruled by MCF-59, including the operator's refinement that made the
recommendation better: the diagnostic must NAME the leftover directories, not
merely count them. A count says a problem exists; the names say which directory
to unlock or remove, and whether it is the same one every build (a permanently
held handle) or a different one each time (transient contention). Same rule as
MC-3's `diff=` tail.

What landed:

* `_reap_superseded_generations` now RETURNS the generation directories still on
  disk after its pass, re-listed rather than inferred — `ignore_errors=True`
  makes a failed removal indistinguishable from a successful one, so the only
  honest survivor count is taken from disk afterwards.
* `_receipt_generation_residue` emits ONE `snapshot_core_cache generation_residue`
  WARNING when the present count crosses `GENERATION_RESIDUE_BOUND` (3, counting
  the live one), carrying `present= bound= live= leftover=` and `generations=`
  LAST — the variable-length list, matching `_receipt_never_converged`'s `diff=`.
  Names are capped at eight, oldest first; `leftover=` always carries the true
  total so the cap cannot make a large residue read as a small one.
* The live generation is named as `live=` and is never among the directories the
  operator is told to remove.
* `ignore_errors=True` stays, the write-back still reports success, and nothing
  deletes harder because the bound was crossed. This adds accounting, not
  strictness.
* A row in the module's channel table, because adding a receipt means adding a
  row — `test_core_cache_channel_table.py` drives both directions.

Five gates in `test_core_cache_generation_residue.py`, each with its own killing
mutation; the failure is simulated at the removal itself (every generation
rmtree becomes the no-op that a held-open directory produces) rather than by
pre-planting directories, because a pre-planted directory would also be removed
by a mutant that reaped indiscriminately and would prove nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(auth): MCF-44 — the rotation cursor gets a field of its own, so advancing it stops rewriting the credentials

Round-robin's cursor was not stored anywhere: it WAS the order of the persisted
credential rows. "Advance by one" meant renumbering every entry's `priority` and
re-saving the whole credential store, which is why H1 had to invent a
non-persisting selection just so a READ could resolve a credential without
writing one. That stage was the symptom; this is the root cause the ledger row
names as the target shape — a typed cursor field, written separately from the
credential rows.

What landed:

* `hermes_cli/auth.py` grows a rotation sidecar beside `auth.json`
  (`credential_rotation.json`): `read_pool_rotation_state` /
  `write_pool_rotation_state`, same atomic 0600 write and the same auth-store
  lock, so no new lock ordering. The path is derived from `_auth_file_path()` so
  it inherits that function's pytest seat belt. The record holds credential IDS
  and nothing else — never token material. No global-root fallback,
  deliberately: a profile that borrows another store's credentials still rotates
  on its own, and sharing a cursor would let one profile consume another's
  rotation slots.
* `PoolRotationCursor` — a frozen dataclass with `last_selected_id`, plus
  `read_pool_rotation_cursor` / `write_pool_rotation_cursor`. A failed cursor
  write does NOT fail the selection (the caller already holds a usable
  credential), but it is not silent either: the degradation is named once per
  provider, because a silent drop with no accounting is the class this line
  exists to retire.
* `_select_unlocked`'s round-robin branch picks the available entry FOLLOWING
  the cursor in priority order and writes the cursor record. It no longer
  rebuilds `self._entries`, no longer renumbers `priority`, and no longer calls
  `_persist()`. Entries in cooldown are skipped without consuming a slot; a
  cursor naming an id that has left the pool restarts at the top instead of
  raising or pinning the first entry forever.

Three consequences, and the third was not in the row:

1. advancing the cursor no longer performs a full credential-store write;
2. `auth.json` no longer moves on a quiescent store, which is the MCF-16 half —
   `_save_auth_store` stamps `updated_at` unconditionally, so two logically
   identical writes produced different bytes on an input the snapshot build
   reads but does not declare;
3. `priority` now means operator intent only. It could not before, and for
   `anthropic` the two meanings actively FOUGHT: `_normalize_pool_priorities`
   re-derives that provider's priorities from source on every `load_pool`, so
   the normalizer overwrote the rotation on the very next load and round-robin
   degraded to "always the first source". Gate 4 in the new test drives exactly
   that, and it is red against the old design.

`select_without_persisting_rotation` SURVIVES this fix, for a reason that
outlives the one it was written for: a probe that persisted the cursor would
consume a rotation slot on behalf of a caller that never used the credential.
Its docstring, `_select_pool_entry`'s and `probe_runtime_provider`'s are updated
to describe the mechanism that now exists rather than the one that did.

Five gates in `tests/agent/test_credential_pool_rotation_cursor.py`, each with
its own killing mutation. Ids only cross into assertions — a `PooledCredential`
repr carries its token fields, and no assertion here may be one failure away
from printing credential-shaped material.

One of those gates was blind when first written and the killing mutation is
what found it: "rotate twice and compare the priority list" is GREEN against
the old design, because two rotations of a two-entry pool return the list to
where it started. It now drives exactly one rotation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(auth): MCF-45 — least_used counted requests in memory and persisted them nowhere

`_select_unlocked` picked `min(available, key=request_count)` and incremented
through `_replace_entry`, a pure in-memory list swap. Nothing on that path
called `_persist`; the only write on the whole selection path was round-robin's.
`load_pool()` rebuilds the pool from disk on every call, so the counter reached
disk on NO PATH AT ALL — every fresh process re-derived the same "least used"
entry and the strategy was inert across processes. Same class as MCF-13: state
that never reaches the place that reads it.

What landed:

* `PoolRotationCursor` gains `request_counts` (`credential id -> requests`) on
  the same sidecar record MCF-44 introduced. One record because it is one
  question — "where is selection?" — asked by two strategies: least-used's usage
  vector is its cursor exactly as `last_selected_id` is round-robin's. A second
  record would be a second authority over the same answer.
* `_sync_usage_counts_from_store` re-reads the durable counts before every
  least-used selection and merges them into memory by MAX. Re-read per
  selection, not per pool, because the agent runtime holds ONE pool object per
  agent for the life of the process (`agent._credential_pool`) — a pool loaded
  once would be blind to every sibling, which is this defect one layer in. MAX
  in both directions: disk never lowers a live in-memory count, memory never
  hides a higher count another process wrote.
* The increment is persisted through `write_pool_rotation_cursor`, so a durable
  counter costs no credential write. Persisting it via `_persist()` would have
  made every request rewrite the whole credential store and re-created the very
  defect MCF-44 just retired.
* Constructing a least-used pool adopts the durable counts immediately, so every
  reader of `entries()` — `hermes auth` listings, the web server's pool view —
  sees the number the strategy actually decides on rather than a stale row copy.
* A probe (`persist_rotation=False`) rotates and counts in memory but writes
  nothing, so it cannot charge a request nobody made.

CORRECTION TO THE ROW, per MCF-61 and verified here: the parenthetical "pools
are not cached" is FALSE — the agent runtime caches one pool per agent object,
predating the row — so within one long-lived process least-used already
distributed. The row's TITLE, the cross-process claim, is exactly right. Gate 3
pins the in-process behaviour that already worked, so a later change cannot
"fix" this by regressing the half that was correct.

Five gates in `tests/agent/test_credential_pool_least_used_durability.py`, each
with its own killing mutation, including one that pins the MCF-44 boundary: the
durable counter must move `auth.json` by zero bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(agent_runtime): HB-1 — the risk-flag vocabulary was an island behind a predicate that could not fire

`agent_runtime/risk_flags.py` (91 lines: a 40-name flag vocabulary, a
prefix set, a normalizer and a membership test) had exactly one
production reader — an arm of `serde._coerce`:

    if annotation.__name__ == "Task" and isinstance(upgraded, dict):

`agent_runtime` has had no `Task` dataclass since the mission-lane
removal (`test_models_serde` asserts `not hasattr(runtime_models,
"Task")`), and an AST class-definition walk over all thirteen
production packages finds ONE `class Task` in the tree: upstream's
`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`, which imports nothing from `serde` and is
never handed to `_coerce`. The predicate could not fire, so the module
was reachable only from itself.

Census method: AST `ClassDef` walk for the predicate's subject, plus
grep for the module/symbol names (identifier-shaped, no dotted or
string-literal forms in play).

Registry: two s72 rows — `Form.MODULE agent_runtime.risk_flags` and a
`Form.CODE` row for the four names, repo-wide. CODE as well as MODULE
because a re-grown normalizer would most plausibly arrive as a private
copy in another module rather than as this import.

Kill proof, both halves: (a) `KNOWN_RISK_FLAGS = ...` reintroduced into
`serde.py` -> RED, `s72 KNOWN_RISK_FLAGS (code) reappeared in
['agent_runtime/serde.py']`; (b) `risk_flags.py` recreated -> RED,
`s72 agent_runtime.risk_flags (module)`. Both reverted; the whole
registry file is 1085 passed.

Suites: test_models_serde.py + test_tombstone_registry.py +
test_persona_chat_history_curation.py = 1147 passed / 0 failed.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(agent_runtime): HA-2 — eleven copies of five helpers, and the gate that can see through a rename

Every duplicate here survived earlier sweeps for the same reason: nothing in
this repo reads BODIES, and the names disagreed.

FOLDED (survivor -> the copies it retired)

* `serde.write_json_atomic`  <- `serve_registry._atomic_write_json`,
  `serve_socket._write_json_atomic`. The same three words in a different
  order. The two OTHER same-named helpers (`chat_session_scope`,
  `mission_chat_steer`) are genuinely different and were left alone.
* `serde.section_rows`       <- `_rows` in read_model / snapshot / stream.
* `serde.optional_text`      <- `stream._text`, `runtime_hud._text`,
  `read_model._optional_text`, `workspace_scope._norm`. The audit predicted
  three; the AST found four.
* `serde.safe_id`            <- `office_store._safe_id`, `board_store._safe_id`,
  `store._safe_model_id`.
* `paths.safe_path_token`    <- `realm_sync._safe_token`,
  `skill_promotion._safe_token`, `persona_profile_binding._artifact_token`
  (whose docstring said outright "Mirror of `realm_sync._safe_token`").
* `paths.unlink_quietly`     <- `chat_live_log._unlink_quietly`,
  `mission_chat_steer._unlink_quietly`.

Homes chosen for a reason: `serde.py` has NO relative imports, so nothing in
the package can cycle through it, and `paths.py` already owns filesystem
naming. `serde.write_json_atomic` is deliberately NOT folded onto upstream's
`utils.atomic_json_write` — that one fsyncs and preserves mode/owner but opens
its temp file in default text mode, so on Windows it writes CRLF, and every
record on this lane is compared as LF-canonical bytes. Two writers, two
guarantees; the docstring says so, so the next reader does not fold them.

WHAT THE AUDIT MISSED, found by re-deriving instead of trusting

* `persona_profile_binding._artifact_token` — a FOURTH `_safe_token` copy.
* `workspace_scope._norm` — a FOURTH `_optional_text` copy.
* Two of the `_safe_token` reads were FUNCTION-LOCAL imports (`store.py:432`,
  `profile_artifact_sync.py:482`) — invisible to any top-level import scan,
  and both would have crashed on the fold. `paths._safe_path_token` also had
  cross-module private callers in `locks.py` (5) and `board_store.py` (4).
* Census method: AST body hashing with docstrings stripped and the function's
  own name, parameter names and annotations normalized away. A hash that keeps
  the signature does NOT match `read_model._rows` to `snapshot._rows` (one
  annotates `Any`, the other is bare) — i.e. it misses the family the audit
  actually named.

THE GATE (`tests/agent_runtime/test_duplicate_helper_bodies.py`)

Deleting eleven copies is worth less than making the twelfth impossible. The
gate hashes every module-level function in `agent_runtime/` the way described
above and fails on any un-baselined collision. `_GRANDFATHERED` holds the five
groups left standing, each with its reason, and has a SECOND test asserting
every row is still a real duplicate — so the baseline can only shrink and a
fixed group cannot leave a stale claim behind. Three of those five rows are
NEW findings this gate produced on its first run (`board_content_hash` ==
`office_content_hash`, `mcp_lane._clean` == `tool_visibility._clean_names`,
`default_scope._get_realm` == `._get_workspace`), and the lock-primitive pair
is a documented REFUSAL, not a deferral.

Kill proof, both halves. (a) A copy of `optional_text` reintroduced into
`read_model.py` under the name `_blank_to_none` with a different parameter
name and a different annotation -> RED, naming
`read_model.py::_blank_to_none == serde.py::optional_text`. (b) Reverted ->
green. The FIRST version of the gate passed that sabotage, which is how the
signature/parameter normalization above got written: a gate that cannot fail
certifies nothing.

No tombstone rows: nothing was retired, every name still exists at exactly one
definition, and the registry's own policy excludes ordinary private-helper
churn. The invariant is "one definition", and the gate is what asserts it.

`agent_runtime/store.py` and `errors.py` are on the audit's EXCLUSION list and
are touched anyway: one import line + one call in `store.py` (a function-local
import of a symbol this commit moves — leaving it would be a crash, not a
deferral), one docstring word in `errors.py`. Both lanes read EMPTY.

Suites: full `tests/agent_runtime/` = 5969 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed
(baseline 5958/1/0; +11 is this gate's 2 tests plus HB-1's registry rows).
`tests/fixtures/stream_frames/MANIFEST.sha256` unchanged. Live-root canary
still revision 67.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(agent_runtime): HA-1 + HA-3 — the parameter whose comment claimed the opposite of what it did

HA-1 and HA-3 are one commit because together they are 67 deleted lines and
they share a checkpoint; both are recorded separately below.

HA-1 — parameters accepted and thrown away
------------------------------------------
`build_snapshot(task_store=, run_store=, incident_store=)` -> the whole
three-level chain. An AST `Name(Load)` walk over
`_build_snapshot_in_runtime_scope` finds the three names never loaded, while
`agent_store` / `event_log` / `prompt_skills_catalogs` beside them ARE. Their
only surviving effect was to set `custom_stores`, the flag that BYPASSES
coalescing — under a comment reading

    Injected stores (tests, doctors) must observe exactly their own fixtures

which is the opposite of what happened: a caller passing `task_store=<fixture>`
got an uncoalesced build of the DEFAULT stores and was told it was looking at
its own. Two tests were doing exactly that. `status.build_status` is the
function that really reads those three and is untouched.

`observability._risk_if_ignored(kind, ...)` -> `kind` never loaded; the body
branches on `severity` alone, so the parameter advertised a kind-specific risk
sentence the function cannot produce.

`state_patches.emit_persona_instance_remove(reason=)` -> `emit_state_patch` has
no field to carry a reason, so the caller computed `safe_reason` and handed it
to a function that dropped it. **The audit was WRONG that the caller-side edit
could wait for a later `EXCL` stage**: a call site passing a kwarg the callee
no longer accepts is a TypeError at the exact moment a persona instance
retires. Both halves land here, and one test pins them together so they cannot
be split again.

HA-3 — fields and walks nothing reads
-------------------------------------
* `PersonaInstance.child_events_offset` — the fifth field of the block S70
  pruned four from. Same block, same argument, missed.
* `GoalRuntimeInstance.started_by`, `.lease_expires_at`, `AgentRun.iterations_used`.
* `realm_sync._board_artifacts` / `._office_artifacts` — the pre-ML-8 publish
  walks, orphaned by the `_board_publish_scan` / `_office_publish_scan`
  chokepoints that exist BECAUSE two independent walks disagreed.
* `ProjectionAccountant.dropped_by_design` — a second authority for a number
  `summary()` already carries as `reasons` + `by_design`; only tests asked it,
  and they now do the subtraction a real reader has to do.

WIRED, not deleted: `archive_orphaned_surface(updated_by=)`. The one verb in
this store that moves an entire surface was also the only one whose event could
not say who moved it. It now travels on `office.surface.updated`.

No contract bump: none of the fields is on any wire allowlist or in any of the
four `tests/fixtures/stream_frames/*.json` goldens, and `serde._coerce` builds
kwargs from `fields()` and ignores unknown keys, so persisted rows still load.
`MANIFEST.sha256` unchanged.

Census method: AST `Name(Load)` / attribute walk over all thirteen production
packages for the parameters and fields; grep for the two private walk names
(identifier-shaped, no string forms).

GATES, and why there are two kinds
----------------------------------
Tombstone rows (`CLASS_ATTR` x5, `CODE` x2) for the fields and the walks. The
registry deliberately CANNOT hold a dropped parameter — its own docstring says
a name scan would fire on any unrelated local — so the parameters get
`tests/agent_runtime/test_s72_dropped_parameters.py`, which checks the
signature by calling. It also asserts the three stores that ARE read are still
accepted, so it is not a gate that can only say yes.

Kill proof, both halves, three sabotages:
(a) `task_store` re-added at all three builder levels -> RED, both the
    signature pin and `DID NOT RAISE TypeError`;
(b) `child_events_offset` re-added to `PersonaInstance` -> RED,
    `s72 models.PersonaInstance.child_events_offset (class_attr)`;
(c) `_board_artifacts` re-added to `realm_sync.py` -> RED,
    `s72 _board_artifacts (code) reappeared in ['agent_runtime/realm_sync.py']`.
All three reverted; the three gate files are 1103 passed together.

Suites: test_parity, test_running_work, test_models_serde,
test_s53_lane_write_lane_removal, test_observability, test_snapshot_coalesce,
test_snapshot, test_state_patches, test_stream_patch, test_office_store,
test_realm_sync, test_persona_assignments, test_s28_status_observe_shrink =
425 passed / 0 failed. Full `tests/agent_runtime/` checkpoint runs once at the
end of the agent_runtime group rather than per stage (15 min each); recorded
here so the exception is not silent.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(agent_runtime): HB-2 + HB-3 + HB-4 — the vocabulary that listed a value nothing constructs

Three stages, 133 deleted lines, one commit: each is small and they share a
checkpoint. Recorded separately so the exception is not silent.

HB-2 — four roll-up vocabularies with no reader
-----------------------------------------------
`PLAN_ACTIONS`, `PROMOTION_BLOCK_REASONS`,
`WIRE_USER_MESSAGE_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`, `DISPATCH_SESSION_REASONS`. Each is a
frozenset/tuple over constants that are ALREADY used at their own sites; the
roll-up itself had zero executable readers between the four.

`PLAN_ACTIONS` is the argument for cutting rather than enforcing them. Its
comment said it was "pinned so callers branch on stable strings" — and it
listed a FIFTH action, `refuse_ambiguous_source`, that nothing had ever
constructed. An AST walk finds `PromotionPlan(...)` only inside
`skill_promotion.py` and every site spells `refuse_invalid`; the CLI reaches
the lane through `classify_promotion` alone. So the constant claiming to close
the vocabulary was the only thing in the tree asserting a value outside it, and
`execute_promotion` carried a branch for it. A set nothing consults does not
make a vocabulary closed — it makes a second place to forget.

The one test on any of them asserted `REASON_CLARIFY_TOKEN in
DISPATCH_SESSION_REASONS` — against a tuple literally built from that
constant, i.e. a test that could not fail. It now asks whether the handler
actually emits that spelling.

HB-3 — one spelling per question
--------------------------------
* `personas.MOTHBALLED_ROLES` — a THIRD spelling of a fact
  `persona_lifecycle.MOTHBALLED_ROLE_TOKENS` owns and `is_runtime_persona`
  reads. Its comment said it existed so nothing would hand-roll
  `role == "pm"` — with zero readers, while the module IMPORTED the two live
  sets and used neither (the repo's single genuinely unused import, now gone).
* `chat_live_log.chat_live_log_root()` — a wrapper over
  `capture_chat_live_log_root` adding a lock-read fast path and no answer.
* `McpAdmissionOutcome.registered_tool_names` — write-only: built from
  `box["tools"]`, carried on a frozen dataclass, read by nobody.
  (`tools/mcp_tool.py::_registered_tool_names` is a different token.)
* `AgentCreateOutcome.ok` — asked only by tests; production spells the same
  question `outcome.refusal is not None`. Three asserts rewritten.
* `mcp_admission`'s `role = str(role_from_persona(persona).value)` try-arm,
  labelled "defensive". It was inverted: `AgentRole` has one member, that
  member is mothballed, and `coerce_agent_role` returns a plain `str` for
  everything else — so `.value` was the branch that could not be taken and the
  `except` was the live path. `str()` covers both (a StrEnum stringifies to its
  own value). `AgentRole` itself is KEPT and now says in its docstring that it
  is retired residue, so it stops reading as a live taxonomy.

HB-4 — orphans and rot
----------------------
* `BoardStore._list_active_cards` / `._list_archived_cards`, orphaned by ML-8's
  `_ordering_cards` chokepoint. Rowed despite being private: they return
  `.cards` and DROP the scan's unreadable count, which is exactly the state
  `CardsUnreadable` was raised to prevent.
* `persona_chat_history._persona_chat_creation_sort_key`.
* `agent_runtime/docs/snapshot_line_count_exception.md` — cites 3,170 lines
  against a `snapshot.py` of 2,621, and of the four seams it names as the split
  plan only `_parity_envelope` exists.
* Doc rot: a broken relative link to a deleted `worker_sessions.py`; a plan
  saying `rebind_persona_profile` has "zero callers" when
  `harness agent set-profile` calls it; and
  `test_neko_supervisor_uses_configured_head_agent_profile_when_not_explicit`,
  whose body asserts the OPPOSITE of its name, renamed to
  `..._does_not_inherit_head_agent_profile`.

A REGISTRY ROW SHAPE BUG, FOUND BY THE KILL PROOF
-------------------------------------------------
The two HB-3 `Form.ATTR` rows were first written as
`"personas.MOTHBALLED_ROLES"` under `scope=_AR`. The ATTR assertion is
`hasattr(<scope module>, row.text)`, so that spells
`hasattr(agent_runtime, "personas.MOTHBALLED_ROLES")` — False for every tree
that has ever existed. **The row passed a full green registry run and was a
gate that could not fail.** It was caught only by re-adding the symbol and
watching the row NOT go red — the same class as this morning's 32-of-155
rows-scanning-zero-files fix. Reshaped to a bare name with the owning module as
scope, and the shape rule is now a comment above the rows. CLASS_ATTR is the
form that takes the dotted spelling; ATTR is not.

Kill proof, both halves, one sabotage per row FORM:
(a) `DISPATCH_SESSION_REASONS` re-added -> RED (CODE);
(b) `MOTHBALLED_ROLES` re-added to `personas.py` -> RED (ATTR, after reshape;
    GREEN before it, which is the finding above);
(c) `AgentCreateOutcome.ok` re-added -> RED (CLASS_ATTR);
(d) `snapshot_line_count_exception.md` recreated -> RED (PATH).
All four reverted; registry + duplicate-body gate + dropped-parameter pin =
1122 passed together.

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(hermes_cli,tools,scripts): H-CLI-2 + H-P1 + H-P2 + H-P3 — advertised and unreachable, at three levels

H-CLI-2 — the flag, and the option to have the flag
---------------------------------------------------
`--all-persona-profiles` on `harness install-harness-skills`: self-described in
its own help text as a "Compatibility flag", dest read by no handler. It was
invisible to `test_every_stage42_global_flag_is_honored` for a structural
reason — `install-harness-skills` never calls `_add_stage42_global_args`, so it
is not a stage42 verb, so its registrations were outside that gate's scope
entirely.

The `cursor` / `since` branches in `_add_stage42_global_args`: one level up
from a flag. AST census of this file — 58 `_add_stage42_global_args(...)` call
sites, and the complete set of control tokens any of them names is
`{dry_run: 29, yes: 7, sort: 7, idempotency_key: 3, limit: 2}`. Neither
`cursor` nor `since` appears, so `--cursor` / `--since` could not be registered
on any verb in the surface's history. (The audit put the call-site count at 37;
by AST it is 58, which makes the conclusion stronger, not weaker. The
neighbouring `read --since-offset` is a different, live flag.)

New gate `tests/hermes_cli/test_harness_flag_and_control_reachability.py`
covers BOTH levels and every subparser, stage42 or not: 430 registrations
scanned, 0 unread; and every branched control token must have a caller, plus
the reverse (a caller naming a token the helper does not branch on believes it
opted in and did not). The `reads` set is `args.<dest>` attribute access and
the `getattr` string form only — bare string constants are excluded on purpose,
or the retirement note naming a removed flag would keep that flag's gate green.

H-P1 — a single-name pin over a two-member family
-------------------------------------------------
`scripts/certification_ladder.py` (57 lines) drove `harness burn-in`, a verb
S6 retired. Its twin `scripts/cert_streak.py` was deleted then and pinned ever
since by `tests/scripts/test_cert_streak.py` — which named ONE module, so the
surviving driver sat beside its tombstoned twin for two months, invisible to
the exact test written to prevent this. The pin is now parameterized over both
names; a PATH tombstone row is the second half.

`tools/agent_chat_dispatch.py`: `shutdown_dispatch_executor` (docstring:
"tests; never on a live lane" — no test called it) and `is_supervised_here`
(born in the same commit as the live `supervised_dispatch_ids`, never
adopted). Two ways to ask one question is how they drift.

H-P2 — a branch that could not be taken, and a schema that lied
--------------------------------------------------------------
`board_tool._resolve_board_target`'s `if task_id:` rung: `agent_runtime.store`
exports `TaskStore` as `TaskStoreStub`, whose `.get()` is `-> NoReturn` and
always raises, so the branch could only ever fall through. Deleted with its
`paths` import, and the module docstring stops advertising a three-rung ladder
that has two. `BOARD_CARDS_SCHEMA` and its mirror in `tool_full_descriptions.py`
both promised a "linked goal" field removed at S3/S4 — a wire description
lying to the model, which a test already asserts is gone from the data.

Also proved here, against `upstream/main` (the probe is live — `cli.py` and
`tools/mcp_tool.py` both resolve): `tools/board_tool.py` is FORK-ADDED, not
upstream. `agent_runtime/task_store_stub.py`'s "DO NOT DELETE" docstring rests
entirely on the opposite premise. Reported, not acted on — see H-P4 ruling (i).

H-P3 — three stale rationales
-----------------------------
* `gateway_home_receipt`'s `RESOLUTION_*` comment claimed main.py imports the
  constants "rather than each hard-coding a string literal". main.py hard-codes
  all four inline (`:665, :677, :679, :702`) and always has, so this was two
  independent copies of one wire vocabulary with nothing comparing them. main.py
  CANNOT import them — the pre-parse runs before any hermes module is
  importable — so the seam stays and a four-literal pin now holds it.
* `upstream_sync_gate.AGENT_TOOL_SEAMS` named `tools/agent_chat_tool.py` but
  not `board_tool.py` or `agent_chat_dispatch.py`, so a sync touching either
  skipped the launcher lane and reported PASS. Widened to `tools/` as a whole,
  so the NEXT agent tool arrives covered rather than arriving invisible.
* `DEFAULT_LAUNCHER_ROOT` was a bare committed machine path; now
  `ETERNIALAUNCHER_ROOT` with that path as fallback (`--launcher-root` still
  wins).
* `windows_env.py` told readers to "keep the two in sync" with
  `hermes_cli/uninstall.py`. `git cat-file -e upstream/main:` says
  `uninstall.py` is UPSTREAM and `windows_env.py` is fork-added, so that is an
  instruction the fork is forbidden to follow. Retargeted to say route around
  it.

AUDIT ROW THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE: H-P3 also claimed
`scripts/backend_postgres_proof.py` hard-codes a personal machine path as a
committed default. It does not — it already reads `ETERNIABACKEND_ROOT` with
the path as fallback, which is the shape the row asks for.

Kill proof, both halves, four sabotages:
(a) `--all-persona-profiles` re-added -> RED, `harness.py:1356
    skills.all_persona_profiles`;
(b) the `cursor` control branch re-added -> RED, naming the token and the 58
    call sites that cannot ask for it;
(c) `certification_ladder.py` recreated -> RED twice, the PATH tombstone AND
    the widened cert-streak pin naming `scripts.certification_ladder`;
    `is_supervised_here` re-added -> RED (CODE row);
(d) `RESOLUTION_ACTIVE_PROFILE_MARKER` renamed to `"sticky_marker"` -> RED,
    "main.py writes no such literal".
All reverted.

Suites: test_harness_flag_and_control_reachability + test_harness_cli (60),
test_persona_skill_policy (10), test_board_agent_tools + test_board_store +
test_t6b_brief_descriptions + test_agent_chat_dispatch + test_dispatch_store +
test_cert_streak (124), test_gateway_home_receipt + test_dep_ensure +
test_upstream_sync_gate (31), test_harness_json_root_observability (5),
test_tombstone_registry (1122) — all passed, 0 failed. `tests/hermes_cli` files
were run individually with `python -m pytest`, never the directory (a
directory-wide run performs a gateway update and starts a gateway process).

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(hermes_cli,agent_runtime): H-CLI-1a + H-CLI-1b — 25 exit codes the runtime could not spend, and the gate that keeps the 26th out

`ERROR_EXIT_CODES` is the harness's exit-status contract: the launcher and
every operator script branch on the numbers, and `error.code` is what a human
is told went wrong. It carried 71 rows. **25 existed only as their own dict
entry** — no `code=` site, no `raise ValueError(<code>)`, no
mapped-and-raised exception class, nothing in the installer PS1, and no reader
in either repo. Two were worse than inert: `goal_not_found`'s hint sent the
operator to `hermes harness goal list`, a verb that no longer exists.

THE CENSUS WAS REGENERATED, NOT INHERITED — and it corrected itself twice
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
The audit's number was 22 (+2). Mine is 25. Getting there took three passes,
and both wrong answers are worth recording because each is a gate-shaped
mistake:

1. **A naive producer scan said 46 dead.** It looked for `code=` kwargs and
   class attributes and missed `raise ValueError("<code>")` — which the
   `ValueError` arm of `_error_code_for_exception` maps straight through when
   the message is a table key. Under-counting producers is how a live code
   gets deleted.
2. **Adding the launcher flipped it to 1 dead.** Because the scan counted hits
   in `mission_control_tombstone_registry_test.dart` — the launcher's own
   registry, where those names appear as PROHIBITIONS. **A name in a tombstone
   table is proof of absence, and counting it as use marked 45 dead rows
   live.** Same shape as the MC-5 `unsubscribe` trap this audit was warned
   about: the token was never the unit of meaning.
3. The launcher half was also VACUOUS at first — a POSIX-style path that
   Windows Python does not resolve, so `LAUNCH.exists()` was False and the
   whole launcher scan silently did nothing. It now asserts the root is a
   directory before scanning.

KEPT, with reasons, not deleted
-------------------------------
Five hermes-unspendable codes stay, each with a real reader on the other side:
`runtime_unavailable` (the LAUNCHER mints it — `mission_control_bridge.dart`
maps a failed CLI process to `exitCode == 124 ? 'timeout' :
'runtime_unavailable'`); `wrong_runtime_root` and `proof_missing` (the
launcher spells both as live SNAPSHOT vocabulary — a different lane, the same
word); `blueprint_not_found` (one launcher stage38 fixture); and
`provider_auth_expired` — a launcher test asserting a code hermes has no way
to emit, which is a cross-stack defect recorded rather than papered over.
Deleting that row first would have turned an honest gap into a silent one.

The four `install_*` codes are LIVE and were never candidates: they are
produced by `scripts/install-mission-control-hermes.ps1`, which the launcher
runs. The original lane's grep roots omitted `scripts/`, which is how they
came one commit from being reaped. The gate now has a dedicated test asserting
it still traces them to that installer.

H-CLI-1b — the exceptions that existed to be mapped
----------------------------------------------------
`InvalidTransition`, `StaleRun`, `ProofMissing`, `RuntimeRootMismatch`: an AST
`Raise` walk over all thirteen production packages AND `tests/` finds ZERO
raise sites for any of them. Each had exactly three references — its own
`class` statement, one import in `harness_support`, one row in
`_error_code_for_exception`'s type->code tuple. Alive solely to be translated
by the thing that translates them.

Their codes did NOT all go with them, and the split is the interesting part:
`invalid_transition` / `stale_run` had no reader anywhere and went with the
25; `proof_missing` / `wrong_runtime_root` stay, because the launcher uses
those words on another lane and both remain spendable through the ValueError
arm.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: `WorkspaceUnresolved` and `"workspace_unresolved"`,
added by MC-8/P10 to this same file with a real raise site
(`office_store.py:442`). Conflating it with the old four in one edit was the
specific hazard flagged at dispatch.

THE GATE (`tests/hermes_cli/test_error_exit_code_producers.py`)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Deleting 25 rows is worth less than making the 26th impossible. Every table
key must be spendable by one of three routes — a literal at a producing site,
a mapped exception class **with at least one raise site**, or the installer
PS1 — or sit in `_KEPT_UNSPENDABLE` with the reader that justifies it. The
mapped-AND-raised distinction is the whole point: those four classes were
mapped and never raised, so four codes looked produced and were not.

`_KEPT_UNSPENDABLE` has the second test every baseline in this repo now
carries: a code that GAINS a producer must lose its row, so the list can only
shrink and cannot leave a stale claim. Runtime 13s (the scan is memoized and
pre-filtered on the ~10 mapped class names rather than on the word `raise`,
which nearly every file contains — that filter is what took it from 127s).

Kill proof, both halves:
(a) `lane_not_found` re-added to the table -> RED, naming it and telling the
    author to wire a producer, delete the row, or baseline it with a reader;
(b) a `raise ValueError("provider_auth_expired")` added to `observability.py`
    -> RED on the OTHER test, "in _KEPT_UNSPENDABLE but now HAVE a producer —
    delete their rows in the commit that wired them".
Both reverted; the gate is 9 passed.

`agent_runtime/errors.py` is on the audit's EXCLUSION list. Both lanes read
EMPTY, and this is the class deletion H-CLI-1b was always going to require.

Suites: test_error_exit_code_producers (9), test_harness_cli (57),
test_office_orphan_surface_archive, test_tombstone_registry (1145),
test_office_class_key_guard + test_office_store + test_store + test_board_store
(96) — all passed, 0 failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(hermes_cli): NEW-1 REFUSED — zero callers is a phase, not a verdict, for a chokepoint

The audit's NEW-1 row proposed reaping `_append_persona_operator_turn`,
`_append_persona_assistant_text` and `_persist_persona_chat_row` (~184
production lines) plus ~250 test lines across six files, as a test-only-alive
island. **The census is correct — zero production callers, every "prod" hit
intra-island, independently re-derived here by an AST `Name(Load)` walk. The
conclusion is refused.**

WHY
---
* **This is not an orphan that lost its lane; it is the door the lane goes
  through, and the lane is currently entering another way.** Mission chat
  stopped appending its own operator/assistant rows when native session
  continuity landed — the runtime persists them WITH the turn. The explicit
  route did not become wrong, it became unused.
* **The relay lane is not hypothetical.** `_append_persona_operator_turn
  (relay_marker=)` carries sender attribution into `finish_reason`, and that
  wire behaviour has already broken silently for eleven days once.
  `test_relay_session_lifecycle.py` drives it at three sites.
* **Deleting one function would delete five enforcement points**: redaction at
  the per-role limit, the assistant-row idempotency check, the live-log mirror,
  typed `PersonaChatPersistenceError` reporting, and the `required=` raise-or-
  degrade split. The next explicit append site would hand-roll all five — which
  is the failure this seam's SHAPE already records. Its mirror is bound by a
  CONTEXT MANAGER and not by a trailing call because the first cut hooked
  append sites by convention and immediately missed one
  (`continuity.return_summary_to_parent_session`), whose rows never reached the
  live log.
* `test_agent_chat_log_path.py` uses the writer to prove the LIVE log keeps
  growing after a path is handed out. Its subject is the live lane; the island
  is the vehicle. Reaping it would mean hand-rolling a SessionDB append plus a
  mirror inside a test — the copy-paste the seam exists to prevent.

WHAT SHIPS INSTEAD
------------------
Under-used is not dead, and the fix for under-used is a contract, not a
funeral. `tests/hermes_cli/test_persona_chat_append_seam.py` pins all five
guarantees plus the relay-marker path, so a future author who wants the seam
gone has to argue with a behaviour rather than with a line count. The keep
decision is recorded in `_persist_persona_chat_row`'s own docstring — and one
of the tests asserts that it stays there, because a refusal nobody can find
gets re-litigated at every audit.

The mirror-wrap pin checks the SHAPE, not just the presence: it asserts
`session_db.append_message` sits INSIDE the `with mirrored_persona_chat_append`
block. A trailing-call version would satisfy a naive "is the mirror called"
check while reintroducing exactly the drift that motivated the context manager.

Kill proof, both halves: `append_message` moved OUT of the `with` block (left
in place, one statement later — the regression a reviewer would most plausibly
wave through) -> RED, "`session_db.append_message` moved OUT of the mirror
context manager. The SessionDB row and its live-log line can now drift apart".
Reverted; 12 passed.

OPERATOR QUESTION, recorded not answered: is the explicit-append lane coming
back (relay / CLI sends), or should the persona-chat write path be declared
native-only? If the latter this goes — deliberately, with its five guarantees
re-homed first, not as a line-count reap.

Suites: test_persona_chat_append_seam, test_c8_one_order_guards,
test_mission_chat_usage_single_writer, test_agent_chat_log_path,
test_relay_session_lifecycle = 94 passed / 0 failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(hermes_cli): H-CLI-3 — two verbs cut, one refused, on one test: does the data have another door?

The audit proposed three uninvoked verbs. Two went, one did not, and the line
between them is the useful part of this commit.

CUT — `harness persona instance resolve-chat-turn`
--------------------------------------------------
A second parser binding the SAME handler as `mission-chat turn-resolve`
(`_cmd_mission_chat_turn_resolve`), with the same four required flags and the
instance id as a positional instead of a flag. Duplicate authority for one
operation, zero invocations in either repo, and the launcher has always emitted
`turn-resolve` — verified by grepping `lib/features/mission_control/` for both
spellings. The alias was reachable only by a human who read the wrong doc line.

CUT — `harness workspace actors`
--------------------------------
Listed persona-instance summaries filtered by workspace, off the same store,
through the same `persona_instance_summary`, that `persona list` already reads.
A convenience filter over an available superset.

REFUSED — `harness contracts dump`
-----------------------------------
The audit's own ruling 5 says KEEP `contract_manifest`. Cutting the verb makes
that incoherent: `contracts dump` is its ONLY production reader, so with the
verb gone the constant's whole importer set is `test_s15_event_contract_
pruning` — the closed loop the comment directly above `contract_manifest` cites
as the reason a symbol is NOT covered code. It is one decision, not two.

Resolved KEEP-BOTH:
* "no committed invocation" is weak evidence for a read-only DIAGNOSTIC.
  Operators run `observe`, `migrate` and `snapshot` by hand too; none appears in
  a committed script and nobody proposes cutting them.
* it is the only door onto the canonical contract registry. A registry you
  cannot dump is a registry you cannot audit, and 12 lines is a poor trade.

**The test the three verbs were judged on: cut a verb whose data has another
door; keep a verb that IS the only door.** Recorded in
`decision_contract_registry.py` beside the constant, where the next sweep will
look, so this is not re-litigated.

OWED, CROSS-STACK, NOT DONE HERE: the launcher's committed
`test/features/mission_control/fixtures/hermes_cli_contract.json` still carries
both cut paths. Its gate asserts launcher-emitted argv EXISTS in the dump and
NOT the reverse (read at `harness_capability_argv_test.dart`), so it stays
green — but the fixture is now stale in the extra direction as well as the 14
paths it was already behind. The refresh is a launcher commit, and the launcher
repo is owned by another agent right now.

Kill proof, both halves: `workspace_actors` parser + handler reference re-added
to `harness.py` -> RED, `s72 _cmd_workspace_actors (code) reappeared in
['hermes_cli/harness.py']`. Reverted. (The replacement comments naming both cut
verbs do NOT re-trip the row — the registry's scanner parses to an AST, where
comments do not survive, which is the property that makes a retirement note
safe to write beside a tombstone.)

Suites: test_tombstone_registry + test_harness_cli +
test_harness_json_root_observability = 1192 passed / 0 failed;
test_harness_flag_and_control_reachability, test_s15_event_contract_pruning,
test_s54_individual_dead_symbols all green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
refactor(agent_runtime): HA-5 + HB-4-EXCL — a perf optimisation for a cost nobody pays, and a read that dropped its own denominator

The audit's `EXCL`-tagged rows. Both launcher lanes read EMPTY, so the
exclusion no longer applies; recorded here rather than assumed.

`IncidentStore.list_open_with_closed_count`
-------------------------------------------
A snapshot-lane optimisation: return the open rows plus a COUNT of the closed
tail, so a runtime with thousands of closed incident files does not coerce them
all into the recursive `Incident` graph on every frame. Its caller went with the
incident observability S9 removed from the wire. `status.build_status` — the one
function that still takes an incident store — calls `list_all()`. What was left
was a real performance argument for a cost nobody pays, and three asserts that
were the method's only exercise. Its dedicated
`..._skips_closed_model_coercion` test goes with it: a mutation-proof for a
lane with no traffic proves the code still works, not that it is still needed.

`PersonaChatClarifyTicketStore.list_tickets`
--------------------------------------------
`return self.scan_tickets()[0]` — the same rows, minus the unreadable count.
`scan_tickets`' own docstring says exactly why that count has to travel: the
adoption metric is a RATIO over the entire store, and *"an adoption ratio that
moved because the operator asked to see fewer rows would be a lying metric"*. A
thin sibling that silently moves the denominator is the identical defect to
HB-4's `BoardStore._list_active_cards`, on a different store, and the reason
both are rowed despite being small. One reader, one signature, no lossy view to
reach for by accident.

`persona_assignments.safe_assignment_state` — no caller anywhere.

REFUSED — H-CLI-5's follow-ons, and why they are not mine
---------------------------------------------------------
The audit chains `RealmStore.bind_server` and `WorkspaceStore.add_agent` /
`remove_agent` onto this stage *if* H-CLI-5 rules their verbs out. An AST census
finds each has exactly ONE production caller: `harness realm bind-server`,
`harness workspace add-agent`, `harness workspace remove-agent`. They are not
dead — cutting them is a decision that `server_id` and `agent_ids` become
WRITE-ONCE-AT-CREATE, which is a data-model ruling an operator owns, not a
dead-code sweep. Left standing, reported.

Kill proof, both halves: `list_tickets` restored on the ticket store and
`safe_assignment_state` restored in `persona_assignments` -> RED on both rows,
each naming its own reason. Reverted; `hasattr` confirms both absent.

Suites: test_tombstone_registry + test_store + test_observability +
test_persona_lister_refusals + test_persona_assignments = 1312 passed /
0 failed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
docs(agent-runtime-harness): HA-4 + R1/R2/R4/R8 — the corrections belong in the documents everyone is told to trust

HA-4 / R1 — dated supersede notes, not silent edits
----------------------------------------------------
`REFACTOR_DEBT_AUDIT_2026-08-17.md` §0 Correction 4 and §1.7, and
`SCOUT_HERMES_SWALLOW_AUDIT_2026-08-17.md`, all say
`runtime.office.resolve_conflict` "NEVER LANDED. Registry holds exactly 7
methods". It landed at `32a392364b`, **four hours after those documents were
committed**. Re-derived here, not inherited: `grep -c '^@method('
agent_runtime/serve_rpc.py` returns **8**. The correction also records what the
audit's own verifier found and these documents do not — **7 of the 8 have
launcher callers**; `runtime.office.unsubscribe` has zero, which is a launcher
WIRING gap and not a hermes deletion. The genuinely CLI-only office verb is
`office.actor.restore`, which the second half of Correction 4 already said.

Supersede notes rather than edits, because the original sentences are cited by
other documents and a silently corrected claim is indistinguishable from one
that was always right.

HA-4 — one name for the incident kind
--------------------------------------
`observability.py` matched `incident.kind in {"model_invalid_output"}` — a bare
literal in a one-element set — while `incidents.MODEL_INVALID_OUTPUT` held the
same string with zero name references. It now imports the constant.

The coupled edit that had to land in the same commit: `test_s54`'s KEPT pin
asserted `"model_invalid_output" in inspect.getsource(observability)`, which
goes false the moment the literal becomes a name. That assertion was also
**source-grep debt line 65** — "an assertion that proves characters exist and
nothing else". It is now a BEHAVIOUR pin: an incident of this kind is severity
"high". Debt line deleted and the register's grandfathered count lowered
79 -> 78, per its own paying-off procedure.

R4 — one rationale, six pointers
---------------------------------
The identical 7-line "Explicit import header. Still exec'd into harness.py's
globals..." paragraph appeared verbatim at the top of all six
`harness_parts/*.py`. It now lives once, in `harness_support.py`'s module
docstring — the module the parts import FROM — with a 4-line pointer in each
part. Same fold as HA-2, applied to prose.

R8 — an unused parameter that is a KEEP, and now says so
---------------------------------------------------------
`RealmMembershipProvider.authorize(self, realm, action)` never reads `realm`.
Left in place with the reason: this is the authorization boundary, and the
default provider being realm-agnostic is a property of the DEFAULT, not of the
contract. The comment explicitly contrasts it with the same day's
`build_snapshot` cut, because "unused" and "not part of the question" are
different findings and the sweep should not be read as licence to strip
interface parameters.

Also: the audit document now carries an EXECUTION STATUS block naming what
landed, what was refused and why, five corrections to its own rows, and the
cross-stack work this repo cannot do.

TWO SOURCE-GREP VIOLATIONS OF MY OWN, CAUGHT AND FIXED
------------------------------------------------------
`tests/test_no_source_grep_assertions.py` is RED at `main` — 26 pre-existing
findings, not mine, not chased. Diffing its output against `main` showed two
findings that WERE mine, both introduced earlier in this branch:
`test_dispatch_session_policy.py`'s replacement test (an `f'"{...}"' in source`)
and `test_s72_dropped_parameters.py`'s call-site check. Both re-aimed per the
register's own instruction. The first turned out not to need a replacement at
all — the real assertion (`decision.reason == REASON_CLARIFY_TOKEN`) already
existed two tests above, so the vacuous test is simply gone with a note saying
why. The second now parses `persona_assignments` and inspects the actual
`Call` node's keywords, which a text scan cannot distinguish from the comment
explaining the removal. Confirmed by diff: **zero findings on this branch are
new.**

Kill proof, both halves: `_severity_for_incident`'s `MODEL_INVALID_OUTPUT` arm
flipped to return "medium" -> RED, `assert 'medium' == 'high'`. Reverted.
(The sabotage is aimed at the ARM, not the literal, because the pin's whole
point is that it no longer asserts on characters.)

Suites: test_s54_individual_dead_symbols, test_observability,
test_harness_parts_namespace, test_dispatch_session_policy = 68 passed;
test_realm_sync + test_harness_parts_namespace = 59 passed; 0 failed.

author: nekwo
message:
test(agent_runtime): MCF-53 sweep — the HERMES_HOME gate named two scan files and read one, silently, for nineteen days

`_python_files` resolved `SCANNED_FILES` as `if path.exists():
files.append(path)`. That is a SILENT SKIP, and one of the two entries —
`tools/mission_goal_tool.py` — was DELETED with the mission lane at
`2154f05428`. So the tuple advertised two files and contributed one, and
nothing in the suite said so.

Measured on the clean tree, per named scope:

    agent                      184
    agent_runtime              128
    hermes_cli/harness_parts     7
    tools/agent_chat_tool.py     1
    tools/mission_goal_tool.py   0   <- silently skipped

`SCANNED_ROOTS` carried the same hole one shape over: a package that moves
makes `rglob` yield nothing, also without a word. And the hole is invisible by
construction, because every assertion in this file is of the form "no
unexpected hits" and an EMPTY SCAN satisfies all of them.

The existing anti-vacuity witness cannot see it. It proves the scan finds
`agent_runtime/chat_session_scope.py`, so it fires only when `agent_runtime`

This is `038c80ac84`'s finding one gate over, and the same rule fixes it: an
unresolvable scope must be COVERED, never SKIPPED.

- `_scope_contributions` resolves WITHOUT deciding, and returns the per-scope

- `test_every_named_scan_scope_resolves_to_something` decides: a scope
  contributing zero files FAILS, naming the scope and saying re-point it or

(`_MCF53_SABOTAGE_ROOT = os.environ.get('HERMES_HOME')` appended to

(The scope token had to be `agent_relocated`, not a letter-case typo: Windows

message:
test(agent_runtime): MCF-53 sweep — the CLI-vocabulary gate could see two of six spellings, and the lane already uses one of the four it could not

`test_the_cli_lane_spells_no_execution_state_or_error_kind_literal` walked
`persona_commands.py` for exactly two shapes: a dict literal keyed
`"execution_state"` / `"error_kind"`, and a CALL KEYWORD of the same names.
A wire value written any other way was invisible.

Measured, by planting one literal per form in `persona_commands.py` and running
the gate against each:

    dict literal            SEEN (red)
    call keyword            SEEN (red)
    kwonly default          BLIND (green)
    positional default      BLIND (green)
    subscript store         BLIND (green)
    annotated local assign  BLIND (green)

The kwonly-default hole is not hypothetical. `persona_commands.py:1387` spells
`error_kind: str = "retired_persona_instance"` in exactly that form — it is the
file's OWN declared exception, and the comment above
`DECLARED_LITERAL_EXCEPTIONS` calls it "the single deliberate literal left in
the CLI lane". That was a claim nothing could check: a second one in the same
spelling would never have been reported. MCF-53's rule at the gate layer, again
— the token is not the unit of meaning, and neither is the shape you happened
to write it in first.

`_vocabulary_literals` now derives the sites structurally across all six forms
and reports `(form, enclosing def, key, line, value)`, so a failure says which
spelling it found and where. `test_the_detector_sees_every_spelling_and_stays_
quiet_on_the_enum` pins the reader against SYNTHETIC source in each form and
against the correct enum-valued shapes — the gate it feeds asserts an empty
list, and that is the shape that keeps passing quietly once the reader stops
reading.

KNOWN BOUND, stated at the function rather than discovered later: this reads
SHAPE, not dataflow. `_X = "failed"` followed by `payload["execution_state"] =
_X` was measured invisible and stays invisible.

SECOND DEFECT, same file, found while fixing the first.
`test_the_declared_literal_exception_still_matches_its_member` carried EVERY
assertion inside a loop over `DECLARED_LITERAL_EXCEPTIONS.get(...)`, which
misses silently. Rename the exempted function and the lookup returns None for
every candidate, the body never runs, and an exemption for a site that no longer
exists sits there reading like a reviewed decision — ready to be inherited by
whatever is next given that name. The sites are collected first and the coverage
asserted OUTSIDE the loop, which is `test_allowlist_has_not_rotted`'s rule one
file over.

Kill proof, both defects, both halves:

- Each of the four blind forms re-run against the FIXED gate: all four now
  RED. The `_X` indirection stays green and is documented as the bound.
- With `_retired_persona_instance_refusal` renamed, the OLD form of the
  exception test replayed against the same tree **PASSED: `1 passed`**; the
  fixed form FAILED with `these DECLARED_LITERAL_EXCEPTIONS name no keyword-only
  parameter in persona_commands.py any more:
  [('_retired_persona_instance_refusal', 'error_kind')]`.

author: nekwo
message:
test(hermes_cli): MCF-53 sweep — the relay gate could see a refusal shape its own lane does not emit

`test_direct_operator_send_carries_no_relay_refusal` read stdout LINE BY LINE
(`line.strip().startswith("{")` then `json.loads(line)`), and the lane it reads
PRETTY-PRINTS. Measured on the real lane in a hermetic root: it returns 2 and
writes

    {
      "capability_id": "mission.chat.message",
      "error": "unknown persona dev",
      "error_kind": "unsupported_persona",
      ...
    }

so the filter collected exactly `['{']`, that entry raised `JSONDecodeError`, it
was `continue`d, and the only assertion in the test never ran. The gate was
looking for a shape the producer does not produce — MCF-53's own finding, with
formatting standing in for spelling.

It had a second silent-pass route on top: `try: args.func(args) / except
Exception: return` accepted ANY failure as success, including the relay guard
itself raising, which is the one thing this test exists to notice.

Kill proof, three sabotages, each a relay refusal planted as the first statement
of `_cmd_mission_chat_message` (inserted BY LINE NUMBER — that function has no
docstring, and a first attempt at this proof anchored on `\"\"\"`, landed inside a
different function, and measured nothing; the invalid result was thrown away
rather than reported):

    sabotage                                        OLD gate      NEW gate
    pretty-printed refusal (what the lane emits)    PASSED        RED
    single-line refusal                             RED           RED
    the guard RAISES `relay_cycle refused`          PASSED        RED

The middle row is why this is a hole and not a total vacuity, and it is stated
rather than rounded up: the old reader could see a refusal written on one line.
It could not see one written the way this runtime writes them.

The fix, and it is not "parse the whole output as one document" — that only
works while the lane emits exactly one:

- `_json_documents` decodes stdout as a STREAM via `raw_decode`, so indentation
  and document count are both irrelevant, and every payload is inspected rather
  than the first.
- `test_the_json_reader_sees_a_pretty_printed_payload` pins the reader on
  synthetic text — the gate it feeds asserts an ABSENCE, which is the shape that
  keeps passing quietly once the reader stops reading. It also records the old
  reader's behaviour on the same bytes: `['{']`.
- A raise is INSPECTED, not swallowed: type name, `code`, `error_kind` and the
  message must all be free of `relay`.
- The claim is backed POSITIVELY before it is made. "No relay refusal" is a
  stability claim, and delivering nothing satisfies it exactly as well as
  delivering (MCF-50), so the test now asserts stdout was non-empty, that at
  least one document decoded, and that the lane died where the premise says it
  dies — on the absent persona store, PAST the relay guard.

`hermes_cli/harness_parts/persona_commands.py` reverted byte-exact after every
run (sha256 86bde67c…), `git status` clean over `hermes_cli/`, suite 9 passed.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(dep_ensure): the install script never ran, because a user profile ran instead

`ensure_dependency` spawned scripts/install.ps1 without `-NoProfile` and with
the caller's stdin inherited. PowerShell loads profiles BEFORE `-File`
executes, so on a machine whose profile upgrades 5.1 sessions to pwsh, the
profile replaced the script with an interactive shell, that shell inherited a
pipe that never closed, and it blocked forever. Two consequences, the second
worse than the first:

  * `hermes postinstall --yes --json`, run as a non-interactive child by the
    Eternia Launcher, hung for 20 minutes and was killed by the caller's
    ceiling. Twice.
  * The profile ended in `exit`, so install.ps1 had NEVER run on that machine.
    The dependency it was ensuring (agent-browser, which is not on PATH there)
    was silently never installed, and `ensure_dependency` reported failure by
    way of the check that follows.

This is the only PowerShell spawn in the repo without `-NoProfile` — claw,
clipboard, gateway, tools_config, voice_mode and tools/environments/local all
pass it. `--yes` never suppressed the spawn; it only skips the [Y/n] prompt.

Adds `-NoProfile -NonInteractive` before `-File`, and `stdin=DEVNULL` on the
subprocess for both the powershell and bash branches — `IS_INTERACTIVE=false`
only ASKS the script to be non-interactive, and a profile or package manager
that reads stdin does not read that variable. EOF is an answer; an open pipe is
not.

The existing test_postinstall_noninteractive.py cannot catch this: it stubs
`ensure_dependency` itself, so the spawn is never constructed. The new test
drives the real function with a failing check and asserts on the argv,
including that the flags precede `-File`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(tests): MCF-66 — the suite could read the operator's Claude Code login, and the token-refresh path could OVERWRITE it

`tests/conftest.py` says in its own header that it deliberately does NOT
redirect `HOME` — "that broke subprocesses in CI". `Path.home()` inside a test
therefore resolves to the operator's real profile, and
`~/.claude/.credentials.json` is Claude Code's file, deliberately outside
Hermes home (`credential_sources.py` refuses to delete it for exactly that
reason). So `HERMES_HOME` never covered this path and relocating it was never
an option.

`_neutralize_macos_keychain_creds` already held the OTHER source
`read_claude_code_credentials()` consults. There was no twin for the file
reader and none at all for the writer.

Two routes into the reader, both verified at HEAD before the fix:

  * `_available_entries` -> `_sync_anthropic_entry_from_credentials_file`
    (`agent/credential_pool.py:904`, called at `:1445` and `:1847`) has **NO
    gate**. It fires whenever a hermetic pool holds an anthropic entry with
    `source="claude_code"` and an exhausted/dead `last_status`. LIVE at HEAD:
    a probe pool of that exact shape reached the file reader.
  * `_seed_from_singletons` -> `read_claude_code_credentials()`
    (`:2510`) sits behind `is_provider_explicitly_configured("anthropic")`,
    which reads files `HERMES_HOME` *does* sandbox. Blocked at HEAD — but the
    brief called that "incidental" and it is worse than incidental: writing
    `active_provider: anthropic` into a test's own hermetic `auth.json` opens
    it, measured, and `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_commands.py:530` already
    writes that line.

The WRITE side is the half the original row never mentioned, and it is the
worse one. `_write_claude_code_credentials` (`agent/anthropic_adapter.py:1230`)
is reached from the adapter's own `_refresh_oauth_token` (`:1218`) and from
TWO pool refresh sites (`credential_pool.py:1385` and `:1467` — the row named
neither). A test that mocks the token endpoint and reaches refresh rewrites
the operator's live Claude Code login with whatever the mock returned. Proved
at HEAD against a SYNTHETIC home: `_refresh_oauth_token` put a
`.credentials.json` on disk.

What changed — tests only, no production file was touched:

  * `_neutralize_claude_code_credentials_file` (autouse, `tests/conftest.py`)
    replaces both module attributes:
    `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_file` returns `None`, and
    `_write_claude_code_credentials` is a no-op. It records CALL COUNTS only,
    never argument values — those are credentials. Same marker-based opt-in
    shape as the keychain fixture:
    `@pytest.mark.allow_claude_code_credentials_file`, registered alongside it.
  * Seven scopes that legitimately need the real code path now declare that
    marker, and every one of them already pointed `Path.home()` at its own
    `tmp_path`: `TestReadClaudeCodeCredentials`, `TestResolveAnthropicToken`,
    `TestRefreshOauthToken`, `TestWriteClaudeCodeCredentials`,
    `TestResolveWithRefresh`, `TestRunOauthSetupToken`
    (`tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py`),
    `TestReadClaudeCodeCredentialsPriority`,
    `TestReadClaudeCodeCredentialsDesync`
    (`tests/agent/test_anthropic_keychain.py`), and
    `test_claude_code_file_detected_by_model_picker`
    (`tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_cli_model_picker.py`).
    No test is allowlisted; no real token is seeded anywhere.

And the gate, because three hand-rolled copies of this defence already sat at
three seams (`test_credential_pool_rotation_cursor.py:79`,
`test_credential_pool.py:1647`, `test_credential_pool_routing.py:382`) — one
concept, three encodings, MCF-55's shape, nothing holding the seam.
`tests/test_claude_code_credentials_file_gate.py` is an AST census over
`tests/` with two rules:

  * a scope carrying the opt-in marker must ALSO redirect `Path.home()` —
    following fixture parameters into the module's own `def`s, because
    `claude_code_only_env` satisfies it that way. The marker alone hands the
    host file straight back, which is the defect, not the fix.
  * a module binding `_read_claude_code_credentials_from_file` or
    `_write_claude_code_credentials` by DIRECT import must declare the marker.
    `monkeypatch.setattr(module, name, stub)` rebinds the module attribute; a
    module that imported the name at load time holds the ORIGINAL function and
    calls the real writer regardless. `test_anthropic_adapter.py` does exactly
    that.

The census caught itself first: the initial cut accepted a DOCSTRING that
merely claimed the test redirects home — and the docstring that fooled it was
one written for this commit. `_walk_code` now skips bare string expressions,
so only executable syntax counts.

Kill proof, both halves, against a SYNTHETIC home — never the real one:

  * Reader patch removed from the conftest fixture — 5 red:
    `test_credentials_file_reader_is_neutralized`
    (`AssertionError: assert {...'source': 'claude_code_credentials_file'} is None`),
    `test_credentials_file_reader_is_the_neutralized_stub`
    (`_read_claude_code_credentials_from_file is NOT neutralized in this test run`),
    `test_ungated_available_entries_route_lands_in_the_stub`
    (`route 1 did NOT reach the credentials-file reader`),
    `test_gated_seed_from_singletons_route_lands_in_the_stub`,
    `test_gate_marker_is_registered`
    (`tests/conftest.py no longer patches _read_claude_code_credentials_from_file
    — the neutralization has a hole`).
  * Writer patch removed — 5 red:
    `test_credentials_file_writer_is_neutralized`
    (`assert [WindowsPath(...ntials.json')] == []` — the file appeared),
    `test_credentials_file_writer_is_the_neutralized_stub`,
    `test_token_refresh_path_cannot_write_the_credentials_file`
    (`the refresh path did NOT reach the writer stub`),
    `test_pool_refresh_path_cannot_write_the_credentials_file`
    (`the pool refresh did NOT reach the writer stub`),
    `test_gate_marker_is_registered`
    (`tests/conftest.py no longer patches _write_claude_code_credentials`).
  * The census itself, both rules:
    dropping the `Path.home` redirect from `claude_code_only_env` reds
    `test_gate_opt_in_requires_a_redirected_home` naming
    `test_codex_cli_model_picker.py::test_claude_code_file_detected_by_model_picker`;
    stripping all six markers from `test_anthropic_adapter.py` reds
    `test_gate_direct_surface_import_requires_opt_in` naming
    `test_anthropic_adapter.py (direct-imports ['_write_claude_code_credentials'])`.
    Every sabotage reverted; green on restore.

`tests/agent/test_credential_pool_oauth_writethrough.py` carries zero defences
today and is NOT exposed: its only `CredentialPool` is `openai-codex`, so the
`self.provider != "anthropic"` guard returns before any file read, and its two
`"anthropic"` mentions are inert rows in a JSON store no pool ever loads. It
is covered by the autouse fixture regardless.

Production behaviour is unchanged. Nothing in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`
moved; `~/.claude/.credentials.json` stays where Claude Code owns it, so the
self-repair autodiscovery still works.

Suite: `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the 119 test files that touch the anthropic
adapter or the credential pool — **119 files, 2058 tests passed, 0 failed**.
Two files in that set (`tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py`,
`tests/run_agent/test_context_token_tracking.py`) time out before collection on
a real TCP connect from `_query_ollama_api_show`; both were reproduced failing
with `tests/conftest.py` reverted byte-exact to HEAD, so they are pre-existing
and unrelated. `tests/agent` in full: 336 files, 3692 passed, 0 failed.
