author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent_runtime): the boot consult memo answered "current" from the cached artifact's own stat, so an append inside the armed window was invisible to every rider behind it

R1's remaining half. `88151d436b` made the memo's stated bound ("the window is a
BOOT") true by code — the shadow validation now closes the lane on every verdict
— but a bound on the window's LENGTH says nothing about what may be claimed
INSIDE it. A boot's riders arrive over about a second (the stale-first read, then
prewarm, hydrate, hub, cli) and the store is live the whole time.

`_pair_stamp()` stats the pointer, the sidecar and the core: the cached ARTIFACT.
That is blind by construction to the thing the cache is a projection OF. An
append moves `events.jsonl`; it does not move the pair; the memo keeps answering
`matched=True` with a judgement taken before the write. Keying validity on the
artifact's own stat rather than on the source's is the mtime anti-pattern one
step worse than the classic one — the audit's R1, and §1's link 2.

WHAT LANDS

`_ConsultStamp(pair, event_offset)`, taken by `_consult_stamp()` and compared by
`_stamp_still_stands()`, replaces the bare pair tuple in both places a memo is
consulted: `_armed_window_read()` and `pre_build_fingerprint()`. The position
comes from `parity.events_position()` — the log's LOGICAL tail, spanning sealed
slices — which costs one stat of the live slice plus an `exists` probe of the
rotation manifest, on a path that already pays three stats.

`None` is refused rather than compared. `events_watermark`'s typed unknown means
"nobody could tell", and letting two unknowns compare equal would read as "the
log did not move" — the fail-quiet default that docstring exists to forbid. An
install whose log cannot be stat'd re-walks per ask.

WHAT THIS IS NOT

Not an event-offset cache key, and the module header's refusal of one is
unmoved: the fingerprint still decides validity, full stop; `event_offset` is
still never an input to the MATCH decision; there is still no event-tail replay
and no second validity authority. The position decides only whether a judgement
computed for an EARLIER ask may answer THIS one without looking again — a
memoisation question, whose two failure directions are a walk (~300-355ms, on a
boot whose store is moving under it) versus an answer about a store that has
since changed. When the memo drops, the next asker WALKS; if the fingerprint
still matches it is still a cache hit. `test_the_reconsult_after_an_append_is_a_
fresh_look_not_a_forced_rebuild` pins that direction on real bytes.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FRAME-LEVEL GUARD

R1 removes the last naturally reachable producer of the behind-core shape on the
demote lane: the append that produces the batch now drops the memo, so
`build_snapshot()` there pays for a real build. `test_a_demoting_batch_never_
ships_a_core_that_predates_its_offset` therefore pins `events_position` to the
boot's value for the duration of the drain, restoring the pre-R1 memo behaviour
byte for byte before the production path resumes. The guard is belt-and-braces
from here — which is what R2 says it is for ("any future stale-core source") —
and the case says so rather than quietly becoming a test of R1.

Sabotage watched: `_consult_stamp()` returning a constant position reds all three
new cases, the first on `1 == 2` reads of the persisted pair across an append.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
test(agent_runtime): the boot's stale paint and its replacement land at ONE offset, and a producer that deduped the second would freeze every launcher while reddening nothing

BO-1's hermes half. `test_a_mismatch_serves_labeled_stale_first_then_
authoritative` pins that the authoritative hydrate ARRIVES and carries the new
value. It asserts nothing about the two frames' offsets, and the shared fixture
set carries no stale frame at all — every golden is `freshness.state="fresh"`.
So the boot shape that hosted the whole 2026-08-21 defect wave crosses the repo
boundary through no golden, and the plausible future "optimization" — dedupe the
same-offset re-hydrate, because it looks like a re-send of a frame the client
already holds — would freeze every launcher on a permanently stale canvas and
red ZERO tests in either repo.

WHY THE OFFSET IS THE CONTRACT

The launcher's ordinary sequence gate is strict `>`, so a same-offset hydrate is
a duplicate and is dropped. `MissionReadModel.staleHeldAwaitsAuthoritative` is
its ONE exemption, and on an idle log it is the only path off a stale paint —
there is no later offset coming to carry the replacement.

THE GOLDENS

`hydrate_stale_first.json` + `hydrate_authoritative_same_offset.json`, byte-
pinned in `tests/fixtures/stream_frames/MANIFEST.sha256` (rows 6 and 7, after
`hydrate_running_work_owner.json`). Both off the real producer path: frame 1
wraps `core_cache.take_stale_first_core`'s labelled core exactly as
`stream_frames` does at its head, frame 2 is a real gated build with the lane
armed and `consult` demoting. `core_source` cache/rebuilt, `core_stale`
true/absent, `freshness.state` stale/fresh — which also pins the producer's
NON-stale token as `fresh` on real bytes for the first time (the launcher's
wiring-test fixtures had drifted to `live`; nothing compared them).

The mismatch is arranged by re-persisting the seeded persona-instance row
through `PersonaInstanceStore._write`. That choice is forced, not convenient: it
must move a fingerprinted input WITHOUT appending an event, because an append
would move the log's tail and the two frames would stop being a same-offset
pair. It is also the honest shape — the event-free durable writer is the class
`core_cache`'s own header names as the reason an event-offset key could never
have worked, and it is what produces this boot in the field.

Every producer fact is asserted at GENERATION time, so a silently-fresh first
frame or a silently-advanced second offset fails the generator instead of being
committed as a golden that pins the bug. Byte-determinism verified over three
regenerations; the five existing goldens do not move.

THE CASES

`test_the_authoritative_follow_up_re_emits_at_the_stale_frames_own_offset`
(beside test 5) drives the real `stream_frames` on an idle store and asserts
`frames[1].watermark.event_offset == frames[0]...`.
`test_the_stale_first_pair_is_same_offset_and_carries_both_freshness_tokens`
asserts the same relation on the committed BYTES — a manifest hash proves the
bytes did not move and proves nothing about what they say.

Sabotage watched: `stream_frames` returning after the stale yield when the built
core's offset equals the stale core's reds the new case on `1 == 2` frames. Test
5 reds with it, and the new case's docstring records why it is still not spare —
they diverge on a producer that delivers frame 2 at a HIGHER offset, which test
5 accepts and the exemption is not written against.

CROSS-STACK DEBT, STATED

The launcher's mirror is a later lane. Until it lands,
`tool/test_quality/check_producer_contracts.py` reds on manifest membership —
correctly. The fixtures README names the two files, the manifest ORDER to insert
them at, and the Dart file that owes the cases.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): a launcher boot receipt and the serve's agent.log shared no identifier, so joining them meant matching wall clocks across a timezone the diag log contradicts itself about

BO-3's hermes half. `agent.log` lines are `asctime level name: msg` — no pid
anywhere. The launcher holds the serve child's pid THREE ways (the spawn's
`process.pid`, and the `booting`/`ready` frames, which it parses for `boot` and
ignores for `pid`) and records it on no receipt. So the only joins a boot
investigation had were:

* wall-clock matching, over a live trap — the diag log's HEADER is UTC while its
  per-line stamps are local time-of-day with the date stripped. That trap
  produced a hand-matching error once already;
* `build_ms` + `sections_top` equality, which `mission_boot_timeline` documents
  in as many words as a deliberately WEAK join.

`pid=%d` (`os.getpid()`) now rides `snapshot_build`, `snapshot_build_core` and
`stream_attach` — the three families a boot investigation joins on, and the
three the launcher's receipt can name a counterpart for.

ADDITIVE, NOT A FORMATTER CHANGE

`%(process)d` on the formatter was considered and rejected: it re-shapes every
line this runtime emits, so every grep anchored on a family token's neighbour
breaks at once — including `snapshot_build reason=demote`, which the 2026-08-21
audit note quotes verbatim off the operator's log. Three additive fields break
nothing. The field goes LAST on all three families, after `snapshot_build`'s
conditional `sections_top` tail, so the rule is one sentence ("pid is the last
field") and no existing adjacency moves.

CONVICTIONS

`test_both_build_families_carry_this_process_pid` drives BOTH threshold arms,
because the wait line has two shapes and an implementation that appended the
field inside the `sections_top` branch would carry it on slow builds only — i.e.
would be missing from exactly the boots nobody investigated until they were.
Compared against `os.getpid()`, not against "some digits": a constant would join
every boot to every other one, which is worse than no join because it looks like
an answer. `test_the_pid_field_did_not_displace_the_fields_already_grepped`
makes the additive claim falsifiable — it pins the two adjacencies the argument
rests on. The three attach cases gain the same field.

Sabotage watched: `values.append(0)` in `_log_snapshot_build` reds three cases,
`assert '0' == '27824'`; reverted, green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): the demote receipt names the file that moved and nothing has ever read it, which is how a cache that invalidated itself every boot went months unnoticed

BO-4. `core_cache`'s own channel table says it: "`CoreDecision.reason` is read by
no caller today… a field census of WHY a cache demoted has exactly one source:
this line." The `fingerprint_mismatch` tail (`inputs= changed= diff=`) is
genuinely good instrumentation with no consumer. So when every serve boot
rewrote `serve_socket.owner.json` and the delivery drain rewrote its mirror
seconds later, no boot's key could describe the store the next boot stat'd, the
lane demoted on every same-commit boot from the day it shipped — and it was
found by hand-diffing mtimes against a build window. The gap was consumption,
never emission.

`agent_runtime/core_cache_census.py` executes the classification the table
already states in prose, and `scripts/core_cache_demote_census.py` runs it over
a log path. It reads and returns: nothing is opened for writing, no store is
touched, no snapshot is built. Safe against a live serve's log.

THE TABLE'S CENSUS RULES, AS CODE

Each was a way this census could lie, and each has a case that reds if it does:

* `absent` is deliberately never logged, so "no demote line" is UNMEASURED, not
  "no demote" — a silent window is `no_demote_lines_parsed` and exit 1, not a
  pass. The `core_source=cache` count rides along as CONTEXT because it is the
  only evidence the lane was asked at all;
* `fingerprint_mismatch` ALONE grows a tail. A `build_stamp_mismatch` is
  counted and never bucketed as a missing measurement — a diff there would name
  every file the operator's upgrade touched and read as store churn;
* an arm that could not compute the diff SAYS SO, so a `diff_reason=` line is
  diff-unavailable and can never reach a clean verdict. The formatter refuses
  the word;
* the scope is `last_pair` by construction, so a diff naming store paths is TRUE
  without naming a defect. Runtime-authored hits are the finding and are flagged
  loud, by name, uncapped;
* `home_mismatch` is not an ordinary miss, and the log cannot tell a multi-home
  install from a persona scope that was live while a build stat'd — so it is
  flagged with both readings rather than resolved into one.

The four runtime-authored names are IMPORTED from the modules that own them,
never spelled — the rule this family already learned the hard way, when
`"drain_state.json"` sat in the exclusion set annotated "per
DRAIN_STATE_FILENAME" while that constant read `dispatch_delivery_drain.json`,
so the exclusion named a file that has never existed. `state.db-wal` has no
owning constant for its full name, so it matches on `core_cache._WAL_SIBLING` as
a suffix — a stated widening, since a WAL sibling exists only because a process
committed to SQLite.

NON-VACUITY

Every line under test is emitted by the real `_log_demote`, with its real format
string and real tail helpers; the cases choose the reason and, once, the diff's
content — never the line's spelling. The last case drives the whole thing
end-to-end: isolated root, converged persisted core, event-less durable write,
real `consult()` that demotes, census reads the receipt. A hand-typed fixture
would let a producer rename leave this census reporting a confident zero forever.

Sabotages watched, all reverted: every path bucketed as store churn reds 7 cases
(`'store_churn' == 'self_perturbation'` plus the four table names and both
separators); a `diff_reason=` arm read as clean reds 2 on
`'no_fingerprint_mismatch' == 'diff_unavailable'`; every reason owed a tail reds
the build_stamp case on `1 == 0`.

The table row that said the reason had no reader is corrected in place: it names
this module, and says that amending a rule there means amending code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
chore(agent_runtime): the fixture file that started building cores was leaving the next file a process whose cache lane could never hit

Three follow-ups on the BO-1/BO-4 slice, none of them behavioural in production.

`test_stream_contract_fixture.py` now BUILDS cores — `_build_stale_first_
convergence_pair` converges a persisted core and pays for a gated rebuild — and a
completed build closes the process's cache lane. Before BO-1 nothing in that file
touched process-global state; now every generating case ended with the lane
disarmed, so a later file asserting a cache-hit boot would have failed for a
reason with no connection to itself. The conftest already resets the captured
fingerprint home for exactly this class of leak; the lane and its memo are the
same kind of state and get the same treatment, locally, in the file that started
building.

`_store_position`'s cost paragraph is corrected to what the code actually does.
It claimed "one stat, plus one exists probe (two, once the store has rotated)";
on a rotated store `log_end_offset` also READS and parses the rotation manifest.
Still a few KB of JSON listing sealed slices rather than any log content, and
still bounded — but the audit bounded this at "one stat per ask", so the
overrun belongs in the docstring rather than in a reader's surprise.

The census test's imported constant moves into the import block it belongs in.

author: nekwo
message:
perf(tools): the transient grace served its verdict without caching it, so a flake that lasted a minute cost a full probe and a warning line on every single call inside the window

The suppression read "do not cache the failure" and was implemented as "do not
cache anything": inside _CHECK_FN_FAILURE_GRACE_SECONDS the last-good True was
returned from a path that re-ran the whole probe -- subprocess, socket dial, SDK
import -- and re-logged the transient warning, every call. Measured on the live
serve: 40 probes and 40 warning lines in 2 s for one check_fn, 759 such lines in
one agent.log, and the storm fired DURING the persona prewarm walk it was there
to make cheap.

The grace verdict is now cached on its own short backoff
(_CHECK_FN_GRACE_REPROBE_SECONDS, 5 s), so the window costs one probe per
backoff interval instead of one per call. Cache entries carry their own expiry
rather than sharing one global TTL, because the two kinds expire differently.
The FAILURE is still never cached, so a recovery is never blocked; _last_good is
not restamped, so the grace window still counts from the real success; and the
backoff is clamped to that window's end, so a True served at second 59 cannot be
read back at second 62 -- a cache may delay a re-probe, it may not extend the
grace it rides inside. Probe-round accounting is untouched: the counter still
fires only where a body actually runs, which is now the honest count.

Gates count probes and warnings, never milliseconds. Sabotaged both ways and
watched red: dropping the backoff cache gives "40 probes for 40 calls"; dropping
the clamp lets the grace True answer past its own window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
perf(agent_runtime): the section named agents_readiness spends most of its time somewhere else, so every plan that read the number off a build log convicted the wrong half

W2-H2 asked for a per-persona memo over profile_readiness_for_persona, on the
premise that the section's measured 1,616-5,089 ms is that walk. Instrumented
first, against the operator's own profiles root, 5 runtime personas:

  first build in a process   4,001 ms   tool visibility 3,054 / walk   947
  steady state, same process   183 ms   tool visibility    36 / walk   146

The section's timer has always wrapped BOTH the readiness walk and the
_agent_summary/resolve_tool_visibility half, and the half it is not named after
is the one that dominates. Within the walk, the skill term is dominant in turn
(770 ms cold, ~99 ms steady, of the 947 / 146) -- config yaml 126/0.3, hash
compare 15/14, runtime deps 11/10, mcp config 7/5, binding resolve 6/6, provider
issue 79 cold / 4 warm behind its own TTL.

So the section is now split, additively: agents_readiness keeps its exact
meaning and span (an operator's older quoted number still means what it meant)
and gains agents_readiness_walk and agents_readiness_tool_visibility beside it.
Two halves that move for unrelated reasons -- a check_fn sweep and a skill
resolution -- are now separately countable, which is what would have let the
first measurement convict the right term without this detour.

The memo itself is REFUSED, with the argument written where the next person will
reach for it (profile_readiness.py). The walk returns per-skill content hashes,
so an honest key must cover skill package content; that key is the stat set
skill_package_content_hash already computes and already caches process-wide one
layer down. Reproducing it above the walk costs ~102 of the 146 steady-state ms
to save the remaining ~44, and adds a cache class that can go stale. A key over
fewer inputs than the body reads is the anti-pattern this campaign is named for;
a key that costs what the body costs is the same mistake wearing a hat.

The gate injects a known delay into one half at a time and requires the other
half not to carry it -- one-sided, so a loaded box makes it more true. Sabotaged
by letting the walk key swallow both halves and watched red: the summary arm
read agents_readiness_tool_visibility 0 against agents_readiness_walk 251.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): the prewarm had a start and no finish, so "the memos were filled before the drop arrived" was a claim about a race that nothing in the process could time

W2-H3. warm_persona_memos ran on a single FIFO daemon worker and logged only on
failure, which means the module's central claim -- the warm beats the operator's
gesture -- could be checked only by reading the create's own cost, the very
number the warm exists to change. One INFO line per finished warm now says which
persona and how long: "persona_prewarm done persona=<id> elapsed_ms=<n>",
format-pinned because an operator joins it to the drop log by grepping it.
Timings only; the gate also pins that the persona display name is NOT on it. The
failure path keeps its warning and gains the same elapsed cost, because there is
one worker and a warm that failed after seconds held the queue for exactly those
seconds -- a census that saw only successes would under-count service time. A
raise emits no done line: a receipt for work that did not finish is a lie the
census cannot detect.

Then the measurement the stage asked for, six synthetic personas warmed back to
back in a fresh process on an isolated home: 2172, 0, 16, 0, 16, 0 ms.

Bounded concurrency is REFUSED on that evidence, and the refusal is written into
the module docstring where the next person will re-ask. The queue's entire cost
is its first item -- the memos it fills are keyed on the callable and the toolset
tuple, not on the persona -- so a second worker cannot shorten the 2,172 ms item
and can only run a second cold sweep beside it, which is the thundering herd the
one-worker design opens by refusing. It would buy 16 ms. Against the stage's own
criterion (can a warm beat a drop ~100 s after boot) the single worker wins by
~98 s.

Sabotaged by deleting the done line and watched red: "expected exactly one done
receipt, got []".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(hermes_cli): the launcher's revision-keyed sprite eviction shipped with no producer on the rows it reads, so a cache key that was built, gated and tested has never once fired in production

The launcher's PetdexSpriteCache.noteSpritesheetRevision evicts a resident
decode whose revision no longer matches upstream's. It landed on 2026-08-21
against a hermes that stamped spritesheetRevision on the `pets sprite` payload
ONLY -- which the launcher reads after it has already decided whether its
resident sheet is stale. So the invalidation half of the (slug, revision) key had
no writer at the moment it is consulted, and the only live invalidation paths
stayed the explicit clears. As-built correction 2 in the drop-latency plan named
this and deliberately left it to hermes.

Installed gallery rows now carry the stamp, through the SAME _pet_sheet_revision
the sprite payload uses. One producer on purpose: the launcher compares this
row's value against the one the sprite payload wrote into its resident decode,
so a second spelling of the same arithmetic would evict every sheet on every
gallery read.

Remote manifest rows stay unstamped, which is an answer rather than an omission:
their sheet is the one behind spritesheetUrl and this process cannot stat it. A
revision fabricated from anything local would be a key that says nothing about
the bytes the launcher would fetch, and the launcher -- which correctly reads an
unstamped sheet as "no evidence of staleness" rather than as stale -- would start
evicting on it.

Three gates, because "the row has a revision" is the weakest of the three claims:
the row matches what `pets sprite` reports for that slug; the value MOVES when
the sheet is actually rewritten; a remote row carries no key at all. Sabotaged
twice and watched red -- a constant producer failed both installed arms
("'rev' == '1787405780681238500:3247'", "the revision did not move when the
sheet did"), and stamping remote rows with "0:0" failed the remote arm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent_runtime): the agents_readiness split was two new parity keys, and parity rides the hydrate frame the Launcher byte-pins, so an observability nicety had quietly become a cross-stack fixture landing

25cd488d33 put agents_readiness_walk and agents_readiness_tool_visibility into
sections_ms. sections_ms rides the parity envelope, the envelope rides the
hydrate frame, and that frame is byte-pinned by the committed stream goldens AND
by the Launcher's mirror of them. The full agent_runtime suite named it:
test_committed_goldens_are_the_generators_bytes,
test_every_generated_golden_has_the_producer_shape and
test_the_lanes_frames_have_the_committed_goldens_shape all went red on
hydrate.json. Their own message is the ruling -- "stream goldens change only in a
cross-stack landing" -- and the launcher half of that landing is not mine to
make. Regenerating the hermes goldens alone would have left the Launcher's
producer-contract byte-compare red on every push: the precise failure this
repo already paid for once, and which the goldens exist to prevent.

So the split moves off the wire and onto a log line, which is where an operator
reads section timings anyway -- sections_top on snapshot_build_core, in
agent.log. New receipt beside it, joining on the same pid:

    snapshot_agents_readiness walk_ms=<n> tool_visibility_ms=<n> pid=<n>

sections_ms is byte-identical to b53ea931fe again: agents_readiness keeps its
exact key, span and meaning, and nothing new appears beside it. The measurement
that motivated the split is unchanged and still recorded (first build in a
process 4,001 ms = 3,054 visibility + 947 walk; steady state 183 = 36 + 146).
An empty split emits nothing -- "the section did not run" is not "both halves
cost zero" -- while a section that ran and cost nothing does report its zeros.

The gate keeps its one-sided injected-delay discriminator and gains an explicit
boundary pin: no key starting with agents_readiness_ may appear in sections_ms.
Sabotaged both ways and watched red -- one timer spanning both halves reported
(walk 251, visibility 0), and leaking a key back onto the wire failed the new
boundary test AND reddened the goldens again at hydrate.json index 4159.

author: nekwo
message:
perf(agent_runtime): three demote builds landed at one offset and wrote back the identical fingerprint three times, because the coalescer only merges builds that overlap

W3-H2. Live serve 2026-08-22 10:50, pid 22588: snapshot_build reason=demote
role=led generations 17/18/19 all at offset 89961793, build_ms 3017/3210/2388,
each followed by snapshot_core_cache_write fingerprint=9d655b54f622 - the same
core, built three times. Five more such pairs in the two minutes around the
drop whose roster_confirmed the operator felt as 8309ms.

The build coalescer cannot merge them: it refuses to let a caller ride an
in-flight build, deliberately, because that build may predate the caller's
arrival. That is a claim about time. The reuse here makes a claim about
POSITION instead, and position is checkable - a core stamps the log offset
captured BEFORE it started reading, so an equal offset now means nothing was
appended from before the build began until this instant.

Same authority and same posture R1 gave the consult memo: equality of
parity.events_position, and an unknown position on either side refuses rather
than letting two Nones read as nothing-moved. Keyed on the core's own pre-build
watermark, never a stat taken after - a post-build stat would absorb an append
the core does not contain, which is the MCF-Q1 shape that erased a just-created
agent from the canvas.

Reuse of the CORE, never a dedupe of emissions: every consumer still builds and
receives its own complete delta, from its own deep copy. The reusing receipt
says core_source=reused_same_offset and keeps the original build_ms - a
build_ms=0 would be a lie about a build that really did cost three seconds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(agent_runtime): the reuse arrived with a second spelling of "how far does this core reach", and the frame guard and the reuse gate must never be able to disagree about that

stream._core_event_offset. Folded onto parity.core_event_offset, beside the
producer of the field it reads: the MCF-Q1 frame guard and the same-offset

message:
fix(agent_runtime): the prewarm's 'not optional' claim was measured false where it was written and true one config knob away, and now the truth is gated

The comment on warm_persona_memos's apply_chat_lane_tool_scope call claimed
warming without it 'would prime nothing the create reads'. Measured: false.

is process/callable-keyed and warms either way; a per-session BOUNDED record
can never reach this pair (ChatToolPermissionStore.get answers None for the

Where the call IS load-bearing: an install whose runtime default is the

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): the "provider first_byte" span opened before run_conversation even began, so 1.8s of hermes assembly wore the provider's name on every turn record

The span opens when the runner's ready-callback returns and closes at the
first streamed delta — and everything of the conversation loop's prologue,
tool-schema serialization (31 tools / 39KB live), prompt-cache decoration,
request middleware, the pre_api_request hook, and the per-request client
build rode inside it. Measured on live turn c59ab99e: 1,762ms of a 13,532ms
"provider" span was hermes (1,338ms prologue + 424ms request build). The
code even admitted it in a comment and called closing it provider-client
surgery.

It is not: the loop already emits run.progress trace payloads into the
mission-chat handler, which holds the turn's marks. request_assembled rides
one such payload, emitted per physical dispatch attempt after the codex
transport preflight and immediately before the provider call — the last
instant every byte hermes will send exists. The handler converts it
first-mark-wins, so a retry ladder keeps the first attempt's instant. The
step spelling lives in hermes_constants because the producer and consumer
sit on opposite sides of a layering boundary and must never disagree on it.

Additive-only: v3 records on disk are untouched, a turn that dies before
the provider has NO request_assembled key, and the launcher audit decodes
phases by its own whitelist so the new key cannot break the deployed tool.

Gates: the streamed-turn fixture walks the real handler and pins
provider_request_started <= request_assembled <= provider_first_byte; the
producer's actual payload feeds the mapper (spelling held at the seam); the
real run_conversation with a mocked client proves the marker precedes the
provider call. Three named sabotages watched red and reverted: misspelled
step, handler dropping the marker, and emission moved below the provider
call ('marker must precede the provider call, got
order=[provider_call, marker]').

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): mission-chat turns get provider TTFB from phase marks; every other lane's first byte evaporates into prose

The streaming path already observes the first delta — _perform_api_call takes
a perf_counter reading at dispatch and hands _stop_spinner to
_interruptible_streaming_api_call as on_first_delta — and then throws the
instant away. Mission chat does not care, because commit 785a35be gave it
request_assembled/provider_first_byte marks on the turn record. Gateway, cron
and CLI turns have no phases block at all: the one "API call #N" line this
loop logs is their entire record of the call, and it carries only the total
latency=. A slow turn there cannot be split into "waiting on the provider"
versus "streaming the body", so it gets blamed by guess.

One token on the line that already exists closes it. A one-slot cell carries
the measurement from the dispatch closure to the log-line closure (three
separate closures in one scope, with the middleware boundary in between), and
_format_ttfb_token renders " ttfb=X.Xs". No new log lane, no new consumer.

The honesty contract holds three ways. Absent is never zero: a non-streaming
call, or a stream whose callback never fired, prints NO token rather than
ttfb=0.0s, which would read as an instantaneous provider that no downstream
reader could distinguish from a real one. The span is monotonic-only —
perf_counter at both ends, so it cannot go negative on a wall-clock
correction. And the cell is cleared at each PHYSICAL dispatch, so a fast
attempt A that died can never lend its instant to the slow attempt B whose
response is actually being logged. The wrapper records before invoking the
original callback, so spinner teardown is not charged to the provider and the
instant survives a callback that raises; first firing wins, because providers
may fire per token and TTFB is the first byte.

Gates: the formatter renders one decimal for a measured value and the empty
string for None; the wrapper records once, keeps calling the original, and a
second firing does not move the instant; and the real run_conversation with a
mocked (therefore non-streaming) client proves the emitted line carries no
ttfb= token. Two named sabotages watched red and reverted: the recorder
defaulting to 0.0 when unobserved ('a non-streaming call observed no first
byte, so the token must be absent entirely; got ... latency=0.0s ttfb=0.0s')
and the wrapper dropping the original callback ('the wrapper swallowed the
original callback; the thinking spinner would never stop').

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
docs(harness): the canon is eight verified domain docs, one master index, and a quarantine for everything not yet built

56 archived files answered every question about this system somewhere, and no
question anywhere. The rewrite is organized by domain instead of by the date a
plan happened to land: architecture, data and shapes, transport, boot, the chat
turn, the office surface, observability, and the performance ledger — each
150-420 lines, each closing with what it supersedes.

Two rules were enforced during writing rather than promised for later. Every
factual claim was verified against HEAD before it entered a domain doc — eight
writer lanes dropped or corrected dozens of archived claims that turned out
false at HEAD, among them: the kill_active chat-swap guard is a silent no-op;
PersonaInstance.mode is stored, not derived; the incremental projector was
RETIRED 2026-08-01 and read_model.db is never populated on the serve path; the

qa+dev MCP admission widening was superseded by profile-declaration authority;
spawned_by is provenance with two live writers, not a store-kept mirror. And
nothing unimplemented lives inline: 27 planned/ files hold the unbuilt designs,
each with its evidence and its opening gate, so a reader of a domain doc reads
only what runs.

Four adversarial verifier lanes then attacked the drafts against the code:
~600 path:line anchors opened and judged, every quoted receipt re-grepped from
the live logs, every commit sha resolved, all 56 archived files claimed by at
least one Supersedes list (zero orphans), and every refuted number - selective
boot ranges, a wrong retention constant, bench figures posing as live
measurements, components presented as sums across two clocks - fixed before
this commit.

normalize_persona_or_template_id(caller) — colon form, profile:alice —
against safe_assignment_token(owner.persona_id) — token form,
profile_alice. One persona, two normalizers, one predicate: every
delivery attempt was refused as foreign and the drain burned all eight
attempts in ~40s against an identical deterministic rejection
(2026-08-24, dispatch-2540634d5cf3 — the lane's first live exercise).

personas_equal() folds BOTH sides through one authority
(safe_assignment_token over normalize_persona_or_template_id) and now
guards all four sites of the shape: the mission-chat fence, open-chat,
chat-delete, and open-new-chat's persona_instance_mismatch. The
instance-pin leg is deliberately BOUNDED: a pin proves ownership, not
whose brain runs — an unconditional short-circuit would accept
--persona profile:bob into alice's thread and run bob's turn there —
so the pin overrides the persona leg only where that leg is silent
(owner row with no readable persona). Both halves pinned.

Recovery and hygiene: 'harness mission-chat dispatch redeliver <id>'
re-arms a dropped row (typed refusals for delivered/pending rows; queue
metadata only, never message bodies), and the drain now fails FAST on
deterministic guard rejections — the row drops on the first
forge_rejected:<kind> with the real reason on delivery_error, keeping
the attempt cap for transient failures. The abandoned reply itself
stays durable and re-deliverable.

Likely the same root as the OPEN 2026-08-22 new-chat-first-send
REJECTED record: the launcher's fallback send path spells the persona
in the form this fence refused.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(tool_search): agent-to-agent send becomes first class — the promotion un-hides without granting

Operator ruling 2026-08-23: "agent message send should be a first class tool."
`agent_chat_send` and `agent_chat_dispatches` now ride eagerly in the
model-facing tools array on every lane that already grants the `agent_chat`
toolset, instead of hiding behind the tool_search bridge and costing a
search + describe round trip before every delegation.

The promotion lives in tool_search as `_NEVER_DEFER_TOOLS`, NOT in
`toolsets._HERMES_CORE_TOOLS`. Core-tool membership is bundle CONTENT: every
`hermes-*` platform bundle is `_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS + extras`, so promoting
there would hand agent-to-agent messaging to every CLI and messaging surface
in the process. Never-defer only un-hides. `classify_tools` partitions the
defs it is handed and never invents one, so a lane without the toolset grant
still sees nothing — pinned by `test_never_defer_does_not_grant`.

The three read-side siblings (threads/open/log_path) stay deferred by design.
Operators can extend the set through `tools.tool_search.never_defer`, which
unions with the built-ins and can never remove one.

Config is threaded through `classify_tools` / `assemble_tool_defs` /
`dispatch_tool_search` / `scoped_deferrable_names` so the new lookup does not
re-read (and deepcopy) the config document once per tool name on a large
catalog. Every signature change is a keyword-only addition with a default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(tool_search): search hits carry their own schema — the describe round-trip stops being mandatory

`tool_search` returned names and descriptions only, so every deferred-tool
invocation cost a second model iteration (~3-6 s) just to fetch the parameter
schema the search already had in hand — the catalog entry holds the full tool
def. The top 3 hits now ship their `parameters` inline, and the bridge
description says so: a match that carries `parameters` is invoked directly
with `tool_call`, and `tool_describe` is only for matches without one.

Bounded on both axes. Only the top `_SEARCH_HIT_SCHEMA_TOP_N` hits carry a
schema — the model almost always invokes one of the first few, and hits 4+
stay cheap. Each schema is capped at `_SEARCH_HIT_SCHEMA_MAX_CHARS`, so one
pathological MCP tool cannot blow up a whole search result; over the cap the
hit is served schema-less and the describe path still serves it. An
unserializable schema takes the same route rather than raising.

`tool_describe` itself is untouched, and the extra `parameters` key is
additive — the search result is a plain tool-result string read only by the
model, so nothing hashed or pinned moves.

author: nekwo

(~12-15s) for no new information.

New item 4 names the receipt (`git show --stat HEAD`, or `git show HEAD` when
the diff is itself the proof) and names the stopping rule. The exemption for

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): a busy root gives four answers — the turn that is already running stops being told its message never landed

"The root is busy" was one refusal, and it was the wrong one for the case that
mattered. `_cmd_mission_chat_message` splits plan -> commit, and ALL of the
lane's dedupe/idempotent-replay logic lives inside the commit phase, i.e. AFTER
the chat-root lease. So a duplicate of the turn that is CURRENTLY RUNNING died
`chat_busy` before any dedupe could see it — and `chat_busy` means "someone
else holds the root", which a caller is entitled to read as "your message never
landed".

2026-08-24: the Launcher's 60 s streaming-inactivity fallback re-presented its
OWN still-running client_message_id while Neko's synchronous `agent_chat_send`
ran 66 frameless seconds. It got `chat_busy`, painted the delivered turn as
rejected, and the agent's reply committed 20 s later into a feed whose stream
subscription was already dead.

The turn journal is per-session JSON and readable WITHOUT the lease, so the
question "whose turn is the busy root running?" is answerable at the seam. The
new `_mission_chat_busy_outcome` reads it and tells four cases apart:

* this message, still running     -> `chat_turn_duplicate_in_flight` (BLOCKED,
  non-terminal: do not resend a new id, do not resolve, re-present THIS id)
* this message, already answered  -> the idempotent replay, served read-only
* this message, unprovable        -> today's `chat_turn_outcome_unknown`
* somebody else's turn            -> `chat_busy`, byte-identical to before

Every branch is reads plus envelope emission. It runs outside the lease it just
failed to acquire, against a root another turn is actively writing, so it may
not transition the journal — which is also why the replay branch deliberately
skips `_publish_persona_chat_projection_event` (that helper writes a
`projection_event_emitted` marker through the journal). `native_committed`
still owes the settling->projected walk; the next lease-holding presentation of
the id finishes it. A torn or missing read falls through to `chat_busy`:
degraded, never wrong.

R5, the agent-to-agent lane: `delivery_client_message_id` derives the
idempotency key from the dispatch id rather than minting one per attempt
(deliberately — it is what makes the chat lane's replay dedupe work), so the
delivery drain genuinely re-presents an in-flight id and genuinely sees the new
kind. Both refund sites now read `_transient_forge_refusals()` instead of
comparing to "chat_busy", or eight unlucky races would walk a deliverable
completion to `dropped`.

Tests pin the four answers, the read-only fence (journal bytes verbatim before
and after), the forensics row for the new kind, and that an UNLEASED resend of
an executing turn still settles to `outcome_unknown` — nothing here relaxes the
orphan path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): the synchronous relay's reply becomes a first-class trace fact — dispatch_reply names its author

A waiting `agent_chat_send` already carried the teammate's answer, but only
inside the tool RESULT blob: the operator saw the order tile and a collapsed
"Result" disclosure, and said so — "i don't see nekos reply."

The reply now rides the same structured lane the order and the target thread
already ride. `dispatch_reply` is the answer (block scrub — per-line secret
drop, newlines kept, 1500) and `dispatch_reply_from` is the display name of the
agent who sent it (120), resolved through the one naming authority every other
surface reads so a relayed reply, a delivered reply and the roster can never
disagree about an agent's name.

Waiting lane only, and by construction rather than by flag: a detached
(`wait=false`) result payload has no `reply` key at all, so it exits at the
empty-reply guard and the background delivery block stays the sole carrier of
that reply. A refusal (`ok: false`) has no answer either — rendering its error
prose in a reply bubble would attribute the harness's "no" to the agent.

The name is a nicety; the trace fact is not. Resolution is wrapped whole, so a
retired or cross-home instance costs the attribution line and never the reply —
absent, never invented, and the console falls back to the id tier.

Against the 4KB event cap the reply sheds second-to-last: its co-resident heavy
field is `tool_result`, the raw JSON that contains the same text, so that goes
first and usually frees the room. `dispatch_order` stays last, keeping the
started event's ladder shape.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(agent_runtime): patch calls leave a local diff artifact — the trace carries its path and +/− counts, never the diff body

A patch tile said "Patched 2 files" and stopped there. The operator could see
THAT something changed and never WHAT, which on the tool that edits code is the
one question the row exists to answer.

The answer was always present and always unreachable. `PatchResult.diff` is a
real unified diff and it rides the tool result all the way here — but a diff
body is file content, exactly what the observability lanes withhold, and the
4KB event cap could not hold one anyway. Publishing it was never the move.

So the body stays on the machine that produced it. `patch_diff_artifacts`
writes one `.diff` per successful patch under the store root and the trace
carries its PATH plus `patch_adds` / `patch_dels` / `patch_mode`. The console
renders the counts inline and opens the file locally when asked; a console
somewhere else resolves nothing and says so. Nothing about a diff is shipped.

Written at the agent_runtime trace boundary, never in `tools/`: that layer is
upstream-shared surface and runs in contexts with no store at all, so an
artifact is a runtime-observability behavior rather than a global side effect
of the tool. `record_patch_diff` reads the result as a dict OR as the JSON
string the real agent loop actually delivers, and swallows its own failures —
a store that will not take a write costs the viewer affordance, never the turn.

Retention is prompt_observability's shape exactly: newest 400 stay live, older
ones MOVE to `patch_diffs_archive/` (archive-never-delete, unbounded archive
side), a failed move leaves the file live for the next write to retry. A diff
over 256KB is truncated at a line boundary with a marker; its COUNTS come from
the full diff, so the numbers on the tile stay honest about the change even
when the file is honest about being partial.

`patch_artifact` needs its own arm at the progress sink: it IS a path, and the
default scalar arm's pathish drop — correct for an undeclared string — would
eat it silently. It gets the `command_full` grade (paths allowed, secrets
dropped) and stays OUT of the Telegram-grade lane entirely, which carries only
the shape of the change and never where it lives.

The artifact is LF on every platform. A unified diff's line ending is part of
its grammar, not the host's convention, so `atomic_write_text` gained a
`newline` passthrough rather than a second writer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet): every attempt gets an address, and looking at a row becomes a verb

`status --json` history entries carried an attempt number and a note but no
file, so a QA surface could show an item's current image and nothing else —
attempt 2 beside attempt 3 was unaddressable. Each entry now carries the
`path` the revision store persisted for that attempt, read back through the
store's own accessor rather than a re-derived filename; `current()` and
`latest()` fold onto the same derivation so the three answers cannot drift.

`characters thumb --draft <id> --row <row> [--attempt n] [--scale 2]` turns
the 2026-08-24 seam hunt's looking procedure into a verb: one row attempt,
NEAREST-upscaled (any smoothing filter averages a one-pixel seam into its
neighbours) onto a flat opaque backdrop (a dark line over transparency
renders as nothing), written to `<draft>/thumbs/<row>-a<n>-x<scale>.png`. It
answers with a path and never bytes, and it is deliberately stage-free —
a composed draft is exactly when an operator goes hunting for a defect.

`draft.json` also gains `authored_by`: provenance for which persona drove
the run, never a home and never a gate — an unattributed draft stays
unattributed rather than being given a guessed author.

author: nekwo
message:
chore: ignore runtime profile homes — decision 6 puts the draft root in the working tree, where a stray add -A would commit a character corpus

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the crop verb finally crops — and the backdrop it composites on finally has something to show through

`thumb` upscaled the WHOLE row strip. That is not the §F.2 procedure, which is
crop one row THEN upscale; the crop is the half that removes pixels and it was
absent. Measured on the live anime-girl draft, the verb wrote a 3072x2048 PNG,
24 MiB decoded, against the 1536x2080 installed sheet's 12 MiB that the crop
exists to avoid decoding — 2.06x the cost of the thing it mitigates — and at
360 px card width its output and the raw attempt differed by at most 2/255 per
channel, 0 of 86 400 pixels by more than 8. It bought nothing. `--frame n`
(default 0) now slices ONE frame cell by the row's own frame count before the
upscale: 384x2048, 0.09 MiB on disk, 3.0 MiB decoded — a quarter of the sheet.
The whole-strip view needs no verb; it is the attempt file the payload already
names as `source`.

`QA_BACKDROP` was a guaranteed no-op on every input the verb can receive. A row
attempt off the provider is a full-bleed magenta field at alpha 255 — measured
(255, 255) on all eight live items — so `alpha_composite` replaced every
backdrop pixel and the flat dark ground the docstring called load-bearing never
rendered. Worse, §F.1's complaint is that the seam is invisible AGAINST the
magenta. The field is keyed out first, which is what gives the backdrop
something to show through and what makes the seam legible.

`--scale 8` wrote a file Pillow classifies as a decompression bomb: 12288x8192
= 100 663 296 px on a live attempt, past `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`, so a
consumer under `-W error` cannot reopen what this package wrote. A scale count
unrelated to the source cannot express that; `MAX_THUMB_PIXELS` budgets the
OUTPUT before the resize and the refusal names the source dimensions.

`approve()` was a fourth derivation of an attempt's path after `current()`,
`latest()` and `attempt_path()` were folded onto `_record_path`. Inline,
`dir / str(record.get("file", ""))` is the item DIRECTORY when the key is
absent, so a record with no file was refused by naming a directory as an image
path while every read path correctly said `None`.

Three spellings of one attempt number, two of them inside a single payload:
`-a{index}` 0-based in the thumb filename, `attempt-{index+1}` 1-based in the
store, and a human line reading "attempt 0 of 3" next to a file called
`attempt-1.png`. One `_attempt_label` helper renders every human line that
shows an attempt and the thumb file is named the store's way — a QA surface
RELABELS, it never renumbers; the payloads stay 0-based machine truth.

`authored_by` absence was discriminable on disk and destroyed at the payload
boundary: a pre-field draft had no key, a `--authored-by`-less start wrote `""`,
and both collapsed to `""` for a consumer that sees only the payload. The key is
now omitted and `authoredBy` is `null`, so absence survives and a backfill can
select the drafts that need one. `SCHEMA` is deliberately not bumped, and why is
recorded beside it: one constant labels `draft.json`, the status payload AND the
installed `character.json` the launcher parses, and an optional draft-only
provenance field is not worth relabelling an installed sheet's manifest for.

Two structural items the review escalated, both about tests:

The pets sprite byte-baseline is asserted by a test at last. Every charsheet
slice's done-when list has carried "pets sprite byte-baseline re-verified", and
the sha lived only in an agent memory note — a gate an agent had to REMEMBER to
read. Split as designed: the sha covers the payload with `spritesheetBase64` and
`spritesheetRevision` removed (both byte-derived; a Pillow upgrade would move
them for no regression, and the KEYS are still required), and the bytes get
their own PNG/dimensions assertion. The pre-split whole-stdout sha
f378cc37fb8033445823409d843b1c44e5ebb23448ce5462216af13f0d076c33 was
re-verified unchanged.

And the fixture rule that would have caught both of the first two defects at
authoring time is written down where the next author will read it: a charsheet
IMAGE test's input comes from `generate_row_strip` through the fake provider,
never from a hand-built PIL image proposed into the store. A hand-built input is
one the author chose to have the property under test — which is how
`assert crop.getpixel((0, 0))[3] == 255, "the crop must be opaque"` came to
survive deleting the backdrop composite entirely. That mutation now kills it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet): the authoring loop becomes a skill — the verb list was never the hard part

A1 gave the pipeline an address for every attempt and a verb for looking at one.
What it could not give an agent is the thing the 2026-08-24 authoring run cost a
competent operator most: that looking is a PROCEDURE, that the first diagnosis
("the code broke it") was wrong, and that a reroll note is a drawing instruction
rather than a complaint. `harness-charsheet-authoring` is that field record,
written as the standing answer for the persona that authors characters —
`required_preload`, the `harness-runtime-model` precedent, no toolset config,
because terminal is already on every unbounded chat lane.

The skill teaches, in this order: a two-probe preflight (which home am I
authoring into, and does the image provider actually return an image), the
thirteen verbs and their stage gates, the crop-and-compare looking procedure,
note craft with the two proven notes as its seed library, the MEDIA and
CHARSHEET-QA lines the console parses, the cost of a sweep and what a failed row
does to the rows behind it, and — when a verb will not run — that the session is
RESTRICTED, never that the feature is broken.

One correction the code forced on the plan, filed launcher-side in the same
breath: decision 6 reads "the draft root is the launcher's serve home,
profiles/base". The serve child is indeed spawned with that home, but it is a
default the turn overwrites: `persona_profile_context` rebinds HERMES_HOME to
the persona's own `hermes_profile` for the duration of every chat turn, so the
draft root follows the PERSONA, not the process. That is why today's anime-girl
draft sits under profiles/alice — and why the skill's preflight echoes the
resolved home instead of asserting one.

Also files the hermes half of A3 (`characters add-state`) under planned/, linked
from 01's Open rows, so the "more strips later" ask has a home before it has a
verb.

Tests, all three proven red-first against complete code:
* the id missing from CANONICAL_SHARED_SKILL_IDS ->
  "assert 'harness-charsheet-authoring' in frozenset({...})"
* the `reopen` row deleted from the skill's verb table ->
  "Extra items in the right set: 'reopen'" — the table is pinned to the LIVE
  argparse tree, so the drift that matters (hermes grows add-state, the skill
  does not) fails here rather than in an operator's turn
* the scanner warning reworded -> "assert 'Do not build a pass/fail scanner' in
  '...'". A skill that teaches a stale claim is worse than no skill.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
docs(charsheet): the skill reads the payload it was handed, not the list it remembers

Two hardenings against drift I could see coming rather than guess at: the A1
polish slice in flight adds a field to the `thumb` payload and turns absent path
values from `""` into `null`. An enumerated field list and a single spelling of
absence would both have gone stale the day it lands, and a skill that teaches a
stale claim is worse than no skill — agents trust it.

So the payload is described as a superset that grows additively, and the
"never rebuild a path" rule now says absence arrives as `null` OR `""`, both
mean no image, and neither becomes a bare `MEDIA:` line. Both sentences are true
before and after that slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the crop verb finally answers "is this a card?" — and absence stops having two spellings in one payload

`MAX_THUMB_PIXELS` was bounded by Pillow's decompression-bomb threshold, which
is a decode-SAFETY question, not the card-WEIGHT question the verb exists to
answer. Launcher risk D.3 states the check plainly — a crop that is not smaller
than the sheet is not a mitigation — and 16M px sits 5x above the sheet, so it
could never enforce it. Measured live: `thumb --draft 20260824-140756-cd645a
--row walk-n --scale 8` succeeded at exit 0, writing 2176x5792 = 12 603 392 px,
**3.94x the 3 194 880-px sheet** it is supposed to be lighter than, with nothing
in the payload to stop an agent declaring that path with a `MEDIA:` line — a
48 MiB decode for a 420px square.

One number was serving two bounds with different correct values, so they are
split. `MAX_THUMB_PIXELS` keeps the write-safety ceiling. `MAX_CARD_PIXELS` is
the card budget and it IS the sheet, derived from `CHAR8.sheet_size()` rather
than written down, so it cannot drift from the thing it is measured against. At
or below `DEFAULT_THUMB_SCALE` — the crop a caller gets by asking for a picture,
and the one an agent hands to a card — an over-budget crop is REFUSED, naming
both numbers and the escape (`--scale 1`). Above it the caller has asked for a
deep zoom on purpose: the file is written, and the payload says `cardSafe:
false` while the human line says "too heavy for a card; open it in the viewer".
A boolean, not a clamp — someone who asked for 8x wants 8x, they just must not
be told it is a card.

`authored_by` was fixed to answer `null` because "absence is a fact a consumer
must be able to read". That is verbatim true of `history[].path`, `current` and
`approvedPath`, which flattened the store's typed `Path | None` into `""` in the
SAME payload — two spellings of absence in one response, one of them on the
field A1 itself introduced. A row whose attempt-1 record has lost its `file` key
answered `history[1].path == ""` beside `authoredBy: null`; B2 cannot tell "no
image recorded" from any other empty value, and an agent following A-4's
`MEDIA:<path>` protocol interpolates it into a bare `MEDIA:` line. All three go
through one `_path_or_none`, so absence cannot acquire a second spelling one
field at a time. No consumer assumed a string: `_item_status`'s only non-test
reader is `_cmd_characters_status`, which reads `pending` alone.

`frame_cell`'s POSITION was untested. A mutation shifting its window by +3 px on
both bounds survived the whole charsheet suite — every assertion read the cell's
SIZE, which a shift does not change, so the verb could have shown an operator
the wrong slice while reporting the right dimensions. A defect is hunted frame
by frame; a cell three pixels off cuts through the neighbour it was meant to
exclude. The new test builds a strip whose every column carries its own x, then
pins each cell against `strip.crop((round(k*w/n), 0, round((k+1)*w/n), h))` and
requires the slots to tile the strip end to end — widths 770/100/13 are the
cases where the division does not divide.

The scale gate moved into `pipeline.require_scale` because the card check has to
multiply by the scale before `upscale_on_backdrop` ever sees it, and `512 * "2"`
is a perfectly good string: without one authority for "is this a scale?", a type
error reaches the caller wearing a budget refusal's clothes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
docs(charsheet-skill): the skill learns the two crop budgets and the typed absence it now has to read

`a80a15121f` landed the skill against A1 as it stood an hour earlier, so its
`thumb` payload list and its one-budget `--scale` line went stale the moment the
card budget split. Its own commit says a skill that teaches a stale claim is
worse than no skill, so: `cardSafe` joins the payload, the `--scale` bullet says
which of the two bounds bites where, and the rule an agent actually needs is
stated as a rule — only a `cardSafe: true` crop may be declared with `MEDIA:`,
because a false one is a viewer artifact and hands the console a decode several
times the sheet's for a 420px square.

The second addition is the one that silently breaks a turn: a path in
`status --json` is now a string or `null`, so interpolating one unchecked emits
a bare `MEDIA:` line and the console renders no card at all.

author: nekwo
message:
docs(charsheet-skill): the skill's input becomes a running record — write it last, from what the slices taught, not first from what the plan believed

Owner ruling 2026-08-24. A0 wrote the skill second and it was stale within one
commit: A1's polish changed the thumb payload and the crop budget the same day,

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the skill an agent LOADS is now the skill this repo ships — and a push proves it

A canonical shared skill has two copies and only the installed one is ever
executed: `skill_utils._skill_resolution_status` answers `invalid_source` for any
id in `CANONICAL_SHARED_SKILL_IDS` whose candidate is not `shared_core`. Nothing
joins the repo copy to it on commit. So `5504706978` and `6ca0622bec` edited
`harness-charsheet-authoring` on `main` and reached no turn at all: the installed
package sat at `a80a15121f`'s text — 14457 B against the repo's 14906 — and the
A0 gate turn's `used_skills` row carried its hash, `964934db6c...`, not the
repo's. Every A0 test was green throughout, because all three read
`docs/.../harness-skills/.../SKILL.md`. A guarantee about what the runtime reads
cannot be pinned in the tree.

The two edits it missed were the two that mattered: `cardSafe` in the `thumb`
payload, and the rule `4eb7422789` made necessary — only declare a
`cardSafe: true` crop with `MEDIA:`. An agent authoring today off the installed
copy could hand the console a crop measured at 3.94x the sheet's pixels for a
420px card, which is the exact regression `MAX_CARD_PIXELS` had just been added
to prevent.

So the check runs where the join lives — on the machine, at push time.
`scripts/verify_harness_skill_install.py` installs every canonical package and
then fails if `harness_skill_hash_mismatches` is non-empty; `--check` verifies
without writing. `.githooks/pre-push` runs it on every push (`git config
core.hooksPath .githooks`, one command per clone, shared by every worktree of
it). It repairs before it verifies on purpose: divergence here is stale MACHINE
state, not a defect in the tree, and the verify afterwards is what makes it a
gate rather than a wish. "Never installed" is reported separately, because
`harness_skill_hash_mismatches` skips a destination that does not exist.

Also in the skill, from the same review:

* Plan SS-F.7 names three environment traps and the skill taught two. The missing
  one fires immediately AFTER the operator does the right thing about trap 1: a
  plan upgrade invalidates the stored token, the probe returns `401
  token_expired` with a local expiry ~15h out, and the skill's only scripted
  answer was "report the image provider is unavailable in this home" — correct
  for a home with no credentials, wrong here, and it sends the operator to check
  `auth.json` placement they just fixed.
* `approve-direction` read "Approving all five advances to `rows`". Five is
  `EIGHT_WAY.authored`; `--directions 4` authors three, and the same table
  documents `--directions` on `start`. On a 4-direction draft the agent would
  report two directions still to approve after the stage had already advanced.

And two things the review found beside the skill:

* `baseImage` was the FOURTH path field still spelling absence `""` —
  in `status_payload` and in `list`'s `_characters_draft_summary` — inside the
  payload `4eb7422789` had just cleaned of exactly that, whose helper docstring
  already claimed one spelling. `path_or_none` is public now, because a
  one-module helper enforcing a payload-wide rule is how the fourth field got
  missed. The CLI test PINNED the defect (`assert summary["baseImage"] == ""`),
  which is why a review found it and the suite did not.
* `planned/charsheet-add-state.md`'s gate step said `rows --only jumping-*`.
  `--only` comma-splits and `run_rows` matches keys exactly, so that is one
  unknown row key and a `ValueError`, not a glob. The five keys are spelled.

Tests, each proven red-first against complete code:
* the gate's failure branch disabled -> "assert 0 == 1" on the never-installed
  probe; the same test then walks repo-moved-on, repaired, and installed-byte-
  mutated
* `generator` dropped from the skill's CHARSHEET-QA object -> "Right contains one
  more item: 'generator'" against the new `tests/fixtures/charsheet_qa_line.json`,
  the producer half of risk D.5's cross-repo pin (the launcher twin is B2's)
* trap 2 reworded back to trap 1's answer -> "assert 'STALE STORED TOKEN, not'
  in '...'"
* `baseImage` reverted to `""` -> "assert '' is None" in both payloads;
  `path_or_none` forced to None -> "assert False where False = isinstance(None,
  str)" on the presence case
* the verb-table regex is scoped to the table now: it still goes red on a deleted
  `reopen` row, and a second markdown table with a backticked lowercase first
  cell no longer poisons the set (proven both ways)

author: nekwo
message:
fix(harness-skills): the gate that was supposed to protect the runtime picked its target from the ambient env — and could have destroyed six packages to report "ok"

`91e23bf0c5` armed a pre-push gate on the one join a test cannot see. Its
closure re-review found the gate itself is the highest-severity defect in the
slice: `get_shared_skills_dir()` resolves through `get_default_hermes_root()`,
which with no `HERMES_HOME` falls to the Windows platform default. A git hook
inherits the pushing shell's environment, and that shell usually has no
`HERMES_HOME`.

Measured with it unset, the gate reported on
`C:\Users\beast\AppData\Local\hermes\shared\skills` — six canonical packages
DIVERGED, `harness-charsheet-authoring` never installed. That tree is the
`%LOCALAPPDATA%` shadow runtime `hermes_process_identity.dart` pins
`HERMES_HOME` specifically to avoid; its six packages are not this repo's
bytes. In default (repair) mode from such a shell the gate would have installed
all seven repo packages over it — `install_harness_skill` did
`os.replace(destination_dir, backup)` then
`finally: shutil.rmtree(backup, ignore_errors=True)`, so those six were
DESTROYED, not archived — then re-verified its own fresh copy and printed
`ok — every canonical package installed and current`, while
`X:\Eternia\.hermes\shared\skills`, the root every persona in the live roster
reads, was never touched and never checked. A gate that passes on the wrong
artifact, with an unrecoverable side effect.

So the root is EXPLICIT now. `resolve_gate_hermes_home` answers from
`ETERNIA_HERMES_HOME`, then `HERMES_HOME` — the same order and the same reason
as `hermes_cli_io.dart`'s `hermesProcessEnvironment`, so the gate targets the
home the serve child was spawned with — then `agent_runtime.head_home`, the
machine root anchor `harness serve` publishes at boot, read through
`chat_session_scope.declared_chat_head_home` rather than a second parser of the
same key. A DECLARATION is not a guess: it is the one durable record of "this
operator's runtime root is elsewhere", written by the process that provably
knew. With none of them, `HermesHomeUnresolved` and exit 2, naming what to set
— the hook's own principle, which already refuses to skip on a missing
interpreter. Printing the resolved root would not have done: nobody reads a
passing hook's output.

Repair-then-verify STAYS — divergence here is stale machine state and the
correct response to it is to fix it. What changes is its blast radius. An
ownership rule ("refuse a destination holding packages this repo does not
own") needs a marker no installed package carries, so it would either red every
first run or need a bootstrap exemption that reduces to trusting whatever is
there. Archiving needs neither: the displaced package moves into the shared
root's `.archive/` — already in `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS`, already the convention
`tools/skill_usage.archive_skill` uses under a skills root — so it stays
resolver-invisible and a wrong repair is one `mv` from undone. Nothing is
written at all when the hashes already match. A failed archive removes the
displaced copy rather than leaving `.backup-*` beside the packages, which is
NOT resolver-invisible and would turn a lost archive into a live collision.

And the hook now records why it is a hook and not CI, because the reason
published for that decision was false. Census of `.github/workflows/`: SIX
job-level `github.repository == 'NousResearch/hermes-agent'` guards across FOUR
files (`deploy-site.yml` deploy-docs; `docker.yml` build/publish/merge;
`skills-index.yml`; `skills-index-freshness.yml`). `ci.yml`'s
tests/lint/js-tests/uv-lockfile and `tests.yml` gate on
`needs.detect.outputs.*` and run on this fork perfectly well. The real reason
is structural: the destination is under the MACHINE's hermes root and a
GitHub-hosted runner has no such root, so CI could only install into a
throwaway filesystem and verify the copy it had just written.

Also from the same re-review:

* `test_charsheet_qa_line_fixture_pins_the_key_set_the_skill_promises` scraped
  the promised key set by structure and reddened on correct prose: a redundant
  restatement of the SAME keys gave `assert 3 == 2`, and reordering the keys in
  the example — identical to any JSON consumer — gave
  `At index 0 diff: 'slug' != 'draft'`. The key SET is the contract; the prose
  around it is not. First `":`-bearing span is required, the next is optional,
  later spans are restatement, and both compare as sets. Same false-positive
  class the verb-table test just retired.
* `FIELD-NOTES.md` gains the reason it sits at the package ROOT. A turn
  receives nothing from it, which is the point, and that is a property of the
  PLACEMENT: `agent/skill_commands.py::_build_skill_message` builds the message
  from `SKILL.md`'s content alone plus `linked_files` or a scan of exactly
  `references/`, `templates/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`. Moving it into
  `references/` as a tidy-up would advertise the raw record to every turn with
  a `skill_view(file_path=…)` instruction beside it.
* Two hermes-side sites still taught the overturned decision 6 — `authored_by`'s
  docstring ("under the one home the console shares") and `--authored-by`'s help
  ("drafts live under the one HERMES_HOME either way"). Both point at the
  launcher's §13.6 now instead of restating it, and both say what `authored_by`
  is actually FOR: not scoping, but letting a reader check that a resume opens
  under the profile that authored the draft.

Tests, each proven red-first against complete code:
* the refusal removed -> the same test's captured output reports the SHADOW
  root, six DIVERGED and one never-installed, exit 1 instead of 2
* `ETERNIA_HERMES_HOME` dropped from the ladder -> `'…\env-home' !=
  '…\launcher-home'`; the declaration rung removed -> `HermesHomeUnresolved`
  raised where the declaration should have answered
* the archive call reverted to `shutil.rmtree` -> "the displaced package must be
  archived, never rmtree'd", `assert []`
* the resolved-home report line removed -> the drift test's
  `home … (via env HERMES_HOME)` assertion fails
* the fixture test: both benign edits red on the OLD assertions and green on the
  new; `generator` dropped from the required object still reds, now as
  `Extra items in the right set: 'generator'`

message:
docs(charsheet): the first slice to run the whole loop writes down what the skill got wrong — including a cardSafe promise that only holds for one sheet size

A2 drove start -> base -> turnaround -> approve-direction -> rows -> thumb ->
reroll-row -> compose -> sprite -> reopen as an operator, on the console lane,
with the installed skill as its only instructions. Ten entries, each FACT then
CONSEQUENCE, cited by symbol.

The one that falsifies a standing note: `cardSafe: true` is read as "lighter
than the sheet this crop replaces" and it is not. `pipeline.MAX_CARD_PIXELS`
is `CHAR8.sheet_size()` — the largest sheet the package composes, not the
draft's own — so on a `--directions 4`, `idle:2` draft the DEFAULT crop came
back at 13.1x its own composed sheet still carrying `cardSafe: true`. The
struck consequence stays in the file with the measurement that killed it.

The rest are the places the skill left an authoring agent to guess: a state
below two frames passes `start` and dies at `rows` four generations later;
`thumb` is row-only so the turnaround stage has no crop verb and the agent
hand-rolled Pillow into the draft directory; `--directions 4` authors three;
`sprite --json` is 428.7 KiB of inline base64 against a 4 KiB pin and a 50 KB
tool cap; `CHARSHEET-QA`'s required `generator` key has no source and changes
meaning at compose.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet): a character grows a state without starting over — and the frame floor stops arriving four generations late

`characters add-state --draft <id> --state jumping:6[:fixed]` is the owner ask
from the 2026-08-24 authoring run: put a state on a character that is already
composed and installed, without re-authoring it. It refuses at any stage but
`rows`, so `reopen` stays the only door and this verb needs no stage logic of
its own; the state is APPENDED to a replaced (frozen) spec, so every row the
installed manifest already published keeps its index and the sheet grows
downward. Nothing is written to the revision store — a row is seeded by
appearing in the spec, which is exactly what an un-generated row already looks
like, and `compose` then refuses while any of the new rows lacks an approved
strip, naming every one. Add only, per owner decision 8. `--state` takes ONE
state; a comma-separated list is refused rather than becoming a second, quieter
spelling of `start --states`.

And the door it opens was a door into a known trap, so the trap is closed
first. `spec.parse_states` accepted a 1-frame state while the prompt builder
demanded 2, so `start --states idle:1` built a draft, spent the base anchor and
three direction generations, and only died at `rows` — with no verb able to
change `--states` afterwards. Two modules, two numbers, one rule. The number is
now `spec.MIN_FRAMES_PER_ROW`, enforced in `parse_states` — the ONE door both
`start --states` and `add-state --state` come through — and READ by
`prompts.build_directional_row_prompt` instead of re-spelled. It is deliberately
NOT raised on `StateSpec`/`SheetSpec`: those are also the deserializers for
every draft.json and character.json on disk, including the drafts the gap
produced, and refusing those at load would make such a draft unreadable rather
than repaired — `list_drafts` drops an unreadable draft with a log line, so it
would vanish from `characters list` instead of being explained. The spec says
what a sheet can hold; `parse_states` says what an operator may ask us to draw.

Because `--only` has no glob, the verb that knows the new row keys is the verb
that spells them: the human line hands back the whole ready-to-paste
`--only jumping-s,jumping-se,...` string, and the payload carries the same list.

Live on the anime-girl draft (home read back from `harness status --json`,
never asserted): reopen, add-state, five rows generated first-try each grounded
on the turnaround reference approved before any row was drawn, compose — 15
filled rows at 1536x3120, three states in character.json, idle/walk still at
row indices 0..9.

The docs correct in the same commit: the planned doc is marked BUILT with the
four as-built facts it did not have; SKILL.md's "add-state does not exist yet"
becomes the real loop, and its cost line stops quoting the 8-way five as if it
were a constant (a `--directions 4` sheet adds three strips, the same defect the
field notes already recorded one sentence over). FIELD-NOTES: the 2-frame entry
is STRUCK with its reason rather than deleted, and three new entries land —
add-state's shape, the no-renumber guarantee, and a measured turn of A2's
`cardSafe` finding: a grown sheet is now 1.50x the fixed MAX_CARD_PIXELS, so
`cardSafe: false` no longer implies "heavier than your sheet" either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
