author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the pin that proved nothing now builds the divergence it exists to catch — and three docs stop asserting what A3 made false

Six confirmed findings from an independent review of A3 (492bd561dc). A3's
runtime behaviour stands and is unchanged except for two refusal messages; what
was wrong was the evidence.

F1 — the anchoring pin was VACUOUS, and it is the one that mattered.
test_the_new_rows_are_anchored_to_the_turnaround_already_approved asserted
result["rows"][key]["reference"] == str(store.current(turnaround_item(d))) — the
expression CharacterDraft._row_reference itself computes — over a fixture where
no direction was ever rerolled, so current() and latest() named the same file.
Proven vacuous: swapping the production call to store.latest left the whole
suite green. The failure it could not see: at turnaround the operator rerolls
one direction, prefers the ORIGINAL and pins it with approve-direction
--attempt 0; that direction sits at approved=0, latest=1, and a state added
later would be silently grounded on the attempt they rejected. The fixture now
BUILDS that divergence (run_to_rows_keeping_the_older_attempt) and the
expectation is written as an attempt index the test chose, never as
store.current. Re-run under the same current->latest mutation: red on
attempt-2.png where attempt-1.png is required.

F2 — SKILL.md told the serving agent something this commit made false, and
SKILL.md is the half that reaches a turn. Its --scale bullet said "at or below
the default the crop must be lighter than the composed sheet (that is the whole
point of cropping)". pipeline.MAX_CARD_PIXELS is a module constant sized from
CHAR8 (1536x2080 = 3,194,880 px); the add-state-grown anime-girl sheet is
1536x3120 = 4,792,320 px, exactly 1.50x it. FIELD-NOTES is deliberately NOT
served to a turn (agent/skill_commands.py::_build_skill_message) and SKILL.md
is, so an agent reading the false line never met the correction struck beside
it. The bullet now names the fixed ceiling and points at
status --json .status.spec.sheetWidth x .sheetHeight for the draft's own size.

F3 — pipeline.py's comment asserted the opposite of what A3 proved: "a sheet
that grows moves the budget with it, and the number can never drift from the
thing it is measured against", above a module constant that does not move.
Option (a) taken per ruling: the budget IS a fixed console decode ceiling and
never was a comparison, so the comment says that and CharacterDraft.row_thumb's
refusal stops claiming a comparison it does not make ("heavier than the sheet
this crop exists to avoid decoding" -> the fixed card budget, "NOT a comparison
against this draft's own sheet"). No semantics change. Option (b) — rebase the
budget on the draft's own spec.sheet_size() — is NOT taken: it changes what
cardSafe means for launcher slice B2, and it is recorded in FIELD-NOTES as an
open question with both measurements (13.1x on a --directions 4, idle:2 draft;
1.50x on the grown sheet).

F4 — the frame-floor rationale stated a mechanism the code does not have,
tagged [READ], in the three places the reviewer had not yet corrected:
spec.py's MIN_FRAMES_PER_ROW comment, test_charsheet_spec.py's docstring, and
planned/charsheet-add-state.md's As-built bullet 3. Measured at the chokepoint
this time: CharacterDraft.load reads JSON only and CharacterDraft.spec is
computed on ACCESS, so list_drafts returns the bad draft; the raise lands one
level up in _characters_draft_summary inside _cmd_characters_list's own
except _CHARACTERS_EXPECTED -> ok=false, exit 2. The WHOLE verb fails and every
draft vanishes, not one. The ruling is unchanged and stronger. That test also
constructed SheetSpec directly and never touched the deserializer the rationale
rests on; it now round-trips draft.spec_from_dict over a real serialized spec.

F5 — add-state --state '' answered with a flag this verb does not have:
"--states is empty; expected e.g. 'idle:6,walk:8'" — the plural flag from
characters start, illustrated with a two-state list add-state refuses one check
later. spec.parse_states now takes the caller's flag/example spelling; the
grammar stays one authority. (start --states '' is not an error at all: an
empty value there means the CHAR8 states.)

F6 — add_state's docstring was wrong for a :fixed state and nothing covered
one. A :fixed row has direction None, so _row_reference answers _require_base()
— the base image, not a turnaround reference. The docstring now says what each
kind of row grounds on, and a test covers a :fixed add-state including its
reference.

Also pinned: "one number, one source" for the frame floor, which the reviewer
found green under prompts.py re-hardcoding MIN_FRAMES_PER_ROW = 2. The
suggested identity assertion cannot catch it — CPython interns every int in
-5..256, so prompts.MIN_FRAMES_PER_ROW is spec.MIN_FRAMES_PER_ROW evaluates
True under exactly that mutation (verified), and a `from X import Y` binding
does not follow a monkeypatch of X either. The guarantee is a SOURCE property,
so it is pinned as one: an AST walk of prompts.py requiring the ImportFrom and
forbidding any assignment. Both halves proven red.

SKILL.md's "A state is added, never removed" bullet — flagged by the reviewer
as completeness belonging to AF, not a repair — is KEPT and recorded in
FIELD-NOTES under a new "For AF" heading, with the reasoning: it is true at the
code and it stops an agent promising a verb that does not exist.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the ne row stops facing north-west — the prompt says which side of the FRAME, and compose refuses a mirrored row

anime-girl's `ne` was drawn facing north-WEST, composed, installed and bundled
into the launcher, and was found by a human looking at a 3D scene. Because the
consumer derives `nw` by flipping `ne` (ADR 0024 ruling 3-B), that one row broke
BOTH rear diagonals while the other six directions stayed correct — which is
exactly why it read as a launcher sector bug and survived every QA pass.

The wrong layer was the PROMPT, not the mirror map and not compose.
`prompts.VIEW_LANGUAGE["ne"]` said "three-quarter BACK view turned toward the
viewer's right: … a sliver of the FAR cheek". Two faults, and only together do
they explain it: the sentence named no side of the frame — no leading shoulder,
unlike its front twin `se` — so its only anchor was a phrase that flips meaning
once the character faces away; and "far cheek" is backwards for a back
three-quarter, where the cheek that clears the head is the NEAR one.

Measured, not inferred. Face offset from the body centroid across s se e ne n:
  idle     +0.0  +5.2  +10.9   -6.5  -0.3
  walk     +1.7  +6.2   +9.9   -8.8  -2.2
  jumping  +0.2  +6.4  +10.5   -9.7  -0.1
Three independent generations — idle and walk on 08-24, jumping on 08-25 —
reversing at the same single step, while `se` carried the same "toward the
viewer's right" phrase in a front view and was right in all three. `nw` got the
mirrored rewrite; the front diagonals are deliberately untouched.

The gate: pipeline.detect_mirrored_art, called from validate_sheet, so it blocks
compose and therefore install. Per directional state it walks the authored rows
in turnaround order and asks of each: would flipping THIS row make the seams it
touches fit better? Threshold 8%, a ratio so it is scale- and palette-free.
Pillow only — numpy is not a dependency of this package and is absent from the
venv the runtime actually runs in. ~1 s on a 15-row sheet.

  defective sheet   idle-ne 19%   walk-ne 13%   jumping-ne 13%   -> refused
  corrected sheet   every judged row clean                        -> installs
  cobalt-robot-courier (4-way, satchel over one shoulder)  1.9%   -> installs

It scores a ROW and not a seam because a seam only says its two rows disagree.
The ends of the rotation touch one seam each and are never judged — they are
named in `handedness.unjudged` with the reason. That exclusion is not tidiness:
an earlier draft judged them and refused cobalt-robot-courier, a correct
character whose back view's single seam preferred the mirror by 11%.

The launcher-side proposal — flag only when BOTH neighbours prefer the mirror —
was measured on the walk state alone. On idle it clears the row: idle-ne vs
idle-n reads 11.84 against 12.10, noise off a near-symmetric back view, and that
2.1% vetoes the other neighbour's 29%. Summing seams lets a weak neighbour
dilute without voting.

Two things pass it by construction and both are pinned by tests so they stay
known: a sheet mirrored on EVERY row (the measure is invariant under a global
flip — only the world outside a sheet says which way is east), and the interior
of a contiguous block. A 4-way scheme is nearly blind too.

Docs corrected in the same commit where they disagreed with the code:
agent/charsheet/__init__.py said the derived directions are "derived at compose
time", false since ruling 3-B; SKILL.md's "do not build a pass/fail scanner"
now draws the boundary this one sits on, and gains the compose refusal an
authoring agent will meet. FIELD-NOTES gains five entries, including that the
approved turnaround reference does NOT determine a row's facing — the `e`
reference is a LEFT-facing profile (-44.8) while all three `e` rows are right.

Tests proven red-first by sabotage round-trip: unwire the refusal ->
blocks_the_install fails; judge the end rows -> the end-row test convicts
idle-n; break the ne/nw left-right symmetry -> the vocabulary test fails.
47 passed in test_charsheet_pipeline; 290 across the four charsheet suites.

author: nekwo
message:
docs(charsheet): what the ne repair actually cost — four findings from running it, not from reading it

The fix landed; then I regenerated anime-girl's three `ne` rows against the live
provider and the run taught four things the code change could not.

A wrong turnaround reference is PERMANENT once a draft leaves `turnaround`:
reroll_direction and approve_direction both require that stage, `reopen` only
goes composed -> rows, and nothing replaces an approved reference afterwards. The
`ne` reference is a north-WEST view from the single 08-24 generation, so the
whole repair had to be made row-side against a reference pulling the other way.

Spelling the target facing was not enough. With the corrected VIEW_LANGUAGE in
the prompt, a note describing the target in frame terms landed ONE of three
rows; a more emphatic "ignore the reference" version failed again on walk-ne.
What landed both remaining rows first try was naming the conflict and giving the
model an operation — "MIRROR THE REFERENCE'S TURN: copy its design, then draw it
turned the OTHER way" — plus one anatomical anchor, "her right ear is the only
ear visible and it sits on the RIGHT-HAND SIDE of her head". Six generations for
three rows.

A row reroll is a one-way door: reroll_row proposes then approves
unconditionally and there is no approve-row verb, so a reroll that comes back
worse cannot be un-approved. Look at the strip before spending the next one.

And the gate answers which SIDE, never how far — the repaired `jumping` row now
reads +15.1 against its own profile's +10.5, a rear diagonal drawn closer to
side-on than the rotation wants. That is correct handedness and an uneven
turnaround, and detect_mirrored_art has nothing to say about it by design.

Result: the draft composes clean through the gate at 1536x3120, the `jumping`
state and every operator note survived (walk-n untouched at 3/2; walk-ne now 5/4
with its 08-24 note intact), and the same gate is still red on the pre-fix sheet.

message:
docs(charsheet): three field-note corrections the review measured — a figure that does not reproduce, and two blind spots the gate entry called exact

Read-only review of 1175d3db90 / 49e983d1aa re-ran every number on the
preserved pre-fix sheet and the repaired install. Three claims did not hold.

1. The two-neighbour falsification is TRUE and its veto figure is not. Measured
   on the pre-fix sheet, idle-ne's seams read idle-e 18.46 -> 12.59 (the mirror
   is 31.8% better) and idle-n 11.84 -> 12.10 (the art is 2.1% better). The
   entry, and `1175d3db90`'s body, both say the vetoed neighbour read 29%.

2. "Two things pass it by construction" is now four. A whole directional STATE
   mirrored passes clean — the fixed point is per state because the chain never
   leaves one — which `add_state` makes reachable in one batch, while the
   cross-state evidence sits unused (idle-e vs a mirrored jumping-e: +22.4%;
   the same pairs on correct art: -15.7% to -68.9%).

3. The gate flags a mirrored row's correct NEIGHBOURS too: mirroring idle-e
   alone flags idle-se at 13.1% and idle-ne at 20.8%. Each is an error, each
   message says reroll-row, and reroll_row auto-approves — so obeying the

Also recorded: the measure has no registration step and reads placement as
handedness. An 8 px horizontal shift of idle-e in a 192 px frame, art
untouched, moves it -38.2% -> +9.4% and refuses. `normalize_cells`'s union-bbox
centring (residual +/-3 px measured) is what holds that off, and it is upstream
pet code this package does not own. A one-sided prop ~10% of the frame width on
ONE row crosses the line: 16 px -> +5.2% (installs), 20 px -> +8.0% (refused).

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the handedness gate stops reading PLACEMENT as handedness, names one culprit instead of three, and can be told it is wrong

Round one's gate works and its diagnosis holds. Its two unsafe properties were
attribution and coverage, and both mattered because detect_mirrored_art blocks
compose and there was deliberately no way past it: a false refusal was permanent
for that draft.

REGISTRATION. The measure paired cells by column index with no alignment step, so
a horizontal displacement between neighbouring rows entered the distance and
therefore the ratio. Measured on the REPAIRED (correct) live sheet by sliding
idle-e sideways and changing nothing else: -7px scored +9.81% and refused, -24px
+18.75%. The reachable driver is a prop, because normalize_cells centres each row
on its union bbox: a bag or a cape off one side of ONE row moves the body by half
its width, and a 24px prop already refused. _registered_distance now takes the
minimum over a symmetric integer shift grid of +/-frame_w/12 for both
orientations. After it the same slides read -18.05% and install, and a one-sided
prop a quarter of the frame wide installs at +5.19%. The grid is a symmetric
MINIMUM and not a correlation peak so distance(shift(flip a,d),flip b) ==
distance(shift(a,-d),b) keeps the global-flip fixed point exactly true.

It is not free, and the honest reading is that half of round one's signal was
placement. Re-measured on real art: the pre-fix ne rows go 18.53/13.05/13.01% ->
12.28/8.52/7.37%; mirroring each interior row of the repaired sheet one at a time
goes floor +8.51% -> +4.33%; the correct rows go <=-9.30% -> <=-4.53%; and
cobalt-robot-courier, the deliberately asymmetric correct character, barely moves
(+1.85% -> +1.72%). Separation narrows from ~7x to ~2.5x. The threshold stays at
8%, set for specificity.

ATTRIBUTION. A mirrored row raises BOTH its neighbours: mirroring idle-e alone
puts idle-e at +13.33% and idle-ne at +11.87%. Round one made each a separate
error, each message says reroll-row, reroll_row proposes then approves
unconditionally, and no approve-row verb exists anywhere - so obeying a three-row
refusal spent two correct approved attempts that cannot be recovered. Only the
local maximum of each contiguous run is reported now; the rest ride as
corroborating and the message says not to touch them.

COVERAGE. A whole directional STATE mirrored passed clean, which add-state makes
reachable in one batch against one reference and one prompt. A second pass
compares the same direction across states: correct art reads -8.27..-75.71%, one
mirrored state reads +7.64..+43.09%, and a row is convicted only against a
majority of the other states, so it needs three. It also recovers what
registration cost - idle-se mirrored reads +4.33% in the rotation and +11.76%
across states. A blank row used to make its whole state unjudged on a sheet that
still installs; a row is now judged whenever it has a measurable seam on each
side, which folds the end rows, short chains and blank neighbours into one rule
and kills both mutations round one left green.

THE OVERRIDE, ADDED. The premise for shipping none was that the false positives
were asymmetric poses, which the ratio handles. The driver is framing, the window
BOUNDS that class rather than removing it (-24px still reads +10.91% registered),
and the populations are 2.5x apart on the only two characters ever measured. So
compose --accept-handedness names ROWS, records them on the installed manifest as
handednessAccepted, keeps every other flagged row refusing, and refuses a name
that was not flagged so the flag cannot become boilerplate.

THE THRESHOLD IS PINNED, AND THE RED EVIDENCE IS IN THE REPO. It had no test: the
suite was green from ~0.03 to 0.25 because the glyph fixture scored an order
above the live band, and the only real defective art lived in one operator's home
under a hand-made backup nothing protected. tests/fixtures/charsheet/ now holds
the anime-girl sheet with its genuinely mirrored idle-ne (+12.05% rotation,
+15.40% states, loudest false +5.03%) and a byte copy of cobalt-robot-courier.
The test asserts loudest false < MIRROR_GAIN_THRESHOLD < quietest true.

ACCOUNTING. handedness.unjudged was read by nothing outside the module: compose
printed WxH, the payload needed --json, and a refusal raised and discarded it.
handedness_summary is one line on both paths.

Corrections landed with the code: the call-site comment said the check runs only
on a sheet whose geometry holds (it runs unconditionally after the other checks);
as_drawn <= 0 dropped a row from flagged AND unjudged; "~1 s on a 15-row sheet"
was 0.08 s unregistered and is ~4.0 s registered. The end-row test moved off the
synthetic badge - registration made that construction pathological - onto the
real 4-way character whose single seam prefers the mirror by +10.91% while its
interior neighbour is diluted to +1.72%.

357 passed across the five charsheet suites; pets sprite byte-baseline re-verified
after the harness.py touch.

author: nekwo
message:
test(charsheet): two of the sixteen sabotages survived — the grid-symmetry and blank-row proofs were measuring pairs that could not tell the difference

Round-trip proof of the previous commit: break the line each test claims to
cover, watch it go red, restore. Fourteen went red. Two did not, and both were
the test's fault.

The shift grid. The symmetry proof compared two ordinary neighbouring cells whose
best alignment sits in the middle of the window, so dropping the +window endpoint
from the grid changed neither minimum and the test stayed green — the exact hole
an asymmetric grid would open, invisible to the assertion written for it. It now
compares a cell against ITSELF slid by exactly the window: the true minimum is 0,
reachable from one end only, and from the other end once both are flipped. The
shifts are asserted to be (+window, -window) so the endpoint is the thing under
test, and the ordinary middle-of-window pair is kept as the second case.

The blank row. The proof blanked `walk-e` — the row whose two neighbours are the
only other rows the chain could judge — so the whole `walk` state went unjudged
under the repair and under the round-one rule alike, and the test could not
distinguish them. It now blanks the END row `walk-s` and mirrors `walk-e` in the
same state: the repair keeps judging `walk-e` and `walk-ne` and catches the
mirrored row (+15.29%), where the old rule would have made the empty row swallow
its whole chain and shipped it. `walk-se`, the blank row's only neighbour, is the
one judgement actually lost.

Also round-tripped: round one's two surviving mutations. `if blank:` ->
`if False:` is now red on the blank-row test; `if len(chain) < 3:` no longer
exists to mutate — the "a row needs a measurable seam on each side" rule made it
unreachable.

357 passed across the five charsheet suites.

author: nekwo
message:
docs(charsheet): five handedness corrections the round-two review measured — an attribution rule that inverts, a timing that is 2x, and two promises no test holds

Round two's own numbers reproduce: the true floor at +4.33%, the false ceiling
at -4.53%, the pre-fix ne rows at +12.28/+8.52/+7.37%, cobalt at +1.72%, the
global-flip fixed point exact on real 15-row art, and the 10 px normalize_cells
residual (which an alpha-weighted centroid does NOT show — the number is the
shift the registration itself picks). These are the places the record is wrong
or short.

STRUCK: "in every case measured the culprit was the run's maximum". It holds
only for exactly one faulty row per run. A correct row slid -24 px puts the
UNTOUCHED neighbour at the maximum (+10.91% against the displaced row's +9.38%),

sheet over three clean runs, 6.46 s for validate_sheet end to end.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): one basis warns, two refuse — the handedness gate stops pointing reroll-row at correct art

Round two's repair stands as a repair: registration, the symmetric-minimum fixed
point and the accounting all reproduce. As a GATE it did not, and it failed in the
dangerous direction — its attribution rule pointed reroll-row at correct art in two
reachable shapes, and reroll_row proposes-then-approves with no approve-row verb
anywhere in the repo.

THE THRESHOLD IS NOT THE LEVER. Measured in both directions, the two populations do
not separate at 8% and nothing else separates them either. True floor BELOW the line
on real art: jumping-se mirrored reads +6.78% rotation / +7.64% states, flagged by
neither pass, composes and ships. The founding defect sits AT the line: jumping-ne
reads +7.37%. False ceiling far above that floor once art is stressed: a CORRECT
idle-e slid reads +9.38 / +17.92 / +18.75 / +7.76% at -24 / -32 / -40 / -56 px, a
BAND and not a threshold. max(false) 18.75% > min(true) 7.64%. So the number did not
move; what one reading is allowed to DO did. A single-basis finding is a WARNING;
ERROR is reserved for two independent bases agreeing about the same row. The
consequence is stated in the code, the payload and SKILL.md rather than hidden:
characters start creates idle:6, walk:8, so on the DEFAULT character this gate can
only ever warn — and on a two-state cut of the live art a whole mirrored state
already scored bit-identical to the correct sheet, so blocking on one weak reading
bought confidence it did not have. compose now prints every warning on the human line.

ATTRIBUTION. "The culprit is the run's maximum" is retired, not re-tuned. Both
inversion shapes reproduce on the checked-in fixture and are now tests. PLACEMENT:
walk-e slid -24px reads +10.48% and drags the untouched walk-ne to +10.68%, so the
maximum is the innocent neighbour and the disturbed row rides under "Do NOT re-roll
them". FLANKED: idle-se and idle-ne mirrored, idle-e correct — what a second
badly-worded diagonal produces — and the correct middle row wins at +14.28% while
its cross-state reading of -75/-97% sits unused in the same payload. Now: a run of
two or more is named only when a second basis convicts exactly one of them,
otherwise it reports "one of N rows and this pass cannot say which" with no
reroll-row line. A lone flagged row is still named.

A NEGATIVE CROSS-STATE READING IS NOT A CHARACTER REFERENCE. The obvious form of
that repair would have retired the defect the gate was built for: a direction
mirrored in EVERY state is a fixed point of the cross-state pass and reads -111.32%
there precisely because it is consistently wrong, numerically indistinguishable from
the flanked shape's -97.62%. What separates them is that ne is over the line in 3
rotations of 3 there and e in 1 of 3 in both inversions, so a contradicted row is
demoted unless its direction is suspected in a strict majority of the rotations.

THE STATES MAJORITY WAS NOT ONE ON AN EVEN NUMBER OF STATES. len(pairs) // 2 + 1 is
2 of 3 on a four-state sheet, so a 2-2 split convicted all four — the two CORRECT
ones at +14.31% basis states, no corroborating marker, while their rotations read
-15.97% — and SKILL.md called that the one case where re-rolling several rows IS
right. One add-state reaches four. It is len(drawn) // 2 + 1 now: a row is convicted
only when its camp is a strict minority; an even split convicts nobody and says so.
The states pass runs through the attribution step, and its len(ranked) < needed case
is an unjudged entry rather than a bare continue.

THE OVERRIDE'S RECORD HALF. handednessAccepted had zero readers in either repo;
it is republished by characters list and sprite_payload now, which is what lets
bundle_character.dart read it without decoding a pixel. It stored row keys only, so
a +40% acceptance and an +8.1% one were indistinguishable; it is {row, gain, basis}
(old bare-key manifests still parse). And one row name waived two independent bodies
of evidence, so the token is <row>:rotation+states; a bare row is refused with the
spelling it needs and a WARNING cannot be accepted at all.

THREE KNOBS NO FIXTURE COULD SEE. REGISTRATION_WINDOW_DIVISOR 12 -> 6 and -> 3 both
left all 62 tests green while moving the false-refusal boundary from -24px to past
-56px; asserted directly now, with the complement the window exists for. The culprit
rule is gone rather than re-pinned. And max(convicted) ranked a branch no input can
reach — two ADJACENT mirrored rows never form a rotation run, they read -5.30% /
-15.36% — so it is len(convicted) == 1 and the unreachable ranking is deleted. When
a fixture cannot reach a branch, delete the branch.

THE normalize_cells PIN DOES NOT DO WHAT IT WAS PROPOSED TO DO, and the note is
struck with the measurement. Replacing normalize_cells with a fit that centres
nothing leaves every composed shift at 0, because extract_strip_frames content-crops
per slot BEFORE the centring runs. The test is kept for what it does measure — 9px
of a 16px window on real art through compose_draft_frames, a 32px prop saturating
it, detection floor 6px measured by injected drift.

TIMING. The residue scan was a Python loop over 1.8M pixels on every compose, 0.39s
of a 3.0s validate_sheet; three Pillow band ops now, 0.031s, identical counts. Suites
cache each distinct mutated sheet. 357 passed / 311.96s -> 377 passed / 187-228s,
worst single test 8.73s against the 30s cap, from 58% to 29%.

Every fix proven red-first: 16 sabotages applied and reverted, both inversion shapes
included; two survived the first pass and both were fixed as CODE (a branch masking
its own knob, and an unreachable ranking) rather than by weakening the assertion.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet): split cardSafe into two flags, and a whole mirrored STATE now refuses

Two owner rulings, 2026-08-25, both landing in the charsheet generator.

RULING 1 — `cardSafe` was two guarantees wearing one name, so it is split.
`MAX_CARD_PIXELS` was a module constant sized once from `CHAR8.sheet_size()`,
so the boolean meant "under the console's fixed decode ceiling" while every
reader took it for "no bigger than the sheet it previews". Measured at both
ends, and both re-verified at the code before implementing: a `--directions 4,
idle:2` draft's DEFAULT crop is 1774x1774 = 3,147,076 px, 13.1x its own
239,616-px sheet, and cleared the budget; `add-state --state jumping:6`
recomposes anime-girl at 4,792,320 px = exactly 1.50x the fixed budget, so a
draft's own sheet can sit ABOVE a ceiling its crops pass.

The constant keeps its value and gets an honest name
(`MAX_CONSOLE_CARD_PIXELS`); `fits_card_budget` becomes `fits_console_budget`;
`fits_own_sheet(w, h, spec)` is new and moves with the draft. `thumb` carries
`withinConsoleBudget` and `withinOwnSheet` — `cardSafe` is gone, not aliased.
The refusal at the default scale still keys on the console ceiling alone; the
sheet bound refuses nothing and is reported at every scale. The payload doc
comment records the consumer rule for the not-yet-built launcher card: inline
only when BOTH are true, otherwise route to the viewer. The CLI line says WHICH
bound was missed, because the two have different remedies.

Both measurements are tests, and they DISAGREE on exactly those cases — the
sabotage that reddens them is `fits_own_sheet` returning the console answer,
i.e. the pre-split state.

RULING 2 — a whole mirrored STATE is an ERROR, on one basis or two.
Verified the premise at the code first: `CHAR8` is two directional states, the
cross-state pass takes its `len(drawn) < 3` branch for every direction,
`state_flagged` stays empty, so `basis: "rotation and states"` is unreachable
and the default character could only ever warn. True as recorded.

`detect_mirrored_art` now escalates a `states` finding covering EVERY judged
row of one state, with two guards: at least two rows (a 4-way scheme judges ONE
row per state across states, and a single mirrored row stays a WARNING per the
ruling), and every judged row rather than a majority (one judged row reading
clean is a block of bad rows, not a bad state). Escalated findings carry
`wholeState` — that state's flagged rows in sheet order — and get their own
message: the rotation is a fixed point of a wholly mirrored state, so its
silence is not a second opinion and no second basis can ever arrive.

The override had to reach it, and could not: `ACCEPT_BASIS_TOKEN` was a single
hardcoded "rotation+states" and `validate_sheet` refused every other spelling,
so a one-basis error would have had NO legal acceptance — an error with no door
on the verb that has no other door. The token is now derived from the finding
(`accept_basis_token`), and the refusal that demands it and the message that
teaches it call the same function. An operator waives a whole-state refusal one
row at a time: `--accept-handedness jump-se:states,jump-e:states,jump-ne:states`.

Focused suites: 386 passed (charsheet pipeline/draft/revisions/spec + the
characters CLI). Every new behaviour was proven red-first by sabotage and
round-tripped back to green.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(charsheet): the handedness refusal shows the door it has, and stops being one 1206-character line

Both defects were found by running `characters compose` on real mirrored art,
not by reading the module.

The escape hatch was undiscoverable on the shape an operator actually hits. The
whole-state branch spelled `--accept-handedness` and the two-basis branch did
not, so what shipped was not a policy of not advertising an override but a DRIFT
between two spellings of the same thing — the class `accept_basis_token` exists
to be the only copy of. Ruling 18 tightens this gate *because* the row-named
override is reachable, and an operator who has LOOKED at the strip and believes
the art was being sent to the one remedy that destroys it: the message's own
words are that a re-roll auto-approves and there is no approve-row verb to undo
it. So the door is SHOWN on both blocking shapes, after the re-roll line,
conditional on having looked, and priced — an acceptance is a permanent public
fact about the character (`{row, gain, basis}` on the manifest, republished by
`characters list`, `sprite_payload` and the launcher's bundle warnings), which
is what keeps it from reading as the cheap way out. The one-way cost of a
re-roll now rides on every branch that hands over an action; it used to ride
only on the optional corroborating tail, so a refusal about an ISOLATED row —
the founding `ne` defect's exact shape — told the operator to spend approved art
and never said the spending could not be taken back.

The diagnostic was one unwrapped paragraph: measured 1206 characters on a single
line, and 1519 when a malformed acceptance made the validator restate the same
finding underneath the acceptance error, 79% of it text just read. It is now a
headline that stands alone plus one `label: value` line per fact — longest line
286 — with NO wrap width chosen here, because a column count picked in this
module is wrong for every consumer that is not an 80-column terminal. A
malformed acceptance folds into the block for the row it names instead of
printing beside it: one row, one block. The raise leads with the failure and the
handedness accounting, so a surface that shows two lines shows what failed and
how far the check could see.

Not changed: the token is still DERIVED per finding by `accept_basis_token`, and
the refusal that demands it and the message that teaches it are still that one
call. The new round-trip test takes the tokens out of the printed refusal and
feeds exactly those back to `validate_sheet`, so a second spelling anywhere
reddens.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(placement): S6 — both workspace spellings everywhere, the join nobody watched gets a reader, and the refusals that wrote nothing stop saying otherwise

Three of the placement plan's remainders, each one a place where the runtime
already knew the answer and no surface would say it.

**The flag was a per-verb accident.** `--workspace` with dest `workspace`
(office, board), `--workspace` with dest `workspace_id` (`agent create`), and
`--workspace-id` (persona instance, mission chat) — one argument, three
spellings, and an operator who learned one verb was refused by the next. D8's
answer is aliases on the EXISTING dests: nothing renamed, nothing removed, both
spellings on all fourteen verbs. The fence is a WALK of the real parser tree,
not a typed roster, because a list of the verbs is a second copy of the parser
that is free to fall behind it. Its discriminator is the dest and a nonzero
value width, never the option string: `realm agents set --workspace` is a
`store_true` selecting which persona definitions a realm publishes, and a rule
keyed on spelling would have demanded a `--workspace-id` alias for a boolean.

**The join had no reader.** The persona-instance row answers "does this agent
exist" and the office actor answers "is it on this level"; `persona instance
reconcile` prunes orphan rows without opening the office and no doctor section
read the two together, so a half-state — a retired instance whose actor
survived, a compensation that archived the row and not the desk — was
representable, durable, and invisible to the tool an operator runs to find it.
`harness doctor` gains `placement_census`: per workspace, `placed` /
`unplaced_rows` / `orphan_actors`, read-only, because both repairs are operator
gestures and the doctor sees one snapshot.

Two properties are the section's whole contract. An unplaced row is a NOTICE,
not a defect — the roster-only recovery door mints exactly that on purpose, and
a canonical operator channel is excluded outright or every healthy runtime
would carry one permanent finding per persona that nobody can clear. And a
SHORT world is `unknown`, never a partition: both scans return the rows they
could read beside a count of the ones they could not, and a census over the
readable remainder reports a perfectly healthy placement as an orphan because
the file that would not decode is its roster row. The first draft here did
exactly that; the test for it went red before the code was fixed.

**A missing key is not a neutral key.** Every `AgentCreateInvalid` arm — the
eight refusals that run before `OfficeStore` is even constructed — carried no
`rolled_back`, and the launcher renders an absent stamp as "the placement could
not be undone". So every mistyped persona id sent the operator hunting wreckage
that cannot exist. `1da669d908` stamped the reservation and placement arms and
stopped short of these; they refuse EARLIER than the one arm it did stamp. The
parametrisation enumerates the arms from the module's own AST, so a ninth arm
cannot ship unstamped by being forgotten.

Also here, guarding a sequencing hazard the plan names: the parser walk asserts
`--pos` is optional whenever an `agent retire` subcommand exists. Today neither
holds and it passes while saying so; it reds the moment S5 lands without S2,
which is the one ordering that would strand every launcher trusting the
manifest marker.

Gate: pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_workspace_flag_aliases.py
tests/agent_runtime/test_harness_doctor.py
tests/agent_runtime/test_agent_create_service.py -q — 44 passed.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(office): S3 — one persona holds one desk, and the rule stops being the client's alone

The one-desk-per-persona rule lived only in the launcher: a gesture guard
(hasAuthoredDeskForPersona) and a render-time count (_scanDeskInvariants). The
client refused what the client authored and reported what it found — neither
stands in front of `harness office actor-upsert`, which is the door the
2026-08-24 incident authored a second `qa` desk through, and the store took the
write.

So the rule moves to the write chokepoint (plan agent-placement-verb D6/D11).
OfficeStore._guard_duplicate_desk runs inside office_lock, after the class-key
fence and the conflict guard, before the revision check and before any write —
including on --dry-run. Both doors keep a TRANSLATION of the typed refusal and
no copy of the predicate: runtime.office.upsert answers ERR_CONFLICT 4090 with
data.reason=duplicate_desk naming the holding actor and item, and `harness
office actor-upsert` exits 4 on the same code, with its own taxonomy row and its
own hint (the default hint points at safe_details, which this envelope never
merges).

The predicate asks about the POST-WRITE state, because an upsert REPLACES the
target actor's items. Three behaviours fall out of that one sentence instead of
three branches: moving your own desk is accepted, a second actor desking the
same persona is refused, and a desk whose only holder is ARCHIVED is accepted —
scan_actors reads the live directory and an archive is not a holding.

A desk's identity is its item_id, and the count is of DISTINCT ids. That is the
same narrowing office_class_key_guard already records, and it is load-bearing
rather than stylistic: the class→instance re-key migration mints the
instance-keyed actor with the old actor's items COPIED VERBATIM and only then
archives the old key, so both rows briefly claim one desk. Counting rows would
have refused the one operator script whose whole job is to move a placement
while catching nothing this fence is for. Measured, not reasoned — counting rows
reddened 27 tests across the class-key and rekey-script suites.

Realm pull stays outside the fence on purpose: office_sync.apply_office_pull
writes actor files directly and never reaches upsert_actor, so a pulled
duplicate is a conflict-lane fact about what a peer published, not a local
write. The launcher's render warning stays for exactly that.

Unknowable is not "no holder": the fence raises ActorsUnreadable rather than
answering from a directory it could only partly read (EG-6.6's rule). It scans
only when the payload carries a desk, so no agent placement pays for it — the
placement verb authors no desk at all, pinned at RUNTIME by
test_verb_authors_no_desk, which creates into a workspace where the fence is
armed and pointed at the write.

test_cli_unbound_placement_sharing_a_persona_but_not_items_is_allowed had used a
second DESK to demonstrate a non-overlapping item id. Its fixture is now an
agent item — its question is the class-key fence's, and a fixture that also
trips the desk fence would stop meaning what its docstring says — with a
companion test pinning the desk arm so the two rules are stated together.

Eleven killing mutations, each proved red then reverted with a sha round-trip.

Docs move with the code: 06's write-verbs section gains the fence, the ordering
of all four guards, the identity rule, the realm-pull boundary and the known
residual (an instance-keyed write claiming a live desk id passes both fences —
the migration's transient made permanent, which the census closes, not a third
fence). Invariant 12 added.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(stream): S0 — the create's frame was never captured, so it was asked live and pinned twice

F6 left one question open and everything in the placement plan stood on the
answer: does an out-of-process `agent create` reach a connected client as ONE
patch frame carrying both halves, or does it demote, or is it dropped at the
fold? The 2026-08-24 "nothing notified the client" was measured against a
hand-assembled `persona instance create` + `office actor-upsert` pair, and no
frame capture existed at all.

Taken live: serve, a `harness stream --fold-entities ...` in a second process,
one `harness agent create` in a third, all against one isolated runtime root.
The receipt is in the plan's F6. It is a patch — two rows, both `created: true`,
`base_offset` equal to the offset the subscriber hydrated at, and it landed
0.359s BEFORE the operator's own command returned. Zero demote receipts.

The frame is now committed rather than remembered. The generator grew a builder
that performs the real create and asks `_batch_frames_with_liveness` — the
promotion decision itself — rather than choosing a lane: a demote fails
generation instead of quietly committing a golden that pins the bug. Its twin,
the same batch rendered for a subscriber declaring only the historical two,
pins the other arm of A.11's intersection hazard so nobody discovers it on a
phone.

These are the first goldens built from a real store WRITE, and three classes of
value had to be pinned rather than measured — event-log byte offsets (a create's
events embed absolute paths), the registry-probed tool scalars, and the wall
clocks. Each is opt-in per frame, so no existing golden's bytes moved.
`ts`/`last_event_ts` in particular can never be global: the delta pair's
one-second gap is its own evidence that it coalesced two events.

Two corrections to the plan land with it. F6 becomes a [READ] with the receipt.
The C-table's launcher mutation was wrong at code — removing the lifecycle token
from `kMissionFoldDeclaredEntities` reds nothing in the fold, because that
constant is only the declaration the subscribe lanes send; the fold
inserts-on-absent unconditionally. The mutation that kills the S0 cases is the
pre-O-L1 fold, and it was run.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(office): S1 — the launcher's placement lattice becomes hermes' too, and a case file makes the two say so

`MissionOfficePlacementPolicy` decided where an unaimed placement goes, and it
decided it in Dart. hermes had nothing: grep `layout|slot|spawn` across
`agent_runtime/` finds nothing that chooses a scene position, which is why
`--pos` is required and why every door with no canvas — the CLI, a cron, a
remote connector over `call` — had no answer to give.

Plan D2 makes hermes the authority and leaves the launcher a prediction, so this
is a PORT and not an invention: `agent_runtime/office_layout_policy.py` carries
the same seven constants and the same scan order, value for value, down to the
strict `<` on the occupancy radius and the lane offset applied INSIDE the scan
rather than to the winning slot.

Two policies that can disagree are the defect D2 exists for, so the agreement is
pinned by `cases.json`, committed byte-identical in both repos under a manifest
each side hashes. Eleven cases: the empty floor, a filled gap, a full row
wrapping, the desk lane, an off-lattice drag blocking its nearest slot, and 200
blockers proving the pigeonhole bound terminates on something free.

Two of them are there because the two repos are ASYMMETRIC and would otherwise
have diverged in silence:

* `hidden` is launcher-only — this store has no such field — so both sides must
  count a tucked-away item as occupying its slot, one by honouring the flag and
  one by never having had it;
* a blank `folder` is hermes-only — `_normalize_item` persists `""` where the
  launcher's decoder substitutes the kind's default — so the policy resolves the
  fallback when it SCANS, or a legacy item blocks the lattice in one repo and is
  invisible in the other.

No caller yet: S2 is what makes an absent position reach this.

The tolerance is 1e-4 and it is not slack. `Vector2` stores 32-bit floats, so
6.4 round-trips as 6.400000095… and the 25-row case accumulates about 1e-6 —
four orders below the tolerance, which is itself four orders below this
lattice's smallest gap. Never assert exact equality across the two sides.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(placement): S2 — a create no longer has to know where it is going, and the ack stops making the client guess where it went

`--pos` was `required=True` and `_position` refused an absent one, so every door
without a canvas had to invent a coordinate: a cron, a script, a remote
connector over `call`, and the launcher's own palette add, which sends a slot it
predicted from a snapshot already a round trip stale. The verb could place an
agent; it could not decide WHERE.

Now absence is a request rather than a refusal. With no `position` the service
resolves the slot through `office_layout_policy` (S1) — the workspace's live
actors in the request's folder, first free lattice slot. With one, it is written
verbatim, exactly as before; a MANGLED aim (a one-element list, a string, a bool
pair, an infinity) still refuses `position_invalid`, because a transport that
lost half a coordinate is not an operator who had no opinion. An explicit JSON
`null` reads as absence, deliberately — a client spelling "no opinion" as `null`
means what one omitting the key means, and refusing one while accepting the
other would make the wire's meaning depend on a serializer's omit-none setting.

WHERE THE POLICY READ SITS, because it is the load-bearing decision here.
Outside `office_lock`, immediately before `upsert_actor`, which takes that lock
itself. Forced, not preferred: `locks._file_lock` is a real file lock acquired
through a fresh handle, so it is NOT reentrant — wrapping read and write in one
`office_lock` deadlocks the write it is meant to protect, and moving the policy
INSIDE `upsert_actor` is the honest close and a store change this strip does not
carry. The window it leaves: two creates that both omit a position and race
between the read and their writes can compute the same slot, and the second
lands on the first. One slot, visible, fixed by a drag. Stated in
`resolve_placement_position`'s docstring and in hermes 06, and filed as a queue
row rather than left for the next reader to find.

The scan excludes the actor it is about to write. Without that, a resumed
attempt whose placement already landed reads its OWN item as a blocker and moves
the agent one column on every retry — an idempotent replay that walks.

The ack gains `position` (what was written, policy or verbatim) and `actor` (the
row as STORED). `actor` is taken off the store's return value, never rebuilt
from the request, which is the whole point: the client stops trusting its
predicted key, position and revision. It renders in `runtime.office.get`'s own
item shape, and that shape now lives in ONE function — `office_models
.office_item_wire_row`, which `_office_projection` also flattens through. A
second copy of those ten keys is the silent-disagreement shape
`_office_projection` was itself extracted to end, one level down.

Both keys are additive: `RPC_CONTRACT_VERSION` does not move, no name joins the
manifest's `methods` list, an old client ignores them, and an old serve still
answers a client that always sends a position.

S6's `test_pos_is_optional_whenever_agent_retire_exists` asserted `pos.required
is True` in its `else`, which made it a BICONDITIONAL and reddened on exactly
the ordering the plan requires (S2 before S5). D12 is one-directional: retire
without an optional position strands a client, an optional position without
retire is strictly more permissive than any client asks for. The rule is now a
predicate pinned over all four combinations — widen it to `or` and the
`(False, True)` row reds — and the live parser test asks that predicate instead
of branching on whichever state HEAD is in.

Two hardenings in files this slice already touched, both from the S6 review:
the alias round-trip's `A or B == "ws"` compared only one operand (precedence),
and the `AgentCreateInvalid` AST walk matched only the bare name, so a raise
spelled `agent_create.AgentCreateInvalid(...)` would have vanished from
`declared` and `covered` together; it now matches both spellings and carries a
floor of eight so a walk that stopped matching cannot read as a pass.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(placement): S5 — the inverse gets a door, and the half of a retire nobody could see stops being unsaid

`PersonaInstanceStore.retire` has archived both halves for months — the roster
row and, through `OfficeStore.archive_actors_for_instance`, every office actor
bound to the instance. What it never had was a door and a receipt. So the
launcher removed a deliberate placement through two unjoined lanes, a half-state
(row archived, desk still on the canvas) was representable, and the office half
was best-effort AND SILENT: `_archive_office_placements` discarded its outcome,
which made "the desk is still there" a fact no caller could be told.

`agent_retire.perform_agent_retire` is the one function three doors now answer
with — `runtime.agent.retire`, `harness agent retire`, and `harness persona
instance retire`, which delegates rather than calling the store a second time.
The prune returns per-actor outcomes at the ONE chokepoint that knows them, so
the ack names every actor that left (`archived_actor_keys`) beside every one
that did not (`office_archive_failures`); an empty failures list is a positive
claim, and the retire still succeeds when the office projection cannot be
reached, because a locked desk file must never make a placement un-retirable.

Retiring the same id twice is an answer, not an error: the replay reads the
tombstone and returns the same ack with `already_retired: true`, its actor keys
re-read from the office archive rather than reconstructed, because a remote
client that lost its ack must be able to ask again. An id that never existed
still refuses `not_found` — the replay reads a TOMBSTONE, and absence alone is
not one. Refusals are `PersonaInstanceRetireError`'s codes 1:1.

The name joins the manifest's method SET without moving RPC_CONTRACT_VERSION,
which is also the launcher's D12 marker for the optional position S2 landed;
`test_workspace_flag_aliases.py`'s one-directional implication stays green
because the marker arrived AFTER the capability it stands for. Scope is
`console` and the method is deliberately off every peer-tier allowlist.

Docs in the same commit: 01 gains the inverse, 06's write-verb table gains the
two cross-store verbs and a section on the receipt, 03's manifest count moves
nine to ten, and plan S5 becomes a pointer.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(placement): S4 — the create stops handing an agent a skill it never checked, and a rename stops erasing the ones it had

The skills phase, its two gates, the `placed` receipt, and the `None -> []`
collapse that made `update-profile --display-name X` a silent skill wipe.

`skills: [id, ...]` on `runtime.agent.create` and `--skill <id>` (repeatable)
on `harness agent create` are byte-parallel doors onto one phase that runs
AFTER the placement. Absent leaves `skill_overrides` at `None` (inherit the
persona's, live); a list — including an empty one, which is an explicit
"override with nothing" — is written at the INSTANCE tier and never at the
persona template, because a template write would silently reconfigure every
other instance of that persona.

Every id must be identical under BOTH `safe_id` and the store's own
`safe_assignment_token` before any root is walked: that is what makes "never
path-joined from input" true, and what makes the ack's `assigned` the list the
store HOLDS rather than one it quietly re-spelled. Then every canonical id is
installed and PROVEN hash-equal — `install_and_verify_harness_skill` asks three
questions, not one, because `harness_skill_hash_mismatches` `continue`s past a
destination that does not exist and a copy that never landed would otherwise
read as a clean bill. Then every id must resolve. Only then is anything
written. Install runs BEFORE resolve, inverting D5's listing order, because a
canonical skill's resolvable copy IS the installed one and resolving first
would refuse `missing` for a skill the next line would have installed.

This is the first place the repo-to-installed hash is a GATE rather than a
report. `profile_readiness` files a mismatch at severity 15 and
`prompt_observability` raises a HUD flag; both are advisory, which is how a
running agent came to be reading a 14457-byte copy of a 14906-byte skill on
2026-08-24.

A skills refusal never costs the agent its desk (D4). The reservation
vocabulary gains `placed` between `instance_minted` and `done`; every skills
refusal carries `phase: "skills"` and `rolled_back: false` — the literal truth
— plus the instance id of the agent that IS standing, and `next_expected` names
the SAME-key retry, which re-enters at the skills phase alone and takes the
CURRENT request's list so a mistyped id can be fixed rather than answered
forever. A `done` receipt with no `skills` field is pre-plan and is never
re-entered; an unknown state stays `reservation_corrupt`, so an old serve
reading a new receipt refuses loudly instead of re-minting.

The `None -> []` fix is the same bug one door over.
`_cmd_persona_instance_update_profile` passed `list(args.skills or [])`, so an
omitted `--skill` reached the store as an empty LIST and its correct
`if skills is not None` contract then wrote `skill_overrides = []`: renaming an
agent cleared every skill it was assigned, silently. The store was never wrong;
the collapse was in the layer whose whole job at that line is to translate
absent into absent. Pinned red-first.

Also, as an S7 precondition: an `idempotent_replay` no longer echoes the
receipt's actor. It re-reads the live row and re-stamps
`position`/`actor`/`revision`, because S7 adopts that row into the launcher's
scene and its `expect_revision` bookkeeping — a frozen revision would refuse
the client's very next guarded write, and a frozen position would snap the
agent back to where it used to be. `actor_fresh` says when the re-read could
not be made, and the recorded row is then returned unchanged rather than
invented. The "no second write happened" witness moves off the ack's revision
(the field this change stops freezing) and onto the receipt file.

Two refusal reasons the plan did not name were needed and are documented in 06:
`skills_invalid` (a malformed `skills` param, refused before any write) and
`skill_assign_failed` (the store fault that would otherwise have escaped as an
untyped -32000 with no `data` at all).

Fifteen killing mutations are registered in `tests/mutation_claims.json`, one
per production change, and the registry immediately earned its place: the claim
for the post-install verification SURVIVED. A copy that RAISES is caught by the
phase's `except` whether or not anything verifies afterwards, so the copy-fault
test could never have discriminated that line — the condition with no other
witness is an install that reports `ok` while the bytes on disk are not the
repo's, which is the 2026-08-24 incident exactly.
`test_an_install_that_REPORTS_success_is_still_re_read_before_it_is_trusted`
pins it, and the claim now kills.

The CI cap is raised 12 -> 16 at its call site, with the reason written beside
it. `--max-candidates` bounds RUNTIME, not quality, and the script's own refusal
offers exactly two cures: split the diff or raise the cap visibly. This slice
selects 14 candidates because it adds a whole phase; capping at 12 would not
have made the change smaller, only four of its guarantees unregistered.

author: nekwo
message:
test(placement): the boundary test stops naming a guarantee it could not fail on, and the shared fixture gains the one case both float widths can stand on

The plan owed S9 a `boundary_item_at_exact_radius` case built from the
constants, because `<` -> `<=` in both occupancy predicates survived both
suites. Building it turned up why it survived, and the answer is two
different answers.

hermes: no lattice-shaped spelling can put the boundary under the predicate.
A distance measured from a `slot_at` point is an exact multiple of 2**-50 and
`float64(0.7)` is a multiple of 2**-53 and of no coarser power, so
`test_an_item_exactly_at_the_occupancy_radius_does_not_block` was measuring
0.7000000000000002 and could not fail. It now asks `_is_blocked` directly,
where the distance IS exactly the radius, with a one-step-inside arm so the
assertion is a boundary and not a predicate that never fires. Red on the
mutation, green on revert; registered as claim
`s9-occupancy-predicate-is-strict`.

The launcher: `<` -> `<=` there is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT, not a coverage gap.
`Vector2` is float32, so at the origin slot every squared distance is an exact
multiple of 2**-42 while the window of squares whose root rounds to
`float64(0.7)` is 0.0005 of one step wide and falls 0.04 of a step from the
nearest one. Nothing the fixture can hand it measures a distance EQUAL to the
radius. Measured, then written down in three places so it is not re-filed as a
gap.

So the shared case pins what IS observable at both widths: the item sits at
`slot_at(0,0) + (1468007 * 2**-21, 0)` = -4.299999713897705078125, one float32
step past the radius; both widths measure 0.7000002861022949; the origin slot
stays free; and `occupancy_radius` is now pinned to within one float32 ulp
instead of within 0.7. The naive -4.3 the plan prescribed would have made the
two repos DISAGREE -- float64 measures 0.7000000000000002 and frees the slot,
float32 measures 0.6999998092651367 and takes it -- which is the first time a
case in this file would have been satisfied by one repo only.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(placement): S9b — the boundary the lattice "could not reach" is one off-axis item away, and the proof said so in five places

S9 closed the occupancy-predicate row with an argument that was true of a
one-axis offset and stated as if it were true of the lattice. A distance
measured along ONE axis from a `slot_at` point is an exact multiple of
`2**-50`, and `float64(0.7)` is a multiple of `2**-53` and of no coarser power
— so `slot_at(0, 0) + (OCCUPANCY_RADIUS, 0)` measures `0.7000000000000002` and
`<` vs `<=` cannot be told apart there. The extension to two axes does not
follow: `dx*dx + dy*dy` is not the exact `(m*m + n*n) * 2**-100` the two
squares would give, because the SUM is rounded.

The counterexample, measured before a word of this was rewritten. An item at
`(-4.300000000000001, 6.400000029802323)` probed from `slot_at(0, 0)` sums to
`0.4899999999999999` — strictly below `OCCUPANCY_RADIUS ** 2`
(`0.48999999999999994`) and below `0.49` — and its root is EXACTLY
`float64(0.7)`. `_is_blocked` returns False under `<` and True under `<=`, on
the real scan, with two coordinates an office store can hold.

So the five sites that carried the impossibility are corrected, not softened:
`_is_blocked`'s docstring, the predicate test's docstring, and both
byte-identical copies of the cross-repo fixture README (the launcher's copy
lands in its own commit). The plan's §C row keeps its history and appends the
withdrawal with the three float64 values. The predicate test is still the right
seam — because it is the DIRECT one, not because the lattice cannot reach the
boundary — and the reach is now pinned by
`test_an_off_axis_lattice_probe_can_measure_the_radius_exactly`. It cannot
enter `cases.json`: the point is not float32-representable, so the launcher
would parse a different floor. `<` -> `<=` reddens both tests; applied and
reverted.

The launcher half is unchanged in substance and re-SCOPED in wording: an
equivalent mutant AT THE LATTICE ORIGIN, where every fixture case sits.

Also: `tests/fixtures/office_layout/** -text`. `cases.json` is committed
byte-identical in two repos and hashed by a `MANIFEST.sha256` on each side, and
neither side had the pin — the third byte-pinned golden pair to ship without
it. The class is a row on the launcher's Mission Control queue.

message:
feat(placement): S8b-b — the door S8b said had no gesture behind it is the launcher's fallback, and it always had one

S8b gave `harness agent retire` the `--correlation-id` that `agent create` has
carried since D-V2, and withheld it from `harness persona instance retire` on a
stated reason: "no gesture behind it is the truth for that door". That was not
measured, and it is false about the door's largest caller.

The launcher's `persona.instance.retire` argv capability IS that door. It is
fired from `MissionOfficeLayoutController.retireAgent`'s `Unavailable` arm, and
`retireAgent` takes `correlationId` as a REQUIRED parameter — so a token existed
on every launcher retire and was dropped by exactly the arm that runs when the
RPC lane cannot carry the call. The partial-coverage window bit hardest where the
diagnostic is needed most: a degraded transport is when an operator has nothing
to join a gesture's two halves with but one grep over the event log.

So the second door publishes the flag. Nothing else moves: `_agent_retire_outcome`
already read `correlation_id` through `getattr(..., None)`, which is why the
whole fix is one `add_argument` and the docstring that asserted the withholding.

Measured live on a hermetic runtime root, not only in tests. One agent placed and
retired through THIS door under one token joins four events — `state.patched`,
`office.actor.upserted`, `state.patched`, `office.actor.removed`. The same gesture
with the flag withheld joins two, and its retire half cannot be reached from the
token at all.

Registered rather than left as prose: `s8b-b-persona-instance-retire-door-has-no-token`
in the executable claim registry, selected by the changed line and KILLED.

Two docs are corrected rather than left to disagree with the code: 06 said this
door "deliberately does not publish the flag", and the coverage plan's P2 still
said the flag reached exactly one argv verb — it reaches three, which is the whole

author: nekwo
message:
docs(placement): D6 is ruled, and the ruling's own context says do not implement it

The operator ruled D6 on 2026-08-27: duplicate desks are allowed, only a
duplicate on the SAME INSTANCE is not — "it's an instantiated system", so the
persona is a template and keying a placement invariant to it is a category error.
That reading is correct about today's code, which calls itself "THE
one-desk-per-persona fence" in as many words.

It is recorded and NOT implemented, which needs saying because the omission would
otherwise read as an oversight.

Re-keying persona → instance is four coupled sites, not one: this fence, the
launcher's `hasAuthoredDeskForPersona`, the render rule that suppresses an
agent's implicit desk when its PERSONA already holds an authored one, and the
`duplicate_desk` Scene Health count. Flip only the fence and a second agent of
one persona renders with NO desk — its implicit desk suppressed by a persona that
has a desk, and no authored desk of its own.

But the same conversation established the thing that actually decides it: desks
are a PLACEHOLDER FOR ARTIFACTS, they do not connect to agents yet, and artifacts
should be standalone. The launcher already half-records this as an operator
ruling of 2026-08-20 — "desks shouldn't be part of the agent, they are separate
things". If artifacts are standalone scene objects then this fence should key on
neither persona nor instance, and the duplicate-desk invariant stops existing
rather than moving. Instance-keying would harden a coupling the design is leaving.

So the next session is told plainly not to "fix" it toward instance keying. No
migration is being deferred either way: `OfficeItem.persona_instance_id` and the
launcher's nullable `personaInstanceId` both already exist. What is deferred is a
decision that should not be taken before the feature it guards is built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: nekwo
message:
feat(serve): W4 — a serve record says which runtime root it is on, and now which HOME it resolved

`store_root` and `hermes_home` are separate axes and one never implied the
other: a serve child spawned with `HERMES_HOME` pointed at `profiles\base`
writes the SAME `store_root` as one that resolved `profiles\alice`. So from
outside a running serve, nothing could say which home it was on.
`harness status --json` answers it live — but only for a process you can
already talk to, which is the wrong end of the question when you are looking
at a directory of records. Verified on the operator's runtime before writing
a line: both live children carried `store_root` and no home.

`register_serve_instance` gains a nullable `hermes_home`, written ALWAYS,
beside `store_root`. Three states, three spellings, and a reader must keep
them apart: a path says *this home*; `null` says *this serve could not
resolve one*; an ABSENT key says *this entry predates the field*. An empty
string would be a fourth spelling of the second that reads like a PATH, and
it is pinned against. That third state is not hypothetical — the two serves
running while this landed have no such key — so NOTHING classifies on it,
and `schema_version` stays 1: an additive nullable key no reader requires is
not a new schema (the `port` / `socket_started_at` precedent).

The value is computed by the CALLER. `serve_registry` imports no
`hermes_constants` and resolves nothing, so the field stays unit-testable
against an injected string; `harness_parts/serve.py` passes
`str(get_hermes_home())` guarded, degrading to None rather than failing
registration — a registry entry is bookkeeping, and bookkeeping must not be
able to fail a boot.

It is a BOOT-time observation, not per-turn authority: the runtime may rebind
a home for a turn and this key will not have moved. The field's comment and
the module docstring both say so. `serve_instances/` stays out of every
freshness fingerprint, untouched.

Red-first: `register_serve_instance() got an unexpected keyword argument
'hermes_home'`, then `the key is ALWAYS written; absence is a fact`, then
`KeyError: 'hermes_home'` on a real boot. Mutating the writer to `""` reds
the null pin (`assert '' is None`). The legacy-record test is a CONTROL, not
a red: it passed before the field existed and after.

Proven on a real serve subprocess against an isolated root, not only in
unit tests: the record carried a `hermes_home` under `profiles\base` beside
a `store_root` under `agent-runtime` — two different paths in one record —
and clean shutdown still removed it.

author: nekwo
message:
docs(gateway): the gate the canon called misplaced turns out to have no reachable caller, and Stage 1 gets its three rulings

Canon 06 records the authorization gap as an ASYMMETRY: `harness persona
instance retire` consults `authorize_coordinator_action` and `harness agent
retire` does not, on the same `perform_agent_retire`, with the two RPC methods
ungated entirely. Both halves check out in the source. The measured state is
worse and simpler.

The gate at `persona_commands.py:4864` runs only when `_coordinator_actor_id`
(`:1654`) returns non-`None`, and that helper answers for exactly two
`--requested-by` spellings — `coordinator` and `coordinator:<id>`. The verb
DEFAULTS to `cli` (`harness.py:998`) and the launcher hardcodes `launcher`
(`harness_capability_registry.dart:1517`). So the gated door is gated only for a
caller that volunteers it is a coordinator, and on every gesture anyone actually
fires all three doors are unenforced. Worse, identity and scope both ride the
same argv the request does: `--coordinator-max-spawns` /
`--coordinator-may-kill-others` (`harness.py:256-261`) let the caller declare
its own grant, and any actor naming itself `operator`/`tony`/`cli` is bypassed
outright (`coordinator_permissions.py:16,68`).

That changes the design. Moving the existing call down to the shared service
functions — the fix canon 06's row proposes, and the one that looked obvious —
relocates a predicate whose inputs the request supplies. So the plan splits
WHERE the check runs from WHO supplies the fact it checks, and puts the gate at
the RPC dispatch layer, which is the only place a proven caller fact exists:
`RpcContext` (`serve_rpc.py:186-215`) is where the socket lane's HMAC-verified
connection lands, and `@method` (`:234`) is a one-line registry a wrapper
composes into. R11's per-device scopes then become a lookup off `connection_key`
instead of a third self-declaration. Five stages, smallest first, each landable:
name the tier in the manifest without enforcing, carry a caller identity, land
the enforcement point with an empty policy, reconcile the CLI gate, then let the
gateway's device credential fill it.

Three rulings for the operator at the foot of the file: A, the chokepoint
placement (recommend the dispatch-layer gate; R11's prerequisite); B, R1's TLS
posture restated verbatim from the launcher plan (recommend self-signed +
pinned fingerprint, as it already holds); C, the W2 relay's legacy-marking
(recommend the retirement plan first — `b11614268` fixed the relay's error
taxonomy on 08-25, so a banner arriving mid-lane either gets ignored or stops
work that is correct to finish).

Nothing was executed. Every claim is a read, the honest bounds say which three
call sites were counted but not read, and the field-notes file records what
contradicted the brief so a later session does not have to re-derive it. Canon
06's Open row gets a one-line pointer — held while a concurrent session's diff
sat on the same region, written once that landed.

The inventory the drift addendum ordered was done first, and it is written down
rather than assumed. hermes already ships two things called `install_id` and
neither can carry this one: `monitoring.install_id` advertises ROTATABILITY as a
feature in its own docstring (a lockout here — Stage 1 pairs a device against
this id) and is scoped to a HERMES home's config.yaml, while a gateway addresses
a store root and the launcher's serve proves those are different scopes; the
telemetry `install_id` is an anonymity primitive, and putting one on a wire frame
turns it into a network address. So: distinct, on scope + lifetime + audience.
What is NOT duplicated is the mechanism — mint-iff-absent, root-is-an-input,
never-raises, a typed `state` instead of an exception — all of it `serve_auth.py`'s
contract restated for a non-secret, and the docstring says where it came from.

Two deviations from the plan's `{install_id, display_name, build}`: `build`
dropped, because the frames already carry one and a nested copy is a second
authority that can disagree; `state` added, because absence cannot distinguish
"predates the lane" from "could not write its identity" — the same rule
`auth.token_file` and `socket.outcome` already follow.

The block NAMES and never authorises. `serve_auth` proves a caller may talk to
this runtime; an id that did both is how "I know your install id" becomes "I am
you", and a test pins that the token is unreachable from the block.

`gateway.listen` (False) / `gateway.port` (0) are declared and read by NOTHING —
Stage 1 binds the listener, `SOCKET_HOST` is still `127.0.0.1`, and no network
behaviour changed. The docker guide asserted no such config key existed; it now
says which gateway the key belongs to, since the word is overloaded here and the
API server's 8642 is untouched by it.

Additive throughout: no existing key changed and neither contract integer moved.

Tests: 18 new identity cases (mint/reload idempotence, per-root distinctness,
rename keeps the id, CRLF, an empty record healed and a corrupt one refused —
asymmetric on purpose, because a zero-byte file's id is held by nobody while a
non-empty one may be a record a paired device still names); the install block
pinned on all three greeting surfaces. `test_gateway_identity` 18 passed,
`test_serve_service_foundations` 27 passed, `test_serve_socket_lane` 57 passed,

author: nekwo
message:
feat(gateway): A1 — every method says what credential it wants, and three pins that had been red since S5 get told

The tier the two agent docstrings and canon 06 stated as prose becomes a
machine-readable fact on the greeting frames. `@method` now takes the tier as a
REQUIRED argument with no default: a default is what turns a registration into a
hole — open, and a forgotten verb ships unguarded; closed, and a forgotten read
verb breaks a working client. Requiring the word makes a tierless method
unrepresentable rather than merely untested, and an unknown tier raises at
import, so a typo is a boot failure with a name in it.

Nothing is refused. `manifest()` gains `tiers` beside `methods` — a key, not a
shape change to any existing method, so `RPC_CONTRACT_VERSION` does not move
(the set-plus-integer rule 03 §2 states and the D12 rollout proved). A client
that ignores the block keeps working, which is the point of shipping the
declaration one stage ahead of the check.

The classification rule is one line: a level MUTATION is `console`, everything
else is `read`. The one row worth arguing is `runtime.persona.prewarm`, and it
is `read` — its own contract is that it writes no store state, emits no event
and mints no id, which is the same sentence that makes `runtime.office.get` a
read. Spending CPU is a rate-limiting question, and rate limiting is not a tier.

Three manifest pins were already RED before this change and are closed in
passing: `test_serve_rpc_office_upsert.py`'s two literals and
`test_serve_rpc_office_subscribe.py`'s `method_names()` list were written before
S5 and never grew `runtime.agent.retire`. Verified against a clean HEAD
worktree, not assumed — the other two literals in `test_serve_rpc_office.py`
were green at HEAD and are moved by this commit alone.

Ruling A of docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/authorization-chokepoint.md,
Stage A1. The completeness test iterates `_METHODS` rather than listing the ten
names: a hand-written list goes green on a method registered with no tier, and
the repo's own tombstone-census lesson is loops, never literals.
