author: nekwo
message:
feat(instance-replication): H1 — the record split, spelled per field so it cannot rot

A realm pull delivers the desk, the persona definition, the profile home and
the skills. It does not deliver the agent: `grep persona_instance
agent_runtime/realm_sync.py` returned nothing, so a pulled placement landed
with no runtime instance behind it and the launcher badged it "Not linked
here". The operator ruled that identity and authored definition travel while
runtime state is born fresh locally — and that sentence is a split of one
32-field record.

A category ("runtime state") is exactly the kind of shorthand that lets one
field drift to the wrong side of a door, so the split is per FIELD: three
disjoint sets over `dataclasses.fields(PersonaInstance)` — 14 travel, 6 are
re-derived on mint, 12 are neither. The totality test is the point of this
stage: a field added tomorrow cannot compile green until somebody classifies
it.

The admission grammar of plan §4 lands here too, pure and store-free: the
shared `sync_admission` door first (secret-shaped through BOTH scanner passes,
machine-shaped with `prose_keys=frozenset()` because an instance body is 100%
wiring), then the three rules this family adds — the session/run family as
`unexpected_key`, a peer-published canonical channel as
`canonical_channel_not_replicable`, and a non-instance-shaped steering parent.

Id safety is asked by ROUND-TRIP rather than by a second regex: an id
`paths.safe_path_token` would rewrite is an id whose row lands under a key that
is not the key the realm agreed on — the merge unit silently renamed, which is
the non-convergence Option B was refused for. Asking the real sanitizer means a
bespoke pattern cannot disagree with it.

No import-time assertion of the partition, deliberately: an unclassified field
would then surface as a collection error on every suite that imports the
module, instead of as one named failure saying which field nobody classified.

Two of the eleven red-proofs initially survived and both were real gaps, not
false alarms — the portability walk was only ever tested through a key the
shared PROSE_KEYS set does not exempt, and determinism turned out to have two
redundant mechanisms where removing either alone is invisible. Both are closed
and the second is recorded in the test's own docstring so the next reader does
not conclude it is uncovered.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(instance-replication): H2 — the agents behind the desks travel with them

`OfficePublishScan` gains a fourth fact, `instance_ids`, off the walk it
already takes. Not a convenience: the refusal gate cannot speak for a walk it
did not take, so a second `actors_dir.glob` would ship agents no local reader
ever admitted existed — the C3 argument, now covering a third thing the same
pass answers. The id is read from the PAYLOAD, not from the actor key, because
payload is truth and the key is routing, even though `_canonical_actor_key`
makes the two equal for instance-bound actors today.

The projection is published at `store/persona_instances.yaml`, a path no older
hermes maps to anything, so an old member degrades to "no instance
replication" instead of writing a persona-instance document over some
unrelated destination. `_kind_for_sync_path` gains the row; the
`_destination_for_sync_path` branch is behaviour-neutral (the path already
reached None through the final fallthrough, pinned by a test written before
the branch) and lands anyway so the next reader does not have to prove the
fallthrough.

The publish arm does NOT refuse on a short read, where the office arm does, and
the asymmetry has an argument: publish replaces the subtree wholesale, so an
office absence is a desk removal on every peer, while an instance absence is
`upstream_absent` — explicitly held, never archived. The shortfall is reported
as `rows_unreadable` instead of costing a whole realm's replication for one
quarantined row.

Baseline after publish, the `_published_profile_file_hashes` precedent: without
it a member who publishes and then pulls sees every row they just shipped as a
HOLD on their own publish.

One red-proof initially survived and it was a test-selection error rather than
a coverage gap — the refusal fixture blinds an actor file, so a second glob
fails to decode it too and the two authorities agree by accident. The
divergence that can only come from having two of them is injected instead,
exactly as the existing C3 test does for the artifact list.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(instance-replication): H3 — a pulled desk that has no agent here gets one

The heart of the plan. `apply_persona_instance_pull` runs at the seam the
argument requires: AFTER the persona-definition and profile-file lanes, because
the mint reads the definition to derive role/profile_id and a mint from a
definition that has not landed builds the wrong agent; BEFORE the workspace
tombstone lane, so a replica is never minted into a workspace the same pull is
about to archive.

Every write goes through a STORE DOOR, `replicate_instance`, never a raw
`persona_instances/` file write. Three facts would otherwise be lost, and one of
them is a mistake made one lane over three days ago: `apply_board_pull` writes
cards with raw atomic writes, so a pull that GIVES you a card reaches no live
consumer while one that ARCHIVES a card emits. A replicated instance that needs
an app restart to appear has not been replicated as far as the operator is
concerned. The other two are the §1.3 derivations and the event ordering.

A replication mint is a THIRD intent class, so it gets
`persona_instance.replicated` rather than reusing `.created` — that type means
"this machine authored an agent" to every consumer that reads it, and one pull
would read as N creates in the log an operator greps. Registered in this commit
with its emitter, per S55; SURVIVING_EVENT_COUNT moves 58 to 59 with its reason
written beside it.

Two phases for `steered_by`, because an edge may name a parent this same pass
has not minted yet — without the split the outcome would depend on the
alphabetical order of instance ids. Phase two runs `_validate_no_steering_cycle`
per edge, so a hostile remote graph whose every edge passes the CONTENT door
still cannot install a cycle; dropped edges get a typed row.

The remote-absent arm is decided before the classifier reaches it: for this
family `upstream_absent` is the only answer, because both of the classifier's
remote-absent arms are delete-shaped and retirement follows the DESK, never the
absence. Unreadable is never folded into absent on either side — absent drives
the MINT arm locally and the upstream_absent arm remotely, so a parse error read
as absence is a delete-shaped decision taken on a read failure.

One red-proof survived, and where it survived was the useful part: the store
door's allowlist is unreachable through the applier because the admission door
already refuses such bodies. It is still load-bearing, because the door is a
public store verb, so it now has a test that calls it directly.

A dropped steering edge leaves its row reading as local drift and does not
self-heal — re-running phase two for kept_local rows would clobber an operator's
own re-steer. Named in the field notes and rowed rather than improvised past.

Mutation: ten new claims; 21 candidates, 21 killed (needs --max-candidates 30,
above the script's default of 12).

author: nekwo
message:
feat(instance-replication): H4 — the replica follows the desk, and never the absence

A `persona_instance` StoreDriftItem family, so the itemized drift and
`realm sync revert` reach these rows; `classify_revert` was already total over
family × kind, so it needed the family's transition rows and not a new table.

The property that makes the family safe is the mint's, not the walk's: a
replicated row is not drift because the baseline was recorded at the REMOTE
hash, so a fresh replica's projection already equals its baseline entry. There
is no special case in the walk — and if the alignment ever breaks, the revert
lane offers to archive correct state, which is why both halves are pinned.

`record_tombstone=False` turns out to be STRUCTURAL for this family rather than
a parameter. A persona-instance record has no realm-visible ledger of its own;
the only place this lane could mint one is the office half, through
`_archive_office_placements` and `remove_actor`'s default. So `retire_replica`
does not run the office half, and that is the whole of the semantics. Adding a
parameter would have implied a ledger that does not exist.

Retire-follows-the-desk needed a resurrection guard, because archiving a row the
realm still publishes would be undone by the very next pull — the retire reversed
in one round trip, and a desk the operator deleted returning with an agent behind
it. The guard is the office surface's own `archived_actor_keys` ledger, asked
through the shared classifier's `locally_archived`, because the actor key IS the
instance id: a second ledger for one identity is how two authorities start
disagreeing. `desk_archived` names the resulting state.

`desks_removed` comes from the office summary's own archive outcomes rather than
a re-derivation. Only that arm knows which archives it took: the ones it fenced
and the ones it tried and could not are both absent from the list by
construction, and retiring an agent for a desk removal that did not happen is
the worst mistake available here.

One red-proof took three attempts and the reason is in the test's docstring: the
held-retire baseline guarantee is invisible with the projection absent (the
baseline is never written on that path) and invisible with it present-and-
matching (phase one silently re-records the entry). Only a locally-edited
replica whose remote also moved lets the drop survive to disk. That is exactly
how a guarantee ends up believed and untested, so the shape is now pinned.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(instant-workspace-switching): WS1 — the pointer becomes a patch, and the switch stops paying for a core

A workspace switch is the cheapest state change this runtime has — two scalars
in a pointer file — and it was among the most expensive on the wire. Neither
`workspace.activated` nor `realm.activated` was patch-covered, so the module's
own rule (one uncovered event demotes the batch) turned every switch into a
full O(world) core: ~842 KB-2.2 MB, `build_ms` median 3,083, and the launcher's
per-row `active` flags flipping at a field-measured p50 of 8.76 s.

Both events now ride a new fold entity, `scope`, whose row is exactly the two
pointers and carries BOTH of them every time — a realm activate can re-park the
workspace, and two half-patches would be two chances to disagree. The producer
sits inside `set_active`, patch-before-event, on the `apply` arm only.

The derivability audit the honesty rule demands is done and PINNED, not
asserted: `snapshot.py` reads `active_id()` in exactly seven places and the
census test names each one, so an eighth reader reddens with instructions
instead of shipping a patch that drops what the core would have said. The audit
did not come back clean — three of the seven are indirect and feed
`prompt_observability`'s per-turn `situational_hud` strings, so the plan's
"nothing else in the core varies with the pointer" is corrected in the field
notes and the residue is written at the coverage entry with the argument for
accepting it (per-turn telemetry, one diagnostic reader, repaired by the next
core).

Two more plan rows were wrong about their own mechanism: there is no `replace`
op on this wire (it would have been unfoldable, silently), so the row is an
`upsert` whose complete-row `changed` IS the replace; and no fourth capability
token was minted — `scope` is a new entity with one op, so the entity name is
already the gate its paired events need.

Version skew rides the negotiation that already exists: a client that does not
declare `scope` gets today's demoted core, per-subscriber, through S5's
promotion. No flag, no version gate (R-W0).

The cross-stack golden ceremony lands here too, and it found a defect it was
not looking for: seven generated goldens carried a stale
`core.decision_contract_hash` from a landing that regenerated nothing, and the
byte pin could not see it because both sides of the comparison were equally
stale. Regenerated with the reason written into the fixtures README.

message:
perf(chat): Stage 3 - the prologue's receipts, and the cache the plan asked for already existed

RE-MEASURED FIRST, and the plan's named site is falsified. §5 Stage 3 said to
cache tool-schema serialization in conversation_loop's request_build, expecting
-0.5-1.0s per turn. The live 2026-09-01 records say the span that CONTAINS that
serialization bills 1 ms warm (51-128 ms cold) and pre_api_hook bills 0, against
an enclosing provider_request_started -> request_assembled span of 703 ms warm
and 2,000 ms cold. On the codex lane the serialization is _responses_tools: a
loop copying four keys per tool and passing `parameters` by reference. There is
nothing there to cache.

And the cache the plan describes ALREADY EXISTS one level down, in
model_tools._tool_defs_cache: keyed on the enabled/disabled/blocked frozensets
plus registry._generation (the epoch), the config (mtime_ns, size), the kanban
toggle and the delegated-child context; bounded and LRU-evicting; both arms
return list(...) so a caller appending schemas cannot poison it;
_clear_tool_defs_cache is the hatch. Building a second one would be a parallel
authority over a question that already has an answer.

So this lands the receipts, which is the other half Stage 3 asked for and the
half that was genuinely missing:

- profile_conversation_turn_context_ms: build_turn_context is timed. It is the
  prologue's largest single call and the owner of the several hundred ms that
  had NO owner on the record at all.
- The system-prompt restore receipt as a POSITIVE pair — exactly one of
  ..._system_prompt_restore_ms or ..._system_prompt_build_ms per turn, never
  both, and neither on a turn that skipped the prologue. That third state is why
  it is a pair and not one key plus a zero.
- The tool-schema memo's hit/miss receipt: thread-local cumulative counters in
  model_tools (the shape probe_rounds_this_thread and bundle_builds_this_thread
  already use) surfaced as agent_init_tool_defs_build_ms / ..._cached_ms.
  NEITHER is emitted when the counter is unreadable: "I could not ask" is not
  "it hit". Deliberately not routed through _emit_init_timing, whose rolling
  checkpoint would silently redefine the existing agent_init_tool_setup_ms.

Every key rides the existing *_ms profile-timing channel that
safe_turn_profile_timing already admits: no schema change, no new phase key, no
config field, no producer surface moved.

The tests pin the JOIN (emitter -> the runner's collector -> the store's
sanitizer), because both halves of that seam were already correct and only the
join was untested — which is exactly how request_assembled was absent from every
live record while every test agreed the wiring was healthy. A first pass tested
the timing helper directly and stayed green with the call site unwired; the
call-site test now drives the real run_conversation prologue.

H3 confirmed in code that every turn constructs a fresh SessionDB whose writer
constructor runs _init_schema (DDL + FTS probe + column reconcile) plus the WAL
checks, and confirmed just as plainly that nobody had measured it. Both halves
are answered here.

THE INSTRUMENT. _cmd_mission_chat_message times its own
_default_persona_session_db() call on time.monotonic and carries the result to

phase that pays this cost and the phase that persists it, and the alternative to

author: nekwo
message:
fix(scope): the newest explicit gesture wins both pointers, and two gates stop lying about what they enforce

Three rulings of 2026-09-01, one lane.

**The reconcile basis race.** `reconcile_active_workspace_to_realm` parked the
workspace pointer under the REALM intent's basis and DISCARDED the refusal when
a newer explicit workspace selection owned it — leaving the realm pointer in one
realm and the workspace pointer in another, both verbs answering `applied: true`,
and nothing on the tree able to notice afterwards. The reconcile now returns its
outcome; `activate_realm` heals a refused one by re-parking the realm pointer to
the winning workspace's realm under THAT workspace's stored basis and answering
`superseded`; `activate_workspace` pulls the realm pointer after an applied
selection. Both arms write through `set_active`, so the scope patch and the
activated event ride along unchanged. `WorkspaceStore.active_intent_issued_at`
reads back the basis `set_active` already wrote, so the heal does not hand-read
a pointer file.

`test_stage13_write_path_integrity` asserted the straddle as its expectation
("each pointer is owned by the newest intent that touched it"). The ruling
supersedes that claim; the test is rewritten and renamed, and the half that
survives — a late realm switch does not drag the workspace pointer — is still
pinned.

**The grep gate.** `test_no_source_grep_assertions` was red on main with twelve
offenders, not the queue row's eleven, and identical at `cf9abaac4b` and at
`98d43d0c86` — pre-existing, and no wave's. The ruling was allowlist with
reasons, so `tests/source_grep_ruled_exemptions.txt` is a SECOND register rather
than eleven more lines in a debt file that declares itself closed. It is closed
too, its count is asserted, stale entries fail, and every line must say what its
test actually pins — a reasonless line is not an exemption and fails twice over.

**The mutation gate.** Its cap refusal named no numbers, so an exit 2 meaning
"your change is big" read as "your claims are bad"; it now names the count, the
cap and the landing cure. And it rewrites source in place, which cost the H
landing ten minutes of phantom red — that is now said in the docstring, the
`--help` and the README, and enforced with an exclusive-create lockfile that
refuses a second mutating run against the same tree. No PID-liveness probe:
`os.kill(pid, 0)` kills on Windows.

Falsified on the way: `tool/test_quality/README.md` claimed CI passes
`--max-candidates 16`; it passes 20, and the same paragraph already carried a
note about being wrong the previous time. Rewritten to point at the command line
and to carry all three lanes.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(mutation-gate): the lock its own tests take, and a claim the gate proved false

Two corrections the first real gate run produced, both of them the gate doing
its job.

**The lock was taken by the gate's own tests.** `tests/scripts/` drives
`run(..., list_only=False)` in several places — genuinely mutating runs — so
those tests exclusive-created `.mutation_gate.lock` in the real working tree,
and were REFUSED outright when nested inside a live gate run. That is not a
corner: it is every future change that touches `run`, and it is what reddened
this branch's first gate run with `baseline failed`. One autouse fixture in a
new `tests/scripts/conftest.py` re-roots `LOCK_PATH` into `tmp_path` —
re-rooting rather than disabling, so the lock's own behaviour stays under test
next door, where `LOCK_PATH` is set explicitly.

**`iws-straddle-a-kept-workspace-is-not-a-refusal` SURVIVED, because the claim
was false.** The comment beside `RECONCILE_KEPT` said a kept arm mislabelled
`superseded` would drag the realm pointer back. It cannot: a kept workspace
belongs to the target realm by definition, so the heal's own
`winning_realm_id == requested_realm_id` check makes the mislabelling a wasted
read. The comment, the test docstring repeating it, and the claim are all
corrected; the claim is re-aimed at the guarantee that is actually there — the
early return keeps the operator's chosen workspace instead of letting the
ladder re-derive one.

A comment that reads like a guarantee and is not one is the thing this gate
exists to catch, so it is recorded in the field notes as the positive case
rather than quietly fixed.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(gateway): P4 — cross-install media, and the one keyhole R-P3 authorised

Closes Stage 8's honest gap 2: an operator on install A could not open a
picture install B's own reply declared, because the MEDIA: line named a path on
a disk A cannot read and neither install could mint a handle for bytes it does
not hold.

Consuming launcher ruling R-P3:

- B MINTS at reply time (media_handles.mint_reply_media, stamped by
  persona_commands._stamp_reply_media at all five reply sites, gated on
  --requested-by peer:). Only the install holding the bytes can hash them.
- The map RIDES the dispatch completion: on the ROW (dispatch_store's `media`),
  with the dispatch.completed event carrying media_count and never the map,
  because the payload cap is 4096 bytes.
- A FOLDS stored maps into the REMOTE half of its media scope, re-validating
  every field — handle grammar, absolute path, image allowlist, re-derived
  media_type — because the map was written by another install.
- A FETCHES lazily through the peer link: agent_runtime/media_proxy.py caches
  first, dials once, and verifies the returned bytes against the handle before
  serving or caching them. Content addressing makes that free and makes the
  cache need no invalidation.
- ONE new verb: peer.media.get, added to PEER_METHOD_ALLOWLIST with its reason.
  It resolves the LOCAL scope only (spelled as an argument), so the lane cannot
  chain A->B->C, and there is no peer.media.index, so a peer can spend a handle
  it was given and enumerate nothing.

The plan named tools/agent_chat_dispatch.py as the mint site; that function runs
on A. The correction and its consequences are recorded in
docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/remote-gateway-p4-field-notes-2026-09-01.md.

Acceptance: two real serve children, two roots, real TLS + HMAC — a console
device on A opens a file that exists only on B, and still opens it after B's
serve is STOPPED (the cache proof, as a fact rather than a counter).

author: nekwo
message:
feat(scripts): the cite-adjacency probe — a gate with a sweep budget, not a report

The unbuilt half of the doc-cite pair, and the half the two open rows were
actually about. `doc_cite_report.py` asks whether a cite RESOLVES; every one of
the four cites measured pointing at unrelated text since `76c6ade663` resolves
perfectly. This asks whether the cited line is ABOUT what the sentence says it
is: the subject the prose names must appear within +/-3 lines of the cite, or
the cited line must sit inside a def/class the prose names (resolved from the
AST, counted separately so the headline can still be read strictly).

**It is a GATE, where the resolution half deliberately is not, because it ships
with a baseline and a ratchet.** Red on any failure not in
`cite-adjacency-baseline.json`, and equally red on any baseline key that has
STOPPED failing — a waiver may not outlive its rot, which is the half a plain
baseline never has and the reason a capped gate stops shrinking. That is the
sweep budget the row asked for: 47 of the 113 measured failures were re-anchored
by hand in `cd9568ec11`, and the 66 that could not be are here with written
reasons rather than a suppressed lane. Baseline keys carry no doc line number,
so inserting a paragraph does not invalidate every waiver.

**What "machine-checkable" means is the whole honesty of the number, so it is
stated and it is narrow.** A cite is judged only when the prose around it names
an identifier that occurs in the cited file; a sentence naming nothing the file
contains is UNCHECKED, never failed. And "around it" is the SENTENCE, measured
rather than assumed: the paragraph-wide first cut reported
`realm_membership.py:1-12` rotted because the sentence BEFORE it named two
classes that live in that file twenty lines below the cited docstring, and
`board_store.py:8-15` rotted because the sentence AFTER it named three models.
Narrowing to the sentence removed both false findings and, at the same time,
raised the failure count 99 -> 113 by removing cites that had been passing on a
neighbour's subject.

The baseline's reasons name which entries are rot and which are the probe's own
blind spots — paired cites where the sentence's symbol belongs to the other
file, docstring ranges whose class is defined below the window, table rows whose
only identifiers are directory names. Those are rows to answer with a better
rule, not a new number, and the reason strings say so.

A zero-cite walk is FATAL, not a clean report.

message:
fix(office): the upsert's two fences, its order, and the names the scan was holding

Four rows off the mission-control queue's placement-verb section, all of them
about ``OfficeStore.upsert_actor``.

**The writer enumeration pinned ONE fence.** ``FENCED_ACTOR_WRITERS`` asked one
question per writer and every answer happened to be about the class-key fence,
so ``upsert_actor``'s desk fence (D6) and tombstone fence (D1) were pinned by
nothing — not because a row was missing but because the table had nowhere to put
one. Re-keyed (writer × fence) over all three fences, with completeness
enforced: a writer that answers two of three reds naming the one it skipped, a
disposition that opens with prose instead of a verdict reds, and each verdict is
read back out of the writer's source (FENCED must name its guard; every other
verdict must not — the negative half being the one a source walk answers
safely). The carve-out's ruling gains its desk and tombstone rows rather than
leaving them implied by the class-key paragraph.

**``ensure_surface`` ran BEFORE ``office_lock``**, so every refusal in the verb
authored a default ``office.json`` on a workspace that had none: the surface was
a side effect of ATTEMPTING a placement rather than of making one. The creation
could not simply move into the existing lock — ``office_lock`` is not reentrant
— so the creation half is now reachable on its own (``_ensure_surface_locked``,
same split and same reason as the ``position_policy`` hook) and runs after every
fence has passed. The unresolved-workspace refusal keeps its old position, and
is now one door (``_refuse_unresolvable_workspace``) rather than two spellings.

**``ActorScan`` carried a COUNT while the reader was standing on the paths.**
``UnreadableActorFiles`` carries the names, bounded, with the remainder spelled
``+N more`` rather than trimmed — a truncated list describing itself as whole is
the defect ``ActorScan`` exists to close one layer down. ``unreadable`` survives
as a property over ``.total``, so the number still lives in exactly one place and
no reader changes spelling. C4's shortfall row now names the file.

**The cross-directory conftest interaction.** The named intermittent red does not
reproduce at this HEAD; what the diagnosis did find is the mechanism one
directory over, measured: every env-gap registry is keyed by file BASENAME and
every owning conftest registers ``pytest_collection_modifyitems`` /
``pytest_runtest_logreport``, which pytest calls GLOBALLY. In a combined run
``tests/gateway``'s row for ``test_update_command.py`` also matches
``tests/cli/test_update_command.py`` — one directory silently deselecting
another's coverage. Ownership is now a required parameter, not a convention.
And ``ChatLaneBundle`` records WHICH component degraded: an incomplete bundle is
never memoized, so the fault was reaching a reuse measurement as "the object
changed" — which is precisely why the one red this cache has produced could only
be diagnosed as a key that had not moved.

message:
feat(push-gate): hermes gets a lane that runs — and a dump that can see itself move

hermes `main` sat red and unreported from `6979bad59`. The verb is fixed
(`65b233d62`); the verb was never the row. The row is that a repo whose CI is
inert had NO push lane at all — `.githooks/` held only `post-merge` — so any red
on `main` survived until a human happened to run a suite. An unrun gate is
indistinguishable from a passing one. Third instance of one class; the launcher
has met it twice and its repair is the shape taken here.

`.githooks/pre-push`, installed by the same `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`
that already installs `post-merge`:

* Lane A, ALWAYS, every push and every ref: `doc_cite_adjacency.py` at its RULED
  scope (`--exclude archive --exclude planned` — the bare walk is red by 829 by
  ruling, and widening it here would make the lane born-red) plus the new
  contract-freshness check. ~11 s warm. Both have the whole tree as their input,
  which is exactly what no trigger set can express — the mistake behind all
  three instances.
* Lane B, on a push landing on `refs/heads/main`: the R3-VALIDATED 4-directory
  parallel lane, ~18 min. Not the runner's whole-tree default: that reads ~142
  failed on a green `main`, all triaged environmental, and a gate reading 142 red
  on a green tree is scenery. `main` is the classifier because hermes has no
  `release` branch — `main` IS the shipping branch and is literally the row. An
  unclassifiable ref line takes the expensive side, never the fast path.

Every control is loud: a non-main push is TOLD which gates did not run and the
command that runs them; `HERMES_PUSH_SUITE_LANE=skip` prints what it skipped;
`HERMES_PUSH_SUITE_DIRS` prints the narrowing beside the validated scope. Missing
python, a missing lane script, a missing bash, or a runner refusing for want of
pytest each FAIL the push naming the fix — this box has had no `.venv` since
2026-08-30 and that open row must not resolve itself as a silent skip.

The hook calls `scripts/run_tests.sh` and never `pytest`. The updater tests are
INSIDE lane B's scope and their real flow does `git branch -f main origin/main`;
a plain `pytest tests/hermes_cli` in the primary detached 11 unpushed commits on
2026-08-01. Re-measured 2026-09-02 from a linked worktree across the six
repo-touching updater files: refs, `main`'s reflog and all 18 worktree
registrations byte-identical before and after.

`scripts/dump_cli_contract.py` + `tests/fixtures/hermes_cli_contract.json` close
the other half. The launcher checks every operator button's argv against a dump
of THESE parsers committed in the LAUNCHER, so a hermes-side argparse change left
every launcher test green while that fixture lied — `ab6254643` left it stale
three days across five hermes commits, found by a human going looking. A hand-run
regen is not a mechanism. Now the repo that MOVED goes red, on its own lane.

The new dump is byte-identical to the launcher's committed fixture as of today,
which is the evidence that the two walkers agree and that an on-sync comparison
means something. Two copies of one walker is a duplicated authority and is not

author: nekwo
message:
fix(bootstrap): importing the CLI is not running it, and three verbs stop taking their own lock

Two collection-time landmines and one self-deadlock, all measured 2026-09-01.

THE IMPORT. `hermes_cli/main.py` ran `_apply_profile_override()` from module
scope, so importing the module pre-parsed whatever argv the process had and
repointed the process's HERMES_HOME. Under pytest that argv is pytest's: `-p
<plugin>` was consumed as `--profile <plugin>`, resolved nothing, and exited 1
from inside a collection import — surfacing as a bare `INTERNALERROR>
SystemExit: 1` naming nothing. With no `-p` at all the same import read the
operator's live `<root>/active_profile` and pointed the whole session's
HERMES_HOME at their live profile, one layer above every hermetic fixture.

The pre-parse moves to `hermes_cli/_profile_bootstrap.py` UNCHANGED (aliased
back onto `hermes_cli.main._apply_profile_override`, which is the name the
tree cites), and the module-scope call is now gated on
`is_hermes_cli_entrypoint(__name__)`: true for `python -m hermes_cli.main` —
runpy runs it AS `__main__`, which is every gateway/systemd/scheduled-task
spawn — and for the console scripts pyproject installs, matched off argv[0]
with pip/nix launcher decoration stripped. Entrypoint-based on purpose: an env
toggle would be a silent fallback any process could set, including the ones
this keeps out. A real `hermes …` invocation is unchanged, and the allowlist is
pinned equal to `[project.scripts]` so a fourth entry point cannot be added
without someone answering whether it needs the pre-parse.

The receipt probe stops exec'ing a slice of main.py's source between two
spellings and imports the real function instead; the four rung literals are
read off the module that now writes them.

THE LOCK. `remove_actor`, `restore_actor` and `resolve_conflict`'s
edit-vs-remove arm each held `office_lock(wsid)` and then called the PUBLIC
`ensure_surface`, which takes the same non-reentrant lock. They survived only
because `ensure_surface` returns before acquiring when the surface exists — so
on a surface-less workspace holding a live actor each contended with itself and
refused `HarnessLockUnavailable` at the deadline. All three take
`_ensure_surface_locked` (6de4cb1b95), and each case is pinned on exactly that
input: the verb completes AND authors the surface, which a verb that merely
stopped refusing cannot satisfy.

The fourth test is the class rather than a fourth patch: a negative source walk
over every module that opens an `office_lock` block, refusing `ensure_surface`
inside one.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(cli): absent is not empty — one seam for it, and a ban the grep census could not enforce

CLASS row, not a nineteenth patch. `persona instance update-profile` read a
repeatable `--skill` as `list(getattr(args, "skills", None) or [])`;
`action="append"` gives `None` when the flag is absent, so an omitted flag
reached `PersonaInstanceStore.update_profile` as an empty LIST and its
`if skills is not None or clear_skills:` correctly wrote it — renaming an agent
cleared every skill it had. That instance was fixed. Three things it left
standing:

* THE COLLAPSE HAS NO SINGLE SPELLING. The queue's census said eleven sites,
  measured by grep for `getattr(args, X, None) or []`. An AST walk for the
  SHAPE finds twenty-five: seven more as `args.X or []`, and seven more again as
  `getattr(args, X, []) or []` and `args.parent or ()` — two spellings no grep
  in this lane had ever looked for. The census was not wrong; it was a grep.
* THREE HANDLERS HAD EACH RE-DERIVED THE CORRECT RULE BY HAND, in three
  paragraphs, in one file — the agent-create params builder, update-profile, and
  `_validated_set_skills_request`. Nothing linked them, so the reasoning was
  per-site.
* EVERY ONE OF THE TWENTY-FIVE IS SAFE TODAY. Each was read: each iterates,
  refuses on empty, or appends. There is no outage here and this change does not
  invent one. It is a trap, and the next verb into it will look like these.

So: `hermes_cli/flag_binding.py` with two readers whose NAMES are the ruling —
`list_flag_or_empty` (the consumer cannot tell the two apart; say so) and
`list_flag_or_absent` (the value reaches a store that reads `is not None` as an
instruction). All twenty-five sites migrated; the three hand-written correct
readers migrated onto `list_flag_or_absent` so there is one spelling.

Three gates, each the kind its guarantee allows:
* the BAN is an AST source walk, because "this must never be written" is the
  one shape a source walk fits — and it carries its own both-directions proof,
  since a ban nobody has watched fire may be matching nothing.
* the READERS are executed, not inspected.
* the PARSER TIER is asserted against the live argparse `Action` objects: a
  reader cannot recover what `default=[]` threw away, so any flag read as
  absent must be declared `default=None`. It caught one on its first run —
  `harness mission-chat queue-skill --skills` is `nargs="+", default=[]`, waived
  with its reason because that verb refuses on empty either way. `dest` is not
  unique across subparsers, so the gate keys on the command PATH and answers
  each collision in writing rather than narrowing the walk.

No parser declaration changed; the CLI contract dump is byte-identical.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(board): "I cannot resolve this receipt" is not "there is no receipt"

CLASS row: "a recorded ack replayed verbatim for a row that is mutable
afterwards", whose fixed instance is `runtime.agent.create`'s STATE_DONE arm
(re-reads the actor, `actor_fresh: false` when it cannot).

THE AUDIT FOUND NO SECOND INSTANCE. Every receipt ledger in the runtime was
enumerated from `paths.py` plus the three key-digest lock helpers and read:
chat-turn reservations, both persona-chat mint stores, the board, the retire
receipt, the mission-chat turn journal, the steer ack, the kanban
`idempotency_key` column, and the three in-memory caches (api_server,
webhook dedupe, the serve poll cache). Each is either id-only with a live
re-read, or records a decision no live row can contradict. Three had reached
the rule independently, and `agent_retire` goes further — it sweeps live
placements BEFORE the archived-keys read, so a replay self-heals rather than
merely reporting. That conclusion is recorded as an invariant in 01 (landed in
the preceding commit, which touched the same file).

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND INSTEAD is the other side of the same seam, and it is a
real defect. `BoardStore._idempotent_replay` returned `None` for FIVE
conditions: no key, no receipt, an undecodable receipt, a receipt naming no
card, and a card_id resolving to neither a live nor an archived file. The
caller cannot tell them apart, so it ran the write again — and `add_card` mints
a new card id per call, so the key whose entire purpose is to prevent a
duplicate produced one, after which `_record_idempotency` overwrote the receipt
and the first card was orphaned beyond reach of that key.

Cards are never hard-deleted (`archive_card` writes the archive copy before
unlinking the active one; `restore_card` does the reverse), so "resolves to
neither" is a truncated or corrupted write, never a routine purge — there is no
legitimate retry this refusal can break.

The three unresolvable conditions now raise `IdempotentReplayUnresolved`.
`None` means exactly one thing again. This is the board's version of
`actor_fresh: false`: a replay that cannot re-read the row it describes says so
rather than inventing an answer — and because the board's ack carries no field
to degrade, it refuses instead.

The code is wired into the taxonomy rather than left to the catch-all, which is
the third time that row has had to be added for the same reason: without it a
REFUSAL exits 1 as `internal_error` and reports a corrupt file on the server as
a harness crash. Family 7 beside `archive_unreadable`/`actors_unreadable`,
whose operator cure is identical, retryable, with its own remedy line.

fix(receipts): a key that names two verbs, an ack that names two states, and a denial that blamed the healthy half

Four queue rows in agent_runtime/, each premise re-verified at b9e7a27988
before anything was written. Two rows were right that something was broken
and wrong about where; both corrections are recorded rather than quietly
applied. Field notes:
docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/board-idempotency-and-typed-receipts-field-notes-2026-09-02.md

1. BOARD IDEMPOTENCY IS PER-BOARD, NOT PER-VERB (verified as filed).
   `boards/<id>/idempotency/` is one namespace and add_card, edit_card and
   move_card all consult it, so a key crossing verbs replayed the OTHER
   verb's card and the second write silently did not happen — move_card
   under add_card's key returned the unmoved card with an ack no caller
   could tell from a real move. The receipt now records its `verb` and a
   crossing refuses `IdempotencyKeyVerbMismatch`, naming both verbs.

   A SIBLING class, not a reuse of IdempotentReplayUnresolved: the two
   disagree about `retryable`. Unresolved is a damaged FILE an operator
   repairs before the identical call succeeds (exit 7, in the retryable
   set); this is a wrong REQUEST refused identically forever (exit 2, cure
   = a key of its own). One code would have made the envelope's retryable
   half lie about half the calls carrying it. Mapped ahead of the
   AgentRuntimeError catch-all with its own hint, which deliberately does
   not say "repair the receipt file".

   A receipt with no `verb` predates the field and is honoured exactly as
   before — refusing it would turn every in-flight key on every existing
   board into a hard failure at upgrade, to protect against a crossing that
   already happened. Decision recorded in the docstring, canon 06 and a test.

   Red-first: 5 of the 6 new board tests fail on origin/main (the sixth is
   the "must not cost the feature" fence and passes both sides).

2. `ChatTurnReservation.replay_ack` LEFT state: "accepted" ON A SETTLED
   REPLAY (verified). chat_turn.py's accept path writes "state":
   STATE_ACCEPTED into the ack, so a replay after settle_chat_turn came back
   saying `state: "accepted"` and `settled: true` at once. `state` is now
   re-stamped from the record.

   The launcher was read (read-only) first: `MissionChatTurnAck.fromFrame`
   is the only decoder and reads turn_request_id, request_id,
   idempotent_replay, settled, exit_code, correlation_id — no `state`, no
   `accepted`, no `verb`. `idempotent_replay` is the only ack field driving
   behaviour; settled/exit_code are carried, never branched on. So `settled`
   stays the live discriminator, untouched, including its pairing with a
   recorded exit code. Red-first: the new test reproduces the exact
   'accepted' == 'settled' mismatch on origin/main.

3. mcp_not_registered_on_lane COULD NOT SEPARATE "no MCP client" FROM "the
   server failed" (substance verified; the row's LOCATION was wrong, and
   the wrongness was the bug). agent_runtime/mcp_admission.py never read
   `_MCP_AVAILABLE` — the flag lives in tools/mcp_tool.py and reached
   admission only as an empty registrar return, the same empty list a
   failed connect produces. So there was no read site to raise at; one is
   created: `mcp_sdk_available()`, the single seam through which
   agent_runtime asks that question, consulted in admit_mcp_servers when a
   server missed the registry (production path only — an injected registrar
   is not the SDK's).

   The new `mcp_sdk_unavailable` denial names the runtime, the `mcp` extra
   (pyproject) and the required RESTART, instead of the old hint's "check
   the server is running and its command resolves" — the two halves that
   are already healthy. That sentence cost weeks: a standing "the chat lane
   admits nothing" gap was planned against while admission, declaration,
   resolution and policy were all correct (root cause 2026-08-26). The
   lane-level mcp_lane row is untouched; it answers a different question.

4. A COLD-SPAWN MEASUREMENT USED AS A DISCRIMINATOR (verified on the prose,
   FALSIFIED on the code). No production code compares an elapsed count —
   profile_runner counts the TRANSPORT_COLD label, and the label is read off
   the live session map. Nothing was rewired. Three prose sites carried the
   stale "~3,200 ms means a real cold spawn" rule and are corrected to state
   the honest discriminator positively (a non-empty admitted SET): the
   TRANSPORT_COLD docstring, profile_runner's T2 comment, and canon 05's
   carry-forward row. launcher_qa is a compiled Dart exe spawning cold in
   ~100 ms, so that rule reads a genuine spawn as a fast failure. An AST
   fence over mcp_admission.py now fails if an elapsed-time comparison
   appears; a grep would have matched the corrected comments themselves.

MUTATION CLAIMS: 9 added, one per behaviour-bearing production line.

TWO STALE CLAIMS RE-ANCHORED, out of scope and reported: the gate was RED
on clean origin/main — `s4-an-omitted-skill-flag-clears-every-instance-override`
and `s4-the-cli-create-door-drops-its-skill-flag` both anchored on source
a3b48a06a2's `list_flag_or_absent` refactor moved, so `--list` exited with a
configuration error and no claim could run. Both re-anchored onto the current
lines with the same operator and the same test; nothing else about them changed.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(cites): the two residuals the probe filed against itself, and a cap the README may not re-type

THE PROBE COULD NOT SEE HALF THE LINE NUMBERS IN THE CANON. `CONTINUATION`
reads the bare backticked `:N` / `:N-M` the canon writes constantly —
`harness.py:1873`, `_cmd_characters_auto` at `:4776` — and there are 299 of
them against 326 path cites in the gated walk. `continued_path` resolves each
against the nearest preceding path MENTION in its own SENTENCE, and
`ContinuedCite` hands it to `verdict` so it is judged by exactly the same rule
and lands in the same baseline key shape.

Both halves of that scope were measured, not argued. SENTENCE, not paragraph:
where both resolve they never disagree (56 of 56), and the 76 the paragraph
would additionally resolve include ones it gets WRONG — 01's `:613` would
inherit `store.py` from a cite two sentences up. MENTION, not cite: 03 writes
`patch_coverage.py::parse_fold_entities_option`, `:404`, and a rule reading
only `CITE` skips the `::` form and hands `:404` to harness.py, which is the
feature meant to catch fabricated findings producing one.

THE OCCURRENCE CEILING IS 20, AND THE CORPUS PICKED IT. A backticked `show` /
`final` / `chat` occurs all over a 5000-line module, so one lands in almost any
+/-3 window; that is how `07|persona_commands.py:3522` passed while its real
subject sat at 4222/4495. Swept at 8/12/16/20/40 (table in the field notes).
Every candidate flips 3522, so that test chooses nothing — what chooses is the
cites each end gets wrong, read one by one. At 40 two REAL rots keep passing on
`realm`/`sync`/`install` (01's `harness.py:616`, cited for `realm sync revert`,
is the `resolve` parser; 01's `:1343`, cited for `install-harness-skills`, is a
`--max-seconds` argument). At 12 and 8 the rule refuses `board_id` (13-20
occurrences) and reports a correct cite as rot. 20 is the only candidate that
catches every confirmed rot and invents no finding.

The reading also forced an exemption: a plain 20 still reported `paths.py:8` —
which IS `def store_root()` — as rot, because `store_root` is that file's
workhorse. A name the file DEFINES pins a line by construction, so `defines`
exempts def/class names from the ceiling on the same AST the `in-symbol`
verdict already uses. Inventing findings to stop inventing findings is not a
trade worth making.

RE-BASELINED HONESTLY, not regenerated. 17 cites re-anchored to their symbol in
the canon (four of them findable ONLY by the two new rules), 2 stale waivers
deleted, 29 added and each read: 9 of those are confirmed-CORRECT cites the
probe cannot vouch for and the reasons say so, because a baseline whose reasons
all read "pre-existing" is a suppression list. 64 -> 91 keys. Lane A exit 0.

Red-first, all of it: the 9 new probe tests were run against HEAD's script and
baseline and all 9 failed; restored, 27 pass. The README pin was run with the
number sabotaged to 16 and failed `assert 16 == 20`; reverted, 2 pass.

ALSO HERE, because it is the same class of defect: `tool/test_quality/README.md`
tells a reader CI's mutation cap and has been wrong twice by its own admission.
`tests/scripts/test_mutation_cap_matches_workflow.py` parses the number out of
the workflow's `mutation-claims` step (as YAML, so the comments naming the
older 12 and 16 cannot be mistaken for the live one) and out of the README
bullet, and hand-types neither. It pins the CI lane only: the per-stage default
and the landing cap have no workflow to be checked against, and inventing a
source of truth for them would be inventing a claim.

`tests/scripts` is outside Lane B's four-directory scope, so neither new test
rides the push gate — they ride CI. `dump_cli_contract.py --check` untouched
and green.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(charsheet,serve): one writer per draft, a drain that waits for a generation, and a bound on the provider call

The hermes half of the long-run lane — the three rows the launcher's
W1b design filed under §4 decision 5, each verified against b9e7a27988
before it was built.

(i) A per-draft lock in `CharacterDraft`. The docstring's packaging claim
was CURRENT, not stale: `agent_runtime/locks.py` exists and is good, but
`agent_runtime` is absent from `[tool.setuptools.packages.find].include`
and three modules in this package record the no-`agent_runtime` boundary
in their own words. So `agent/charsheet/draft_lock.py` is stdlib: an
`O_EXCL` lock file beside `draft.json` carrying `{draft, verb, pid, host,
started}`, held for the whole of `turnaround`, `rows`, `auto`, and both
re-rolls, re-entrant per THREAD so `auto` holds it once around its whole
plan while the serve pool's other worker is refused `DraftBusy`.

The holder is written into the file rather than taken as a byte-range
lock because the refusal has to NAME it: a 15-minute batch and a crashed
one are otherwise indistinguishable. There is no pid liveness on either
host — `os.kill(pid, 0)` kills the process on Windows, which the mutation
gate already refuses to probe for — so the stale policy is one age
ceiling on both, 45 minutes: above the launcher's 30-minute long-run
ceiling so it can never break a live run, above hermes's own 22-minute
worst-case `auto`, and low enough that a crash clears itself.

DIVERGENCE, argued in the field notes: `DraftBusy` was NOT added to
`_error_code_for_exception`. That function's only caller is
`emit_harness_error`, and no `characters` verb calls it — the lane emits
the flat pets error shape. A row there would be unreachable, which is the
dated ruling written into that very function ("a mapping row for an
exception nothing throws is not defensive, it is a claim about the
runtime that is false"). The token travels on the lane that exists
instead: `_CHARACTERS_EXPECTED` catches `CharsheetRefusal`, and the flat
payload gains `code`, `busy` (the holder, lock path included) and a
`status` `next` hint — no `alternatives`, because hermes cannot cancel a
running generation and there is no second legal move.

(ii) The drain and the busy frame hold for the generate verbs.
`_LONG_RUN_COMMANDS` sits beside `_CHAT_TURN_COMMANDS`, `is_long_run` is
derived by the same prefix match on the same argv tail, and both counts
are ADDITIVE: `busy` gains `long_runs`, `drain_timeout` gains
`held_by_long_runs` + `long_run_request_ids`, and `terminal` becomes
`not (chat_turn_ids or long_run_ids)`. `held_by_chat_turns` keeps its
name and meaning; a read-only grep of the launcher's `lib/` finds no
reader for it (or for `drain_timeout` at all), while `chat_turns` on the
`busy` frame HAS one, and that key is untouched. Cancel semantics are
unchanged.

(iii) A per-call deadline in `pipeline.py`. There was no real timeout to
wire: `imagegen.generate` takes no `timeout` parameter, and the backends
each set their own — 300s openrouter, 300s openai-codex read, 180s krea
poll — except `openai`, which builds a bare `openai.OpenAI()` whose SDK
default is 600s with retries. So `_within_deadline` runs the one seam on
a daemon thread and raises `ProviderTimeout` at
`charsheet.provider_timeout_seconds` (config.yaml, default 300 — the
largest ceiling any shipped backend sets for itself, so hermes never cuts
off a provider inside its own contract). This is what bounds (ii): a hold
that a wedged image backend could keep open forever is not a hold.

Red-first, each: a second writer refused mid-batch from inside the first
batch's provider call; a drain deadline expiring during `characters rows`
re-arming instead of terminating, with the request landing afterwards;
a provider that never answers refused, on time, with its type. Ten
mutation claims, ten killed — including one this branch's own first run
SURVIVED, which correctly identified a release-path guard that could
never be false; the guard is gone and the claim now aims at re-entrancy.

Field notes: docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/long-run-lane-hermes-field-notes-2026-09-02.md
Canon: 03 §1's chat-turn paragraph now covers both marks, cited by symbol.
Nineteen line cites across 01/03/04/05/07/08 re-anchored where this
diff moved them, and two pre-existing claims rotted by a3b48a06a2
re-anchored so the gate could run at all.

message:
fix(sync): the arm that gives you something was the silent one, in three places

Four sync-honesty rows, all verified against ca8eb228c9 before a line moved, and
one target refused on the evidence. Field notes:
docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/sync-honesty-field-notes-2026-09-02.md.

1. `realm_sync_status` fails closed on the REMOTE half only.
   It called `_authorize` first and raised, so a member whose credential expired
   lost the store drift, the held skill packages, the held profile artifacts and
   the workspace rows — every one a credential-free LOCAL read — at the moment
   the diagnostic was worth having. The authorization now gates the clone, the
   fetch and therefore the freshness of ahead/behind; a denial rides the
   `remote_checked: false` / `remote_check_error` pair an unreachable remote
   already rides, so nothing on the launcher moves (its `_RemoteUncheckedNote`
   renders it today). `publish` / `pull` still refuse WHOLE, and `_authorize`
   now says why in a docstring. The degrade has a floor: no local repo, no
   degrade — the verb re-raises, and never attempts the clone it was refused.
   Red-first: `test_status_answers_local_facts_when_the_remote_half_is_denied`,
   `..._carries_the_backends_own_denial_code_not_a_generic_one`,
   `..._still_refuses_when_the_denial_leaves_no_local_facts`.

2. `OfficeStore.resolve_conflict`'s adopt arm emits its actor patch.
   `take="remote"` wrote the peer's row with a bare `_write_actor` while its
   edit-vs-remove sibling emitted a `remove` through `_archive_actor_locked`
   even with the domain event suppressed — the H1 asymmetry, one method down
   from the verb that closed it.
   `office.actor.conflict_resolved` STAYS off `LIVE_COVERED_DOMAIN_EVENT_TYPES`,
   against the row's target and on this module's own derivability rule: every
   arm archives the conflict sidecar, which takes the key out of the office
   row's `conflict_actor_keys`, and no `office_actor` patch carries that field
   (the launcher's `_applyOfficeActorPatch` never writes it; `_officeSurfaceFields`
   names it among the keys no patch may move). Covering it would clear the desk
   and leave the sync strip's conflict pill lit for the session. `take="local"`
   emits no patch at all, which is a second, independent refusal. The comment
   block has now been wrong about this event twice; both dead reasons are kept
   beside the live one.
   Red-first: `test_the_adopt_arm_emits_the_actor_patch_its_archive_sibling_always_did`,
   `test_take_local_writes_no_actor_and_therefore_emits_no_patch`, and the
   coverage test's assertion moved from "no patch" to "an upsert, still demoted".

3. The board pull's adopt arms reach the live lane.
   `apply_board_pull` wrote defs and cards with `atomic_json_write` past
   `BoardStore`, so a pull that ARCHIVED a card emitted and a pull that GAVE you
   one — or rewrote the column taxonomy — emitted nothing and advanced no
   watermark. `BoardStore.adopt_remote_board` / `adopt_remote_card` are the
   office twins' shape (remote revision verbatim, `updated_by` records the sync,
   nothing re-derived, absence asked under the write's own lock), and both
   `apply_board_pull` and `realm_revert._adopt_from_upstream` route through them.
   Bytes unchanged: `board_content_hash` excludes `updated_by`, so the baseline
   still keys off the remote CONTENT — asserted, not claimed. `archived_card_ids`
   is deliberately NOT unioned here; that moves a resurrection guard and is a
   decision about data, filed as its own row.
   Red-first: `test_pull_that_adopts_a_card_emits_what_a_local_add_emits`,
   `test_pull_that_adopts_a_board_def_emits_the_board_event`,
   `test_adopting_a_board_a_member_has_never_had_emits_created`,
   `test_reverting_an_edited_card_writes_through_the_stores_evented_door`.

4. `plugins/memory` finishes an import instead of half of one.
   The loader did `sys.modules[full_name] = mod` and never bound the child on
   its parent, so `import plugins.memory.x` worked forever and
   `from plugins.memory import x` raised forever, depending on which ran first —
   a product shape (a plugin's own sibling import, any caller patching into a
   provider), not a test shape. `_publish_module` does both halves at all five
   registration sites; `_unpublish_module` undoes both on the `exec_module`
   rollback, or the fix would trade one two-answers-for-one-name defect for
   another aimed at the failure path. `tests/hermes_cli/conftest.py` is NOT
   touched (another agent owns it this session); its repair loop is now
   redundant for this loader's providers and still needed in general — see the
   field notes §5.
   Red-first: `tests/plugins/memory/test_provider_loader_import_identity.py`
   (3 of its 4 red without the fix; the rollback test guards the fix, not the
   original defect).

Canon: 01 §Realms and workspaces, 01 §The board, 06 §The board, 06 §The fold
model, 07 §The honesty contract. Five drifted cites in 01/03/06 re-anchored to
symbols rather than re-numbered.

author: nekwo
message:
perf(tests): the identity guard stops walking sys.modules, and doctor stops reading the operator's store

Two rows, one branch, because both live in tests/hermes_cli's fixtures.

ROW 1 — the residual aging floor, attributed in field notes §15 and cured here
as §15 prescribed. The setup half of `_sys_modules_identity_is_restored` walked
every entry in `sys.modules` per test and asked `hasattr(parent, child)`:
0.42 ms/test fresh, 29.9 ms aged, ~65% of the growth as the mapping filled
626 -> 14,843 during a run. The guarantee is untouched — `before =
sys.modules.copy()` and the teardown restore stay, they ARE the guarantee — and
the per-test O(sys.modules) module-object work is gone:

  * `child in vars(parent)` instead of `hasattr`, so no parent's PEP 562 module
    `__getattr__`, and no lazy-import machinery behind it, ever fires (~24 ms of
    the 29.9);
  * the walk runs only when `len(sys.modules)` changed since the last pass, and
    then skips every name already bound (~5 ms);
  * a name is remembered as done only after its PARENT resolved, so a child
    whose package is not imported yet is reconsidered by the pass that follows
    that import. Without this the count gate would be a hole, not a free skip.

Both pollution classes the guard's docstring names were re-run in one process in
the order that reproduces them, with the counterfactual:
test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py then
test_doctor.py::TestHonchoDoctorConfigDetection is 39 passed, and 1 failed with
the repair disabled — the documented `'module' object at plugins.memory.honcho
has no attribute 'honcho'`, verbatim.

New: tests/hermes_cli/test_module_identity_guard.py (8). Red-first against the
pre-fix walk planted back into `run()`: 3 failed / 5 passed. The three that fail
are the `__getattr__` probe, the count gate and "only the new name is examined";
the five that assert the GUARANTEE are green both ways.

ROW 2 — `doctor.HERMES_HOME` was bound at module import, and under pytest that
import happens at COLLECTION, before the hermetic-home fixture runs, so every
path diagnostic read the operator's live store. The tree already documented the
damage: `TestGitHubTokenCheck._isolate_home` records that
`setenv("HERMES_HOME")` alone left doctor running `PRAGMA integrity_check`
against the developer's real state.db and blowing a 300 s per-file budget.
Importing the module also loaded the operator's real `.env` into the test
process. `run_doctor` now resolves the home, and that `.env`, at call time;
hermes_cli/doctor.py's entry in tests/test_no_frozen_hermes_home.py shrinks from
{HERMES_HOME, _DHH, _env_path} to {_DHH}, which stays because it is a display
label and never a filesystem read. 31 `monkeypatch.setattr(doctor_mod,
"HERMES_HOME", ...)` sites across 4 files became `monkeypatch.setenv`.

Red-first: the two new TestDoctorResolvesTheHomeAtCallTime tests fail 2/2 with
the import-time binding planted back. They assert on a file doctor must have
READ (a planted skills-hub lock.json count), not on the printed home, so
patching the label cannot fake them. Mutation claim
`doctor-home-is-read-at-call-time-not-at-import` anchors `run_doctor/HERMES_HOME`
and is KILLED by the gate.

ROW 2's PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, and the correction is the more useful half. The
row said the import-time binding is why the suite runs the operator's live
`profiles/alice/node/agent-browser.CMD`, and that fixing it would let the gateway
fence's exemption be deleted. It does not: none of doctor's three
profile-relative browser candidates exists under that root, and the probed path
comes from `shutil.which("agent-browser")` — the operator's PATH, which
scripts/run_tests.sh forwards verbatim. Measured with the binding already fixed,
deleting the exemption still reds 19 tests in test_doctor.py alone. So the
exemption was NARROWED rather than deleted: it was spelled "any argv without a
hermes entry point", which also let an `npm --prefix <real root> install`
through, and is now spelled as the probe itself — two tokens, an agent-browser
basename, `--version`. Four new parametrized cases pin that and fail 4/4 against
the old spelling.

Numbers, the load caveat they must be read under (the whole-run aged AFTER arm
is OWED — the box saturated), the corrected mechanism, and the two residuals
this lane found and did not fix: field notes §16; hermes-suite-perf.md
§Follow-ups marked landed.

author: nekwo
message:
feat(cli): the refusal names the choices, and the sprite verb can answer without the sheet

Two CLI-ergonomics rows. One of them was filed on a premise the code does
not support, and the honest half is smaller than the row asked for.

ROW 1 — "no subcommand enumerates placeable templates" is FALSE.
`harness agent list` walks `ensure_persisted_personas` — the exact
`{**catalog, **stored}` merge `agent_create._persona_is_unknown` checks
against — and has always emitted one row per placeable definition (five,
live, at 0c9fb95410). `persona_not_found_message` already named it. So no
`persona templates` verb was built: that is rung 2 of the Footprint Ladder
for a problem rung 1 covers.

What was actually missing is that the refusal handed back the NAME of a
command, which cures nothing for a script, a cron or a remote `call` leg
that cannot run a second one — and that NOTHING said `--persona` takes two
spellings for one agent. Both are now answered from one function:

- `accepted_persona_spellings` is the single authority. It offers
  `profile:<token>` only for a profile with exactly ONE owner, because the
  CLI's synthesis lane fills defaults through `profile_persona_resolution`,
  which answers nothing for a shared profile: the spelling would still
  parse (D-U1 exempts every `profile:` id from the roster check) and would
  mint a defaults-less agent DIFFERENT from the id printed beside it.
- `persona_not_found_message` appends the placeable ids with both
  spellings, bounded by `PERSONA_CHOICE_LIST_LIMIT` so a large roster
  cannot turn a refusal into a page. Best-effort: a roster this second read
  cannot open degrades the message back to its cure sentence rather than
  converting an actionable refusal into a fault.
- `_agent_definition_row` gains `persona_spellings` and `skills`, so the
  verb the refusal points at answers the question it is pointed at for.
  Additive; `binding_source` already carried the catalog-vs-store fact.

ROW 2 — `characters sprite <slug> --json --no-sheet`. `sprite_payload`
read and base64'd the sheet on every call (468.8 KiB live). It now takes
`include_sheet`; the metadata-only shape omits `spritesheetBase64`, never
reads the bytes, and carries `sheet` — the absolute path, the same key
`characters list`'s installed rows use — in the SAME slot, so the default
is byte-identical, key order included. `spritesheetRevision` stays: the
launcher's provenance record hangs on it. NOT mirrored onto `pets sprite`:
that verb is served by `_pet_sprite_payload_for_launcher`, a different
function, which was the row's own condition.

Contract dump regenerated (+1 flag, nothing removed). The launcher's own
committed fixture is now stale by that flag and its re-sync is owed at
landing, recorded in its `tool/hermes_cli_contract/README.md`.

Proof: 494 tests green across the nine touched/adjacent files; five new
mutation claims, all KILLED (`--base 0c9fb95410 --max-candidates 12`,
7 candidates selected, exit 0); cite-adjacency and `--check` both green —
six cites into `hermes_cli/harness.py` that THIS change's line insertions
drifted were re-anchored. Field notes:
docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/cli-ergonomics-field-notes-2026-09-02.md

author: nekwo
message:
fix(postinstall): the PATH shim stops exec'ing itself, and a test stops writing one into the operator's home

Three queue rows, all three premises checked against the tree first.

**The shim exec'd itself.** `_resolve_hermes_exe` took its directory from
`tools.environments.local._resolve_hermes_bin_dir()`, whose first rung is
`shutil.which("hermes")`. The shim is written into a directory this module then
puts ON PATH, so from the second `postinstall` on, `which` answered with the
shim and `render_posix_shim` emitted `exec "<shim>"` into `<shim>` — five stuck
`/bin/sh` processes on an operator's Mac, the oldest 34 days old.

Fixed in three fences, not the one the row named:

* `_hermes_exe_dirs` resolves `sys.executable`'s bin/Scripts dir FIRST — the
  console-script of the venv this process runs out of, which is the
  unreachable-from-PATH executable the shim exists to reach — then argv0, then
  PATH.
* `register_hermes_command` REFUSES, typed (`error="shim_target_is_shim"`) and
  without writing, when the resolved target still lands on the shim's own path.
  That is not belt-and-braces: `pip install --user` puts the genuine
  console-script AT `~/.local/bin/hermes`, which is the POSIX shim path, and no
  ordering can fix a case where nothing stands behind the shim.
* Every candidate directory must be ABSOLUTE. Found because the red-first
  revert of the ordering PASSED: `shutil.which` searches the cwd before PATH on
  Windows and this repo's root holds a `hermes`, so it answers `.\hermes` — a
  relative exec target means a different broken command in every directory the
  operator stands in.

`tools/environments/local.py` is deliberately untouched: its PATH-first order is
correct for prepending the install dir onto a SUBSHELL's PATH, where the shim on
PATH is the right answer. Both orders now say so in their own docstring.

**A test could bake its own HERMES_HOME into a real shim.** The production
derivation was already canonical — `cmd_postinstall` passes `get_hermes_home()`
and no caller passes a scratch path. The hole was an absence on the test side:
`_hermetic_environment` redirects `HERMES_HOME` and, by an explicit ruling, does
NOT redirect `HOME`, so the HOME-anchored install dir stayed REAL for every test
in the tree. The derivation moves into one seam, `_shim_install_dir()`, and an
autouse `_isolate_hermes_shim_dir` pins it into `tmp_path` — redirecting the
seam rather than `HOME`, which that ruling forbids, and autouse rather than
per-test, because the tests that already remembered are not the population this
protects. Reproduced first: with the redirect removed (and the install dir
pointed at a scratch stand-in so nothing real was touched) a genuine
`hermes.cmd` landed there baking a pytest temp `HERMES_HOME` — the operator's
Mac artifact exactly.

**`backfill-home` lost the directory on the skipped arm.** The skipped rows are
precisely the population an id cannot disambiguate — a copied draft keeps the id
inside its own `draft.json` AND the home it was made in — so an id collision
printed two rows differing in nothing. The verb's docstring already stated the
rule; one of its two arms did not implement it. `migrate-home`'s skipped arm was
checked as asked: it has the same shape of asymmetry, partly mitigated by its
`reason` string, and is filed rather than fixed here — it needs `directory` on
the `_relocate` rows in `agent/charsheet/draft.py` too.

Also: `cmd_postinstall` now SAYS what happened. The whole `PathSetupResult` was
readable only inside the `--json` branch, so a human running `hermes postinstall`
was told nothing — neither a refusal nor the "add this dir to your PATH" line.
`error` rides in the `hermes.postinstall/1` summary beside `note` (additive; no
consumer of these keys found in the launcher's `lib/`).

Every new test proven red-first — the covered line reverted, the red watched,
the file restored from a byte copy. Seven proofs, listed with their observed
failures in the field notes. Proof 1 passing on the first attempt is what
uncovered the relative-rung hazard.

Runs: `tests/hermes_cli` 591 files / 4419 passed / 4 failed (4268 s, contended
box). All four triaged: three are load flakes that pass on a quiet box (a 10 s
cross-process readiness deadline; `assert elapsed < 0.2` measuring 1.109; a
spawned process not yet exited), and the fourth,
`test_every_harness_flag_has_a_reader`, is RED ON `origin/main` — proven by
substituting `git show origin/main:hermes_cli/harness.py`, which reports the
same six flags at line numbers exactly 7 lower, the +7 lines this slice adds.
Six harness flags are advertised in `--help` and read by no handler; filed.
The failing set was also re-run with this slice's conftest fixture removed and
was no smaller. Touched files re-run green: 108 passed.

Gates: mutation 10 candidates / 10 KILLED at the default cap of 12; cite
adjacency green (one cite this change rotted, `05-chat-turn-lane.md`'s
`harness.py:4974` for `_provider_visibility_catalog`, repaired to a symbol cite
rather than a bumped line number); CLI contract green and unchanged, so no
launcher fixture re-sync is owed.

Incidental, and unblocking: two mutation claims were ALREADY stale on
`origin/main` — `s4-an-omitted-skill-flag-clears-every-instance-override` and
`s4-the-cli-create-door-drops-its-skill-flag` anchor on lines `a3b48a06a2`
replaced with the `list_flag_or_absent` reader — and the gate refused to run at
all until they were re-anchored. Pre-existence verified against
`origin/main`'s own source and claims file; same operator, same test, same
defect, in the manner of `a14057e22f`.

Field notes: docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/postinstall-shim-field-notes-2026-09-02.md
