author: nekwo
message:
feat(prep cost Stage 8): one registry walk per root per turn, and the fourth walker joins the other three

CP-4 and CP-5. The CP-9 read billed this stage on live turns rather than on the
sandbox profile it was armed with: skill work is 74-89% of the pre-admit span,
median 88.2%, with `observability_skill_rows_ms` at 157-547 ms against a 30 ms
target.

Two things the source audit changed about the shape, both recorded as
clarifications in the plan before any code was written.

`_skill_root_registry`'s process cache does NOT skip the walk. It is validated
BY fingerprint, so reaching it re-runs `iter_skill_index_files`, a whole-root
`rglob("*.md")` and a stat per path; only the frontmatter parse is skipped.
Sharing resolution RESULTS while each lane still called it would have moved
nothing, so what is shared here is the registry map itself.

And there is a fourth walker the plan's §0.3 did not name. `used_skills_context`
resolves one name at a time through the SINGULAR `resolve_skill`, which walks
every root per name — unbatched, inside the very span the read measured. A turn
naming a dozen skills walked every root a dozen times. It now takes the same map.

The map is keyed by RESOLVED ROOT PATH, and that is what makes the hand-off safe
rather than merely convenient: the observability row runs inside
`persona_profile_scope` and the context builder does not, so the two lanes can
legitimately enumerate different root LISTS. A per-path key needs no agreement
about the list — a root both lanes see is walked once, a root only one lane sees
is walked by that lane, and no lane is ever handed a root it did not ask for.

It is turn-local by construction: born in the handler frame, dead with it, never
attached to the context, the row, a persisted record or a wire frame. That is
the "do not serialize" rule satisfied by giving it nowhere else to live, rather
than by remembering to strip it — the shape Stage 6's `timings` leak argues for.

Separately, CP-4b: `skills_inventory._content_hash` read every byte of every
file of every shared skill on every turn. It is now memoized on a fingerprint of
exactly the files it hashes, copying the `(relpath, mtime_ns, size)` shape
`skill_utils.skill_package_content_hash` already uses over that identical set.
The registry fingerprint could not have keyed it — that covers resolver-visible
markdown, so a support-script edit moves these bytes while leaving it identical.

A deviation stated plainly: the walk-count tests were authored after the
implementation, not before. Against the pre-stage source they read 3 failed /
3 passed, but two of those reds are AttributeError on the new walk counter
rather than a behavioural disagreement, because the counter is part of the
stage. The mutation proof is therefore this stage's load-bearing evidence: five
mutations, all killed, two of them by tests that predate this stage and pin
precedence, collision and content-change semantics the shared map has to
preserve.

Nothing here claims a millisecond. The read gives the before; the after is ten
live turns after landing, and Stage 9's gate reads off that re-take.

Also re-anchors fifteen live canon cites the line shifts moved, each verified
byte-identical before it was written, and renumbers three waived keys to follow
them (none added, none deleted, count unchanged at 67). Cites under archive/
were deliberately left alone — that tree records what was true when it was

author: nekwo
message:
fix(readiness): the codex card asked the pool; the turn asked the auth store

The Mission Control office card for "Neko Mission Lead" (persona role
alice_supervisor, hermes profile neko) carried an amber "Provider credential
attention req..." line while every one of that agent's chat turns succeeded.
The launcher was reporting hermes honestly -- the string is
persona.readinessSummary, rendered straight from the agents_readiness snapshot
section -- so the divergence was entirely on this side.

WHAT IT TURNED OUT TO BE. profile_readiness._pooled_provider_issue answered
"can this agent serve a turn?" from load_pool("openai-codex").peek() and
NOTHING else. That is only the FIRST of the run path's credential sources:
resolve_runtime_provider takes the pool first (should_use_pool = provider !=
"openrouter", so codex qualifies) and, when the pool yields no entry, falls
through to resolve_codex_runtime_credentials(), which serves the turn from the
singleton token set in providers.openai-codex.tokens. One authority answered
the card and a different one answered the request.

Verified against the live profile store (read-only), 2026-09-08:

  credential_pool["openai-codex"] -- one entry, source "manual:device_code",
    last_status "exhausted", last_status_at 2026-09-08T16:45:54 local,
    last_error_reset_at null => _exhausted_until = last_status_at + the
    default one-hour TTL, so _available_entries() returns [] and peek() is
    None. That entry's own access token expired 2026-06-18.
  providers["openai-codex"].tokens -- last_refresh 2026-09-03T14:23:54Z,
    access token valid to 2026-09-13T14:23:55Z.
  suppressed_sources {"openai-codex": ["device_code"]} -- so the singleton is
    never seeded into the pool and the pool can never pick the working
    credential up.

and in the profile's own agent.log the same day:

  16:46:02 agent.credential_pool: credential pool: no available entries
                                  (all exhausted or empty)
  16:46:06 agent.conversation_loop: API call #1: model=gpt-5.6-luna
                                  provider=openai-codex ... latency=4.5s
  (again 16:47:44 / 16:47:47)

The turn is served by a credential the readiness probe refuses to look at. The
amber is false by construction, not a race, and it persists for the whole
cooldown -- an hour by default, longer for a persisted 429 reset.

THE CHANGE. Readiness now asks the run path's own sources, in the run path's
order, and reports attention only when NEITHER can serve:

* hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py::codex_credentials_resolvable_read_only --
  new, and deliberately sited beside the openai-codex order inside
  resolve_runtime_provider, because the defect is the two drifting apart:
  (1) the pool's own availability rules via peek(), then (2) the auth store.
* hermes_cli/auth.py::codex_auth_store_credentials_present -- new, a READ-ONLY
  mirror of resolve_codex_runtime_credentials' credential sources minus every
  branch that spends something: no refresh, no Codex usage-endpoint probe, no
  CLI import, no auth.json write, no cooldown clear. It is its own function
  rather than refresh_if_expiring=False on the resolver because the resolver's
  write/network branches are reached exactly when the singleton is unusable --
  the case readiness cares most about.
* agent_runtime/profile_readiness.py::_pooled_provider_issue ->
  _codex_provider_issue, calling the above. The rename is the fix: the old name
  described the whole defect.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MIRRORED, and why it is written at the site: the
resolver's OTHER fallback, _pool_codex_access_token, is a second and looser
read of the same pool -- it consults only last_error_reset_at, never the
last_status cooldown _available_entries just used to refuse the row. Mirroring
it would mean readiness could never report attention while any pool row held
any token string, including a long-dead one, which would retire the true
positive along with the false one. (That looseness is a run-path defect in its
own right; rowed, not fixed here.)

MCF-16 is intact and is now pinned rather than assumed: readiness refreshes no
token, advances no rotation cursor and leaves auth.json byte-identical.

RECORDED REDS. Five assertions, five mutations, each applied and reverted, run
through scripts/run_tests.sh:

M1 -- restore the pool-only answer in _codex_provider_issue
     (load_pool("openai-codex").peek() and its emptiness check):
  4 failed, 1 passed

author: nekwo
message:
perf(snapshot): the build asked Windows for the same path 662 times, and the answer never changed

The operator reported this Windows install feels slower than their Mac install of
the same runtime. Profiled it rather than guessed: one warm `build_snapshot`,
counted and attributed at the syscall.

The leading hypothesis was half right. `core_cache.build_input_fingerprint` stats
4,428 inputs and costs 77-88 ms warm, ~3% of a 2.5 s build — it already takes its
triples off `os.DirEntry`, which Windows populates from the directory enumeration,
so it is not the gap. But 378 ms of a 714 ms instrumented build (53%) IS Windows
path syscalls, and `nt._getfinalpathname` — `Path.resolve()`, which OPENS the path
to ask for its canonical name, ~71 us against a POSIX realpath's few microseconds —
is the term that separates the two platforms.

662 of the build's 1,231 `realpath` calls, and 394 of its 3,035 `os.stat` calls,
came from ONE function: `hermes_constants.get_default_hermes_root`, reached through
`_get_profiles_root` (394), `harness_root_config_path` (158), `get_shared_skills_dir`
(36), `machine_roots_registry_paths` (32), `mission_chat_workdir` (22) and
`harness_skill_destination` (20). Every one asked about the same two paths.

The function is otherwise pure path arithmetic over two strings, so this memoises
its one filesystem question on (HERMES_HOME, platform default). The key carries the
platform default deliberately: keyed on HERMES_HOME alone it would leak one answer
across the `Path.home()` fixture AGENTS.md prescribes for profile tests. Paired A/B
over the same store, alternated by stashing only this file, nine warm uncoalesced
builds per run: 608.8 / 635.1 ms before, 411.0 / 411.3 ms after — -32.5% / -35.2%.

Two other candidates were sized the same way BEFORE any code was written and both
were refused on the number: memoising `runtime_environment_status` bought 7 ms, and
disabling the core-cache write-back entirely bought 4 ms. They are rowed on their
structure, not shipped as perf.

Also here: `test_no_hermes_home_returns_native` was red on `main` on Windows — it
asserted `~/.hermes` while the native default there is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`. It
now pins `sys.platform` the way its Windows sibling already did. And the
`05-chat-turn-lane.md` cite of `hermes_constants.py:1533` follows its comment block
to :1606, since this commit moves it.

RECORDED REDS — each new assertion mutated, run, output pasted, reverted, green
re-verified (`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_hermes_constants.py`, 48 passed).

  M1, `test_repeat_calls_ask_the_filesystem_once` — deleted the memo lookup so
  every call recomputes:

    >       assert calls == [], f"the memoised call re-resolved {calls}"
    E       AssertionError: the memoised call re-resolved
            ['...\test_repeat_calls_ask_the_file-3\.hermes\profiles\coder',
             '...\test_repeat_calls_ask_the_file-3\.hermes']
    E       assert ['X:\Eternia...e-3\.hermes'] == []
    FAILED ...::TestGetDefaultHermesRootMemo::test_repeat_calls_ask_the_filesystem_once
    2 failed, 46 passed, 6 skipped

  M2, `test_the_key_carries_the_platform_default_not_just_hermes_home` — narrowed
  the key to `(env_home, "")`, i.e. HERMES_HOME alone:

    >       assert outside_native == env_home
    E       AssertionError: assert WindowsPath('.../a/.hermes')
                                == WindowsPath('.../a/.hermes/sub')
    FAILED ...::test_the_key_carries_the_platform_default_not_just_hermes_home
    1 failed, 47 passed, 6 skipped

  M3, `test_reset_makes_the_next_call_pay_again` — made
  `reset_default_hermes_root_cache` a bare `return`:

    >       assert calls, "after the reset the next call must hit the filesystem again"
    E       AssertionError: after the reset the next call must hit the filesystem again
    E       assert []
    FAILED ...::test_reset_makes_the_next_call_pay_again
    1 failed, 47 passed, 6 skipped

M1 also reddened M3's own control line ("the memo must be warm before the reset"),
which is the control doing its job: a memo that never caches makes the reset test
vacuous, and it says so rather than passing.

Focused suites, all green: `tests/test_hermes_constants.py` (48), the 15 store/
profile-root suites that reach `get_default_hermes_root` or `_get_profiles_root`
(222), the 12 `hermes_cli`/`scripts` ones (137), `tests/test_coverage_claims_resolve.py`

the live serve's readiness walk costing 5-10x the same walk in a quiet process, the
core cache's 2,094 writes against zero serves, `agent/skill_utils`' own 1,178

message:
feat(realm sync): a workspace LEVEL is a synced family, and hermes stores its bytes verbatim

The launcher measured, at 6d79b6d724, why it could not put a workspace's level
into a realm from its own side (EterniaLauncher
docs/spatial/planned/one-engine-one-catalogue-levels-per-workspace.md, "R15's
office half LANDED ... and its realm half did NOT"): it never writes the sync
repo, an unknown path is DROPPED on pull (_destination_for_sync_path -> None),
and publish_realm_sync rmtrees the realm subtree and rebuilds it from the
artifact list, so a file the launcher planted is deleted at the next publish.

This is the board/office precedent one family over:

* a `level` artifact kind minted from store/levels/<workspace token>.json,
  scoped to the realm by workspace TOKEN (the address is in the filename
  because hermes does not parse the document);
* apply_level_pull, called after the generic loop, at WHOLE-DOCUMENT
  granularity against a never-synced baseline sidecar -- the flow_graphs shape,
  not the per-actor one, because a level is one document: adopt / converge /
  keep-local / HOLD, with the held remote parked in a conflict sidecar;
* `hermes harness level {show,set}` so the launcher can hand hermes the bytes
  and read them back.

THE CONTRACT: the bytes are the launcher's SceneSerializer output VERBATIM.
hermes validates exactly two facts (UTF-8 JSON, an object carrying a numeric
`version`) and reformats nothing -- so the launcher's one-prop-per-line
indentation, which is what makes a realm-sync diff per-prop hunks, survives
every machine that pulls. Identity for the MERGE is the JSON value (parse,
canonicalise, hash), so two publishers who disagree only about whitespace
converge instead of conflicting while the stored bytes stay their author's.

Deliberately NOT a store_drift family. realm_revert subscripts
_PROCESS_ORDER[row.family] directly and dispatches on family for the store
door, so a drift row with no revert arm hands `revert --all` a KeyError and
offers an exit that does not exist -- the reason _flow_graph_status_row records
for why the canvas was not one either until its revert arm landed. The level
family gets the same top-level `levels` status row instead; its revert arm is a
filed follow-up, and test_the_level_family_is_not_a_store_drift_family pins the
decision so a later lane has to make it rather than inherit it.

Also re-anchors six doc cites into hermes_cli/harness.py: the `level` subparser
inserted 20 lines after old line 1047, which left every cite below it pointing
at somebody else's parser (67 -> 74 failures, 8 of them unwaived). The three
prompt-observability cites into paths.py were 144 lines adrift ALREADY and
waived as "NOT MECHANICALLY RE-ANCHORABLE"; this change's +51 moved them again,
so they are anchored to the true lines and the waiver is deleted as genuinely
stale rather than accidentally so.

MUTATION RECORDS -- green baseline first (83 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0 over
test_realm_sync, test_flow_graph_sync_pull, test_harness_parts_namespace,
test_harness_json_root_observability), each mutation applied, run, reverted:

A. pull_realm_sync never calls the applier
   -  level_summary = apply_level_pull(realm.id, subtree)
   +  level_summary = LevelPullSummary()
   => 8 passed, 2 FAILED, EXIT=1
      test_a_pulled_level_lands_through_the_store_door
        E  AssertionError: assert [] == ['ws_launcher_eb9b9c']
      test_publishing_then_pulling_is_not_a_hold_on_my_own_environment
        E  AssertionError: assert [] == ['ws_launcher_cbeffc']

B. the level is never minted as an artifact (publish deletes it)
   -  artifacts.extend(level_scan.artifacts)
   => 7 passed, 3 FAILED, EXIT=1

message:
feat(reconcile): a scoped instance whose only placement is archived is a ghost, and the reconciler says so

A placement IS its instance (operator ruling, July 2026). So an instance whose
only office placement has been archived is a GHOST: the character left the floor
and the roster kept counting it. Measured on the live store 2026-09-11 — the
Default workspace reported `agents: 3` against two drawn characters for a week,
because `personainst_chara_a2_7b31d0e4`'s actor was archived on 09-04 and its
`persona_instances/` row stayed `state: idle`. Nothing here self-healed it:
`persona-instance reconcile` HELD the row (it is backed by a seeded persona, so
not an orphan) and had no classification for this state at all.

The launcher's half is fixed in its own repo — its archive lane was routing that
removal to `runtime.office.remove` on the strength of the id's SPELLING. This
half is a different guarantee: a row that reaches this state by ANY route (an
older launcher, a hand-run `office actor-remove`, a realm pull) gets reported
and reaped.

Phase 2b, `classify_unplaced_persona_instances`. A row is a candidate when all
four hold, and not one of them is a question about an id's shape:

  1. it names a `workspace_id`;
  2. it is NOT the persona/profile's canonical operator channel. The
     base-profile foundation gives every agent a free PROFILE row and those are
     chat channels, never placements — the same discriminator `agent retire`
     refuses on (`canonical_persona_channel`), asked through ONE derivation:
     `is_canonical_persona_channel` now delegates to a new
     `row_is_canonical_persona_channel(instance_id, persona_id)` so the pure
     classifier does not re-spell it;
  3. an ARCHIVED office actor in that row's OWN workspace names it — positive
     evidence that it WAS placed there;
  4. NO live office actor ANYWHERE names it. Not "in its own workspace": an
     instance re-placed onto a second floor is on a floor.

The HELD rules stay in force and are now shared rather than copied —
`_held_reason_for` is the one spelling for both prune classifiers in this
module. The min-age grace applies here (`allow_recent_hold=True`), which is what
keeps "removed the desk, still chatting to the agent" from becoming a reap.

`office_placement_evidence` gathers both halves through the `scan_actors`
chokepoint and returns `(None, None)` the moment any workspace scan reports
unreadable files. That is the whole safety posture, not an edge case: the
central question is a NEGATIVE one, and a negative computed over a short read is
a false positive that archives a live agent's row. `None` classifies nothing and
says so in `skipped`, which the CLI prints — a skipped phase and a clean phase
both show no prunes otherwise.

The prune itself is the existing archive-never-delete lane: typed
`persona_instance.pruned` event, its own timestamped archive directory,
`apply=False` writes nothing, the cross-store `_has_live_binding` belt, and the
reap is discounted from the live set phase 5 asks its owner-liveness question
against.

NOT IN THIS COMMIT, and filed as a row in the launcher's Mission Control queue
rather than left implied: the snapshot `_parity_warnings` arm. Its evidence is
"an ARCHIVED actor names this instance" and the snapshot's `offices` section
carries LIVE actors only. Measured on the live store: 82 archived actor files /
59 KB across 2 workspaces against 4 live actors, with no retention policy — so
carrying the ids on the wire is an unbounded per-snapshot list and decoding them
in `_offices_summary` is a 21x increase in files read on the snapshot build
path, both growing with every removal forever. That is a cost that wants a
ruling, not a side effect of this lane.

RED-FIRST — tests/agent_runtime/test_persona_instance_unplaced.py
  command for every entry below:
    bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent_runtime/test_persona_instance_unplaced.py

  H-M1  killing mutation: treat an archived placement as LIVE —
                          `for actor in live_scan.actors` -> `for actor in full_scan.actors`
        applied to:       agent_runtime/persona_instance_identity.py::office_placement_evidence
        red:              6 of 12 failed —
          test_the_live_defect_archiving_the_actor_alone_leaves_a_ghost
            assert set() == {'personainst_chara_a2_7b31d0e4'}
          test_a_just_removed_placement_is_HELD_not_pruned
            assert set() == {'personainst_chara_a2_7b31d0e4'}
          test_an_instance_bound_to_live_work_is_HELD   IndexError: list index out of range
          test_an_unreadable_office_store_classifies_NOTHING_and_says_so
            assert set() == {'personainst_chara_a2_7b31d0e4'}   (its positive control)
          test_reconcile_dry_run_reports_the_ghost_and_writes_nothing
          test_reconcile_apply_archives_the_ghost_and_never_deletes_it
        reverted:         12 passed

  H-M2  killing mutation: delete the `row_is_canonical_persona_channel` guard
        applied to:       persona_instance_identity.py::classify_unplaced_persona_instances
        red:              1 of 12 —
          test_the_canonical_persona_channel_is_never_classified
            assert 'personainst_qa' not in {'personainst_qa'}
        reverted:         12 passed

author: nekwo
message:
feat(mission-chat): a provider refusal is a typed verdict, not an unknown outcome

The operator's OpenAI Codex plan ran out. The provider answered HTTP 429 with
`error.type = usage_limit_reached`. Mission Control said "Hermes cannot prove
whether turn agent-chat-recovery-1789167163134553 completed" and offered
**Abandon & resend** — so the operator resent, into the same wall, and still
was never told their plan was out of usage.

Second instance of the class `budget_exhausted` was minted for on 2026-07-26: a
KNOWN terminal cause reported as "I cannot prove what the provider did". The
2026-07-26 fix added one more boolean to a two-boolean table. This one retires
the class instead: `classify_turn_failure` now reads a typed verdict OFF THE
EXCEPTION, and the table answers only what is left.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE
--------------------------------------
What reaches the chat lane's `except Exception as exc` on a live 429 is a
`ProfileRunnerError` whose `str()` is `AIAgent._summarize_api_error` TEXT —
and nothing else. The SDK exception never leaves `agent/conversation_loop.py`:
it is summarized into a result dict there (`{"failed": True, "error": <text>}`)
and re-raised as a fresh `RuntimeError` subclass at `profile_runner._run`'s
tail. `status_code`, `.body`, `response.headers` — everything
`extract_api_error_context` reads — are gone four frames before the classifier
sees anything. So the prose really was the only signal available, and the fix
had to be to CARRY the context, from fork-owned code, rather than regex it.

WHAT SHIPPED
------------
* `profile_runner` (fork-owned): `_ProviderErrorCapture` wraps the agent's own
  `_extract_api_error_context` for the length of one run — the call the
  conversation loop already makes, on every API error, with the live SDK
  exception in hand — and `ProfileRunnerError` grew a `provider_error` block.
  Upstream `run_agent.py` / `agent/*` are untouched.
  The capture hands its block over ONLY when the terminal result's `error`
  string equals the summary it captured: a 429 that a retry recovered, followed
  minutes later by an unrelated death, must not report a plan wall that is not
  there.
* `mission_chat_outcome`: `ProviderRefusal` + the pure `provider_refusal(exc)`.
  A refusal is 401/402/403/404/429, or a 400 the harness classified as
  something other than a repairable one. A 5xx, a timeout, a reset, a stream
  that died after first byte stay `outcome_unknown` — that ambiguity is real
  and is pinned in both test files.
  New `ChatErrorKind.CHAT_TURN_PROVIDER_REFUSED` / `ExecutionState.FAILED`,
  terminal, `turn_resolution_required: False`, `next_expected` naming the wait.
* `mission_chat_turns`: new JOURNAL state `provider_refused`, mirrored through
  every lifecycle set exactly as `budget_exhausted` is, reachable only from
  `executing`. NOT the legacy `failed` the plan named: `failed` belongs to the
  pre-journal streaming vocabulary and `next_turn_state` refuses a journal ->
  legacy write by construction, so that write would have been dropped and the
  record would have stayed `executing`. Plus `safe_provider_refusal`, because
  the journal metadata is a strict whitelist and an unsanitized nested block is
  silently discarded.
* `persona_commands`: the refusal arm on the failure frame, and the honest
  refusal for a resend of an id already spent on one.
* the three harness-runtime-model docs that list `error_kind` values.

KILLING MUTATIONS — applied, red recorded, reverted
---------------------------------------------------
| # | mutation                                                  | red |
|---|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----|
| a | drop the refusal arm from `classify_turn_failure`         | 3 fail; the live-429 seam test reports `blocked`/`chat_turn_outcome_unknown` again — the incident verbatim |
| b | add 503 to `PROVIDER_REFUSAL_STATUS_CODES`                | 2 fail; `test_a_server_error_stays_ambiguous[503]` + classifier row 4 |
| c | `next_expected` stops reading the reset                   | 1 fail; positive control: with-reset and without-reset stop projecting differently |
| d | `_ProviderErrorCapture.block_for` stops checking identity | 1 fail; a recovered 429 is attached to "Connection reset by peer" |
| e | `_safe_journal_metadata` stops admitting the block        | 1 fail; `KeyError: 'provider_refusal'` off the real record |
| f | the CLI's `elif provider_refused` journal arm is disabled | 3 fail; `assert 'outcome_unknown' == 'provider_refused'` — the incident, in the record |
| g | the frame drops `provider_refusal`                        | 1 fail; `KeyError: 'provider_refusal'` on the envelope |

Mutation (e) SURVIVED on its first attempt and that is why
`test_the_refused_turn_record_carries_the_block_through_the_real_write_path`
exists: the sanitizer was pinned and the PATH through it was not — a capture is

author: nekwo
message:
feat(realm sync): the SKILL family joins the three-way model — direction, not just divergence

The skill family was the last synced family deciding TWO-way (canonical package
vs the per-realm inbox mirror, `skill_promotion.classify_promotion`) with no
never-synced baseline. Four consequences, all structural, and the launcher's
SKILLS HELD card could only ever offer "adopt theirs" because of the first:

1. no DIRECTION — "I edited it" and "they edited it" are the same
   `hold_divergent`, so nothing could offer "publish mine";
2. every realm-side skill update was a HOLD for every member who merely OWNED
   the skill, where every sibling family fast-forwards that case;
3. after publishing a real local edit the hold SURVIVED, because nothing recorded
   a baseline and nothing refreshed the inbox the drift is computed from;
4. a local skill edit lit nothing at all — `store_drift` had no skill family, so
   the sheet read "In sync" over a canonical package that differed from the
   realm's, with no revert row.

And the phantom the operator actually saw on 2026-09-12 was a fifth: the
decision was made on `skill_package_content_hash`, a BYTE hash, being asked a
CONTENT question. 13 of 29 files in their canonical `launcher-mcp-operations`
carried CRLF, the realm's copy was LF, `diff -r --strip-trailing-cr` between
them was empty, and the lane classified `hold_divergent` forever. The existing
`test_pull_converges_eol_only_difference` covers the other direction only (CRLF
ARRIVING against an LF canonical, which the mirror normalizes on the way in);
a Windows editor writing the canonical copy was never covered.

Design authority (diagnosis + contract packet):
`EterniaLauncher/docs/mission_control/planned/held-skill-publish-direction.md`
section 4. The launcher half of the change is building against that section in
parallel.

WHAT LANDS

* `agent_runtime/sync_text.py::canonicalize_text_bytes` — the body lifted out of
  `realm_sync._canonicalize_text_bytes`, which becomes an alias (no behaviour
  change on the publish path). It had to move because `skill_promotion` may not
  import `realm_sync`.
* `skill_promotion.skill_package_sync_hash` — same walk, same exclusions, same
  digest shape as `agent.skill_utils.skill_package_content_hash`, over each
  file's canonicalized bytes. `_package_hash` is now this, so every promotion
  DECISION and the provenance receipt carry the sync hash.
  `skill_package_content_hash` itself is untouched: the resolver cache and the
  installer-ownership manifest want the byte hash on purpose (design section 7).
* `paths.skill_baseline_path` + `agent_runtime/skill_sync.py` — the baseline
  sidecar (`{schema_version: 1, entries: {"skill::<slug>": <sync hash>}}`), the
  ONE classifier `classify_inbox_package`, and `resolve_held_skill`.
* `apply_skill_inbox_pull` is three-way through the shared
  `sync_merge.classify_three_way_pull`. New buckets `updated` (their change,
  mine untouched → installed, my previous canonical archived) and `kept_local`
  (my edit, theirs unmoved → nothing written). `skills_drift` = `held` = both
  moved = CONFLICTS ONLY. `_held_skill_packages_for_realm` and the pull loop go
  through the SAME classifier (surfaced on `list_inbox_packages`' additive
  `decision` / `baseline_hash` columns), so the sheet's card and the pull result
  cannot disagree — they could, and did.
* `publish_realm_sync` records the baseline for every published package and then
  RE-MIRRORS the inbox from the subtree (the subtree is the realm once the push
  lands), before the sidecar recomputes `skills_drift`.
* `DRIFT_FAMILY_SKILL` with an empty container, `store_drift.skills` counts
  summed by `_any_store_drift`, and the revert arm (`changed` → adopt the
  realm's copy, mine archived; `added` → archive mine, no realm-visible
  tombstone; `removed` → reinstall from the inbox, else drop the stale entry).
  `realm_sync.publishable_skill_packages` is now ONE authority for "which
  packages does this realm publish", shared by the publish, the post-publish
  baseline and the drift walk — three copies of that filter chain would be free
  to disagree, and a drift row for a package the publish would not ship offers a
  Publish that changes nothing.
* `hermes harness realm sync resolve <realm> --key skill::<slug> --take
  local|remote --yes --json`, dispatched on the `skill::` prefix; `realm sync
  held` lists skill holds as `kind: "skill_hold"`. Both takes record baseline :=
  the realm's hash ("I have seen their version"); `remote` installs the inbox
  copy through the ONE guarded door, `local` writes NOTHING to the package so
  the next status says `changed` and the next publish ships it. No per-skill
  publish verb and no second write path.

Every write still goes through `skill_promotion.execute_promotion`: one live
namespace, archive-never-delete, atomic install, provenance outside package
dirs, `promotion_refusal` consulted before any write.

CONTRACT CHANGE worth naming: a `PromotionPlan`'s `source_hash`/`canonical_hash`
and a provenance record's `content_hash`/`previous_hash` are now the SYNC hash.
Four existing cases in `test_skill_promotion.py` asserted them against the byte
hash and are updated with a `_sync_hash` helper beside the kept `_pkg_hash`.

author: nekwo
message:
docs(realm sync): the mutation record for the skill three-way lane — eighteen named kills, and the first round's mistake

The evidence the previous commit's checks are owed:
`docs/agent-runtime-harness/planned/skill-three-way-sync-mutation-record-2026-09-12.md`.
Eighteen mutations, each applied to the tree, run against the test(s) it must
red, and reverted from pre-mutation bytes with the restore re-hashed and printed
— a sabotage round that cannot prove it reverted has left running code behind.

The two the design note MANDATES (section 4.4) are recorded TWICE, and the note
says why. First round they were applied by renaming their calls to undefined
names; both "reddened" with a `NameError`, which is a crash rather than a
measurement — it proves the line executes and says nothing about what the
assertion detects, so a test asserting nothing would have passed that round
identically. Redone as genuine deletions of the two blocks:

* delete the baseline write → `KeyError: 'skill::foo'`, the baseline carries no
  entry for a package this publish just shipped;
* delete the inbox re-mirror → the inbox still holds the realm's pre-publish
  bytes (`b'...# Realm v1\n' != b'...# Mine v2\n'`), so the hold the operator
  published away survives the publish.

Also recorded: the throwaway sabotage of
`agent_runtime/sync_text.canonicalize_text_bytes` that proved the WORKTREE's code
is what runs under this venv (which has the primary checkout installed editable)
before any of the eighteen were trusted.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(harness): `skills inbox` projects the three-way decision beside the two-way action

The listing verb hand-picked its row keys and dropped the `decision` and
`baseline_hash` columns `list_inbox_packages` gained when the skill family
joined the three-way model (a0d5f9aa84), so an operator reading the verb still
saw `hold_divergent` for a package the pull would fast-forward. Found on the
first live read after landing.

Mutation record: with the projection missing `decision` the new test fails
`KeyError: 'decision'` (observed before the patch); with it present, 14 passed
across the verb test, the CLI contract dump, the root-observability meta-test
and the line-endings gate. The test's positive control writes its CRLF fixture
as BYTES — text mode on Windows rewrites CRLF as CR CR LF, which is a different
document after canonicalization, and that cost one red run before it was seen.

author: nekwo
message:
fix(realm sync): an install that predates the skill baseline records agreement as its baseline

Measured live on 2026-09-12, minutes after a0d5f9aa84 landed: the operator's
realm had an inbox mirrored on Sep 1 and no skill_baseline.json, and the first
local edit of launcher-mcp-operations classified HELD (new_both) — "both changed"
over a change only one side made. new_both is the honest verdict when nothing is
known, but something was known the moment before the edit: canonical and inbox
agreed.

The rule, deliberately NARROW: `seed_converged_skill_baselines` records a missing
baseline entry ONLY where the canonical copy and the inbox copy already agree
(sync hash, so a CRLF working copy of an LF inbox counts). Persisted at two
doors — `realm_sync_status` (before the held read and the drift walk) and
`apply_skill_inbox_pull` (over the PRE-mirror inbox, before the mirror rewrites
it). Disagreement seeds nothing and stays held; the operator's resolve records
the baseline there.

The broad rule ("the inbox stands in for the baseline") was tried first and is
wrong: after a pull that HELD a package the inbox carries a version the member
never accepted, so seeding from it reads an untouched-but-stale local copy as
*my edit* — kept_local, a `changed` drift row, and a Publish that regresses the
realm's newer copy. It reddened seven existing hold/resolve tests the moment it
ran, which is the measurement the docstring cites. Two in-memory seeds (drift
walk, inbox listing) were also removed: agreement classifies `converged` with or
without a baseline, so no mutation could kill them.

Mutation record (each applied → named test → reverted, file hash verified):
  M-A drop `record_converged_skill_baselines` in realm_sync_status
      → test_a_pre_baseline_install_reads_my_edit_as_drift_not_a_hold
        KeyError: 'skill::foo' (no baseline was recorded)            exit 1
  M-C drop `record_converged_skill_baselines` before the pull's mirror
      → test_a_pre_baseline_install_fast_forwards_a_realm_change_on_pull
        assert [] == ['foo']  (updated is empty; the package was held) exit 1
Green: 144 passed across test_realm_sync_skill_inbox, test_skill_promotion,
test_realm_revert and the skills-inbox verb test (exit 0).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
